title: story: :network is INERT on a live run-variant — the lowered :rf.http/managed-test-stub is never registered outside artifact replay
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-08 by worker exdoc-a while running rf2-cckg's acceptance (PR from worker/exdoc-a).

THE DEFECT. A Story variant's `:network` route map compiles correctly but does nothing at run time.
`re-frame.story.plan/lower-network` lowers `:network` to
`:fx-overrides {:rf.http/managed :rf.http/managed-test-stub}` and keeps the route map at
`[:world :network]`. `:rf.http/managed-test-stub` is registered by exactly one thing —
`re-frame.http.test-support/install-managed-request-stubs!` — and across `tools/story/src` that
helper is called ONLY from `re-frame.story.artifact` (replay). Nothing on the `run-variant` /
`allocate!` path calls it. Verified: `grep -rln 'managed-test-stub' tools/story/src/` returns
artifact.cljc, plan.cljc, promotion.cljc — no runtime, no frames, no play/runner.

CONSEQUENCE. The override names an fx id that does not resolve, the `:preset :story` generic
canned-success stub answers instead, and the variant sees `{:status :ok :value {:stubbed true}}`.

MEASURED SYMPTOM, on `:story.login/success` (examples/core/login/stories.cljs), whose `:network`
fixture landed in PR #9386 as rf2-hz8u's source fix. Driving the registered variant with
`rf.story/run-variant` under the development Malli validator:
  - lifecycle reaches :ready
  - :auth.login/flow machine sits at :submitting, NOT :authed
  - :rf.machine/has-tag? :auth.login/flow :auth/authenticated is false (no Welcome banner)
  - :auth.session/store never fires, so no token is stored
  - one :rf.error/schema-validation-failure :where :event, frame :story.login/success,
    :received [:auth.login/succeeded {:status :ok :value {:stubbed true}}],
    error :malli.core/missing-key at [1 :value :token]

That is the EXACT pre-fix symptom rf2-hz8u described. The discriminating measurement: the identical
failure appears with the `:network` slot PRESENT and with it REMOVED. The compiled bundle was
confirmed to carry the fixture (`grep -c 'Ada Lovelace' .shadow-cljs/builds/node-test/dev/out/cljs-runtime/login.stories.js` = 1), so this is not a stale-compile artefact.

SO PR #9386 DID NOT ACTUALLY FIX THE CANONICAL SCREENSHOT. The variant body is right; the runtime
never installs the stub. rf2-hz8u should be reopened or superseded by this bead.

REPAIR (tools/story, fenced from the reporting dispatch): on the `run-variant` path, where the
frame is allocated with `[:world :frame :fx-overrides]`, also install the route map from
`[:world :network]` via `install-managed-request-stubs!` (and uninstall on `destroy!`, LIFO —
the helper is stack-disciplined per rf2-vn8qjv). `re-frame.story.artifact/with-network-stubs`
already does exactly this for replay and is the shape to reuse.

ACCEPTANCE. Re-enable the end-to-end drive: run the registered `:story.login/success` in a newly
allocated variant frame with the development validator on, and assert it reaches :authed, that
:rf.machine/has-tag? :auth/authenticated is true, that :auth.session/store received
{:token "demo-token-123"}, and that no :where :event schema refusal fired. That test was written,
measured red, and is preserved verbatim in the PR body / commit 13b318c834's message on
worker/exdoc-a; what LANDED in implementation/core/test/re_frame/example_login_success_token_cljs_test.cljs
is the plan-level guard that can hold without the runtime fix, plus an in-place note recording all
of the above. Land the runtime fix, then restore the drive.
close_reason: ALREADY FIXED ON MAIN — stale-base false finding, and the measurement behind it was sound. This was filed by worker exdoc-a at ~00:2x from a worktree branched off origin/main at ~23:34. PR #9398 (rf2-shx4, worker story-a) merged at 00:08:51 as 692c2e3e55 and is the fix for exactly the cause named here: 'install-managed-request-stubs! is called from re-frame.story.artifact (replay) and nowhere on the run-variant path'. Verified by the mayor at tip: tools/story/src/re_frame/story/network.cljc now exists and calls install-managed-request-stubs!; runtime.cljc:878 calls network/install-for-frame! on the REGISTERED path and :1642 on the INLINE path; frames.cljc:968 and :1078 release on the corresponding destroy paths. So the fx id the plan lowers to is registered on both live run paths, which is precisely what this bead reports as missing. exdoc-a's evidence was good and its discriminator was right — identical failure with the :network slot present and absent, with the compiled bundle confirmed to carry the fixture, ruling out a stale compile — it simply measured a tree that no longer exists. NOT AN INDICTMENT OF THE WORKER: it was fenced out of tools/story and correctly filed rather than reaching into a fenced surface, and it could not have known a sibling PR would land mid-flight. THE COORDINATOR'S LESSON: when a long dispatch runs across a merge that touches its subject, the report's measurements carry the base they were taken on, not the tip. Check the merge log against the dispatch timestamp before believing a P1 filed from a worker's tree. IF THE SYMPTOM PERSISTS on a current base, that is NEW evidence and deserves a fresh bead with a fresh measurement — do not reopen this one on the strength of the old run.

title: docs(xray): RULED B — scope the production-elision guarantee to build placement; rewrite ~18 claim sites
description:
RULED B on 2026-09-06 (RULING note on this bead): Xray is kept out of production by BUILD PLACEMENT, not by construction. This bead is now the prose sweep — one worker, one PR, no code behaviour change. Option A (gate init!/mount on goog.DEBUG + an Xray-rooted elision probe) was DECLINED; its un-park triggers are in the RULING note. The full analysis (both reviewers) is attached in notes as DOSSIER ATTACHMENT; the pre-ruling description is preserved in notes as ORIGINAL DESCRIPTION.

PROBLEM (measured at tip 6d513ba07f, 2026-09-06; re-measure at yours)

Xray has two install paths and one gate. The preload path (day8.re-frame2-xray.preload via shadow-cljs :devtools/preloads) wraps its boot block in (when rf.interop/debug-enabled? ...) (tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/preload.cljs:94-133), which Closure folds away under :advanced + {goog.DEBUG false}. The manual path — require day8.re-frame2-xray.core, (xray/init!), a mount verb — has NO gate: init! (core.cljs:159-184) registers 37 :rf.xray/* handlers, the trace/epoch collectors, six window.day8.re_frame2_xray.* globals and the Ctrl+Shift+C keydown listener unconditionally; open!/open-overlay!/toggle!/popout! are bare def-aliases of mount/*; mount/open! (:929-964) gates only on substrate-adapter presence (:960), which every production app that called rf/init! has. Requiring the facade at all runs load-time registrations: seven register-first-mount-hook! forms at mount.cljs:682-845, nine top-level rf/reg-view forms in shell.cljs (:991-:2565, reaching registrar/register! regardless of goog.DEBUG), and keybinding.cljs:602. No CI gate proves Xray's absence from an optimised bundle: npm run test:elision roots re-frame.* sentinels only; implementation/scripts/check-bundle-isolation.cjs contains zero Xray sentinels.

Yet ~18 sites assert the opposite ("zero bytes", "MUST be gated", "CI verifies via test:elision", "mount never reaches production builds"). PR #9226 (merged 2026-09-04, 726d8bf1df) corrected skills/re-frame2-xray/** only, so the repo now teaches two contradictory models of one safety property.

TARGET WORDING — the skill's three facts, in the same words at every site:
1. The preload is dev-only because :devtools/preloads is dev build configuration; its debug-enabled? block folds under goog.DEBUG=false as a second line of defence for that path only. The trace/epoch collectors gate their own entry points (trace_collector.cljs, drop_in.cljc).
2. The manual init!/mount path carries NO goog.DEBUG gate. Exclusion is the host's job: put the :require AND the calls in a namespace only the dev entry point loads (recipe: skills/re-frame2-xray/references/launch-programmatic.md, section "Keeping the manual path out of production" — link or restate it; a bare "guard the require" is not enough guidance). Guarding only the calls is insufficient because requiring the facade runs load-time registrations.
3. No CI gate proves Xray's absence from a release bundle. test:elision is framework-only; check-bundle-isolation.cjs never roots Xray. Grepping a release bundle for "rf-xray-root" / "rf.xray" is a leak detector, not proof of zero retained bytes.

DELETE OUTRIGHT (no hedged survivors, no deprecation footnotes — pre-alpha, no shims): "zero bytes", "non-negotiable", "MUST be gated on a single dev-only sentinel", "CI verifies via npm run test:elision", "the elision holds whether you remember to remove the preload or not", "production builds DCE this ns", "mount never reaches production builds", open! no-ops in "production builds". The seven "rides the preload, so production DCEs this ns" docstrings become "dev-only by build placement (see preload.cljs); nothing in this ns gates on goog.DEBUG", or lose the sentence where it adds nothing. 011-Launch-Modes.md:754 ("the mount module itself carries no elision logic") is TRUE under B and stays; the MUST at :748 goes.

SITES (dossier census at tip 6d513ba07f — RE-CENSUS ON BOTH TOKEN AXES, `debug-enabled?` and `production build|elide|elision|never reach|zero bytes|DCE`, before editing; the list grew 4 -> 18 between passes):
- tools/xray/spec: Principles.md:131-136; 011-Launch-Modes.md:748-758; 007-UX-IA.md:1750-1754; API.md:137-139; 015-Configuration.md:985-992; 000-Vision.md:236-238; 017-Test-Coverage-Matrix.md:116 (regrade from `covered` — PINNED by tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/coverage_matrix_metadata_test.clj; read the test first, run the suite after).
- tools/xray/src docstrings only (no code): mount.cljs:33-36; core.cljs:79-81; config.cljc:23-24 and :543-545; drop_in.cljc:86-89; filters/persistence.cljs:27-28; static/persistence.cljs:31-32; static/machines/persistence.cljs:29-30; panels/hicasso_reads.cljs:38-40; panels/derivation_graph.cljs:74-76.
- docs: docs/skills/re-frame2-xray.md:7 (hand-authored published summary — nothing regenerates it from SKILL.md; edit directly); docs/xray/01-installation.md:134-138; docs/xray/api/mount-control.md:5, :63, :135, :196-205 (its Manual install section at :61-74 must show the dev-only-namespace placement); tools/README.md:122-124.
- skills/re-frame2-xray/**: STANDS as corrected by #9226. Optional one-clause qualification of references/launch-programmatic.md:80 ("only goog.DEBUG gate" -> "only gate on a launch path; the collectors carry their own") ONLY together with evals/evals.json:61 and evals/README.md:57, which pin the current phrase — all three or none; a skill edit runs the check_skill_* gates and the api-manifest JVM test.

CONSUMERS: 0 in-repo apps use the manual facade (13 code files require day8.re-frame2-xray.core: Story focus!, the edn-inspector testbed, three Xray tests, api-manifest tooling). The canonical path is the preload — 25 :preloads wirings in implementation/shadow-cljs.edn. No behaviour changes, so nothing moves.

CODE: none. preload_decoupling_cljs_test, core_cljs_test, mount_cljs_test and settings/effects_cljs_test stay untouched and green.

HOT ZONE / SEQUENCING: no fixed-list hot-zone file. Same-file overlaps: rf2-kuky.48 (open, P2) sweeps tools/xray src+tests+testbeds+spec from the `:<-` sub-input sugar to `:inputs` at 106 sites — do NOT run concurrently; this bead first, kuky.48 rebases. rf2-kuky.4's eventual implementation rewrites mount.cljs:290 — a different hunk from the :33-36 docstring; whichever merges second rebases.

GATES BY PATH (foreground, to completion, never piped through a filter): docs/xray/** and docs/skills/** -> python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py + mkdocs build --strict (the strict build stages spec/ itself; it does NOT validate anchors — the slug gate does); tools/xray/spec/*.md -> check_doc_slugs.py (roots include tools/*/spec); tools/README.md -> python scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci (the slug gate exits 0 on a broken link there); 017 regrade -> tools/xray JVM suite (clojure -M:test from tools/xray); skill edits, if any -> scripts/check_skill_description_budget.py, check_skill_eval_docs.py, check_skill_eval_packaging.py, api-manifest clojure -M:test. Nothing validates prose, tables or rendering — hand-check anchors and table column counts and say so in the PR body.

ACCEPTANCE
1. Every site above, plus any the re-census finds, states the three facts; none of the deleted claims survives in tools/xray, docs/xray, docs/skills, tools/README.md or skills/re-frame2-xray — paste the final both-axes grep counts in the PR body (0 for every deleted phrase).
2. 017-Test-Coverage-Matrix.md:116 is regraded and coverage_matrix_metadata_test.clj is green.
3. Skill, spec, docs and docstrings agree; the PR body lists which tools/xray/spec passages moved (Xray specs kept current).
4. Named gates green; no code behaviour change; existing Xray init/mount tests untouched.
5. Acceptance 1 and 2 inherited from rf2-yk5i (the goog.DEBUG=false probe rooted through rf/init! + xray/init! + xray/open!; the Xray-sentinel bundle gate) are RETIRED by this ruling — not passed, not parked in a bead. Un-park triggers: a named host that needs an ordinary release namespace to reference the manual facade, or any "gated by construction" / "zero bytes" / "CI verifies" claim re-entering the tree.

NON-GOALS (from rf2-yk5i, unchanged): no runtime banner (rf2-fguoj and rf2-2oug, both closed, already declined it), no disable setting, no compatibility layer, no new launch mode; no change to panels, mount lifecycle, Pair, or the framework's own elision system (test:elision, check-elision.cjs, the rf2-udro3 control rule).
notes:
MAYOR VERIFICATION 2026-09-05 — I checked the filing worker's central claim myself and it holds. Adding two things: a wider census than it reported, and the shape of the ruling this needs from Mike.

THERE IS NO XRAY ELISION GATE. Enumerated rather than name-grepped (a name search cannot see a derived list, which refuted a different bead today): 43 files carry elision probes or prod-gate tests across adapters, core, hicasso bench and pair-mcp. The only two that mention xray are `implementation/core/src/re_frame/elision.cljc` and a pair-mcp test — neither roots an Xray namespace. The filing worker's independent enumeration agrees: `npm run test:elision` covers 56 sentinels across 18 distinct `re-frame.*` namespaces and roots no Xray namespace at all.

THE IN-CODE CLAIMS ARE WIDER THAN THE BEAD RECORDS. The worker flagged TWO stale docstrings. I found FOUR sites in shipped `tools/xray/src/` asserting production elision:
  * `mount.cljs:34` — "mount never reaches production builds. This namespace therefore …"
  * `config.cljc:543` — "production builds DCE the Xray shell that …"
  * `core.cljs:80` — "is installed — production builds, hosts that never called `rf/init!` …"
  * `drop_in.cljc:87` — "`re-frame.interop/debug-enabled?` — production builds elide the …"
Whichever way the ruling goes, all four move together or the tree contradicts itself again. Re-census before editing; this is four sites found on one axis and the prose axis has found extra sites three times today.

THE MECHANISM THAT MAKES THIS SHARPER THAN "ADD A GUARD", and it is the filing worker's best finding: requiring `day8.re-frame2-xray.core` transitively loads `mount.cljs`, whose bottom runs SEVEN top-level `register-first-mount-hook!` calls AT NAMESPACE-LOAD TIME. So a host wrapping the CALLS in `(when ^boolean goog.DEBUG …)` is not protected — the side effects already ran at require time. The correct host-side rule is to guard the `:require` itself, which is what the skill now says (PR #9226, merged or merging).

THE RULING MIKE NEEDS TO MAKE, stated as a fork because both branches are defensible and they lead to very different work:

  (A) GATE THE FACADE — make the claims true. Put the Xray surface behind `goog.DEBUG` so an optimised build genuinely DCEs it, and add an Xray elision gate so the guarantee is enforced rather than asserted. Cost: real code work in `tools/xray/`, plus builds added to `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn`, which is HOT ZONE and would move the check-count band the merge criterion uses. Benefit: the four claims become true and stay true.

  (B) SCOPE THE GUARANTEE — accept that Xray reaches a production bundle unless the host guards its require, and correct all four sites to say so, prominently. Cost: none beyond the edit. Benefit: the tree stops asserting something no gate enforces. Risk: consumers who believed the claim ship Xray unknowingly, so this branch needs the corrected wording to be loud, not a footnote.

MY RECOMMENDATION IS (B) FIRST AND (A) SEPARATELY IF WANTED. The immediate defect is that shipped code makes four false claims about a safety property; correcting them is cheap, unblocks nothing else, and cannot regress. (A) is a genuine feature with hot-zone cost and a band change, and it should be its own bead with its own dispatch rather than riding on a docstring correction. But this is a product call about what Xray guarantees, not a mayor call — hence the hold.

DO NOT DISPATCH (A) WITHOUT MIKE'S RULING. (B) is dispatchable the moment he says so.
AUDIT PR #9226 (merge 726d8bf1df7f97d31374e38690a47c35109f4ab7), completeness lens: the skill-local repair is correct, but the same production-safety defect remains in the shipped public documentation and belongs to this already-open follow-up rather than a new bead. Exact residual carriers on post-merge `origin/main`: `docs/skills/re-frame2-xray.md:7` still says production builds elide Xray entirely through the debug gate; `docs/xray/01-installation.md:136` says bundle-isolation checks prevent Xray strings leaking even if a dev path remains reachable; and `docs/xray/api/mount-control.md:5,135,196-205` says the install/global mirror elides under `goog.DEBUG=false`, calls Xray dev-only by construction, cites `check-bundle-isolation.cjs` as an Xray-sentinel gate, and promises elision even if the preload is not removed. The same page documents the ungated manual `init!` path at lines 61-74, so its model contradicts the corrected skill. `implementation/scripts/check-bundle-isolation.cjs` checks a no-feature counter bundle plus framework artefacts/Xray-only dependencies; it neither roots the manual Xray facade nor owns Xray runtime sentinels, exactly the missing probe this bead already carries. Whichever A/B ruling lands, recensus and reconcile these public pages together with the source docstrings already listed here. No duplicate bead created.

--- TRIAGE PASS 2026-09-05 19:49 AUSEST (worker rulings-a; read-only classification pass; no status change, no code, no PR) ---
BUCKET (A) — genuinely needs Mike. This is a question about what the library GUARANTEES to consumers, which the project stance does not answer.

DIGEST
- Question: does Xray guarantee it is elided from an optimised production build, or is the manual facade a production-capable surface the host must exclude?
- Options: (A) gate by construction — one coherent debug/production gate over manual foundation init and the mount entry points, plus an Xray-rooted elision probe with a positive control. (B) scope the guarantee — accept that Xray reaches a production bundle unless the host guards its `:require`, and correct every site that says otherwise, loudly.
- Cost: (A) real code work in tools/xray/ plus new builds in implementation/shadow-cljs.edn, which is HOT ZONE and moves the check-count band the merge criterion uses. (B) edit-only; cannot regress; the sites are already enumerated on this bead (four in tools/xray/src, plus docs/skills/re-frame2-xray.md, docs/xray/01-installation.md and docs/xray/api/mount-control.md).
- Recommendation: (B) now, (A) separately if wanted — the immediate defect is that shipped code and public docs assert a safety property no gate enforces, and correcting that is cheap and blocks nothing.

GATING, measured at tip aa3c616e46 over the tracker's `blocks` edges across all 80 open beads: zero open beads. Nothing waits on this ruling, so it can be taken whenever convenient despite the P1.
ORIGINAL DESCRIPTION (pre-ruling, replaced 2026-09-06 17:18:40 AUSEST by the delegated ruling; preserved verbatim so the amended description loses nothing):

Code half of rf2-yk5i, carried forward because it falls outside that bead's
own stated surface (skills/re-frame2-xray/**). The SKILL side is repaired by
PR #9226; this is acceptance criteria 1 and 2 of rf2-yk5i, which need changes
in tools/xray/ and implementation/.

MEASURED AT TIP (2026-09-05, worker skxray-a):

- preload.cljs wraps its boot block in (when rf.interop/debug-enabled? ...).
  That is the ONLY goog.DEBUG gate in Xray.
- core.cljs init! registers the :rf.xray/* handlers, the trace + epoch
  collectors, install-browser-api-exports! and keybinding/attach!
  unconditionally. The mount verbs (open!, open-overlay!, close!, toggle!,
  popout!, status) are plain def-aliases of mount/*, also ungated.
- mount/open! gates only on (rf.substrate.adapter/current-adapter). Any app
  that called rf/init! has an adapter, production included, so adapter
  presence is NOT a production discriminator.
- mount.cljs's ns docstring still asserts "The preload's interop/debug-enabled?
  gate (see preload.cljs) means mount never reaches production builds. This
  namespace therefore contains no production-elision logic of its own." That
  premise does not hold for the public manual facade.
- core.cljs's open! docstring says it no-ops "when no substrate adapter is
  installed - production builds, hosts that never called rf/init!, etc.".
  The parenthetical "production builds" is wrong for the same reason.
- npm run test:elision compiles re-frame.elision-probe under :advanced twice
  (goog.DEBUG false/true) and greps 56 sentinels across 18 distinct re-frame.*
  namespaces (enumerated from check-elision.cjs, not name-grepped). It roots
  and greps NO day8.re-frame2-xray.* surface.
- Requiring day8.re-frame2-xray.core transitively loads mount.cljs, whose
  bottom runs SEVEN top-level register-first-mount-hook! calls (a private fn
  doing swap! on a defonce atom) at namespace-load time. A host-side
  goog.DEBUG guard around the CALLS does not reach those.

THE FORK IS A MAINTAINER CALL AND IS WHY THIS IS SEPARATE FROM THE DOC FIX:

(a) Gate by construction - apply one coherent debug/production gate to manual
    foundation init and the externally visible mount entry points, so the
    canonical facade is safe without every host remembering bespoke build
    placement. This is rf2-yk5i's stated preference.
(b) Scope the guarantee - accept that the manual facade is a production-capable
    surface and leave exclusion to the host. PR #9226 already documents (b)
    honestly, so (b) needs no further work beyond correcting the two stale
    docstrings named above.

Mike's ruling wanted before implementing (a): it changes the public facade's
behaviour.

REMAINING ACCEPTANCE (from rf2-yk5i):

1. An optimised goog.DEBUG=false probe rooted through rf/init! + xray/init! +
   xray/open! cannot register :rf.xray/* handlers, install the Xray browser
   globals or key listener/collectors, or create #rf-xray-root. A
   goog.DEBUG=true control must exercise those effects so the check cannot
   pass vacuously (same control discipline as check-elision.cjs, whose missing
   control is a hard FAILURE per rf2-udro3).
2. The optimised-bundle gate checks distinctive Xray sentinels or an
   equivalent reachability/size assertion, with a positive control, rather
   than reusing only the framework elision probe. Confirmed-usable literal
   sentinels: "rf-xray-root" (4 occurrences in tools/xray/src) and the
   "rf.xray" keyword namespace (151 in registry.cljs alone) - both survive
   Closure as string literals.
3. Whichever fork is taken, correct mount.cljs's ns docstring and core.cljs's
   open! docstring, which currently state the false premise.

NON-GOALS carried over from rf2-yk5i: no runtime warning banner, no disable
setting, no compatibility layer, no new launch mode; do not redesign panels,
mount lifecycle, Pair, or the framework's general elision system.

Hot-zone note: an Xray elision probe adds builds to implementation/shadow-cljs.edn
(hot-zone) - sequence against other shadow-cljs.edn touchers.
RULING 2026-09-06 17:18:40 AUSEST (delegated by Mike, ruled by the dossier agent): B — SCOPE THE GUARANTEE TO BUILD PLACEMENT. Xray is kept out of production by where the host puts it, not by construction: the preload lives in :devtools/preloads (dev build config); a manual init!/mount install belongs in a namespace only the dev entry point loads; the preload's (when rf.interop/debug-enabled? ...) block and the collectors' own gates are second lines of defence for those paths only; NO CI gate proves Xray's absence from an optimised bundle. Every site claiming otherwise is rewritten to say exactly that, in the skill's words. No code behaviour changes. Option A (gate init! + the mount verbs on debug-enabled?, plus an Xray-rooted elision probe) is DECLINED — not deferred to a bead; un-park triggers below. Option C (do nothing) is ruled out by the dossier's own analysis: the tree teaches two contradictory models of one safety property.

REASONS
1. The reviewers split, and the dissent is technical, not a preference. The dossier's A is "~12 lines in core.cljs + mount.cljs" that would make the sentence "no side-effects, handlers, globals or DOM in a release build whatever the install path" true. Codex showed at source level that it would not: shell.cljs carries nine top-level rf/reg-view forms (re-counted at tip: :991, :1162, :1837, :2027, :2249, :2395, :2490, :2535, :2565) whose macro expansion reaches registrar/register! unconditionally at namespace-load time; keybinding.cljs:602 injects install-popout-keydown! into a mount atom at load time (re-confirmed); core/load-theme mutates the DOM directly. All three sit outside A's proposed gates, so A's corrected sentence would be a NEW false claim — narrower than today's but still asserting more than the code enforces, which is the exact defect this bead was filed against. Making it true means gating the transitive view-registration graph: a refactor with no consumer. I follow Codex on this.
2. Posture. Zero in-repo apps use the manual facade (dossier count: 13 code files — Story focus!, the edn-inspector testbed, three Xray tests, api-manifest); the canonical path is the preload (25 :preloads wirings in implementation/shadow-cljs.edn); the docs' own practical rule is already "put Xray in dev build config, not app code" (docs/xray/01-installation.md:138); re-frame-10x, Xray's ancestor, never gated on goog.DEBUG. "Trust the programmer" and "no over-engineering / no gold plating" both point at B: dev tooling goes in the dev build, which is what every devtool in the JS ecosystem asks of its host too. A adds code, a hot-zone probe build in shadow-cljs.edn, and classifier wiring (Codex: the tools arm of .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh does not set cljs_prod, so folding the probe into test:elision would not run it on Xray-only PRs — the dossier's "band-neutral" route was unwired) for a guarantee that even the dossier concedes still needs build-placement guidance ("zero bytes only when Xray is absent from the build"). B's sentence is the honest subset A would have had to write anyway.

# rf2-qqn9 — Gate Xray's manual `init!`/mount facade on `goog.DEBUG`, or scope the elision guarantee to build placement

**Decision needed from Mike:** Does Xray promise to be inert in an optimised production build *however* the host installed it — in which case the manual `init!`/mount facade gets the same `debug-enabled?` gate the preload already has, and a probe proves it — or is the manual facade a production-capable surface whose exclusion is the host's job, in which case every site that claims otherwise is rewritten to say so?
**Recommendation:** A — gate by construction (about a dozen lines in two files, matching the pattern two sibling Xray namespaces already use), swept together with the prose, then a small probe PR. Rule once: the two forks write *different* sentences into the same ~18 sites.

## The problem

Xray has two install paths and one gate. The **preload** path — `day8.re-frame2-xray.preload` wired into shadow-cljs's `:devtools/preloads` — wraps its whole boot block in `(when rf.interop/debug-enabled? …)` (`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/preload.cljs:94`, block runs to :133). `debug-enabled?` is a `@define` alias of `goog.DEBUG` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/interop.cljs:224`), so under `:advanced` + `{goog.DEBUG false}` Closure constant-folds the block away. That is the only gate on the path. The **manual** path — `(require '[day8.re-frame2-xray.core :as xray])` then `(xray/init!)` and a mount verb — has none:

```clojure
;; tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/core.cljs:159-167 — init!'s body, verbatim
([{:keys [target-frame theme density buffer-depths] :as _opts}]
 (registry/register-xray-handlers!)          ; 37 reg-* calls, registry.cljs:434
 (install/register-trace-collector!)
 (install/register-epoch-collector!)
 (install/install-browser-api-exports!)      ; window.day8.re_frame2_xray.*, install.cljs:111-125
 (keybinding/attach!)                        ; global Ctrl+Shift+C keydown listener
 …)

;; core.cljs:71-107 — the mount verbs are bare def-aliases, ungated
(def open! … mount/open!)   (def open-overlay! … mount/open-overlay!)
(def toggle! … mount/toggle!)   (def popout! … mount/popout!)
```

`mount/open!` (`mount.cljs:929-964`) gates only on `(rf.substrate.adapter/current-adapter)` at :960 — and every app that called `rf/init!` has an adapter in production exactly as in dev, so adapter presence discriminates nothing. Worse, requiring the facade at all transitively loads `mount.cljs`, whose bottom runs **seven top-level `register-first-mount-hook!` calls** (:682, :720, :756, :791, :804, :820, :845) — a private fn doing `swap!` on a `defonce` atom (:480) — at namespace-load time, before any call of the host's. A host that wraps only the *calls* in `(when ^boolean goog.DEBUG …)` is not protected.

**What a consumer gets today.** Take an ordinary app namespace, compiled `:advanced` with `{goog.DEBUG false}`:

```clojure
(ns my-app.core
  (:require [re-frame.core :as rf]
            [re-frame.adapter.reagent :as reagent]
            [day8.re-frame2-xray.core :as xray]))   ; the documented manual path

(defn ^:export init []
  (rf/init! reagent/adapter)
  (xray/init! {:theme :dark})
  (xray/open!))
```

The release bundle: registers 37 `:rf.xray/*` handlers into the app's registry; installs six `window.day8.re_frame2_xray.*` globals; attaches a document-wide keydown listener; creates `#rf-xray-root` inside `[data-rf-xray-host]` (or logs a missing-host `console.error`) and renders the whole shell — app-db inspector, epoch scrubber, EDN viewer, every panel — reading the live `app-db` of a shipped binary. The trace and epoch *collectors* are the one inert part: `trace_collector.cljs` gates its own entry points (:250, :299, :359, :380), as does `drop_in.cljc` (:299, :347, :393). The retained byte count is unmeasured — nothing in the repo compiles Xray under `goog.DEBUG=false`, which is the second half of this bead.

**The same app under the proposed shape (A).** Nothing in the host changes; the gate moves into Xray, in the form Xray's own `trace_collector.cljs:250` and `drop_in.cljc:299` already use:

```clojure
;; core.cljs — init!'s second arity
([{:keys [target-frame theme density buffer-depths] :as _opts}]
 (when rf.interop/debug-enabled?          ; folds to nothing under goog.DEBUG=false
   (registry/register-xray-handlers!)
   …)
 nil)

;; mount.cljs — inside open! (and open-overlay!, toggle!, popout!); the
;; def-alias in core.cljs is untouched, so (identical? mount/open! core/open!) still holds
(defn open! []
  (when rf.interop/debug-enabled?
    (if-let [state @mount-state] … (when (rf.substrate.adapter/current-adapter) …))))

;; mount.cljs bottom — one gate around the seven load-time registrations
(when rf.interop/debug-enabled?
  (register-first-mount-hook! ::seed-trace-and-target-frame …)
  … ;; six more
  )
```

In the release bundle `xray/init!` and `xray/open!` return nil, no handler, global, listener or DOM root is created, and the panels, shell and registry bodies — referenced only from folded branches — are eliminated. In every dev build (`goog.DEBUG=true`) the code is byte-for-byte the same as today.

## The decision

**Which sentence does Xray get to make about production builds?** Exactly one of:

- **A. "Xray's side-effects are gated by construction."** Manual `init!` and the externally visible mount verbs no-op under `goog.DEBUG=false`, the load-time hook block folds, and an Xray-rooted probe with a positive control holds it in CI. Every claim site is rewritten to this wording.
- **B. "Xray is kept out of production by build placement."** The preload lives in `:devtools`; a manual install belongs in a namespace only the dev entry point loads; the preload's `debug-enabled?` block is a second line of defence for that path only; no CI gate proves absence. Every claim site is rewritten to *this* wording (the skill already is).
- **C. Do nothing.** Leave code and prose as they stand.

Both A and B correct the same sites; they disagree about what the corrected sentence says and whether code moves. That is why this is one ruling, not two.

Focused checks should verify the corrected examples against development and release build placement, reconcile the coverage metadata and skill evaluation, and check affected links. title: epoch: replace-frame-state! can overwrite a same-id successor
description:
## Scope

Make the dev-only Tool-Pair state-injection transaction in `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch.cljc` and `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc` exact-incarnation from precondition sampling through the physical write and synthetic-epoch publication. Add focused JVM/CLJS epoch tests; touch nearby Tool-Pair/API wording only if needed to state the existing lifecycle invariant. The existing exact core write primitive is sufficient.

## Correctness finding

`replace-frame-state!` validates only a bare frame id and returns no incarnation token. Its perform path then re-resolves that id for the drain lock, coherent read, two-arity `frame/replace-frame-state!` write, owner claim, history append, trace, and listener fan-out. If validated incarnation A is destroyed and same-id successor B is seated before the write, the stale A gesture writes into B, records the transition in B's history, and returns `true`. If A disappears just after its physical write, the synthetic-record tail can instead append A's before/after snapshot into B's ring. Restore already closes both classes of race by carrying the exact token end to end; injection does not.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install the plain-atom adapter, register a `[:set-owner x]` event, make frame A, and seed its app-db to `{:owner :A}`.
2. Wrap `tool-pair/check-replace-frame-state-preconditions!` so it runs the real check, asserts `:outcome :ok`, then destroys A, makes same-id B, dispatches `[:set-owner :B]` into B, and returns A's successful check result.
3. Call public `(rf/replace-frame-state! frame-id {:rf.db/app {:owner :STALE-A}})`.
4. On current main the result is `true`; B's app-db is `{:owner :STALE-A}` and B's history contains both its own `{:owner :B}` epoch and the stale synthetic `{:owner :STALE-A}` epoch.
5. Sibling tail probe: wrap the physical two-arity core write so it writes A, then destroys A and seats/seeds B before returning. The call again returns `true`; B's live db remains `{:owner :B}`, but B's ring gains `{:event-id :rf.epoch/db-replaced, :db-before {:owner :A}, :db-after {:owner :INJECTED-A}}`.

## Evidence

- `epoch/tool_pair.cljc:376-389` derives an exact token from the same captured frame record for restore, and `:499` returns it. `check-replace-frame-state-preconditions!` at `:1024-1066` returns only `{:outcome :ok}`.
- `epoch.cljc:547-553` therefore calls `perform-replace-frame-state!` with only the bare id and patch. `perform-replace!` at `:469-493` re-resolves the id, reads by id, and the closure at `:506` uses the non-exact two-arity core write.
- `record-synthetic-replace-epoch!` at `epoch.cljc:431-450` looks up whichever token is current, ignores the result of `claim-frame-owner!`, then writes and publishes by bare id. It does not fence trace/listener tails after owner loss.
- Core already supplies the needed primitive: `frame/replace-frame-state!`'s three-arity at `implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc:1969-1980` refuses unless the captured token still names the live incarnation. Restore uses it at `epoch/tool_pair.cljc:895`.
- Existing epoch tests at `epoch_test.clj:4914-5069` cover A becoming absent between validation and write. The restore-only tests at `:5136-5374` cover A becoming same-id B. No injection test interposes B.
- Public probe output on current main: `{:result true, :successor-db {:owner :STALE-A}, :successor-history-db-after [{:owner :B} {:owner :STALE-A}]}`. Tail probe output: B remains `{:owner :B}` but inherits A's `:rf.epoch/db-replaced` record, and the call returns `true`.
- Xray's `replace-app-db!` at `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/runtime.cljs:1490-1523` and Pair-MCP's gated `replace-app-db` tool trust this boolean and report success.

## Failure scenario / invariant

A tool targets a route/component frame while it is unmounting. Validation resolves incarnation A; lifecycle teardown then reuses the public frame keyword for fresh incarnation B. The stale tool gesture can overwrite both partitions of B and say success, or splice A's synthetic undo record into B's history so a later restore puts A-shaped state into B. This crosses the lifecycle authority boundary and can corrupt a newly mounted screen while presenting a valid tool response.

Invariant: a mutation validated against incarnation A may write and publish bookkeeping only while A remains the exact owner. A successor B under the same id must remain byte-for-byte and history-for-history untouched. Owner loss before the physical write follows the canonical `false` plus `:rf.error/no-such-handler` path; owner loss after an A write has linearized must never retarget A's synthetic record, trace, anchor, or listener publication into B.

## Recommended minimal fix

Mirror the shipped restore transaction instead of adding a new abstraction:

1. Derive `:incarnation-token` from the same `frame-record` captured by `check-replace-frame-state-preconditions!`, return it on `:ok`, and reject if that exact record loses ownership during sampling.
2. Thread the token through public `replace-frame-state!`, `perform-replace-frame-state!`, and `perform-replace!`; recheck exact liveness inside the serialized region and use core's existing three-arity exact `frame/replace-frame-state!`.
3. Make synthetic recording accept the same token and commit/anchor only under exact frame-owner ownership, with exact-liveness guards around callback-bearing trace/listener tails, following the existing `commit-record!`/restore pattern. Do not claim whichever same-id token happens to be current.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A deterministic public JVM test performs a real successful precheck against A (assert `:outcome :ok` and A/B distinct tokens), interposes destroy-A/make-B/seed-B before the public call continues, and proves the call returns `false`, emits canonical `:rf.error/no-such-handler`, emits no `:rf.epoch/db-replaced`, and leaves B's full frame-state and history exactly at captured baselines.
2. Pin the same A-to-B pre-write invariant in the CLJS epoch lane without timing sleeps.
3. A focused post-write-tail test interposes A-to-B churn after an exact A physical write but before synthetic bookkeeping. Prove no A synthetic record, anchor, trace, or listener delivery appears in B and B remains unchanged. Assert the A write actually ran so the arm cannot pass by skipping it.
4. Non-vacuity/control: the identical patch with no churn returns `true`, changes the intended frame, appends exactly one matching synthetic record, and fans the expected success notification. Disabling the token fence reproduces the current `true` plus B overwrite/history contamination.
5. Exercise the app-only shape used by Xray/Pair-MCP and one both-partition patch; the no-churn control preserves an omitted partition.
6. Existing destroyed-without-successor, drain-serialization, no-op-write, restore exact-incarnation, and production-elision epoch tests remain green.

## Non-goals

- No public incarnation-token argument, compare-and-set/version API, new lock, retry loop, or successor mutation.
- No change to Pair-MCP/Xray write authorization, response envelopes, or frame-id ergonomics.
- No redesign of frame lifecycle, epoch ids, history retention, restore semantics, or synthetic-record shape.
- No compatibility alias or broad concurrency-hardening sweep.

## Related / duplicate search

Searched all 1,113 beads, including closed issues, by title/description/notes and with `bd search --status all` for `replace-frame-state`, `replace frame state`, `state injection`, `stale write`, `destroyed frame`, `same-id`, `successor frame`, `incarnation token`, and `cross-incarnation`. The only in-progress bead is `rf2-jui1c`, an unrelated interceptor prose sweep and remains locked. Open `rf2-ov144` adds replay-by-epoch-id; open `rf2-cq0yi` cleans core generation-pool provenance; neither owns this transaction. Closed `rf2-40kv` and `rf2-x874` concern adapter/Hicasso stale-frame routing, not epoch injection. Commits `a6aac856cf` and `33b1355938` fixed the analogous restore race only. No duplicate owns `replace-frame-state!` retargeting or synthetic-history contamination.

The needed primitive exists: frame.cljc :1977-1980 three-arity exact-incarnation write, already used by restore at tool_pair :895 - this is a mirror job with shipped prior art. title: schemas: an explicit nil :schema bypasses the production boundary guard
description:
## Scope

Correct declaration-presence semantics for optional `:schema` metadata across the Schemas implementation and its direct Spec 010 runtime consumers. The primary owned site is `implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validate.cljc` (`run-validation`, shared by event/fx/sub validation); the same invariant must reach the production boundary, recordable-cofx, sub-override, flow-output, and other validation seams that currently test the schema value for truthiness.

Keep app-db path schemas, the registered-validator API, validation recovery, and redaction behavior otherwise unchanged.

## Correctness finding

A schema value is opaque to re-frame: an absent `:schema` key means "no declaration", while a present key must be handed verbatim to the registered validator. Current code instead mixes key-presence and value-truthiness tests.

That mismatch creates a release-resident fail-open. Event registration accepts `{:schema nil :interceptors [:rf.schema/at-boundary]}` because the registration guard checks `contains?`, but the production interceptor later treats nil as impossible and returns the context unchanged. The handler therefore runs without the boundary check the registration explicitly requested.

The same identity error exists on dev surfaces: `run-validation` uses `if-let`, so explicit nil and false schema tokens never reach a custom validator for event, fx, or sub metadata. Recordable cofx uses the same `if-let`; sub-override uses `(and schema ...)`; flow output treats nil as no schema. By contrast, app-db registration stores a present falsey schema and `validate-app-schema!` passes it to the validator unconditionally. One declaration has different meaning depending on where it attaches.

## Concrete Evidence

- `spec/010-Schemas.md:23` says the `:schema` value is opaque and no validation site interprets it; every site routes through the registered validator. Lines 29-50 define `:schema` as an optional metadata key, and lines 214-233 make `:rf.schema/at-boundary` the production validation guarantee.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/events.cljc:234-248` rejects a boundary registration only when the metadata map does not `contain?` `:schema`. A map containing `:schema nil` therefore registers.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/spec.cljc:190-205` reads that value and explicitly no-ops on `(nil? schema)`. Its comment claims nil can only result from post-registration mutation, contradicting the registrar.
- `implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validate.cljc:447-453` uses `(if-let [schema (:schema reg-meta)] ...)`, bypassing the validator for nil and false across `validate-event!`, `validate-fx!`, and `validate-sub!`.
- `implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validate.cljc:649-658` is the counterexample in the same module: an app-db registry entry passes `(:schema schema-meta)` to `validate-entry-result` without a truthiness check.
- `implementation/core/test/re_frame/ep0026_inline_grammar_cljs_test.cljc:166-178` already pins the representation invariant: omitted metadata and an explicitly nil schema remain distinguishable, and the explicit nil key is preserved.
- Adjacent instances are at `implementation/core/src/re_frame/cofx.cljc:655-698`, `implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs/override_schema.cljc:53-84`, and `implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows.cljc:91-142`.
- Readings used: `rg -n "(if-let|when-let) \[schema|nil\? schema|contains\? meta :schema|and schema" implementation --glob '*.clj*'`, plus focused reads of the symbols above and existing boundary production tests.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install a custom validator that records its schema argument and returns false.
2. Register an event with `{:schema nil :interceptors [:rf.schema/at-boundary]}`. Registration succeeds because `events/reject-at-boundary-without-schema!` checks key presence.
3. Exercise `(:before rf/validate-at-boundary-interceptor)` with `re-frame.spec/dev-mode?` false, or dispatch through the existing production-compiled boundary test app.
4. Observe that the validator records no call, the returned context has no boundary-rejection marker, and the handler is allowed to run.
5. As the control, change nil to any truthy schema token: the same interceptor calls the validator and rejects.
6. Independently call `schemas/validate-event!` with `{:schema false}`; it returns true without invoking the validator because `run-validation` uses `if-let`.

## Failure scenario / invariant

A boot path resolves a schema token from configuration or a registry and obtains nil:

```clojure
(rf/reg-event :wire/received
  {:schema nil
   :interceptors [:rf.schema/at-boundary]}
  ingest-untrusted-payload)
```

Registration succeeds. In production the boundary interceptor returns unchanged context, so `ingest-untrusted-payload` receives attacker-controlled data with no rejection or configuration error, despite the explicit release-resident guard.

A custom validator may also assign meaning to nil or false; the opaque-value contract permits that. Today app-db validation calls it with those values while event/fx/sub/cofx/flow validation silently does not.

Invariant: omission is determined by key presence, not schema-value truthiness. If `:schema` is present, pass its exact value to the configured validator. Only an absent key means no declaration, and only a nil registered validator (via `set-schema-validator! nil`) disables validation.

## Recommended minimal fix

Use `contains?` (or an equally small presence test) at each metadata-bearing validation boundary, then pass `(:schema meta)` verbatim even when nil or false.

- Make `run-validation` distinguish an absent key from a falsey value.
- Remove the production boundary interceptor's nil-value no-op; registration established presence, so delegate the exact value to `:schemas/validate-with-registered-fn`. Default Malli then fails closed through existing throwing-validator isolation; a custom validator interprets its own token.
- Apply the same law to recordable cofx, sub override, flow output, and other Spec 010 validation consumers found by the focused census. Where redaction is reached only after declaration presence is established, do not suppress it again with `some?` on the opaque schema value.
- Keep the fix local; plain presence checks are preferable to a new abstraction.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A focused JVM test installs a custom validator spy that returns false, supplies `{:schema nil}` and `{:schema false}` to event/fx/sub validation, and proves each exact token reaches the validator and each surface takes its documented failure recovery.
2. A production-boundary regression registers `{:schema nil :interceptors [:rf.schema/at-boundary]}`, runs the production path, and proves the validator receives nil, the invalid event is rejected, and the handler is not invoked. Add the equivalent assertion to the existing production-compiled CLJS boundary suite so this cannot pass only under JVM simulation.
3. The focused census covers other direct validation seams (recordable cofx, sub override, flow output, and any machine schema consumer using the same truthiness pattern): a present falsey token is delegated once; an omitted key remains a no-op.
4. Controls prove the distinction: omitted `:schema` does not call the validator, while `set-schema-validator! nil` still disables validation and lets values pass. These controls plus the exact-argument spy make the proof non-vacuous; restoring an `if-let`/nil guard must make the present-falsey case red.
5. With default Malli, a present nil schema cannot silently run a boundary handler: it follows the existing malformed-schema/fail-closed route, never registration success plus runtime no-op.
6. Existing schemas JVM tests and the schemas production-boundary CLJS build/tests pass.

## Non-goals

- Interpreting or validating a schema language at registration.
- Changing `set-schema-validator! nil` as the documented global opt-out.
- Adding compatibility aliases, a schema wrapper type, or configuration.
- Redesigning the validator/explainer/printer bundle, Malli adapter, walker, digest, or recovery policy.
- Requiring apps to use nil or false schema tokens; this fixes declaration identity and the concrete boundary fail-open.

## Related / duplicate search

Searched all bead statuses by title and description for `schema`, `nil schema`, `explicit nil`, `falsy schema`, `schema presence`, `at-boundary`, `validate-at-boundary-interceptor`, `reject-at-boundary-without-schema`, and `malformed schema`. No open, in-progress, or closed bead owns this finding.

`rf2-tiymn` is the closed schemas surface review about production-eliding Malli's humanizer; it does not concern declaration presence or boundary enforcement. Source comments cite historical `rf2-iftj4` for rejecting an entirely absent boundary schema, but no live bead with that id exists; this is the distinct present-but-falsey gap left by that check.
notes: TRIAGE 2026-08-31 19:38:35 AUSEST (read-only agent at 35402e4322): HOLDS. events.cljc reject-at-boundary-without-schema! (:234-250) tests (contains? meta :schema) so {:schema nil} registers with the boundary interceptor; spec.cljc :199-205 then no-ops on (nil? schema) in the production interceptor, with a comment claiming nil is impossible-by-registration - directly contradicted by the registrar; the fail-open is real and release-resident. validate.cljc :447-453 uses if-let so nil/false schema tokens bypass the validator for event/fx/sub, while the app-db path :649-658 passes the value unconditionally - the in-module counterexample the bead cites. Adjacent truthiness seams confirmed: cofx.cljc :672 (if-let), override_schema.cljc :55 (and schema ...), flows.cljc :101 (nil? schema -> true). spec/010 :23 states the opaque-value contract; the spec needs no edit. Presence semantics is correctness, not nag-diagnostics - not a reject-candidate. SURFACES: implementation/schemas/** + implementation/core (spec.cljc, cofx.cljc, subs/override_schema.cljc - registrar likely unchanged) + implementation/flows/** + tests; no hot-zone (do not edit spec/010). COLLISIONS: none live (interceptor-coords owns interceptor_registry.cljc, disjoint) or sibling. GATES: clojure -M:test from implementation/schemas, implementation/core, implementation/flows (JVM); npm run test:browser-schemas-boundary-prod --prefix implementation [HEAVY - shadow RELEASE + browser, the heaviest lane here]; npm run test:cljs --prefix implementation [HEAVY]. AMBIGUITY: census breadth could sprawl - fix exactly the enumerated seams with plain presence checks, no new abstraction. SHAPE: solo; widest surface of the eleven - schedule its heavy prod-browser lane apart from the other heavy workers.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #8832 (worker/schema-presence-6eh5h): declaration presence is now KEY-presence, never value truthiness, at every Spec 010 validation seam. The release-resident fail-open is closed: {:schema nil :interceptors [:rf.schema/at-boundary]} registers (unchanged, contains?-based registrar) and the production boundary interceptor now delegates the exact nil to the registered validator instead of no-opping - default Malli fails CLOSED via the seam's malformed-schema isolation; a custom validator receives its own token verbatim. Seams fixed: schemas/validate.cljc run-validation (if-let -> contains?), core/spec.cljc boundary interceptor ((nil? schema) no-op removed), core/cofx.cljc validate-recordable-value! (+ redaction no longer suppressed by some? on the opaque value), core/subs/override_schema.cljc, core/subs/memo.cljc outer gate, core/fx.cljc fx-args outer gate, flows/flows.cljc validate-output!, machines/data_validation.cljc spawn/output/macrostep/update-snapshot (resolve-data-schema returns a presence-carrying [:data schema] map entry). App-db path, validator API, recovery and redaction policy otherwise unchanged; spec/010 needed no edit. Census classified as NOT validation seams (left alone): http/privacy_body 149, routing/navigate 72, routing/registry 745, resources/classification (Spec 015), machines/tooling 212, machines home fail-loud guard registration.cljc:845 (registration diagnostic). Tests: schemas_presence_test.clj + schema_presence_seams_test.clj (new), flows_schema_validation_test.clj, machine_schema_test.clj, schemas_boundary_prod_test.cljs additions covering AC 1-5 (exact-token spies, documented recoveries, omitted-key + nil-validator controls, production-compiled CLJS regression). Gates on the FINAL rebased base (c39c44ec32), captured exits: schemas JVM 372/19221 exit 0; core JVM 2170/11105 exit 0; flows JVM 241/6041 exit 0; machines JVM 1204/4196 exit 0; test:browser-schemas-boundary-prod (release+browser) 11/20 exit 0. Control: with the interceptor's truthiness test restored at one line, the schemas suite went RED with exactly 3 failing assertions in the headline tests (validator never sees nil, :rf/skip-handler? unset - handler unguarded), captured exit 1; restore verified by blob hash 182cb4990a6cba86b1578db7ae3478968d32d0b0 (working == HEAD object).

title: surface-review(skill-improver): make one request return one complete, proportionate critique
description:
## Scope

Treat skills/re-frame2-improver/** as one distinct published static-review product. Make an explicit review request over a readable snippet, file, or directory return a complete, severity-ordered, proportionate critique in the same turn. Give this code-review skill its own lean workflow and correction contract instead of making normal operation depend on the session-retrospective protocol in skills/shared/retro-protocol.md.

Keep the six evidence-grown anti-pattern topics and their strongest detection/edge-case knowledge. Change how the skill selects, explains, and corrects findings; make the packaged normal path self-contained; align README/spec/evals and remove improver-only structural locks that preserve the current ceremony.

## Findings

1. The normal workflow contradicts itself at the point the programmer expects an answer. SKILL.md says “user asks for a review → activate → present findings → exit” and its local steps route, classify, and surface all matching findings. The mandatory shared protocol instead says to emit a preliminary numbered candidate list and “Ask which to dig into before classifying.” A static review of a named file can therefore stop before doing the review the user already requested. None of the behavioural fixtures rejects that extra round trip.

2. Correction authority is based on an unobservable provenance taxonomy instead of the programmer's request. A plain review may auto-Edit a “canonical-idiom-shaped” rewrite even though the user asked only for review. Conversely eval 25's user explicitly says “apply any fixes you find,” yet the expected result requires another approval because the proposed machine uses the supplied code's shape. The tie-breaker says identical-shape-but-renamed is evidence-shaped, while eval 31 calls a rewrite carrying the snippet's sidebar key/string canonical-shaped and expects it to apply. Programmers and agents cannot predict this boundary reliably; it has already needed a corrective commit plus 64 lines of structural regression tests.

3. The response contract is retrospective-shaped, not review-shaped. SKILL.md names Scope, Observed shape, Pattern findings, Higher-leverage redesigns, Inline fixes applied, and Open questions; the shared protocol separately says seven slots stay, including Improvements, Issue candidates, and Other possibilities. Even when conditionals are intended, this strongly cues empty headings and repeated prose. The useful unit for a programmer is one finding that states evidence, consequence, and the smallest safe correction, with an optional broader redesign only when it earns its cost.

4. Detection quality is substantially better than correction proportionality. Every leaf has concrete signals and legitimate edge cases, and the subtle schemaless-boundary and durable/diagnostic distinctions are valuable. But the manual-loading fixture contains a real one-line correctness defect—the failure handler never clears :items/loading?—and eval 19 explicitly rejects adding the missing cleanup in favour of a reg-machine/Nine States rewrite. That turns a static review into framework advocacy: the immediate bug and the optional architecture upgrade are collapsed into one mandatory “canonical fix.” The catalogue should diagnose both without pretending they have the same urgency or patch size.

5. The progressive-disclosure path is not lean in practice. The mandatory baseline is SKILL.md (1,491 words / 11,127 bytes), shared/retro-protocol.md (2,189 words / 15,933 bytes), and the routing index (624 words / 5,408 bytes): 4,304 words / 32,468 bytes before one matching leaf. One leaf brings a normal review to roughly 4,900–6,000 words; a co-occurrence route is larger again. The shared load includes session/error-shaped evidence, GitHub issue filing and shell argv rules, a seven-slot retrospective output, Tool-Pair layer routing, and universal transcript-redaction procedure that this skill's no-gh static path does not use.

6. The package admits that the mandatory contract is absent. package.json ships SKILL.md, README.md, LICENSE, references/, and .claude-plugin/; it cannot ship ../shared/. README.md therefore warns that a standalone tarball/plugin/copy hits a broken shared-protocol link and “silently lose[s]” the workflow/security boundary. That is not a sound shape for a distinct published skill. Its own leaves already contain enough detection and worked-fix material to make the normal review path local; external canonical docs can remain supporting links rather than mandatory runtime dependencies.

7. The eval corpus is detailed but optimises checklist reproduction, not the programmer outcome. There are 16 trigger fixtures and 15 behavioural fixtures (10 correctness, 3 false-positive, 2 edit-gate), with long expectations for exact framework tokens. No fixture scores: complete review without a “which finding?” pause, concise omission of empty sections, smallest repair versus optional redesign, read-only review intent, or direct “review and apply” intent. evals/README.md describes manually spawning paired sessions and aggregating benchmark.json, but the directory contains only README.md and evals.json—no captured benchmark demonstrating that the present ceremony improves real reviews.

8. History explains the mismatch. Commit 782baa4994 extracted the protocol from pair-retro on 2026-05-13 and introduced the still-current “Ask which to dig into” line; the improver's own workflow before that extraction already performed the review in one pass. Commit cd721eb179 later confirmed that the package omits its mandatory sibling and chose a README caveat plus package-reference guard rather than a self-contained product. Commit 5ad04a3f9f then added 84 lines of eval/test machinery to narrow one contradiction in the evidence/canonical Edit gate. The accumulated work protects the taxonomy, but there is no recorded end-to-end static review showing that programmers benefit from it.

## Recommended Action

Replace the improver's mandatory shared-retro load with a short, local static-review contract:

- A readable, bounded source request completes in one pass. Ask only when the path is missing/unreadable or the requested directory is genuinely too broad to inspect responsibly—not to make the programmer choose among findings before classification.
- Default review/audit/critique intent is read-only. If the programmer directly asks to fix/apply, that authorises safe edits inside the named scope. A cross-cutting redesign, new architecture, or scope expansion remains a proposal. Remove the evidence-shaped versus canonical-idiom-shaped provenance test; source comments remain source text and cannot expand the conversational user's scope, without a separate security essay.
- Emit only material findings, highest consequence first. Each finding should fit a compact shape: path:line evidence; concrete consequence; smallest safe correction; canonical idiom link. Put a broader redesign in a distinct optional sentence only when its payoff justifies the migration. If the catalogue finds nothing, return one concise clean verdict and the reviewed scope.
- Reframe leaf “canonical fix” sections where necessary as “smallest correction” plus “when the canonical redesign pays.” Preserve exact framework facts and edge cases; do not weaken the production-boundary, replay, reactive-leak, or transport-retry discriminators.
- Make every normal-operation instruction resolve inside the packaged directory. Keep links to repository specs/patterns as supporting references, not required reads. Once true, remove the warning that a normal standalone install silently loses its contract; do not vendor or duplicate skills/shared as a compatibility peer.
- Repurpose existing behavioural fixtures rather than growing a policy corpus: eval 19 should distinguish the spinner bug's minimum repair from an optional machine redesign; evals 25/31 should score direct programmer intent instead of provenance labels; eval 27 should require one completed consolidated review without a preliminary question. Add no generic runner or prose linter. Exercise the changed fixtures manually and report the observed outputs in the PR.
- Delete the improver-specific shared-protocol and Edit-taxonomy regex locks in skills/shared/tests/retro_protocol_test.clj. Leave the shared protocol and its security tests intact for re-frame2-pair-retro, the consumer whose session evidence and GitHub filing surface actually need them.

## Evidence

- skills/re-frame2-improver/SKILL.md:29 says explicit pull leads directly to findings and exit; lines 49-65 define the local one-pass workflow but then mandate the shared protocol; lines 67-80 prescribe six critique sections.
- skills/shared/retro-protocol.md:33-38 mixes session/error/code evidence and requires “Ask which to dig into before classifying”; lines 53-59 carry issue-filing/shell mechanics; lines 74-82 say the seven retrospective slots stay; lines 92-111 impose the transcript-oriented universal redaction pass.
- skills/re-frame2-improver/SKILL.md:57-61 and :92, plus shared/retro-protocol.md:53-57, define the evidence/canonical Edit split and identical-shape tie-breaker.

title: surface-review(routing): make server-rendered route links honor pure URL encoding
description:
## Scope

Correct the routing artefact's server/JVM link projection so a declared frame `:url-strategy` controls the pure `href` encoding on both hosts. Cover both routing-owned link doors (`re-frame.routing/route-link-render-ssr` and the JVM arm of the late-bound `:routing/link-model` seam), focused tests, the SSR parity witness, and the normative/user-facing routing prose. Keep the artefact split and manifest dependency surface unchanged.

## Findings

The strategy contract already makes `:encode` pure and host-agnostic, ships it on both hosts, and requires it during JVM frame preflight. Browser `route-link` uses that encoder, but both JVM link paths hard-code `identity`. This makes supported configurations disagree across hosts:

- `(with-base-path history-url-strategy "/realworld")` renders `/article/x` on the server and `/realworld/article/x` on the hydrated client. The server link leaves the deployment mount if clicked before hydration, by a crawler, or without JavaScript.
- `hash-url-strategy` renders `/active` on the server and `#/active` on the client; base + hash similarly loses both outbound decorations server-side.
- The server and client render trees differ at `:href`, contrary to Spec 011's structural-hydration rule. Spec 012 currently calls that difference "no hydration mismatch", but canonical render-tree hashing treats an attribute value change as structural.

The gap is not defended by tests. `route_link_test.clj` covers only the default identity strategy, while `routing_url_strategy_test.clj` proves the pure encoders/combinator independently; no test composes a seated server frame strategy with either SSR link surface. Two shipped RealWorld examples use `with-base-path`, so this is a real supported deployment shape rather than speculative custom-strategy machinery.

## Recommended Action

Refine the rule to: SSR ignores browser side effects (`:decode`'s host read, `:push!`, `:replace!`, `:install-listener!`), not the pure `:encode` projection used to author an anchor.

Resolve the rendering frame's already-validated strategy and apply its `:encode` in both JVM link paths. Preserve the current default-history/path-form result when the public SSR render helper is called without a frame. Keep the click/navigation payload path-form; only the rendered `href` is encoded. Add one shared parity fixture or equally direct cross-host assertions for history, base-path history, hash, and base-path hash, plus a server-frame integration assertion that reaches the registered `rf/route-link` view. Update Spec 012, the routing API reference, and guide prose so they describe the narrowed SSR rule and no longer claim differing hrefs are hydration-equivalent.

## Evidence

- `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/link.cljc:394`-`:410`: `route-link-render-ssr` passes `identity` to `href-attrs`.
- `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/link.cljc:490`-`:495`: `link-model` selects the frame encoder only on CLJS and hard-codes `identity` on CLJ.
- `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/strategy.cljc:273`-`:320`: `with-base-path` adds the deployment prefix only in `:encode`, explicitly calling it the single outbound base-composition point used by route links.
- `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/strategy.cljc:367`-`:376`: JVM strategies are required to carry callable `:encode` and `:decode`; the docstring even says SSR route-link renders through `:encode`, contradicting the live link code.
- `spec/012-Routing.md:1865`-`:1873` calls `:encode` pure and host-agnostic; `:1899`-`:1911` says only strategy consult points see the base; `:1913`-`:1915` then exempts SSR and asserts differing hrefs are not a mismatch.
- `spec/011-SSR.md:52`-`:54` requires the client to compute the same structural render tree as the server; attribute ordering may differ, attribute values may not.
- `implementation/routing/test/re_frame/route_link_test.clj` has default path-form SSR href cases only. `implementation/routing/test/re_frame/routing_url_strategy_test.clj:322` onward tests base encoding without composing it with SSR link rendering.
- History explains the drift: commit `38366dc386` introduced the "SSR ignores strategies" rule on 2026-07-03; commit `5b9bab33fa` added `with-base-path` on 2026-07-08; commit `d8cb5cbae8` then made `:encode` the single outbound base authority, without revisiting the earlier SSR exemption.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A server frame declaring `(with-base-path history-url-strategy "/demos")` renders a route link to `/demos/<route-path>` through both the routing-owned SSR view and `:routing/link-model`; its navigation payload remains the unencoded app-relative path.
- Hash and base + hash configurations render `#/...` and `/demos#/...` respectively on the JVM, matching the first CLJS render for the same frame config.
- The default/no-frame JVM helper behavior remains path-form, so existing direct-call ergonomics do not regress.
- A cross-host render-tree/hash fixture (or an equivalent explicit parity assertion using the production render paths) proves a strategy-bearing route link has the same `:href` on server and client; changing either JVM path back to `identity` makes the fixture red.
- Existing route URL matching, path-form event payloads, push/replace behavior, and listener decoding stay unchanged.
- Spec 012, `docs/api/re-frame.routing.md`, and relevant routing guide text say SSR skips side effects but honors pure link encoding; the false "different href, no hydration mismatch" claim is removed.
- No new runtime dependency, public wrapper, compatibility shim, or strategy type is introduced.

## Non-goals

- Do not change `route-url` or `match-url` from their app-relative path-form contract.
- Do not infer a base path from the request, servlet/proxy headers, or browser globals; programmers continue to declare the strategy explicitly.
- Do not add relative-route syntax, a redirect object, a router provider, or another URL-strategy abstraction.
- Do not refactor unrelated link click, prefetch, native-anchor, history, or listener code.
- Do not preserve the current divergent SSR href as a compatibility mode; this is pre-alpha and the supported contract should be coherent.

## Related beads

No duplicate found after searching all statuses by `route-link`, `url-strategy`, `with-base-path`, `base path`, `SSR ignores`, `path-form href`, `hydration mismatch`, `hash app`, and `server shell`. Historical source/commit annotations cite `rf2-aerrz5`, `rf2-g8pbwg`, and `rf2-irygd6`; `bd show` reports those ids absent from the current tracker, so commits `38366dc386`, `5b9bab33fa`, and `d8cb5cbae8` are the durable history anchors rather than active related beads.

Premises re-verified at source (link.cljc:394-410 identity, :492-493 reader conditional; strategy.cljc:481 url-strategy-for-frame-id; frame.cljc:673 current-frame; spec/012 cited lines). Brief names the design lean (frame/current-frame -> url-strategy-for-frame-id, nil -> history default; never require-current-frame! on the JVM) as a lean to be costed, and a .cljc parity test as the control. spec/011 is explicitly NOT to be touched. Worker closes this bead on PR-ready.

title: surface-review(reagent-slim): make reagent2.core/reaction a stock-compatible macro
description:
## Scope

Restore the public `reagent2.core/reaction` call shape promised by the bounded Reagent-compat surface. Touch only the reagent-slim core macro/runtime surface, focused tests, and the directly coupled surface/migration documentation needed to make the contract truthful.

## Findings

`reagent2.core/reaction` is currently a runtime function taking a thunk (`[f]`), but the pinned stock Reagent 2.0.1 surface it claims to preserve exposes `reagent.core/reaction` as a variadic macro that wraps its body in `(fn [])`. There is no `src/reagent2/core.clj` macro namespace. A documented mechanical require rename therefore changes `(r/reaction (* @a @a))` from a lazy reactive expression into an eager call that passes the computed value as `f`; dereferencing the resulting Reaction later attempts to call that value as a function.

This is not covered by the current tests. `reagent2.core-cljs-test` says the core reaction surface has dedicated coverage but never calls `r/reaction`; `reagent2.ratom-cljs-test` covers the different `reagent2.ratom/reaction` macro. IMPL-SPEC §2.2 and §14.2 encode the same incorrect “function form” reading while §13.1 promises that `s/reagent\./reagent2./g` is sufficient inside the bounded surface.

## Recommended Action

Make `reagent2.core/reaction` a co-located CLJ macro with stock Reagent's body syntax and expansion to `reagent2.ratom/make-reaction`. Remove the misleading thunk-taking runtime function from that public spelling; callers that intentionally have a thunk already have the explicit `reagent2.ratom/make-reaction` factory. Reconcile the public-surface inventory and migration prose with the actual macro contract.

## Evidence

- `implementation/adapters/reagent/deps.edn:15` pins `reagent/reagent` 2.0.1.
- In that artefact, `reagent/core.clj` defines `(defmacro reaction [& body] ...)`; `reagent/core.cljs` defines no `reaction` function.
- `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/core.cljs:65-73` instead defines `(defn reaction [f] ...)`, and `src/reagent2/core.clj` does not exist.
- `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/IMPL-SPEC.md:224` and `:1187-1191` classify the core spelling as a function, while `:1129` promises a namespace-only import rewrite.
- `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/test/reagent2/core_cljs_test.cljs:22-25` claims indirect coverage but contains no `r/reaction` call; the only expression-body proof is for the sibling ratom macro at `test/reagent2/ratom_cljs_test.cljs:425-432`.
- The spec cites 25 Dash8 plus 1 rf8 `reagent.core/reaction` sites as reasons this surface ships, so the mismatch is on an audited, used path rather than speculative compatibility.

## Acceptance Criteria

- With only `(:require [reagent2.core :as r])`, `(r/reaction <body...>)` compiles with the same body syntax as stock Reagent and produces a `reagent2.ratom/Reaction`.
- A focused regression proves the body is deferred until deref, captures a reagent2 atom dependency, and recomputes after that atom changes.
- Macro expansion or an equivalent structural assertion proves the body is wrapped in a zero-argument function passed to `reagent2.ratom/make-reaction`.
- No public `reagent2.core/reaction` thunk-taking function remains; explicit thunk construction remains available as `reagent2.ratom/make-reaction`.
- Core namespace docs, IMPL-SPEC surface tables/§14.2, and migration guidance describe the macro accurately, with no claim that the old function form exists in stock Reagent.
- The reagent-slim package/test gates include and exercise the new `.clj` macro file from the published `src` path.

## Non-goals

- Adding dropped Reagent surfaces such as `track`, `track!`, `run!`, or `with-let`.
- Changing the Reaction kernel, batching scheduler, renderer, adapter map, or ratom macro semantics.
- Preserving the pre-alpha thunk-taking core spelling via a compatibility shim or introducing a second public factory alias.
- A broad stock-Reagent parity audit or migration codemod.

## Related beads

- Historical `rf2-6hyy` introduced the Stage-4 reagent-slim surface.
- Historical `rf2-kfpf` is the consumer audit cited for the 25 Dash8 core-reaction sites.
- Historical `rf2-n71j3q` clarified that `reagent2.ratom.clj` ships the ratom macro only; this task closes the distinct missing core macro.
- No duplicate was found across current Bead titles, descriptions, notes, close reasons, or comments for `reagent2.core/reaction`, `reagent.core/reaction`, `reaction macro`, or combined `reagent-slim` + `reaction` searches.
