title: [MERGED #10121] children-of-pair mixed-ceiling exposure — REPRODUCED and fixed; scope narrowed to the public function, not a mounted-widget mis-render
description:
`children-of-pair` carries the **same mixed-ceiling exposure** that `rf2-zk4he` fixed in
`sequential-diff-children`, but with the **OPPOSITE failure mode** — it loses nothing, and instead
**mislabels surviving elements as newly added**.

**Reported by `rf2-zk4he`'s worker (PR #10114, merged `b61ad91f75`)** while answering that brief's
question about sibling exposure, and **explicitly marked by it as READ FROM SOURCE, NOT EXECUTED** —
so this item inherits that status. **The first job here is to reproduce it, or to refute it.**

## The mechanism, as reported

Since `rf2-jh12f`, `bounded-vec` dispatches on `counted?`: it realises a counted collection whole and
caps a non-counted one at `count-bound` (**1001**). So a lazy before-side and a counted after-side
receive **different ceilings** — the condition `rf2-zk4he` fixed one level over.

`children-of-pair` bounds both sides the same way, but walks **`(range (max …))`** rather than
`(range (count b-vec))`. **So it never drops a row** — the data-loss failure `rf2-zk4he` repaired does
not arise here. What it does instead is **fill the truncated before tail with `::missing`**, and
`::missing` in a before slot **forces the `:added` render path**. A survivor whose prior value was
merely never realised is therefore **rendered as a structurally new element**.

**That is a confident lie rather than a silent drop**, which is the trade `rf2-zk4he`'s brief named as
the thing to avoid — reached here by a different route, in the sibling function.

## What already exists to build on

**PR #10114 introduced the vocabulary this probably wants**: `::unrealised` (`unrealised-sentinel`,
public beside `missing-sentinel`), meaning *before value not realised* as distinct from *absent*. It is
deliberately **not structural**, so `leaf-diff-op` falls through to the projection. That worker pinned
its behaviour **in both directions** — an `::unrealised` slot renders `data-rf-diff-op "modified"` and
no `"added"` node, while `::missing` in the same slot against the same projection renders `"added"` and
suppresses `"modified"`. **Read that test before writing a new one; the both-ways pin is the part that
makes it evidence rather than a coincidence.**

## Scope

**First: reproduce or refute.** Construct the mixed case — a non-`counted?` before side against a
`counted?` after side — drive `children-of-pair`, and establish whether a survivor past the before
bound really does render as `:added`. **Say plainly which you found.** If it refutes, close with the
measurement and stop; that is a complete and valuable outcome.

If it reproduces: correct it so a survivor with an unrealised prior renders as **unknown**, not as
added. **Prefer reusing `::unrealised` to inventing a fourth state** — two sentinels for one idea is
worse than either alone — and say which you chose and why.

**OUT OF SCOPE, each a live temptation:**
- **Do not touch `sequential-diff-children`** — `rf2-zk4he` fixed it and its append-only property
  (*"the zip is never widened, re-based or re-ordered"*) is load-bearing for `rf2-vu42n`.
- **Do not re-open the projection stage** — that is `rf2-bmed1`.
- **Do not raise or remove `count-bound`**, and do not make `bounded-vec` unconditional; the `counted?`
  split is correct and `rf2-jh12f` measured why a KIND test cannot replace it (`Cons` is `IList`
  without `ICounted`; `IntegerRange` IS `ICounted`).
- **No serializer or virtualization redesign.**

## FENCE

`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/edn_inspector.cljs` is **held by live worker `rf2-bmed1`**,
and `rf2-re7dn` and `rf2-et4l0` are queued on it behind that. **Not dispatchable until `rf2-bmed1`'s
change MERGES** — a surface fence releases on the merge, not on the worker's report. **Re-derive every
line number then**: this file has taken three merges today and `rf2-bmed1` will add a fourth.
`children-of-pair` was at **`:1404-1405`** at trunk `b61ad91f75`; treat that as stale on arrival.

**AND CHECK WHETHER `rf2-bmed1` MADE THIS MOOT.** Its brief told it explicitly not to touch
`children-of-pair`, so it should not have — but its bound sits upstream of this walk, and an upstream
bound can change what reaches here. **Read its merged diff and its close reason before starting**, and
if the defect no longer reproduces, say so and close on that measurement.

## LANE

This is `.cljs` — every `edn_inspector*` / `edn_widget*` test file is `.cljs`, none `.cljc`, so the
**node lane grades it and the node lane IS the shadow-cljs exclusive**. Take it only when it is granted;
two concurrent runs **WEDGE SILENTLY** — no error, no exit file, no output.

## Gates, briefly

`npm run test:cljs` is the gate. `python scripts/lint_kondo.py` is JVM-side and needs no lane — **read
its finding lines and warning count, not merely its exit code**, since `--fail-level error` exits 0 on
an unresolved symbol in this tree. `check_doc_slugs.py`, `check_readme_links.py --ci` and
`mkdocs build --strict` do **not** grade this; say so rather than running one for appearance.
**Nothing grades whether a docstring is true.**

**The control is the deliverable**: show the gate red before the fix and green after, and verify any
restore by hashing the bytes against `git rev-parse "HEAD:<path>"`, a match by either
`git hash-object` form being good (`i/lf w/crlf`, default form expected).

## File health

`i/lf w/crlf`. **Never `sed -i`** — it rewrites every line ending as bare LF at exit 0 while `git diff`
stays silent, **even when the pattern matches nothing**. Three numbers with Python on the bytes before
and after: total CR, total CRLF, bare LF; require CR == CRLF and bare LF == 0.

## Census discipline

**Never cap a locator** — take the count and the listing together from the same needle. `\b` matches
across a hyphen in this tree, and `\b` after punctuation (`counted?`, `bounded-vec`) can never match
when the next character is also non-word; use fixed strings. Strip comment MARKERS, not comment lines,
or a comment-borne claim deletes itself from your own census. Take the control FROM the target with a
nonsense needle beside it at 0.

The brief handed it rf2-bmed1's quotable *"not made moot — different failure mode, function not

## IT NARROWED ITS OWN FINDING AGAINST INTEREST, AND THE MAYOR VERIFIED THE NARROWING

**Both the item and the brief read as though the render path reaches this arm generally. It does not.**
Mayor-verified at source after the merge, and the dispatch is on **KIND**, not on vector-ness:

    (cond
      (and diff? (#{:vector :list :seq} kind))  (sequential-diff-children before value kind path projection)
      diff?                                     (children-of-pair before value kind)
      :else                                     (children-of value))

So every sequential in diff mode goes to `sequential-diff-children`; `children-of-pair` receives maps,
sets, records and map-entries — whose slots are key/member-addressed, as the comment above it says. And
`engine/project` returns a **map in both branches** (the `identical?` short-circuit returns a literal
map), so `project-for` is always truthy when `diff?`. **A lazy-before/vector-after SEQUENTIAL pair
therefore never reaches this walker from a mounted widget.**

**The defect is live on the PUBLIC function** — `children-of-pair` is `defn`, not `defn-`, documented,
and named in the item as a downstream-caller surface — **and on the no-projection path. It is not a
mounted-widget mis-render today.** That is a real reduction in the severity of the worker's own result,
volunteered, and it is correct. **A worker that quietly let an overstated item stand would have left the
tracker claiming a user-visible bug that is not one.**

**No fourth state. `::unrealised` reused**, exactly as the item preferred: sentinel definitions read
**exactly two** at `:615` (`missing-sentinel`) and `:626` (`unrealised-sentinel`), and `::unrealised`
occurrences rose 12 → 15.

**Keyed on the CEILING BEING REACHED, never on KIND** — `edn_inspector.cljs:1628`:

    past-before (if (and (endless-candidate? before)
                         (= b-count count-bound))
                  ::unrealised
                  ::missing)

**So a lazy seq that genuinely ends below the bound still yields `::missing`**, which is right — its
absence is real, not unrealised. `b-count` is read off the already-bounded vector, so **no extra element
is realised**, which is the property `count-bound` exists to protect.

REPRODUCED, then fixed. PR #10121 (branch worker/xrchild-idydb, base 5a19ce71ed).

## Reproduce-or-refute: REPRODUCES

The finding was inherited as READ FROM SOURCE, NOT EXECUTED. It was executed here and it
holds. Driving the public `children-of-pair` with the mixed-ceiling shape — a 1050-element
LazySeq before side (not `counted?`) against a 1050-element vector after side (`counted?`,
tail element replaced) — the emitted triple at after-index 1049 was

    [1049 :changed-at-tail :day8.re-frame2-xray.views.edn-inspector/missing]

and rendering that row through `render-node` against `(engine/project before after)`
produced, from the gate's own failure output:

    [:span {:data-rf-diff-op "added", :data-rf-diff-wash "1", :data-rf-diff-stripe "1", ...
      [:span {... :color "var(--rf-xray-diff-gutter)"}} "+"] ...
        [:span {:data-rf-diff-op "added"} [:span {:data-rf-type "keyword" ...} ":changed-at-tail"]]]

with the projection's own op for that path appearing nowhere in the tree. Four assertions
failed on the unfixed tree, captured exit 1; all four green after the fix, captured exit 0.

Mechanism, confirmed at source: `bounded-vec` dispatches on `counted?` (rf2-jh12f), so the
two sides get independent ceilings; the arm walks `(range (max ...))` so it drops nothing,
and fills the truncated before tail with `::missing`; `leaf-diff-op`'s third cond clause
reads `::missing` in a before slot BEFORE it consults the projection and returns `:added`.

## DOMAIN NARROWING — the one place this differs from the item's framing

The item and the dispatch brief both read as though the render path reaches this arm
generally. It does not, and the narrowing is worth recording because it bounds the user-
visible blast radius without weakening the defect.

`render-node` routes EVERY sequential in diff mode to `sequential-diff-children` first
(the `(and diff? (#{:vector :list :seq} kind))` arm); `children-of-pair` is its fallback,
taken on `(not (and projection a-vec b-vec))`. And `engine/project` returns a MAP in both
of its branches — the `identical?` short-circuit and the Editscript branch — so
`project-for` yields a truthy projection whenever `diff?`. Therefore, from a mounted
widget, the two-sided sequential arm of `children-of-pair` is not reached at all: the
fallback fires only when a side is non-sequential, and there the single-side branch emits
`::missing`, which is correct.

So the defect is live on (a) the public function itself — it is public precisely so tests
and downstream renderers can probe the union, and it returns the SAME triple shape as
`sequential-diff-children` to the same renderer — and (b) the no-projection render path,
where `leaf-diff-op` reaches `:added` with no projection to fall through to. It is NOT a
live mounted-widget mis-render today. It was one API-shape change away from being one:
`sequential-diff-children`'s own docstring promises the fallback is the "same answer for
the no-removal case", and that promise was false in exactly this shape.

## Was it made moot by rf2-bmed1? NO — re-derived, not inherited

rf2-bmed1 (merged 58bcee487f) added `bounded-projection-pair` and `differs-within-bound?`
and did not touch `children-of-pair`, exactly as its brief required. Its bound is upstream,
so the mootness question was real; the answer is no, and the reason is decision 1 in
`bounded-projection-pair`'s own docstring: THE BOUND FIRES ONLY WHERE BOTH SIDES COULD BE
ENDLESS. The mixed-ceiling case has one `counted?` side, so `endless-candidate?` is false
for it, the `cond` falls through, and the pair is returned unbounded and unchanged. The
upstream bound never touches this shape. Confirmed by execution rather than reading: the
defect reproduced at trunk 58bcee487f, i.e. WITH rf2-bmed1 merged.

## Representation: `::unrealised` reused, no fourth state

As the item preferred. It already means "before value not realised" as distinct from
"absent", it is deliberately not structural so `leaf-diff-op` falls through to the
projection, and `change-annotation` already renders it as an explicit unknown. rf2-bmed1
introduced no sentinel on the grounds that where both sides share ONE ceiling there is no
unknown tail to name; this is the mixed-ceiling case it named as the one `::unrealised`
stays correct for.

Discrimination: `sequential-diff-children` tells a genuine addition from an unrealised
prior by asking the projection whether the row is `:added`. This walk has no projection,
so it reads the ceiling: `(and (endless-candidate? before) (= b-count count-bound))`.
Keyed on the ceiling being REACHED and never on the before side's KIND — a lazy seq that
ended on its own below the bound was realised in full, so absence past it is KNOWN and
`::missing` remains the true answer. No extra element is realised to separate the two
cases; a before side of exactly `count-bound` elements reads unknown, which is the safe
direction and costs exactly the element the bound exists to refuse.

## Tests

Two deftests beside the rf2-zk4he family in
`tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/edn_inspector_cljs_test.cljs`, shaped after
PR #10114's both-ways pin. P1: the survivor carries `::unrealised` and renders the
projection's own op, with a `::missing` CONTROL in the same slot against the same
projection still forcing `:added` and suppressing that op — so neither assertion can pass
vacuously. P2, all green on trunk, refusing wrong fixes: both-`counted?` surplus stays
`::missing`; a SHORT lazy before side that ended below the ceiling stays `::missing` (the
discriminator that refuses a blanket sentinel swap); and a realisation counter against a
guarded endless generator refuses a fix that widens the bound to find out.

Per the rf2-bmed1 warning, both halves vary at once: the existing suite missed this because
its fixtures pair two vectors (one shared ceiling) or differ in length.

  captured exit 1. With the fix: 12368 / 61999, 0 failures 0 errors, captured exit 0, and

- `python scripts/lint_kondo.py`: errors 0, warnings 1957, exit 0 — identical to the base,

- Ratchets over the touched paths, each exit 0 and unchanged:

  `check_thrown_error_messages.py`, `check_retired_spellings.py`,
  `check_retired_composition_vocab.py`, `check_retired_image_keys.py`,
  `check_architecture_census.py`.
- NOT graded by this change, stated rather than run for appearance: `check_doc_slugs.py`,
  `check_readme_links.py --ci`, `mkdocs build --strict`. No markdown is touched, and nothing
  grades whether a docstring is true — the three docstring corrections here (on
  `children-of-pair`, its vector bullet, and `unrealised-sentinel`, which had named only one
  of the two walkers that emit it) were checked by hand.
- The surface classifier, handed PATHS, arms `cljs_node_test`, `cljs_browser`,
  `examples_compile`, `tools_jvm`, `mcp_conformance`, `story_xray_browser`; the five beyond
  the node lane run in CI. Control: a path known to arm 6 armed 6.

The item's `:1404-1405` for `children-of-pair` was stale as the item itself warned; it sat
at `:1510`, +106. Every figure in the dispatch brief's table was correct at that trunk, as

## Incidental observation, deliberately NOT acted on

In the reproduction fixture the projection classifies after-index 1049 `:same` rather than
`:modified`, although that element genuinely changed — the before side is a `:seq` and the
after a `:vector`, so R7 reads a kind change at the parent. That is the projection stage,
explicitly out of scope here (rf2-bmed1's ground), and it does not affect this verdict: the
property pinned is that the row defers to the projection instead of overriding it, and the
test asserts the rendered op equals whatever the projection itself reports for that path.

Out of scope and untouched, each verified: `sequential-diff-children`, the projection stage,

title: Incomplete Routing query display: declared sensitive route values bypass the egress projection
description: PR #10057 (a11cc31afd0efb3ffaf27cde6a174b215d14e9c5) newly displays CURRENT ROUTE query with (pr-str query) in panels/routing.cljs:226-230. The production input is raw frame state: app_db_diff_subs.cljs:109-112 reads :rf.db/runtime from rf/frame-state-value; routing/current-route-slice-value (:665-671) merely get-ins [:rf.runtime/routing :current]; routing_helpers/project-topology-data forwards current-slice unchanged. No originating-frame classification or Xray egress profile is consulted before query text reaches the UI. Current origin/main retains the full chain. A correctly declared route such as spec/012-Routing.md Route data classification example (:query schema promoting :token and :sensitive [[:query :token]]) therefore displays the live token even under the default local-redacted profile. This is a missed explicit data-hygiene declaration, not a claim that arbitrary undeclared trace carriers form a security boundary. Project the route slice through the existing framework routing/runtime-path classification at its actual observed host frame before rendering; preserve ordinary query display and handle redacted/large sentinels without seq/type errors. Add a real navigation test with a promoted classified query key, an unclassified sibling and the default profile, plus explicit local-raw behavior as applicable. Evidence is the merged/current source call chain and the documented route-lowering contract; no mounted browser reproduction claimed.

(`:1271`). There is no third. Controls both ways: `rf-xray-fade-in` reads 4 occurrences in
`tools/xray/src`, `rf-xray-diff-flash` reads 0, a nonsense token reads 0.

## SITE 1 — DIFF FLASH. Settled; you are confirming, not discovering.

`007-UX-IA.md:1169-1178` specifies it in full shipping detail: 400ms ease-out wash on each touched
App-db slice when a new epoch lands, yellow tint `rgba(251, 191, 36, 0.20)` holding for the first

Three against one, and `007` is the outlier — **the identical shape as rf2-qfqpf one bullet above

title: Draft research prompt for Story parity and differentiation
description: Write ai/findings/Story/astra/prompt.md for independent research comparing Story with Storybook and representative alternatives, defining evidence and parity tests, identifying stronger re-frame2-native workflows, and producing a report with prioritized recommendations under the pre-alpha project stance. This task writes the prompt; it does not execute the research.
design:
# Research brief: Story parity, ergonomics, and opportunities to be better

You are researching Story, re-frame2's component and application-state development tool. Produce an independent, carefully evidenced product and technical assessment, with concrete recommendations, in this repository's `ai/findings/Story/astra/` directory.

The user wants Story to have feature parity with Storybook and comparable JavaScript and non-JavaScript alternatives, while taking full advantage of re-frame2's strengths, idioms, and ethos. Answer two questions:

1. How can we test how close Story actually is to that objective today?
2. Where could Story be meaningfully more powerful, more ergonomic, and more productive for programmers and their AI assistants?

Investigate and write the report. Recommendations need evidence and judgment; a catalogue of features or an aspirational roadmap alone will not answer these questions.

## Project posture

> Posture is that we are pre-alpha and focused on elegance, power and a masterpiece.
> But we are not over-engineering or gold plating. Also, we trust the programmer.
> We're trying to facilitate high productivity for them (and the AI they use) via a
> library with excellent ergonomics and low friction. We don't need to litigate every
> last fine detail and drown in the minutiae.

Apply this posture to the analysis and the recommendations. The goal is an excellent workshop for creating SPAs: minimal, expressive APIs; useful defaults; composable capabilities; short feedback loops; and excellent tools. Pre-alpha permits simplifying or replacing awkward designs. It does not justify unreliable everyday workflows.

Feature parity is a serious objective. Start by understanding what users can accomplish with the alternatives. Do not quietly narrow parity to the areas where Story already looks strong, or label an inconvenient omission a deliberate divergence without a reason. At the same time, parity does not require reproducing another product's API, implementation, plugin count, commercial service, or accumulated complexity. Explain which outcomes matter, how Story can provide them idiomatically, and which differences we should consciously accept.

Look for improvements that remove concepts, configuration, repeated work, and unnecessary friction as well as improvements that add capability. Do not recommend a framework within the framework, a new policy system, or a large infrastructure project when a small primitive, better integration, or clearer workflow would solve the problem.

## Working scope and deliverables

description:

Source:

- share.cljs:245-250 recursively visits every map and unconditionally removes a matching key regardless of its grammatical role.

Concrete trigger:
```clojure
(def d {:initial :idle
        :states {:idle {:on {:source-code :done}}
                 :done {}}})
(share/encode-share-url {:machine-id :editor :definition d}

The function-delay finding from rf2-fzbj.13 is a separate key/value treatment defect; its repaired behavior should coexist with this one.

1. Actual CLJS share encode/decode preserves the event reproducer and its one projected transition.
2. Both spellings survive in valid event/state/region identities and named guard/action maps; equality or semantic edge/node comparisons establish preservation.
3. Genuine :source-code/:source-coords annotation fields are still absent, including when colocated in a definition containing identically named topology entries.
4. Existing macro-stamped privacy and :fn topology regressions remain green.

title: mcp-conformance: reject siblings on closed dedup wrappers
description:
Reject recognized dedup envelopes with sibling keys before expanding their cache. The Node harness currently accepts an invalid closed wrapper and erases sibling status/data before semantic assertions inspect it.

Ownership and review identity

- Surface tools_mcp_conformance; parent rf2-gwye; SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2; WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review).
- Baseline 9e8ca973767f4ecff455421e48e1765d59783261; reviewed head 4df6a3303c68c77ced1f84ce92178bed1d7f7879; owned paths unchanged from baseline.
- Repair site: tools/mcp-conformance/lib/dedup-envelope.cjs:228-245.
- Consumer: tools/mcp-conformance/test/_runner.cjs:504-530; regression homes test/dedup-envelope.test.cjs and test/is-error-matches-ok.test.cjs.
- Contract: wire-vocab/test/re_frame/mcp_conformance/wire_vocab/schemas.clj:158-178 declares DedupTable a CLOSED single-key map; wire_vocab_test.clj:316-346 already rejects wrapper siblings in JVM fixtures.

Trigger and reproduction

    const resp = {isError: false, structuredContent: {
      'rf.mcp/dedup-table': {
        'de-dupe.cache/cache-0': {'ok?': true, value: 42}
      },
      'ok?': false, reason: 'failure'
    }};
    structured(resp); // {'ok?': true, value: 42}
    assertIsErrorMatchesOk('probe', resp); // accepts

Expected: reject the wrapper as malformed; neither inner nor sibling ok? has precedence in a closed-envelope contract. Actual: decodeDedupEnvelope checks marker ownership and cache object type, then returns expandCache without checking the wrapper's key set. Siblings vanish, so the semantic relation passes on the sanitized value. A plain unwrapped `{'ok?':false}` with isError=false is rejected by the same helper.

A fresh JVM 1.12.0/Malli 0.16.4 probe of the actual schemas/DedupTable independently accepts the single-key wrapper and rejects this sibling-bearing form. That pins a real disagreement between the Node live-response path and the canonical JVM schema, not an invented stricter requirement.

Impact: a server regression adding status, metadata or another discriminator beside the marker can pass Node conformance even though the wire envelope violates the established contract. The existing JVM synthetic fixture does not validate every live Node response and therefore does not close this gap. No claim is made that today's production server emits the malformed shape.

Suggested repair and acceptance

For a recognized dedup marker, require Object.keys(structuredContent) to contain exactly the marker before expansion, with useful sibling diagnostics. Mirror lib/overflow-marker.cjs's existing closed-wrapper check. Leave ordinary unwrapped values untouched and allow arbitrary additive fields inside the reconstructed payload. Reject both harmless metadata siblings and the conflicting status example through the actual structured/assertIsErrorMatchesOk path. Accept valid wrappers and ordinary payloads. A mutation removing the wrapper key-set check must fail the new tests.

Validation and limits

Executed current Node helpers in probe-tools_mcp_conformance-1.cjs, exit 0; valid escaped-reference, missing-reference, cycle and bare isError-mismatch controls also behaved as expected. Executed current canonical DedupTable using cached JVM/Malli dependencies in probe-tools_mcp_conformance-4.clj, exit 0. Logs and exit files are under ai/surface-review-20260913/tools_mcp_conformance/. These are characterizations, not full conformance-suite passes. No source mutation, dependency install, shared build or live server.

Known references and disposition

Fresh revalidation and independent split of rf2-fzbj.14 F2. Searched current and closed tracker descriptions for read/decoder/wrapper references and titles for conformance/dedup; no dedicated identical issue found. Read rf2-fzbj.14 and rf2-fzbj histories newest first, limit 3. The earlier overflow wrapper repair is present and supplies the established local pattern; this issue is confined to the independent dedup decoder.

REMEDIATION FENCE: preserve rf2-fzbj's hold until Mike rules who owns remediation. This is a review deliverable and dispatches no fixer; prior issue statuses and notes remain untouched.

title: Pair eval-cljs: preserve trailing line comments at generated source boundaries
description:
Terminate caller-provided eval source with a newline before appending wrapper syntax. A valid `eval-cljs` form ending in a semicolon comment currently becomes unreadable because every source wrapper appends its closing delimiters on the comment's line. This breaks ordinary, awaited, and frame-scoped evaluations. A small source-boundary repair preserves normal ClojureScript comments without introducing a parser or restricting programmer input.

Ownership: tools_pair_mcp, `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/**`. Review parent: rf2-gwye. Baseline: 9e8ca973767f4ecff455421e48e1765d59783261; rechecked HEAD: 9238907fec4e0cc708bc518aa7fa83db6c0182e7. The owned tracked paths have no diff from that baseline. SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2. WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review).

Source and mechanism:

- `src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/result_envelope.cljs:201`: the default result wrapper concatenates `(do `, form-str, and `)}` without a line break.
- `src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/await_promise.cljs:81`: the await wrapper concatenates `(fn [] `, form-str, and `)` the same way.
- `src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/eval_cljs.cljs:227`: wrap-in-frame appends `)` directly to form-str. The entry point composes this wrapper before the other two at lines 274, 287, and 312.
- The remainder of each generated wrapper is also concatenated without a newline. Therefore a final line comment consumes the required closing syntax and the source reader reaches EOF with open collections. This fails before evaluating the user's expression, independently of app state or the runtime preload.

Concrete reproducer:

Call `eval-cljs` with `{"form":"(+ 20 22) ; expected answer"}` against any connected build. The input is valid source and evaluates to 42 by itself. Repeat with `"await":true`, with an existing `"frame"`, and with both options. Expected: the usual successful result with value 42, including the direct-value fast path for await. Actual: generated source is unreadable with an EOF/unterminated-collection error. Removing the comment or adding a final newline to the input makes every wrapper readable again. Adding a newline only outside a previously built frame wrapper is insufficient: its closing parenthesis has already been swallowed by the comment.

Impact: copying valid annotated expressions into the Pair REPL gives a tool-created syntax failure and forces the programmer/agent to alter otherwise valid code. P2 correctness defect in the advertised source-evaluation primitive; no data mutation or disclosure claim.

Suggested repair:

Ensure each of these three source-composition boundaries inserts a newline between caller source and generated suffix. Preserve the source itself, REPL-special passthrough, frame semantics, and async semantics. Do not strip comments with a regex, quote the source as data, or add a validation framework. The repair can be a small shared source-boundary helper or explicit newline separators at these three sites.

Acceptance:

1. Through the compiled tool/runtime path, the exact input above returns 42 for normal, await, frame, and frame+await calls.
2. Keep ordinary expressions, existing final-newline input, multiline comments followed by code, and strings containing semicolons working.
3. Existing result-envelope, frame-binding, and promise-await tests remain green. Run canonical `npm test` in a dedicated worktree and the relevant existing live eval lane when repairing; do not cite a compile-only exit as a suite verdict.

Validation performed:

Executed the actual-source process-local Babashka probe at `ai/surface-review-20260913/tools_pair_mcp/trailing-comment-tools_pair_mcp-1.clj`, exit 0. It reads and evaluates the current production wrapper definitions (not reimplemented string builders), evaluates the standalone caller form to 42, and invokes a real Clojure reader on their emitted source. It asserts reader EOF for sync, await, frame, frame+sync, and frame+await compositions, with readable no-comment and final-newline controls for each. Evidence: `probe-trailing-comment-tools_pair_mcp-1.log` and `.exit` in the same ignored directory. The reader operation itself is the failing boundary; the probe does not infer runtime argument identity from substring matching.

Limits: this is direct source-reader validation using the shared Clojure/CLJS line-comment grammar, not a CLJS compiler, browser, MCP wire round trip, or full module suite. No source edits, dependency installs, shared builds, persistent servers, or Git mutations were made. The exact downstream MCP diagnostic was traced from source rather than executed, so the finding rests on generated source being unreadable, not on a particular error-envelope spelling.

Deduplication and references:

Revalidated existing single-finding rf2-fzbj.6 and will reuse it for the distinct EDN-data quotation defect; its remediation fence remains intact. That issue does not cover raw eval source lexical boundaries. Searched current tracker including closed titles for eval-cljs/eval/comment/newline and Pair descriptions for trailing comment, line comment, REPL-special, and wrap-form; no identical dedicated owner found. Existing result_envelope_test.cljs:62-88 covers REPL-special recognition and passthrough, while the inspected default-wrapper rows assert generated strings; those inspected cases do not exercise a trailing line comment. No claim is made that all tests lack such a row.

This bead is a fresh review deliverable only. No fixer is dispatched and no prior remediation decision is changed.

title: resources: produce and index infinite-feed tags on page success
description:
Produce and index the declared feed tags whenever an infinite page succeeds. This restores the existing whole-feed invalidation contract used by mutations.

F2 — P2: successful infinite reads never produce tags, so tag invalidation cannot find the feed

Sources: src/re_frame/resources/events.cljc:2861-2906 accepts a page success through entry-replace-page, settles/prunes its ledger row and reconciles readiness, but never reads the resource :tags callback, installs produced tags or reindexes the changed entry. state.cljc:1160-1202 and :1230-1275 append/replace page facts without producing tags. Contrast the scalar success at events.cljc:2440-2446 and :2464-2473, which evaluates :tags, installs them and reindexes. The actual invalidation matcher at events.cljc:1530-1538 intersects each entry's stored :tags, so this fails even though that matcher scans entries rather than relying solely on the missing reverse index.

Trigger/reproducer:
1. Register a valid infinite resource with :scope :rf.scope/global, :params-schema :map, :infinite true, :next-page-param (fn [_ _] nil), and :tags (fn [_ _] #{[:review/items]}). Register a scalar control with the same tag producer. A vector page needs no page->items accessor.
2. Ensure each resource under a live owner, then deliver its accepted success with value [1 2]. Use page-succeeded-handler for the infinite read and succeeded-handler for the scalar control, as their actual lowering dictates.
3. Send [:rf.resource/invalidate-tags {:scope :rf.scope/global :tags #{[:review/items]} :cause :write}].
Expected: both successfully loaded resources expose the declared produced tag and match invalidation. In particular spec/016-Resources.md:1604-1605 says a feed's tag invalidation and mutation :invalidates operate on the whole feed.
Actual measured: infinite :tags #{}, :tag-index nil, invalidation :fx [], :invalidated-at nil; scalar :tags #{[:review/items]}, matching index membership, :invalidated-at 100 and a :rf.resource/refetch dispatch. An instrumented tag callback was invoked only for the scalar control, never for page success.
Impact: the normal mutation-invalidates/feed pattern silently leaves stale feed data. Declaring tags does not make an infinite read invalidatable, and successful further pages/refetches do not repair the missing tag facts. This is a failed shipped invalidation contract, not a request for deferred item-level optimistic feed patching.

Repair: on every accepted infinite page success, evaluate the registered tag producer against canonical params and the resulting feed data under the resource's existing tag callback contract; install the produced tag set and update reverse indexes for that entry. Do so after page append/replacement has assembled the authoritative accumulation, so tags follow the current feed, not just an old or isolated page. Preserve unrelated owners and tags on other keys and scopes. Align any callback-data documentation only if necessary to make the accumulated data contract precise; do not add a second tag API.
Acceptance:
- A public resource test declares a constant feed tag, loads page 0, invalidates it under an active owner, and observes a request; an owner-free twin becomes durably stale without a request. Include the scalar control.
- A mutation :invalidates integration test updates an item, invalidates the declared feed tag and observes authoritative feed refresh while preserving the visible page window.
- Append/replacement tests use data-dependent tags and prove tag/index membership is updated, including removal of obsolete tags and preservation of other scopes. A negative control skipping page-success tag production must fail the new tests.
Review provenance and scope

Surface: implementation/resources/** (impl_resources, 85 tracked files). Source root C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2. WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review). Fresh review baseline 9e8ca973767f4ecff455421e48e1765d59783261. Owned source was unchanged against baseline at review completion. All paths in the finding are relative to implementation/resources unless explicitly prefixed spec/.

This is an independent finding split from aggregate rf2-fzbj.7 for current review parent rf2-gwye. The prior parent remediation fence remains in force: until Mike rules who remediates rf2-fzbj. This review authorizes issue filing, not implementation. Preserve existing normative deferrals.

title: [implementation/core] Atomically extract cache-clear disposal batches
description:
Atomically take and empty the subscription cache before disposing the captured batch. `clear-sub-cache!` currently reads a snapshot and resets the cache in separate operations, so a concurrently acquired reaction can be erased without ever being disposed. Use the existing atomic atom primitives and preserve removal-before-callback ordering.

Surface: implementation/core (impl_core). P2 correctness defect.
Reviewed baseline and HEAD: 9e8ca973767f4ecff455421e48e1765d59783261.
SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2.
WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review).
Source: implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs/cache.cljc:473-492 (`@cache` at 475 followed by `reset!` at 478). The adjacent `dispose-all-for-frame-destroy!` has the same extraction spelling at 557-568; explicit cache clear is the executed trigger here, not a claim that a destroy/admission race was reproduced.

Trigger and observed behavior
1. Cache contains reaction A. T1 starts `clear-sub-cache!` and records snapshot {A}.
2. Before T1 resets the atom, T2 subscribes a different query and installs B with a live owner.
3. T1 resets the atom to {}, erasing A and B, and disposes only the previously recorded snapshot {A}.

Expected: the removal operation and condemned batch must agree. A concurrently acquired B either linearizes after the clear and remains live, or belongs to the removed batch and is disposed exactly once. Erased but undisposed is not a valid outcome.
Actual, reproduced on current source in both JVM configurations: `{:late-cached false, :old-disposes 1, :late-disposes 0}`. The probe verifies B is actually cached before allowing the reset to proceed.

Impact: the runtime loses ownership bookkeeping for a reaction it never retired. An ordinary unsubscribe cannot find it, disposal callbacks/resources can be stranded, and a later subscription creates another identity for the same query. This is a JVM concurrency issue; ordinary CLJS execution cannot interleave host threads between these two statements.

Standalone reproducer (Clojure, fresh process with the core source classpath)
```clojure
(require '[re-frame.core :as rf] '[re-frame.subs :as subs]
         '[re-frame.subs.cache :as cache] '[re-frame.frame :as frame]
         '[re-frame.interop :as interop]
         '[re-frame.substrate.plain-atom :as plain])
(rf/init! plain/adapter)
(let [id :review-clear/frame old-q [:review-clear/old]
      late-q [:review-clear/late] entered (promise) resume (promise)
      disposed (atom [])]
  (rf/reg-sub (first old-q) {} (fn [_ _] :old))
  (rf/reg-sub (first late-q) {} (fn [_ _] :late))
  (rf/make-frame {:id id})
  (let [state (:sub-cache (frame/frame id))
        old (subs/subscribe old-q {:frame id})
        original-reset! clojure.core/reset!]
    (interop/add-on-dispose! old #(swap! disposed conj :old))
    (with-redefs [clojure.core/reset!
                  (fn [a v]
                    (when (and (identical? a state) (= {} v))
                      (deliver entered true) @resume)
                    (original-reset! a v))]
      (let [job (future (cache/clear-sub-cache! id))]
        (try
          (assert (= true (deref entered 5000 :timeout)))
          (let [late (subs/subscribe late-q {:frame id})]
            (interop/add-on-dispose! late #(swap! disposed conj :late))
            (assert (contains? @state late-q))
            (deliver resume true)
            (assert (nil? (deref job 5000 :timeout)))
            (prn {:cache @state :disposed @disposed})
            (interop/dispose! late))
          (finally (deliver resume true) (future-cancel job)))))))
(shutdown-agents)
(System/exit 0)
```
Observed output is `{:cache {}, :disposed [:old]}` before explicit probe cleanup. The scoped redef matches only this exact frame-cache atom and {} value, and delegates unchanged to the real reset!. It widens the actual read/reset window without changing cache contents or disposal logic. Other thread acquisition uses real `subscribe`. The orphaned probe reaction is explicitly disposed after measurement.

Repair and acceptance
- Replace the separate `@cache`/`reset!` extraction with the OLD map returned by `(reset-vals! cache {})`; dispose that exact old map. Preserve the intentional remove-before-callback order, disposal cause binding, per-key trace reasons, and best-effort per-entry disposal.
- Apply the same extraction discipline to the neighboring frame-destroy batch helper so the two batch paths remain consistent. Do not invent a new ownership API or broaden this into a frame lifecycle redesign.
- Add a deterministic concurrent-acquisition regression: every removed entry must be disposed exactly once; any acquisition after the atomic extraction remains cached and live. Also cover overlapping clears so a reaction is not placed into two condemned batches.

title: surface-review(fresco): close first-render ownership and hydration rejection gaps
description:
Recommendation: make first-root construction release ownership when Hiccup lowering throws, and make the mounted test kit's hydrate! reject setup failures through its promised channel. These are two bounded P2 correctness findings with small local remedies; neither calls for more input validation, a new lifecycle abstraction, or broader runtime machinery. Keep this task open until the two public-path regression witnesses and repairs land.

Scope and revision

Owned slice: implementation/fresco/**, including implementation/fresco/test_kit/**.
Reviewed revision: 1c9ff9697b0fa3a018c7a4371e02983ad2e79b2f.
SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2.
WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review).
No source edits, builds, server startup, dependency installs, commits or pushes were performed by this reviewer. The root coordinator owns durability.

Coverage

Substantive source-path review covered src/re_frame/fresco/impl/{collector.cljs,generation.cljs,frames.cljs,mount.cljs,roots.cljs,codec.cljs,frame_boundary.cljs,controlled.cljs,presence_react.cljs,portal.cljs,overlay.cljs}, src/re_frame/fresco/{native.cljc,server.cljs}, and the public facade connections. This included cold versus held subscription reads, commit-time ownership, generation fences, frame replacement, cached subscribe identities, active-root tracking, hydration tree stability, controlled-field echo/composition, host and outward crossings, and selected optional lifecycle paths. The test-kit review covered test_kit/src/re_frame/fresco/{test.cljs,test/runtime.cljs,test/mounted.cljs}: L1 event capture, L2 fixture cleanup, mounted construction/teardown, residue checks, and virtual-clock ownership/handback. Inspected fresco/deps.edn and test_kit/deps.edn for the kit's source and packaging boundaries.

Tests inspected, not run: client_root_lifecycle_dom_cljs_test.cljs, public_root_lifecycle_dom_cljs_test.cljs, test_kit_mounted_dom_cljs_test.cljs, test_kit_clock_dom_cljs_test.cljs, and neighboring collector/native test rosters. The existing mounted failure tests distinguish codec-stack failures from React-reported body failures, but those tests drive the test kit's catching-root! rather than the shipped client-root constructor. The clock suite already has a real registered ::boom setup handler whose throw establishes the setup-failure shape used in finding 2.

Exclusions: this was a focused review, not an exhaustive proof of every form helper, accessibility projection, evidence/tool schema, optional overlay interaction, macro expansion, browser behavior, or packaging/release lane. No whole-suite or bundle-green claim is made. The review did not treat missing example tests as a defect.

Finding 1 — P2: the first client render can allocate a React root that no public teardown owns

Owned source: implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco/impl/mount.cljs:248-257 (root!), :104-113 (render!), :527-533 (mount-client-root!), :553-558 (render-client-root!), :561-569 (unmount-client-root!). Lowering trigger: implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco/impl/codec.cljs:1278-1295 (expand-seq), :1821-1870 (as-element/root-element).

Trigger/reproducer, after normal adapter initialization and with an attached container:

(def root (h/client-root))
(def boom (js/Error. "row formatting failed"))
(def rows (map (fn [_] (throw boom)) [1]))
(try
  (h/render! root [:ul rows] container)
  (catch :default e (assert (identical? boom e))))
(h/unmount! root)
(h/render! root [:div "recovered"] container)

The root Hiccup and sequence shape are supported. The mapped function stands for ordinary user code that fails while formatting a row. No invalid Hiccup, malformed option, subscription from an escaped extent, or throwing React component is needed. An empty vector is a simpler refusal trigger, but is not the reason to repair this.

Exact causal path: root! calls React createRoot at :252-253, then calls render! at :256. render! evaluates (tree handle hiccup) before invoking the raw Root's .render. codec/expand-seq forces the root's lazy children and user code throws on that stack. root! has no cleanup catch, so it never returns. Consequently mount-client-root! never reaches track-active-root! at :533, and render-client-root! never reaches the reset! completion at :558. The opaque public handle is still inert (or carries a previous, already-dead live record), and the new Root is absent from active-roots. Neither h/unmount! nor the package drain used by destroy-adapter! can reach it.

Expected: an escaping first-render exception propagates unchanged and leaves no unowned React root attached to the caller's container. A subsequent retry through the same handle is an ordinary fresh mount.
Actual: React has already marked the container with its newly allocated root, while Fresco discarded the only returned Root handle. h/unmount! becomes a no-op; the retry calls createRoot again on an already-rooted container, producing React's duplicate-root warning in development. If the caller abandons the mount, that container retains an untracked root. This is a failed-construction/recovery defect, not a claim that an ordinary throwing defview body loses its root: those body errors are handled on React's own path, after .render receives the tree, and do not demonstrate this gap. No claim is made that this pre-render failure committed subscriptions or child effects.

Repair: either finish building the initial element before createRoot takes ownership, or catch the escaping initial render/lowering exception after allocation, unmount that exact new Root, then rethrow the original exception. Preserve the existing successful update path, public opaque handle and active-set liveness rule. The hydration constructor already lowers its element before hydrateRoot, so do not generalize this finding to that path.

Acceptance:
- A public h/client-root + h/render! witness uses valid lazy Hiccup whose user computation throws during initial lowering; it observes the same exception object and verifies no allocated root remains owned by the container without a reachable cleanup. Constructor/unmount spies can establish exact ownership; include a real DOM retry that produces no duplicate-createRoot warning.
- h/unmount! after the failed call is safe, and a corrected render through that handle succeeds and later unmounts exactly once.
- Existing create-once/update-later and adapter-disposal root lifecycle witnesses stay valid. Do not change React's reporting policy for component-body errors.

Validation for finding 1: the Fresco control flow was inspected at the stated revision; it was not executed through a compiled Fresco bundle. A nonmutating Node probe against the installed React 19.3.0 used a minimal in-memory DOM-shaped container, called createRoot without rendering, asserted that its root marker was already present, called createRoot a second time, and asserted the actual duplicate-root warning. Probe exit 0, output: {"probe":"React host premise only; no Fresco execution","rootMarkedBeforeAnyRender":true,"repeatedCreateWarned":true,"react":"19.3.0"}. React's local source independently shows the marker being assigned in createRoot and cleared in Root.unmount. This establishes the host premise, not browser/Fresco end-to-end reproduction.

Finding 2 — P2: hydrate! throws a setup-event failure synchronously instead of rejecting

Owned source: implementation/fresco/test_kit/src/re_frame/fresco/test/mounted.cljs:898-906 (explicit rejection contract), :631-647 (mint-frame!), :913-926 (hydrate! construction before first try/Promise). Supporting runtime source outside this slice: implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc:2875-2896, where escaping or captured setup-event failures call raise-setup-step-failed!.

Trigger/reproducer, with normal test adapter initialization:

(rf/reg-event ::hydrate-seed-boom
  (fn [_ _] (throw (js/Error. "seed failed"))))
(-> (hm/hydrate! [:div "ready"]
                  {:initial-events [[::hydrate-seed-boom]]})
    (.catch (fn [e]
              ;; This rejection handler is never reached today.
              (assert (= :rf.error/initial-events-step-failed
                         (:rf.error/id (ex-data e)))))))

The event registration and initial-events vector are valid. The setup handler fails during construction, as real setup handlers may. mint-frame! calls rf/make-frame, whose strict setup semantics tear down the failed frame and throw the canonical initial-events-step-failed error. hydrate! invokes mint-frame! in the outer let at :916; its first catch only encloses hydrate-root! at :922, and its Promise construction happens later. The failure therefore escapes synchronously, before there is a promise to attach .catch to.

Expected: the promise-returning test helper reports this setup failure as a rejected promise carrying the same core refusal. Its documented contract explicitly says every failure is a rejection and explains that a synchronous throw bypasses an attached .catch.
Actual: the call throws on the test's own stack. A normal (-> (hm/hydrate! ...) (.catch ...) (.then done)) asynchronous test bypasses its failure and completion handlers and may time out, obscuring the real setup failure. This is a usability/correctness gap in the error channel, not a request to suppress the handler failure. Core already rolls back the frame on this particular path; this finding does not allege a frame or clock leak from that setup failure.

Repair: put the complete hydration construction, including mint-frame!, behind one rejection boundary. Preserve the original ExceptionInfo/error object and existing cleanup for resources actually allocated. A Promise executor or one outer try converting synchronous construction failures to Promise.reject is sufficient; no new error id, retry machinery, or extra argument validator is needed.

Acceptance:
- Drive hm/hydrate! with a registered setup handler that throws, as the existing clock suite already does for mount!. Assert the call returns a Promise without a synchronous throw, rejects exactly once with :rf.error/initial-events-step-failed, and reaches the test's completion continuation.
- Verify the failed call adds no frame/container/standing mount and leaves a clocked peer untouched if one is present. Do not demand a second rollback of the frame core has already destroyed.
- Retain the existing codec-refusal and adoption-timeout rejection/cleanup witnesses and normal successful hydration behavior.

Validation for finding 2: source-supported exception-path trace, supported by the existing setup-failure fixture and core's explicit raise path. No compiled CLJS or browser reproduction was run. Before merging a repair, establish the red public-helper witness and then rerun it green.

Known issues/history and duplication check

Searched live and closed bead titles/descriptions for Fresco/Hicasso, root/mount, hydrate, construction and clock; read relevant current closure records and bounded recent history. rf2-kuky.59 closed the normal-root adapter-disposal gap by publishing the drain at the process boundary; finding 1 occurs BEFORE a Root enters that now-correct active set, so that completed repair does not cover it. rf2-3awu's later-task frame-recreation readset reacquisition repair is present in collector/dispose-cell! and is not re-filed. rf2-323z's renderer-owned :platform :server fix is present in server/render and is not re-filed. The mounted source cites historical rf2-4mvd for clock cleanup after mount! setup failure, but that id did not resolve in the current tracker; it is not treated as a current open obligation or as proof of a hydrate! fix. No duplicate live task for either precise failure path was found.

Unverified risks

No additional speculative risks are promoted to findings. Browser execution, a production bundle and fault-injected red/green gates remain validation work for the repair, not claims earned by this read-only review.

title: xray: the Schemas tab reads the RETIRED :spec key, so it shows zero event and zero sub rows against a live registrar
description:
THE XRAY SCHEMAS TAB READS A RETIRED METADATA KEY, SO AGAINST A LIVE REGISTRAR IT SHOWS ZERO
EVENT ROWS AND ZERO SUB ROWS. The panel is not subtly wrong; it is empty.

MAYOR-VERIFIED AT SOURCE, trunk 11739a11e5, with a nonsense control reading absent:

  tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/static/schemas/panel.cljs:108
      (when-some [spec (:spec meta)]
    (and the surrounding docstrings at :10, :35, :36, :106, :118 all describe a `:spec` slot)

  implementation/core/src/re_frame/reg_meta.cljc:55
      #{:doc :schema :tags :platforms :ns :line :column :file}     <- `:spec` is NOT a member
  implementation/core/src/re_frame/reg_meta.cljc:96
      {:spec :schema}                                              <- the M-54 rename map
  implementation/core/src/re_frame/reg_meta.cljc:112
      "A RETIRED bare key (`retired-bare-keys`, e.g. `:spec`) throws"

So `:spec` is the v1 payload-schema key, renamed to `:schema` per MIGRATION §M-54. A live
`reg-event` / `reg-sub` cannot carry `:spec` -- registering it HARD-ERRORS rather than being
silently swallowed, deliberately, because swallowing it would disable payload validation. The
panel therefore asks every registration for a slot none of them can have.

=== WHY NO TEST CAUGHT IT, AND THIS IS THE HALF WORTH KEEPING ===

The existing tests pass because they INJECT SYNTHETIC METADATA MAPS THROUGH THE OVERRIDE SEAM
rather than going through a real registrar. A synthetic map can carry `:spec`; a real
registration cannot. **That is a hollow gate in the precise sense this project means it: the
test proves the behaviour via a path production does not take.** Apply the mechanical test when
repairing -- delete the signal, keep the fault, does the test still pass? A row that still
passes with `:schema` unreadable is testing the fixture, not the panel.

So the repair has TWO parts and the second is the one that stops recurrence:
  1. Read `:schema` (and decide whether to keep reading `:spec` as a fallback -- probably NOT,
     since a live registrar cannot produce it and a dead fallback is the thing that hid this).
  2. Give it at least one row that reaches the panel through a REAL registration, so the
     override seam is no longer the only path under test.

Also update the five docstrings at :10, :35, :36, :106 and :118, which all name the `:spec`
slot and are now describing a key that throws.

=== PROVENANCE ===

Found by the rf2-k97c.3 worker (staticfs-a) while migrating this panel to a Fresco boundary in
PR #9622. It correctly did NOT fix it -- out of slice scope -- and explicitly asked for a
visible bead rather than leaving it as an appended note, on the standing ground that findings
appended to a bead get read as evidence rather than as work. That judgement was right and is
why this exists.

Independent of the Fresco migration: the panel is equally empty on Reagent.

description:
Residual of the MERGED-PR AUDIT of #9551. Filed as a NEW bead rather than reopening rf2-9w7h,

TWO CONTRADICTIONS REMAIN in the new read-location contract, and they pull in opposite
directions — one over-restricts the operator rule, the other under-restricts the artefact the
pilot is actually handed.

## 1. The operator rule now contradicts both pilot briefs AND a standing ruling

`workspace.md:54` adds an explicit exception forbidding spec pages EVEN WHEN the site serves
them. But both copied pilot briefs say the published documentation site is readable IN FULL,
and that if the site publishes a page the pilot may read it.

**There is already a ruling on this and it goes the other way**: the 2026-09-09 ruling on
rf2-hic-063 section 3(b) says the fence IS the site build, and that narrower brief wording is
the DEFECT rather than the contract. rf2-9w7h's own description named those briefs as the
correct model to follow.

instructions and without a superseding ruling. A pilot citing a served spec page is following
its brief, while this operator page now calls the same act barred.

`/core/hicasso/00-installation/` and `/xray/` are 200 with distinct real titles; the design
workspace URL and a made-up page both 404.

briefs. Distinguish READING A PUBLIC SPEC PAGE from OPENING THE CHECKOUT'S SPEC TREE. Do not
add an unratified corpus exception.

## 2. The generated workspace still hands the pilot links its brief forbids

`workspace.md:40-48` says there is no reading exception and expressly bars the checkout's own
docs — but `:124` says pointing at `../re-frame2/docs` grants nothing new, and `:126` excuses

prepended note, preserving meaningful anchors and the barred-source link handling, and remove
the competing checkout-reading exception.

Validate the ACTUAL GENERATED copies for both pilots, not the templates: intended public docs
URLs and anchors resolve, no docs link points into the checkout, and the copied note, the

Keep the existing local/root build-input arrangement and every held publication/pilot gate
unchanged. rf2-vfmb's earlier link repair was correct under the OLD checkout-reading policy —
the address/fence transition is the cause here, so this creates no duplicate repair owner.

CI green does not establish this: the relevant CI passes and checks the same source, but

title: [tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp] replace-app-db emits its db arg via pr-str — same print-is-not-quotation defect as rf2-j2wz
description:
Found by worker xray-a while delivering rf2-j2wz (PR #9369) and explicitly left out of scope, correctly:
rf2-j2wz names only `dispatch` and `dispatch-dry-run`, so widening it would have been scope sprawl. The
worker could not file this itself — `bd create` rewrites `.beads/issues.jsonl` inside a worker worktree,
which workers must never commit — so it asked the mayor to file it. Filed 2026-09-07 19:15 AUSEST.

THE DEFECT, same class as rf2-j2wz on a different tool: `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/spec/003-Tool-Catalogue.md`
(around §1641) says `replace-app-db`'s `db` argument is "parsed as EDN and emitted into the runtime call
via the normal `pr-str` path". That is the print-is-not-quotation bug rf2-j2wz fixed for dispatch — a
value that is PRINTED into a form is not the same as a value QUOTED into it, and the difference shows up
exactly where the data contains something the reader re-evaluates.

WHAT rf2-j2wz DID, as the model for this one: it did NOT invent a mechanism. The `::quote` node was
already documented in the eval-form DSL's own namespace docstring and had simply never been implemented
— that docstring line was its only occurrence in the whole tree. The fix implemented what was already
published. Check whether the same node now serves `replace-app-db` directly.

VERIFY BEFORE BUILDING (this brief's premises are claims, not findings): re-read that catalogue section
at tip, since rf2-j2wz's own fix may have already changed the emission path it describes; and establish
whether the defect is in the DOCUMENT (describing a path that is no longer taken) or in the CODE (still
taking it). Those need different fixes and the distinction is not obvious from the sentence alone.

LANE: `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp` is graded by `mcp-conformance`, which sits in NO tier of the fast-PR
spine. The default profile is `npm run test:mcp-conformance`; the `-- --live` profile is the only lane
that actually EVALUATES a generated form, so it is the one that can witness this class of defect. Run
both and quote both.

FENCE: rf2-zhef (open) also touches this artefact — the MCP kind enum's `flow`/`frame` members. Different
surface within the same tool; check it has not landed first.
notes:

The runtime repair uses the existing rt-quote node correctly for both call arities, and the catalogue now describes literal data. The new replace_app_db_test.cljs cases stub the evaluator with with-captured-eval! and inspect the emitted string using reader/read-string plus quoted-datum (lines 35, 66, 203-243). They prove the quote syntax, but never evaluate the generated form or observe the resulting app-db data. CI run 34121924046 DID pass the six-test hermetic live suite; its inventory is overflow, turn-observation, redaction, isError, cofx and event-meta. The only live replace-app-db call is the writes-disabled refusal in live-re-frame2-pair-turn-observation.cjs:518. Thus neither the new tests nor that passing live suite witness this specific data-versus-evaluation repair. All nine changed CI blobs match landed.

Add the requested live replace-app-db case with writes enabled: drive a db containing a nested list and symbol through the tool's generated-form evaluation, read the resulting runtime db and assert those values remain data (with an observable non-execution control where useful). Keep both arities covered without inventing a new evaluator or broad input guards. Run/quote the default and live conformance lanes with this case reached. This is the replace-app-db owner; rf2-j2wz remains scoped to dispatch/dispatch-dry-run.

REOPENED BY THE MAYOR 2026-09-07 23:5x AUSEST — THE WITNESS THIS BEAD SHIPPED FIRED ON CI, AND IT IS RED FOR THE ORIGINAL DEFECT.

The close above is honest about what it could not do: 'NOT executed locally: the live lane needs a booted shadow-cljs fixture + nREPL + headless Chromium.' CI ran it on PR #9396 and it FAILED — job 'MCP conformance tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp (rf2-cum40)', run 34127xxxxx, exit 1:

  OK   connect -> server attached on nREPL (--allow-writes)
  OK   replace-app-db {db} -> committed (one-arity)
  FAIL: one-arity replace-app-db: the injected list MUST read back as the LIST `(inc 41)`.
        A `:value 42` here is the print-is-not-quotation regression rf2-olqo fixed
    at assertQuotedDatumSurvived (tools/mcp-conformance/test/live-re-frame2-pair-replace-app-db.cjs:122:11)

So the ONE-ARITY path evaluates the injected form under live nREPL: (inc 41) comes back as 42. The commit succeeded; it is the READ-BACK that is wrong, which is precisely the print-is-not-quotation shape this bead owns. The rt-quote runtime fix that merged in PR #9380 (b053f17f07) therefore does NOT cover this path, or does not survive the live round trip.

WHY THIS IS THE GOOD OUTCOME RATHER THAN A SETBACK, and it is worth recording: the merged-PR audit reopened this bead asking for LIVE-EVALUATION EVIDENCE precisely because the unit lane cannot see this. The worker built that evidence, said plainly it could not run it, and let CI grade it. The witness then caught a live defect on its first execution. A witness that fires the first time it runs is the argument for building it.

WHAT IS NOT YET KNOWN, and must not be assumed either way: whether the runtime is wrong or the witness's expectation is. The witness asserts the injected list survives as a LIST. Determine which before changing anything — if the tool's contract really is to evaluate, the witness is the thing to correct, and this bead closes on that instead. VERDICT 2026-09-08 00:0x AUSEST (worker livefix-a, PR #9396, commit 8a9bd3b647): NEITHER (A) NOR (B) AS THE BRIEF FRAMED THEM. The RUNTIME IS CORRECT; the WITNESS's expectation was wrong — but not about evaluation-versus-quotation. It was wrong about the READ-BACK SHAPE.

THE EVIDENCE THE BRIEF DID NOT HAVE. The CI failure quoted in the reopening note is truncated at the assertion message; the assertion's own `Got:` tail is decisive and reads:

  {:ok? true, :exists? true, :path [:rf2-olqo/expr], :value [inc 41], :elision true}

`:value [inc 41]` — `inc` is still a bare symbol beside `41`, nothing evaluated. The read-back is NOT `:value 42`. Had `pr-str` been used, `(inc 41)` would have evaluated to `42`; it did not. So the rt-quote repair that merged in PR #9380 (b053f17f07) DOES hold across a live nREPL + browser round trip on the one-arity path. (A) is refuted by the runtime's own output. The failure was the POSITIVE assertion `/:value\s+\(inc 41\)/`, which is why the message named the regression it was written to catch while the regression had not occurred — the two throws carry different messages and only the second is the `42` control.

(B) IS ALSO REFUTED — THE CONTRACT IS DATA TRANSPORT, NOT EVALUATION. tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/spec/003-Tool-Catalogue.md §replace-app-db (the line concluded from, verbatim):

  **`db` is EDN data, not host source**: parsed as EDN and emitted into the runtime call as a `(quote <datum>)` literal (no `rt-raw` splice) — the same injection-closing posture `dispatch` takes (rf2-vflrg, rf2-olqo). Corroborated by rf2-j2wz's acceptance criteria, which this bead names as the same shape: "Dispatch and dispatch-dry-run pass nested lists, symbols, and emitter-tag-shaped vectors verbatim as event data; inert marker expressions are not evaluated." Note the wording — verbatim as event DATA, i.e. identity of the datum, not preservation of a printed delimiter. And replace_app_db.cljs:111-112 uses `ef/rt-quote` on BOTH arities, so there was never a one-arity gap.

WHY THE READ-BACK IS A VECTOR, established at source rather than inferred. `get-path` does not hand back the stored value verbatim. tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/elision.cljs states it: "`get-path` tool: the value at the requested path is run through the walker before pr-str." That walker is `rf/elide-wire-value`, and its shared map/vec/set/seq skeleton — implementation/core/src/re_frame/elision.cljc:785-791, the `(or (vector? v) (seq? v))` branch — accumulates into a `(transient [])`:

  (or (vector? v) (seq? v))
  (let [idx (volatile! -1)]
    (persistent!
      (reduce (fn [acc vv] (conj! acc (walk-tree vv (index state (vswap! idx inc)) decider)))
              (transient []) v)))

Lists and vectors both come out as VECTORS. So a correctly quoted list can NEVER read back through `get-path` as `(inc 41)` — the witness asserted a shape the read surface is structurally incapable of producing, and would have gone red against any conforming runtime. This is the egress wire's own normalisation, identical for a value stored as a vector all along; it is not a defect and implementation/** is fenced for this bead. `:elision true` in the envelope is the echoed default arg, not a marker that this slot was elided — the value is present and intact.

THE FIX (commit 8a9bd3b647, one file, tools/mcp-conformance/test/live-re-frame2-pair-replace-app-db.cjs). `assertQuotedDatumSurvived` now asserts the datum's ELEMENTS in either bracketing — /:value\s+[[(]inc 41[\])]/ — and KEEPS the `:value 42` negative as a separate assertion, because that is the only one of the two that distinguishes quotation from evaluation. The delimiter is the egress walker's business and grading it graded the wrong surface. The file header gained a "What the read-back is NOT evidence about" section so the next reader meeting `[inc 41]` does not re-file this. The symbol arm (`js/window` must not resolve to `#object[Window ...]`) is UNCHANGED and remains a sound discriminator — a symbol is a walker leaf, unaffected by the collection normalisation.

WHAT IS STILL UNGRADED, stated plainly. The TWO-ARITY (frame-targeted) arm has still never executed — it sits after the assertion that threw, so its status remains UNKNOWN, not passing. Code reading says it should pass (same `ef/rt-quote`, and `re-frame2-pair.runtime/current-frame` exists at skills/re-frame2-pair/preload/re_frame2_pair/runtime.cljs:295 and is already called through `eval-cljs` by the cofx and turn-observation live tests), but that is a prediction, not evidence. description:
Discovered during rf2-lrtt normative spec audit, separate from the original correctness review count. Snapshot 90e9b0008ac96bb59e0e9f6ec03de8e1d650f21d; relevant panels.cljs, shell.cljs and 008 spec unchanged against mayor HEAD 462164b00ed960c710e70a5e7f532d5083dd8b5f.

Expected/intended contract: tools/xray/spec/008-Embedding-Contract.md:109-125 promises mount-shell! opts :frame selects the Xray OWN frame, distinct from the inspected host target. frame_singleton_guard_test.clj:4-29 records rf2-1w07r / rf2-lnluk / rf2-r0o63 de-singleton intent: N shells must not collide in one app-db. shell.cljs:2572-2587 explicitly supports per-instance :frame-id. Preserve this contract, not document away the implementation gap.

Actual exact call path: tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels.cljs:364-383 mount-shell! reads only opts :mode, constructs [shell/shell-view {:mode mode}], and renders it. :frame never reaches shell-view. shell.cljs:2617-2619 therefore defaults frame-id to :rf/xray; its explicit subscriptions at2641/2655 and frame-provider at2721 all use that default. Per-panel render-panel! does honor :frame, so this is the full-shell adapter seam, not a global frame resolution change.

Concrete two-instance sequence (source-traced, not executed): in an initialized host with Xray's default shell frame seated, mount two distinct DOM roots using (panels/mount-shell! host-a {:frame :review/xray-a}) and (panels/mount-shell! host-b {:frame :review/xray-b}). Both trees receive the same :rf/xray provider despite distinct requested own frames. Changing selected tab/focus or opening a modal in A changes the shared own-frame state read by B; requested custom own frames are never selected. Pre-seating custom frames does not repair the dropped argument. Omitted :frame should continue to share the documented default.

Smallest repair: resolve opts :frame with the existing default, ensure that own frame using the existing frame seating seam, and pass it to shell-view as :frame-id. Keep :mode, target selection and mount teardown semantics intact; no new lifecycle model.

Existing two_instance_isolation_cljs_test.cljs:25-27,54-61 tests frames and direct shell-view :frame-id usage, bypassing mount-shell!. The source singleton guard prohibits literal singleton patterns but cannot detect a discarded caller option. Add the regression at the public full-shell boundary.

Dedupe: active+closed searches mount-shell, embed, Xray instance, shell frame and singleton; fully read closed rf2-ws60 (unrelated private egress sentinel) and open rf2-bitb (manual init target seating). Relevant memories matched no mount-shell!/de-singleton IDs. Historical rf2-1w07r, rf2-lnluk, rf2-r0o63 and rf2-nesy9 are unavailable in the current tracker; source/test contract records are the available witnesses. No current duplicate found.

Execution limits: source-only supported call trace and current-main comparison; no CLJS/browser execution, compilation, builds, shared suites or runtime fixes.
acceptance_criteria: Mount two actual full shells through panels/mount-shell! into separate roots with distinct :frame options. Assert each shell reads and dispatches against its requested own frame; a selected-tab/focus/modal change in one leaves the other unchanged. Cover omitted :frame default, preserve :mode, and prove the new regression fails when the :frame-to-:frame-id forwarding is removed. Do not bypass mount-shell! by mounting shell-view directly.

These are useful option-forwarding and seating tests, but cannot observe whether a mounted shell's subscriptions or UI callbacks use its requested frame. Removing shell-view's actual provider/callback routing would leave these new assertions unchanged. The existing two-instance data tests have the same boundary limitation. The PR-smoke feature matrix runs the panel-gallery's direct shell-view/frame-id composition, so that green does not exercise this public mount-shell! path either.

Complete the original criterion: mount two actual full shells through panels/mount-shell! into distinct real roots with distinct :frame opts, interact with a shell tab/focus/modal control, and assert its displayed state changes while the other shell stays unchanged. Retain default-frame/mode controls and demonstrate the DOM regression fails when the mount seam's forwarding is removed. Keep the current small runtime fix; this asks for the already-specified integration witness, not an expanded lifecycle API or general coverage project. Actual PR CI Node 11335 tests/57179 assertions and Xray PR-smoke 5 scenarios/10 matrix rows pass; those totals do not turn the render stub into a real mount.
