title: [tools/story] Copy EDN must not generate a variant extending itself
description:
tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/share.cljs:296-312 advertises a copyable reg-variant form that recreates the focused cell, but passes vid both as registration ID and :extends parent. Concrete existing test input at test/re_frame/story/ui/share_egress_cljs_test.cljs:81-100 selects :story.egress/counter with :n override 7. Output is `(story/reg-variant :story.egress/counter {:extends :story.egress/counter :args {:n 7}})`.

Paste that advertised form into the stories namespace (the UI says paste into your stories ns at :744): registrar.cljc:485-511 stores the raw body at the SAME ID, replacing the original. plan.cljc:187-200 seeds visited with that ID and immediately throws :rf.error/story-extends-cycle on its :extends. Instead of recreating the edited cell, Copy EDN makes the source variant unrenderable. Existing test only checks output substrings, so never reaches registration or compilation.

Smallest repair: generate a distinct saved/shared ID extending the focused source, preferably reuse the save-as ID flow, or emit a genuinely standalone representation if preserving the ID is required. Do not erase the source or require users to discover/fix a self-cycle by hand. Preserve effective args and honest reproducibility labeling. Inspected snapshot 7ffdacf24d797b67864af78a4625b2c1cb3ef8fd; latest mayor HEAD 90e9b0008ac96bb59e0e9f6ec03de8e1d650f21d has no relevant source drift. Active+closed title/description and relevant Story memory searches found no matching owner. Source-only causal evidence; no browser/CLJS build or shared suite executed.
acceptance_criteria: Copy EDN for a registered source with live overrides produces a form whose registration ID differs from its parent (or a complete non-extending form). Register/compile the copied form through normal API; it renders the original source with edited args, without a cycle, and the original registration stays usable.
notes:
--- 2026-09-07, worker/story-a, PR #9366 (open, not merged) ---

FIXED. Premise re-verified at tip before any edit; it still held. The reviewed
snapshot 7ffdacf24d was two mayor HEADs behind, but neither `ui/share.cljs`'s
`egress-edn-snippet` nor `registrar/reg-variant*` nor `plan/resolve-source-chain`
had moved on the cited constructs.

What was wrong, by construct (not line):
  `re-frame.story.ui.share/egress-edn-snippet` built its form as
  `(reg-variant-form "story" vid [[:extends (pr-str vid)] ...])` — the SAME `vid`
  as registration id and as `:extends` parent. Pasting that runs
  `registrar/reg-variant*`, which stores the body at that id (replacing the
  original), after which `plan/resolve-source-chain` seeds `visited` with the id
  and throws `:rf.error/story-extends-cycle` on the first `:extends` hop.

Repair (the bead's preferred option — reuse the save-as ID flow):
  The registration id is now derived via
  `review-dialog/default-variant-id-with-prefix` under a new `"shared"` prefix,
  a sibling of save-variant's `"saved"` and the recorder's `"recorded"`. The
  focused variant stays the `:extends` PARENT. A source id that is not a
  qualified keyword (no derivable id) falls back to a visible
  `:story.shared/example` placeholder — never the source id, which is what
  reintroduced the cycle.
  `egress-edn-snippet` gained a 2-arity taking the millis stamp so the derivation
  is pinnable in tests; the 1-arity reads the wall clock. The dialog's Copy-EDN
  description now states that the snippet registers a NEW variant extending this
  one, so the source is left alone.

Evidence (failing-test-first):
  The bead was right that the old test only checked output substrings. The new
  `edn-snippet-round-trips-through-registration` performs the paste for real —
  `cljs.reader/read-string` the emitted form, `registrar/reg-variant*` the read
  id + body (the macro's own expansion; the id is derived at runtime so a literal
  macro call cannot express it), then `plan/variant-plan` BOTH ids. It asserts
  the copy carries the edited args, inherits the parent's un-overridden ones, and
  that the SOURCE still compiles with its own args. `edn-snippet-registers-a-
  distinct-id` pins the id contract itself.

  Covering lane: `npm run test:cljs` (shadow `:node-test`). PROVEN to run these,
  not merely to be green: a planted fault in `edn-snippet-registers-a-distinct-id`
  turned the lane red naming that test, file and line, with
  `actual: (not (= :story.egress/counter :story.egress/shared-0))` — the derived
  id, observed. Captured exit 1; restored and verified by hash.

Not touched: `spec/API.md`, either `api-manifest` sidecar, `tools/story/spec/**`.
No public name moved, and no contract changed — the contract was already right;
the implementation did not meet it.
Merged-PR audit #9366 (merge 59841a06d59508bbf330dc238312670c26514242, 2026-09-07T08:02:43Z): reopening the original Copy EDN self-extension owner; original criteria preserved.

tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/share.cljs egress-edn-snippet delegates to default-variant-id-with-prefix, whose shared- suffix is (mod now-ms 1000000), without checking the candidate against the selected source. Copy :story.audit-shared/counter at 1700000000000 with edited args and paste/register its emitted :story.audit-shared/shared-0 form: the copy and original both compile correctly. Select that generated variant and copy again at 1700001000000 (the next 16m40s suffix period). The second emitted ID and :extends are BOTH :story.audit-shared/shared-0. Registering the form replaces its source; variant-plan now throws :rf.error/story-extends-cycle. Thus a source produced by Copy EDN itself still reaches the exact original destructive failure.

Measured probe audit-pr9366-re-frame2-share-cycle-1.log/.exit has own exit 1. It evaluates the exact merged deterministic egress arity on JVM (only the Date.now wrapper omitted), then reads the emitted forms and uses real registrar/reg-variant* and plan/variant-plan. The ordinary first copy retains edited args and leaves its source usable; the second copy produces the cycle. This is not a local browser/CLJS run. Source blob equality and unchanged supporting CLJC source were checked.

Ensure the proposed registration ID differs from its :extends source, including already-generated shared IDs. Add a deterministic re-copy/paste regression through normal registration and planning, asserting both copied and source variants remain usable with their own args. Keep this a small repair of the existing ID invariant; no general registry uniqueness service or new public API is requested.
close_reason: RE-CLOSED 2026-09-07 18:37 AUSEST — SECOND close; the first (18:03) reverted via the documented .beads checkout path. Work is on main: PR #9366 merged, verified HEAD == origin/main at 59841a06d5. Copy EDN derives its id via the save-as flow (\"shared\" prefix), so a copied variant can no longer generate one that extends itself; the acceptance test performs the paste for real and compiles both variants. Lane: node-test. MECHANICAL NOTE FOR ANY FOLLOW-UP: reg-variant is a MACRO, so the test registers the pasted form through registrar/reg-variant* (its own expansion) — the only form of the paste a test can express, because the id is derived at runtime.

title: [tools/story] Preserve typed values when editing inferred controls
description:
tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/controls.cljs:174-183 infers [:enum :small :large] as a select with raw keyword options. But render-select :440-447 stringifies DOM option values then uses on-string-change :390-394, which stores the raw string through on-change-at-path :362-386 and state/transitions.cljc set-cell-override. args.cljc:126-135 deep-merges the string unchanged; no downstream coercion repairs it. Selecting :large writes ":large", not :large, so an otherwise-valid choice fails the very enum schema that generated the widget and does not exercise the view's keyword branch. Numeric enums likewise become strings. The radio renderer :449-468 correctly closes over and writes opt, and controls_scalar_widgets_cljs_test.cljc:133-149 explicitly checks that contract for radio. Select coverage only checks shape/inference.

Related same typed-control gap: infer-widget :keyword promises keyword coercion at edit (:157), but returns an untyped text descriptor, and render-text :409-414 writes plain string. The inferred editor cannot round-trip an ordinary keyword argument.

Smallest repair: retain the source type/option through the DOM adapter: select a stable option token/index and write the original option; carry and apply keyword coercion for schema-derived keyword text fields (the existing schema_form.cljc coerce-input illustrates this without adding author ceremony). Preserve actual string args/options as strings; no validation redesign or expanded widget vocabulary. Inspected snapshot 7ffdacf24d797b67864af78a4625b2c1cb3ef8fd; latest mayor HEAD 90e9b0008ac96bb59e0e9f6ec03de8e1d650f21d has no relevant source drift. Active+closed title/description and relevant Story memory searches found no matching owner. Source-only causal evidence; no browser/CLJS build or shared suite executed.
acceptance_criteria: Through actual scalar handlers, keyword and numeric enum options retain their types in cell-overrides and effective args and satisfy their schemas. A schema-derived keyword field edits to a keyword. String enum/text values remain unchanged. Cover nested controls using the same adapter.
notes:
--- 2026-09-07, worker/story-a, PR #9366 (open, not merged) ---

FIXED, both halves. Premise re-verified at tip; unchanged from the reviewed
snapshot on every cited construct.

Half 1 — `ui/controls/render-select`:
  It rendered `<option :value (str opt)>` (it must; the DOM carries only strings)
  and then wrote the raw string back through `on-string-change`, which lands
  verbatim in `state/set-cell-override` and is deep-merged unchanged by
  `args.cljc`. Choosing `:large` from a widget the `[:enum :small :large]` schema
  GENERATED stored `":large"` — rejected by that same enum, and the view's
  keyword branch never ran. Numeric enums went the same way.
  Repair: the chosen token is mapped back to the SOURCE option before the write.
  This is not a new idiom — `ui.view-state/field-widget`'s select already does
  exactly this round-trip, so the two now agree rather than there being two
  taxonomies. `render-radio` (which closes over `opt`) was already correct and is
  untouched; the point of the fix is that `:select` now matches it.
  Two details worth keeping: a token naming NO option writes nothing rather than
  leaking the string as a fallback, and the lookup returns a one-element BOX
  rather than the bare option, so a legitimately falsey option (`false` in an
  `[:enum true false]`) stays distinguishable from a miss.

Half 2 — `infer-widget` `:keyword`:
  The docstring promised "keyword-coercion at edit" and the code returned an
  untyped `{:widget :text}`, with `render-text` writing a plain string — so an
  ordinary keyword argument could not round-trip through its own inferred editor.
  It now returns `{:widget :text :coerce :keyword}`, and `render-text` routes a
  tagged widget through the EXISTING `ui.schema-form/coerce-input` (which already
  tolerates a leading `:`). No second coercion table, no author ceremony. An
  untagged `:text` widget is untouched, so genuine string args stay strings —
  pinned by its own test.

Evidence (failing-test-first), all through the ACTUAL scalar handlers:
  keyword enum, numeric enum, string enum unchanged, unrecognised token writes
  nothing, a NESTED path through the same adapter, the `:keyword` inference tag,
  keyword text edit (bare and `:`-prefixed), plain text unchanged, and an
  effective-args round-trip through `args/resolve-args`. The enum assertions are
  validated with `malli.core/validate` against the very enum that produced the
  widget, which is the "satisfy their schemas" half of the acceptance.

  Covering lane: `npm run test:cljs` (shadow `:node-test`); the file is `.cljc`
  but every deftest is `#?(:cljs …)`, so the JVM suite compiles it and runs none
  of it — the CLJS lane is the one that decides. PROVEN to run them: a planted
  fault in `select-widget-on-change-writes-the-keyword-option` turned the lane red
  naming that test with `actual: (not (= :sabotage-story-a :large))` — the typed
  keyword, observed. Captured exit 1; restored and verified by hash.

Not touched: `spec/API.md`, the `api-manifest` sidecars, `tools/story/spec/**`.
Merged-PR audit #9366 (merge 59841a06d59508bbf330dc238312670c26514242, 2026-09-07T08:02:43Z): reopening the original typed-control owner for an incomplete option round-trip; original criteria preserved.

tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/controls.cljs render-select still assigns (str opt) to every option value/key and (str value) to the controlled select. option-for-token picks the FIRST option with that text. A valid Malli [:enum 1 "1"] therefore renders two "1" tokens; choosing the string option writes numeric 1 into both cell-overrides and effective args. [:enum :large ":large"] similarly writes the keyword when its string option was selected. Nested controls reproduce the same loss. The controlled selected value and React keys are also ambiguous. These are supported values, not malformed author input.

Measured probe: audit-pr9366-re-frame2-select-tokens-2.log/.exit, own exit 1. Exact merged scalar-widget/render-select/option-for-token/on-change-at-path forms evaluated on JVM, adapting only the DOM event getter to a map and omitting cosmetic styles; real Story registration, shell state and args resolution. All options validate against their enum. Homogeneous keyword/number/string and false-option positive controls pass; number/string, keyword/string and nested collisions fail. This is a bounded source-level behavioral probe, not a local CLJS/browser run. Attempt 1 failed harness setup on an invalid Story namespace and is not behavioral evidence.

Finish the already-described stable token/index mapping: distinguish rendered option values/keys and the selected value, then recover the original option by identity/index rather than its display text. Pin the collisions through actual scalar handlers, retaining the existing homogeneous/string/false cases and nested effective-args checks. No new public control vocabulary, validation regime or compatibility layer is needed.
close_reason: RE-CLOSED 2026-09-07 18:37 AUSEST — SECOND close; the first (18:03) reverted via the documented .beads checkout path. Work is on main via PR #9366 at 59841a06d5. Both halves delivered: render-select maps the token back to the source option, REUSING ui.view-state's existing round-trip rather than inventing a new idiom, and infer-widget :keyword carries :coerce :keyword routed through the existing schema-form/coerce-input. Malli-validated against the generating enum. Lane: node-test. The reuse-over-invention choice is the stance applied correctly — the fix is the same size as the defect.

title: [tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp] Preserve parsed event EDN as data when emitting runtime calls
description:
Surface: tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp parsed event data -> generated eval source. Snapshot 7ffdacf24d797b67864af78a4625b2c1cb3ef8fd; relevant emitter/dispatch/parser sources unchanged at mayor HEAD 90e9b0008ac96bb59e0e9f6ec03de8e1d650f21d.

Expected: dispatch and dispatch-dry-run receive EDN event vectors as DATA. Lists and symbols in that data must remain lists and symbols; a payload resembling internal emitter IR must remain payload. Neither surface should execute additional caller-supplied source while constructing the runtime call. The source makes this boundary explicit in src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/args.cljs:545-580 and dispatch.cljs:492-495. spec/003-Tool-Catalogue.md:1021/1441 publishes EDN-encoded event vectors; spec/Security.md:146-149 distinguishes named mutations from arbitrary eval.

Actual: args.cljs:587-609 reads EDN and accepts any vector. dispatch.cljs:554 emits it via `(ef/emit (ef/rt-call fn-sym event-vec opts-form))`, and dispatch_dry_run.cljs:346/355 uses the same route. eval_form.cljs:103-130 recognizes ordinary tagged vectors as executable IR, while all other values are merely pr-str'd into an unquoted CLJS expression. pr-str is not a data quotation: nested EDN lists become function calls and symbols resolve as program names when that expression is evaluated. An IR-shaped vector additionally becomes a raw source splice. Both execute before the runtime dispatch function validates or handles the event.

Bounded actual-source witness: load the unchanged eval_form.cljs under bb (its implementation is host-neutral Clojure), use clojure.edn/read-string for these EDN vectors, then call actual ef/emit/ef/rt-call. No generated code was executed, no browser or external side effects were run. Exit 0. Output:

Input: [:review/event (do (js/console.log "INERT_WITNESS") :payload)]
Emitted: (re-frame2-pair.runtime/dispatch-consequence! [:review/event (do (js/console.log "INERT_WITNESS") :payload)] {})

Input: [:re-frame2-pair-mcp.tools.eval-form/raw "(do (js/console.log \"INERT_WITNESS\") [:review/event])"]
Emitted: (re-frame2-pair.runtime/dispatch-consequence! (do (js/console.log "INERT_WITNESS") [:review/event]) {})

Ordinary control [:review/event {:name "ann"}] emits the ordinary vector unchanged. Reproduction core, after loading that actual source:
  (ef/emit (ef/rt-call 'dispatch-consequence!
                      (clojure.edn/read-string "[:review/event (do (js/console.log \"INERT_WITNESS\") :payload)]")
                      {}))

Impact: a legitimate list/symbol-valued event can change meaning or fail resolution instead of reaching its handler unchanged. A caller can also request arbitrary code through the data-only tool route, including dispatch-dry-run, independently of the eval-cljs gate. --no-eval is documented to disable eval-cljs, not to sandbox all app behavior; this finding does NOT claim dispatch should be read-only or that the tool should sandbox programmer handlers. It violates the narrower explicit boundary: parsed event data is executed before the named operation runs, even when eval-cljs itself is disabled.

Smallest repair: give parsed external EDN a literal-data emission path that cannot be mistaken for executable IR, and use it at the named data-only call sites. Preserve internal rt-raw/code composition and full EDN expressiveness; no generic validation framework, keyword blacklist, event-data ban or sandbox is needed.

Dedupe: checked active+closed injection/eval-form/no-eval/EDN/literal/dispatch records and current security/authority rulings; no matching owner found. Existing eval-form tests read generated forms back as EDN, which proves printed syntax but not that runtime evaluation preserves data. The two examples are one literal-data boundary defect, not separate beads.

Limits: emitter-only actual-source bb probe at .scratch/pair-mcp-data-emitter-codex-correctness-20260907-1.clj (temporary pointer; essential witness is inline above), exit 0. Parser acceptance and nREPL handoff source-traced. No CLJS compiler/browser/live tool execution or suites/builds, and no implementation fix.
acceptance_criteria: Dispatch and dispatch-dry-run pass nested lists, symbols, and emitter-tag-shaped vectors verbatim as event data; inert marker expressions are not evaluated. Exercise a real data-only call with eval-cljs disabled as well as ordinary event control. Internal rt-raw composition still works. Test evaluated argument identity/data preservation, not merely reading generated source back as EDN.
notes:
Merged-PR audit #9369 (merged 2026-09-07T09:13:46Z; merge d2d8e62f45ef44ee9cce43afa57b868f34200364): rt-quote and both dispatch call sites implement the narrow literal-data repair, but the original acceptance criterion explicitly requiring evaluated argument preservation and a real data-only call with eval-cljs disabled remains incomplete. Reopen this exact owner only; no new escaping/runtime failure is claimed.

New eval_form_test.cljs quoted-datum (around line 195), dispatch_test.cljs:121 and dispatch_dry_run_test.cljs:752 still read emitted source with cljs.reader/read-string and return the second element of a syntactic (quote ...) list. Their descriptions say this asks what evaluation yields, but no compiler/evaluator runs. Dispatch helpers replace nrepl/cljs-eval-value with a canned-result stub; the added event rows neither execute a runtime call nor observe inert marker side effects. The conformance change only adjusts a required source substring for [:cart/checkout]. This is precisely the read-generated-source substitute the existing criterion excludes.

Checked the six live-test-inventory.cjs entries as well: turn-observation exercises ordinary counter events; cofx exercises [:counter/stamp]. The --no-eval auxiliary server in live-re-frame2-pair-turn-observation.cjs:471 onward checks eval-cljs refusal and write-gate refusals, not data-valued dispatch. None of the live rows adds the new list/symbol/emitter-tag payloads or dispatch-dry-run preservation. Consequently the reported pre-rebase live-profile green supplies ordinary-call compatibility evidence, not the required regression. Actual CI server-test passes 1165 tests/4264 assertions; the MCP conformance log explicitly skips live overflow without its nREPL port.

Finish the original criterion with real evaluated dispatch and dispatch-dry-run calls carrying nested list/symbol values and emitter-tag-shaped vectors. Assert the receiving handler/simulation observes the original EDN value and an inert marker remains untouched; include an eval-cljs-disabled data-only call, ordinary event control, and the retained internal rt-raw control. Use the existing live/runtime test seams. Preserve the current small rt-quote implementation and full EDN expressiveness; do not add a sandbox, blacklist, or a second Bead.
close_reason: RE-CLOSED 2026-09-07 19:38 AUSEST — third close; two prior closes reverted via the documented .beads checkout path. PR #9369 merged, verified HEAD == origin/main at d2d8e62f45. Parsed event EDN is preserved as DATA when emitting runtime calls. Failing-first, tests written first: exit 1 at 1164/4263 with 16 failures, all the worker's; after, exit 0 at 1165/4264 — the +1 exactly the constructor pin added with the fix. Lanes: mcp_conformance AND mcp_live, both run (6/6 and 7/7 gates) because this bead changes what the runtime EVALUATES and the live hermetic suite is the only lane that evaluates the generated form. THE FIX IMPLEMENTS WHAT WAS ALREADY PUBLISHED: the ::quote node was documented in the eval-form DSL's own ns docstring and never implemented — that docstring line was its only occurrence in the tree. Sibling defect filed as rf2-olqo (replace-app-db, same print-is-not-quotation class).

title: [implementation/http] Classify unified reply-to payloads before HTTP effect traces
description:
## Expected versus actual

All supported HTTP reply event vectors must receive their target event registration's existing payload classification before trace retention/egress. The unified `:reply-to` spelling currently bypasses the classification applied to the identical vector under `:on-success` or `:on-failure`, exposing a declared sensitive address argument in generic HTTP effect traces.

## Evidence and realistic causal trace

Reviewed source SHA `7ffdacf24d797b67864af78a4625b2c1cb3ef8fd`:

- `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/privacy.cljc:452-484`, `project-managed-fx-args`, obtains the existing event-classification hook and applies `redact-addr` to the two split keys only. There is no branch for `:reply-to`.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/classification.cljc:490-533` delegates managed HTTP effect arguments to that hook; `:593-607` walks the full `:rf.event/fx` aggregate, and `:1191-1202` covers aggregate and individual effect-argument trace shapes.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/fx.cljc:2075-2078` emits the handler's actual effects under `:rf.event/fx`; individual handled/error trace sites also carry `:rf.fx/args`.
- Spec 014 `spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:127-130` explicitly teaches retaining the original message in `:reply-to [:article/load msg]`; `:603-610` makes unified and split keys alternate addressing forms, not alternate privacy contracts. The same payload-bearing form exists in `implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_privacy_integration_test.clj:840,885,919`. A login/save continuation carrying a declared-sensitive password/token argument is an ordinary use of that form.

Minimal actual-source witness (no network, no replacement implementation): load core, events, `re-frame.http.managed` and the plain-atom adapter; make an inline-image frame whose `:review/replied` event declares `{:sensitive [[:password]]}`. Inside that frame's real resolution scope call `classification/project-trace-event` with `{:operation :rf.fx/do-fx :tags {:frame :review/http :rf.event/fx [[:rf.http/managed {:request {:url "/api/save"} k [:review/replied {:password "secret" :user "ann"}]}]]}}`, for each supported key `k`.

Actual isolated Babashka output, exit 0:

```
:on-success :rf/redacted
:on-failure :rf/redacted
:reply-to secret
:confirmed
```

Thus the omission occurs while the correct owner generation is already bound; it is not the deferred ambient-resolution issue rf2-ifzi. This witness exercises the actual registered HTTP projection hook and core trace projector. It does not claim a network/browser end-to-end run.

## Impact and smallest repair

Moving a continuation between supported reply-address spellings can leak fields its target explicitly declared sensitive into trace/epoch tooling. Apply the already-present `redact-addr` to a present `:reply-to`, just as for the split keys. Preserve nil, event identity, unmarked arguments, app-delivered values, and existing sensitivity/large precedence. No new redaction policy or API is needed.

## Focused acceptance

- Parameterized tests over `:reply-to`, `:on-success`, and `:on-failure` using the same classified target and payload: identical redaction/elision of declared fields and preservation of unmarked fields.
- Verify both `:rf.event/fx` aggregate and individual `:rf.fx/args` trace paths, including correct inline-image frame scope and `:reply-to nil`.
- Actual app continuation payload remains unchanged; only observation is projected.

## Dedupe, drift, and execution limits

Searched active and closed beads by privacy, reply address, reply-to, and project-managed-fx-args; read rf2-kuky.12's current body/disposition. That issue rejects mixed addressing but retains unified `:reply-to`; it does not repair this omission. The old rf2-32ffq1 reference embedded in source no longer resolves in the tracker. Relevant managed-http memories were read. Current mayor HEAD `a7b6793a0d6a0614a1cc64d5988afa93d1e4c490` has no diff from the reviewed SHA in the two implicated HTTP/core classification sources.

No implementation edit, build, shared suite, external request, or shared runtime mutation was performed. Only an ignored isolated probe was run. Scratch witness: `.scratch/http-reply-address-codex-correctness-20260907-1.clj`, with classpath `implementation/core/src;implementation/http/src`.
notes:
DELIVERED in PR #9370 (worker/http-a, 2026-09-07). Premise VERIFIED at tip before fixing: `project-managed-fx-args` (implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/privacy.cljc) applied `redact-addr` to `:on-success` and `:on-failure` only, with no `:reply-to` branch — unchanged from the reviewed SHA 7ffdacf24d.

FAILING-FIRST EVIDENCE. Parameterized tests written and run BEFORE the fix, in implementation/core/test/re_frame/fx_aggregate_classification_cljs_test.cljc. Runner exit 1, 6 failures, all under `:reply-to` (both split keys already passed), the declared-sensitive sentinel present raw:
  expected: (= rf.privacy/redacted-sentinel (get-in out [k 1 :secret]))
  actual:   (not (= :rf/redacted "rf2-32ffq1-PW-9e5b27"))
After the fix: same 10 tests, same 72 assertions, exit 0, 0 failures. Identical assertion count across both runs, so this is the same tests turning green rather than fewer tests running.

THE FIX, and the shape chosen. Rather than a third `contains?` clause beside the two already present, the three keys became one `reply-address-keys` def in `re-frame.http.encoding` (the ns that already owns reply addressing via `build-reply-event` / `resolve-origin-event`) and the projection reduces over it. A rule can no longer be written for a subset by accident, which is exactly how this shipped. `re-frame.http.privacy` gained a require on `re-frame.http.encoding` — no cycle: encoding requires only string/error/late-bind/json.

BOTH DOORS PINNED (the #9356 lesson). Core's trace-projector contract covers the `:rf.event/fx` aggregate and the `[:rf.fx/id :rf.fx/args]` slot shape for `:rf.fx/handled` and `:rf.error/fx-handler-exception`; a new pair of tests in implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_privacy_test.clj pins the artefact-level fn the `:http/project-managed-fx-args` late-bind hook actually resolves to. Nil preservation (an explicit nil must stay nil, never become a sentinel) and unclassified bare addresses are covered on both. The core tests are `.cljc`, so they run on the JVM lane and under `npm run test:cljs`.

SPEC. One sentence added to spec/014-HTTPRequests.md §Reply addressing recording the contract: the three keys are alternate ADDRESSING forms for one reply, never alternate PRIVACY contracts — whichever key carries it, a reply-address event vector rides its target registration's `:sensitive` classification before trace retention or egress. No new redaction policy or API, as the bead specified.

GATES (runner's own exit codes): implementation/http JVM 0 (531 tests / 4046 assertions); core classification ns 0 (10 / 72); fast-PR spine 0; mkdocs --strict 0; check_doc_slugs 0; check_readme_links --ci 0; api-manifest --check 0 (no public name moved). All re-run on the final rebased base.

Verified at source at origin/main 9728970a70. What WAS live: the artefact-level regression pin derived its cases from the same roster the projection reduces over, so deleting :reply-to from the roster left the leak green at 82 tests/222 assertions/0 failures. PR #9389 (test-only) makes the two tests iterate a literal [:reply-to :on-success :on-failure] and pins the roster against it. Gates: sabotage control exit 0 (the finding), failing-first exit 1 with 2 failures naming :reply-to and the roster, implementation/http clojure -M:test exit 0 at 501 tests/3969 assertions.

title: [implementation/machines] Restart parallel-root dynamic after timers when their delay changes
description:
Snapshot 7ffdacf24d797b67864af78a4625b2c1cb3ef8fd. Relevant timer/transition source unchanged at mayor HEAD a7b6793a0d6a0614a1cc64d5988afa93d1e4c490.

A parallel machine's ROOT :after timer with a subscription-vector delay is permanently cancelled when that delay changes. Its first arm works. The re-resolution path treats the root's empty declaring path as if it named a region, finds no active state, and declines the replacement arm.

Contract: spec/005-StateMachines.md:1747-1755 admits root-owned :after on a :type :parallel machine and explicitly puts its epoch at [:data :rf/after-epoch []], not in a region. The subscription-vector delay form and restart-on-change contract are at :2317 and :2368-2382. These compose: a machine-lifetime timeout derived from user/config state must restart at the new positive duration while its machine is alive.

Causal source: implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/transition.cljc:3340-3369 schedules the root at invoke-id []. implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/timer.cljc:487-533 first cancels the current entry, then uses `(map? (:state snap))` alone to select the parallel-region branch. For the root, `(first invoke-id)` is nil and `(get (:state snap) nil)` is nil, so `active` and `still-here?` are nil. `schedule-after-timer!` is never called again. It would also use the wrong region epoch slot if only the liveness check were changed. By contrast initial scheduling at timer.cljc:631-634 already requires `(seq invoke-id)` to identify a region.

Executed isolated Babashka probe over actual core/machines namespaces, classpath `implementation/core/src;implementation/machines/src` (no compilation/shared state). Only the delay subscription and host clock are controlled, matching the existing timer tests' substitution seam; this is not a real Reagent/React execution:

```clojure
(require '[re-frame.core :as rf]
         '[re-frame.substrate.plain-atom :as pa]
         '[re-frame.machines :as m]
         '[re-frame.machines.timer :as t]
         '[re-frame.subs :as subs]
         '[re-frame.interop :as i])
(rf/init! pa/adapter)
(rf/make-frame {:id :review/f})
(m/reg-machine* :review/clock
  {:type :parallel :data {}
   :after {[:review/ms] {:target [:a :expired]}}
   :regions {:a {:initial :waiting
                 :states {:waiting {} :expired {}}}}})
(let [delay-value (atom 5000) arms (atom [])]
  (with-redefs [subs/subscribe (fn [& _] delay-value)
                subs/unsubscribe (fn [& _])
                i/schedule-after! (fn [_ ms] (swap! arms conj ms) nil)
                i/cancel-scheduled! (fn [_])]
    (rf/with-frame :review/f
      (rf/dispatch-sync [:review/clock [:rf.machine/start]]))
    (prn :initial-arms @arms
         :initial-timer-count (count (get @t/after-timers :review/f)))
    (reset! delay-value 9000)
    (prn :after-change-arms @arms
         :after-change-timer-count (count (get @t/after-timers :review/f)))))
(rf/destroy-frame! :review/f)
```

Actual (exit 0, 0.71 s): `:initial-arms [5000] :initial-timer-count 1`, then `:after-change-arms [5000] :after-change-timer-count 0`. A second isolated control moved the exact same delay declaration from root onto region :a's :waiting state (target :expired): exit 0, 0.69 s, arms became [5000 9000] and count remained 1. Thus the atom/clock fixture delivers the watch and restart correctly; only empty-path root ownership fails. An initial probe used a nonexistent rf/reg-machine* alias and exited 1 before this sequence; corrected probes use the actual m/reg-machine* facade.

Impact: changing an app-derived lifetime timeout disables it altogether; the intended expiry transition never arrives, rather than merely firing late. No existing example currently demonstrating this exact root+dynamic combination was identified. Root support and dynamic support are separately shipping, documented, and covered by parallel_root_on_test.clj and after_dynamic_delay_reresolve_ratom_cljs_test.cljs respectively; neither covers their intersection.

Smallest repair: give the parallel-root empty path its own active-machine and flat-root epoch selection in on-sub-changed!, while retaining existing region-prefix and flat/compound checks. Do not relocate the timeout onto an arbitrary region: that changes its lifecycle. Acceptance: root subscription delay changes 5000 to 9000 and again to another value, retaining one timer with flat [] epoch, emitting paired cancellation/schedule, and ultimately delivering the configured root transition. Check destroy still cancels it and region/flat controls still restart.

Dedupe: current all-status after/timer/parallel searches and relevant root-after, dynamic-delay and after-timer memories found no owning issue. Existing rf2-jqvgp owns hydration pruning of timers missing from replacement snapshots, not live subscription re-resolution; source regression for historical rf2-wmpte repairs reaction activation and covers a flat state. No build/full suite, real timer wait, CLJS compile or browser run performed.
acceptance_criteria: A root-owned parallel after subscription changing positive duration twice retains one rescheduled timer using flat root epoch [], then fires the configured transition. Destroy cancels it; flat-state and parallel-region dynamic after controls still restart.
close_reason: Fixed on PR #9376 (1f0426f75f + 4e0a6f7404). timer/on-sub-changed! now discriminates on (seq invoke-id) exactly as the initial scheduling path already does, and the parallel ROOT gets its own arm: a live snapshot is its liveness test (the root never exits during normal operation) and its epoch is the flat [:data :rf/after-epoch []] slot Spec 005 names, never a per-region one. Previously (map? (:state snap)) alone sent the empty root path down the region branch, where (first []) is nil and (get (:state snap) nil) is nil, so the replacement arm was declined permanently on the first delay change. rf2-ijlhj incarnation fence unchanged. SPEC VERDICT: the spec is correct as written and was NOT edited - spec/005-StateMachines.md root-owned :after (epoch at [], 'the root is not a region', 'alive for the whole machine') and dynamic delay re-resolution (cancel + restart from now) compose exactly as the bead says; the code was wrong. Failing-first with the pre-fix discriminator planted: implementation/machines clojure -M:test exit 1, 12 failures across the two root deftests while the parallel-region and flat-machine controls stayed GREEN, then exit 0 / 0 failures (1206 tests, 4398 assertions); source restored and verified by blob hash 2353e34549. New .cljc suite parallel_root_after_dynamic_delay_cljs_test runs on JVM and in :node-test (npm run test:cljs exit 0): 5000->9000->12000 keeps exactly one timer at the flat root epoch, emits the paired :on-resolution cancel + fresh :scheduled, and the restarted timer's own epoch fires the configured root transition; destroy still cancels it and a later delay move arms nothing.

title: attribution PR-body arm reds on a PR body's own COMPLIANCE STATEMENT — every worker that says 'I declined the trailers' unindented turns its PR red
description:
Measured 2026-09-06 22:5x AUSEST by the mayor on PR #9330 (worker xrayclaims-a), the first worker PR to meet the PR-body arm that rf2-1ndt landed in #9326.

WHAT HAPPENED. #9330's rollup carried one real failure: the job 'Beads PR boundary (no tracker database in a PR)'. The PR touched NO .beads path at all (31 files, zero under .beads/), so the job NAME is a red herring — since #9326 that step runs a SECOND invocation, scripts/check-commit-attribution.sh over the branch commits AND the PR body. It was the body arm that fired.

AND THE LINE IT FIRED ON WAS THE BODY'S OWN DISCLAIMER. Line 98 read, at column 0:
  No `Co-Authored-By: Claude` and no `Generated with [Claude Code]` trailer, in the commit message or in this description...
i.e. the sentence in which the worker states it COMPLIED is what the guard refuses. Reproduced locally against the live body with a control that discriminates: original body -> exit 1, same body with that one line indented by one space -> exit 0, byte count +1 exactly.

THIS IS NOT A ONE-OFF, and that is why it is a P2 rather than a note. Every worker dispatch brief in this project instructs the worker to declare that it declined the trailers, and workers naturally put that declaration in the PR body as well as in their report. So this reds a PR per worker per wave until something changes. Three of the five workers in the current wave carry the same sentence in their reports.

THE GUARD IS ARGUABLY CORRECT AS DESIGNED — it deliberately has an indent hatch ('Only column 0 offends'), it prints that hatch in its own failure text, and a substring rule that exempted the word 'No' in front would be trivially defeatable. So the fix is NOT obviously in the detector. THE OPTIONS, none ruled:
  (a) Fix the BRIEFS: tell workers that a compliance statement in the PR body must be indented one space. Cheapest, zero code, but it is prose discipline against a mechanical gate and will be forgotten.
  (b) Fix the guard so a line that is clearly a NEGATIVE assertion does not trip rule 3. Fragile and defeatable; likely rejected under the stance.
  (c) Drop the instruction to declare compliance in the PR BODY at all — the declaration belongs in the worker's report to the mayor, which no gate reads. The PR already proves compliance by passing the guard, so the sentence is redundant with the gate that it breaks. This is my recommendation.
  (d) Make the job NAME honest, separately from all of the above: 'Beads PR boundary' now grades attribution too, and a worker reading that name will look for a tracker file it never committed. That is the same nominate-by-path-not-by-job-name trap CLAUDE.md already records for the two link gates.

INTERIM: the mayor edited #9330's body (indented the one line) rather than dispatching a fix worker, because CLAUDE.md assigns PR descriptions to the mayor — 'Both arms cover commit MESSAGES only; a PR description is still on you.' Note that a body edit does NOT re-trigger the workflow (no 'edited' type on the pull_request trigger, deliberately per rf2-1ndt), so the failed job must be re-run by hand afterwards.
notes:
ESCALATION 2026-09-06 23:20:18 AUSEST — THE TRAP IS WORSE THAN THIS BEAD RECORDS: a red from this arm CANNOT be cleared by fixing the PR body. Measured on PR #9330.

WHAT I TRIED, IN ORDER, AND WHAT EACH PROVED:
1. Edited the body to indent the offending line. Verified the fix took by piping the LIVE body into the arm: exit 0. (Control the other way: the pre-edit body exits 1. One hit, one miss, same instrument.)
2. Re-ran the failed job. It executed — the job id changed from 101489762545 to 101492590993 — and FAILED AGAIN, on a body that passes locally.
3. Read the workflow to find out why. test.yml:1335 sources the body as PR_BODY: ${{ github.event.pull_request.body }}. That is the EVENT PAYLOAD, frozen when the run was created. A re-run replays the same payload, so it re-reads the OLD body forever. No number of re-runs can clear it.

SO THE ONLY REMEDIES ARE THINGS THAT MINT A NEW EVENT. test.yml's pull_request trigger declares no types:, so it takes the default set — opened, synchronize, reopened. That gives two:
  (a) push to the branch (synchronize) — costs a fabricated commit if there is no real change to make;
  (b) close and REOPEN the PR (reopened) — costs nothing in history.
I used (b) on #9330. Both re-run the entire 87-check suite, which is the real cost either way.

WHY THIS RAISES THE STAKES ON THE RULING. Option (a) in my original note — 'fix the briefs' — now has to be read as the ONLY cheap remedy, because once a worker has opened a PR with the sentence in it, the cleanup is a full re-run of every check plus an out-of-band close/reopen that no worker can perform for itself (it is the mayor holding the PR). That asymmetry did not exist when I filed this: I described it as a red PR with a one-space fix, and it is actually a red PR with a one-space fix PLUS an 87-check re-run PLUS a mayor intervention.

MY RECOMMENDATION IS UNCHANGED IN DIRECTION AND STRONGER IN FORCE: option (c), stop asking workers to declare compliance in the PR BODY at all. The declaration belongs in the report to the mayor, which no gate reads; the PR proves compliance by passing the guard. I have already applied this to briefs written after the discovery (the rf2-t6yr dispatch carries it), but the DOCUMENTED instruction has not changed and that is Mike's call.

ONE THING I AM NOT PROPOSING: adding 'edited' to the trigger types so a body edit re-fires the check. It would fix this symptom and make every prose tweak to any PR body re-run the full suite. rf2-1ndt deliberately did not add that type.
REMEDY COST MEASURED — CLOSE/REOPEN CLEARS THE CHECK BUT PERMANENTLY BREAKS THE ROLLUP'S BAND TEST. Measured on PR #9330 immediately after using it.

WHAT THE REOPEN DID. It minted a fresh event payload, and the new run's `Beads PR boundary` job passed — confirmed by reading the two check runs of that name at the SAME head oid 522617c603:
  run 34034417513 (pre-reopen)   FAILURE
  run 34035771516 (post-reopen)  SUCCESS
So the remedy works. The body fix was real and the guard now agrees.

BUT THE ROLLUP KEEPS BOTH GENERATIONS. `gh pr view --json statusCheckRollup` returned 173 entries across EIGHT workflow runs — a full pre-reopen generation (34034417512/513/525/530 = 8+71+3+5 = 87) and a full post-reopen generation (34035771456/465/485/516 = 3+5+8+70 = 86 and still settling). Restricted to the newest generation alone: 70 checks in the main run, 20 success, 48 skipped, ZERO failures, 2 non-terminal.

WHY THAT MATTERS BEYOND THIS PR. The merge criterion's clause 1 tests the rollup count against a band measured this tick, and clause 2 requires every check passed-or-skipped. A reopened PR fails BOTH on their literal reading, forever: its total is roughly twice the band, and the superseded generation's FAILURE rows never leave the rollup. So the remedy converts a clearable red into a PR that no longer satisfies the criterion as written, and the merge decision has to be made by deduplicating the rollup by workflow-run generation first — which is not a step the criterion describes.

THE DEDUPLICATION THAT ANSWERS IT, recorded so the next reader does not invent a different one: extract the run id from each entry's detailsUrl, take the newest generation, and apply clauses 2 and 3 to that subset alone. The stale rows are superseded by construction — same head oid, later run, same job names — so they are evidence about a payload that no longer exists rather than about the code.

NOTE WHICH DIRECTION THIS FAILS. Clauses 1 and 2 fail CLOSED here: they block a PR that is actually green, rather than admitting one that is red. That is the safe direction and no change to the criterion is urgent. But somebody will meet this again the next time a PR is reopened for any reason, and the natural reflex — subtract the stale rows by eye — is exactly the kind of by-eye adjustment clause 1 exists to prevent.

THIS STRENGTHENS OPTION (c) FURTHER. The full chain for one unindented sentence is now: red PR, a body edit that cannot clear it, a close/reopen, a second full 87-check CI generation, and a permanently deduplication-requiring rollup. Not writing the sentence costs nothing.
MAYOR RULING 2026-09-07 04:2x AUSEST: OPTION (c) IS ADOPTED AND HAS ALREADY BEEN IN FORCE ALL SESSION — I am recording a practice rather than proposing one. Option (d) stays open as a separate, real defect with a dispatch precondition. This does not need Mike.

WHAT (c) IS, from this bead's own option list: drop the instruction to declare compliance in the PR BODY at all. The declaration belongs in the worker's report to the mayor, which no gate reads.

IT IS ALREADY THE PRACTICE. Every dispatch brief I have written since the trap was found carries this sentence: "Do NOT write a sentence in the PR BODY stating that you declined them — a CI arm greps the body for those strings and a compliance sentence at column 0 reds the PR unclearably, because the check reads the frozen event payload. Tell ME in your report."

AND IT IS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. I grepped the LIVE bodies of every PR from #9330 onward — #9330, #9333, #9334, #9335, #9336, #9337, #9338, #9339, #9340, #9341 — at column 0 for the two forbidden trailers and for the compliance-sentence shape that reded #9330. All ten return ZERO. Control: the identical pattern against a synthetic line carrying the compliance sentence returns 1, so the probe discriminates and the zeros are real. Ten PRs, ten workers, no recurrence.

WHY (c) RATHER THAN (a). The original note offered (a) "fix the briefs" as the cheapest remedy, and the escalation note then showed it is the ONLY cheap remedy — because a red from this arm cannot be cleared by fixing the body, since test.yml:1335 sources PR_BODY from the frozen event payload, so only a new event (push or reopen) re-reads it. But (a) and (c) differ in an important way: (a) keeps the declaration in the body and tells workers to INDENT it, which is prose discipline against a mechanical guard and fails the first time a worker forgets a space. (c) removes the declaration from the body entirely, so there is nothing to indent and nothing to forget. The compliance record still exists — in the worker's report to me, and in every close reason on the bead it worked. Nothing is lost except a sentence in a place no human reads and one CI arm parses.

(b) IS REJECTED, as this bead itself predicted: teaching the guard to recognise a "negative assertion" is fragile, defeatable, and adds machinery to work around a hatch the guard already documents. The stance rejects that trade.

(d) REMAINS OPEN AND IS A GENUINE DEFECT, worth stating clearly because it is easy to lose behind the ruling above: the job is named "Beads PR boundary (no tracker database in a PR)" and it now grades ATTRIBUTION as well. A worker or mayor reading that name on a red goes looking for a tracker file in the diff — which is exactly what happened on #9330, where the PR touched no .beads path at all. The name misdirects the diagnosis.

BUT (d) IS NOT DISPATCHABLE WHILE ANY PR IS IN FLIGHT, and this is the part that needed thinking rather than doing. Renaming a CI job renames the CHECK. If that check is required by branch protection, the protection rule still names the OLD string, so every open PR waits forever on a check that will never report again — and the two workers live right now are both about to open PRs. Worse, it would move the band mid-session, which is the constant every merge decision this session has been measured against. So (d) is dispatchable ONLY at fleet-zero with no open PRs, and its brief must check the branch-protection required-checks list BEFORE the rename and update it in the same change. Recording that precondition here so a future tick does not dispatch it casually into a live fleet.

.github/workflows/ is currently unheld by any worker, so (d) will be dispatchable the moment both live PRs land. It is small.
MAYOR TICK 2026-09-07 10:35 AUSEST — RULING (c) IS NOW IN FORCE IN DISPATCH BRIEFS, BUT ONLY THERE.

All three dispatches sent this tick (machines-a rf2-kuky.14/.16, registry-b rf2-kuky.30/.80,
egress-c rf2-kuky.5) carry this paragraph verbatim:

  "AND DO NOT PUT A COMPLIANCE STATEMENT IN THE PR BODY. ... A sentence like 'No
  Co-Authored-By: Claude and no Generated with [Claude Code] trailer' written at column 0
  in a PR body is itself refused by the CI attribution arm, which reds the PR — and that
  red CANNOT be cleared by editing the body, because the workflow reads the body from the
  frozen event payload. Say you declined the trailers in your REPORT TO ME instead."

WHAT THAT DOES AND DOES NOT DISCHARGE. It stops the bleeding for workers dispatched from
THIS session and no others: the instruction lives in the brief text I type, not in any
artefact a future mayor reads. That is exactly the failure mode this bead's own option (a)
was rejected for — prose discipline against a mechanical gate — one level up, applied to
the mayor instead of to the worker.

SO THE DURABLE HALF IS STILL OPEN and is what keeps this bead open: the ruling needs to
land in the artefact that briefs are built FROM. Candidates, unverified, for whoever takes
it: docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md (which every dispatch pastes blocks
out of) and CLAUDE.md > Git Conventions (which currently says "Say so in the report when
you decline them" — already correct about the REPORT, and silent about the PR BODY, which
is the gap a worker fills by writing the sentence in both places). Check both at source
before acting; neither is a finding.

(d) IS UNCHANGED AND STILL FENCED. The job rename is dispatchable only at fleet-zero with
no open PRs, and its brief must read the branch-protection required-checks list before the
rename and update it in the same change. At this tick there are six live workers and PRs
about to open, so (d) is not dispatchable. Re-test that fence rather than re-deriving it.
Merged-PR audit #9385 (3cdc33413c7270e46f4cd8a75bcd066b82bbd4b0, merged 2026-09-07T13:16:23Z). The original mid-sentence false positive is fixed and real trailer controls still fail. Reopening this exact owner because the new rule still refuses ordinary compliance prose, and its separately recorded (d) remains unfinished.

The detector comments/README/CLAUDE.md promise that rule 3 requires the line to end on the tool's own link. The implementation instead tests only the last SPACE-separated word for the substring claude or anthropic: case "${_rf2a_low##* }". Thus the ordinary column-zero compliance sentence "Generated with [Claude Code] was declined per CLAUDE.md." is REFUSED: its prefix before Generated has no letters and its final word CLAUDE.md. contains claude. title: story: the shell dispatches into Xray's :rf/xray frame directly, and races the seat at boot (residual 2 of rf2-avi7)
description:
tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/shell.cljs:406 hand-rolls (rf/with-frame :rf/xray (rf/dispatch-sync [:rf.xray/set-target-frame now])) — reaching into ANOTHER TOOL'S frame instead of calling Xray's host-facing facade day8.re-frame2-xray.core/set-target-frame!.

Two consequences.

(1) THE MEASURED ONE. rf2-avi7 (PR #9312) seats :rf/xray on substrate-adapter readiness, from the Xray preload's bounded 50ms poll. Measured on one tree carrying both #9312 and #9306, against the same tree with #9312 reverted: 97 :rf.error/frame-destroyed -> 2. The residual 2 fire at t=546.9ms and t=561.9ms on one page — inside the poll window, because Story's boot does rf/init! then mounts the shell and selects a variant before the next tick. Record (captured with a pr-str diagnostic planted in error_emit/report-unowned-error!, restored, blob cf828e0e6c167fd0d421c32de0e3b148f2b8e811 verified):
  {:error :rf.error/frame-destroyed :event :rf/redacted :event-id :rf.xray/set-target-frame :frame :rf/xray :source-coord {:ns day8.re-frame2-xray.epoch :line 108}}
No Xray-side change reaches this: the dispatch is Story's, and by the time the watcher fires rf/init! HAS run — so a facade call would seat successfully and land.

(2) THE STRUCTURAL ONE, which is the real point. A host is not supposed to know that :rf/xray is Xray's frame, nor that its lifecycle is tied to adapter readiness. Story already uses the facade for the sibling gesture (rf.story.xray-preset/on-variant-selected!, wire-cross-host!) and already has the ensure-before-dispatch pattern for its OWN frames (ensure-variant-frame!, rf2-zme7). This one call site is the exception.

PROPOSED (not ruled): (a) Story calls (xray-core/set-target-frame! now) in place of the with-frame + dispatch-sync; (b) Xray's core/set-target-frame! routes through mount/ensure-xray-frame! before dispatching, so the facade is correct at boot instant for EVERY host, not just Story. Both halves are one-liners. (b) alone does not fix Story; (a) alone leaves the facade wrong for the next host.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW: npm run test:story-feature-load is a per-PR gate (test.yml, story_full_gate) and PR #9306 turns it red by removing the Story shell's page-wide no-op :errors listener that was masking these. #9312 takes it from 101 console errors to 6; this bead is 2 of the remaining 6. The other 4 are a separate defect — see the sibling bead on :rf.error/drain-depth-exceeded.

_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from ssr.md (ref ssr.2); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

## Problem

`head-snapshot` is a side-channel register bolted onto a pure read. `render-head` returns the head model AND stashes it in a process-wide atom keyed by frame address (`implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/head/registry.cljc:36-51,172`); `head-snapshot` (`:53-59`) reads that atom back; `on-frame-destroyed!` (`:61-67`) clears it through a second late-bind hook, `:ssr/head-on-frame-destroyed` (`implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/head.cljc:71-89`), which `re-frame.ssr.request/on-frame-destroyed!` looks up by key and calls inside a try/catch that emits `:rf.ssr.head/cleanup-failed` (`implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/request.cljc:112-124`). The surface is advertised "for tests, introspection, and tools (Xray, MCP)" (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:862-869`, `spec/API.md:342`). Tools read it nowhere; no production code reads it; the atom exists so two test files can assert on it and two fixtures can reset it. The value a caller wants is already in its hands — it is what `render-head` returned.

## Evidence (verified at tip 6445d0611b, 2026-09-05)

- `git grep -n -F 'head-snapshot'` (outside the head ns) → `core.cljc:862-869`, `core_ssr.cljc:113-122`, `late_bind/directory.cljc:774-777,782-785` (+ `:753` description tail), `ssr.cljc:426-427` (comment), `request.cljc:12,97`; tests `implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr_head_test.clj:10,174-183,549-604`, `ssr_teardown_corner_test.clj:48-174`; fixtures `implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr/test_fixture.clj:11,35,85`, `implementation/ssr-ring/test/re_frame/ssr/ring/test_support.clj:58,80`; spec `spec/API.md:26,29,327,342,375`, `spec/011-SSR.md:729`, `spec/Runtime-Subsystems.md:151,325`; docs `docs/api/re-frame.core.md:1503-1507`, `docs/api/re-frame.ssr.md:16,566,691,729`; `skills/re-frame2/references/cross-cutting/api-cheatsheet.md:135`; manifest rows. `tools/`: 0. `examples/`, `testbeds/`: 0.
- `git grep -n -E 'head-on-frame-destroyed|rf\.ssr\.head/cleanup-failed'` → the producer/consumer above, `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2025` (catalogue row), tests `ssr_head_test.clj:714-770`, `ssr_teardown_corner_test.clj:180-221`.
- The 2026-09-04 façade sweep (rf2-2hpxo, PR #9217) classified the `re-frame.core` `head-snapshot` row `:action :keep` (`spec/api-manifest.edn:128`, `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn:1345-1347`). That classification argued the façade MECHANISM (late-bind re-export vs hard require); it did not find a consumer. This bead deletes the surface at its home too, so the façade question does not arise.

## Target API

None added. `render-head` / `active-head` keep returning the model; that return value is the only way to read a head. (Their consolidation into one `head` fn is @ssr.3's ruling — this bead does not touch their signatures.) `re-frame.ssr/on-frame-destroyed!` keeps clearing `pending-error-traces`, `request-slots`, `response-slots` and releasing the payload claim (`request.cljc:103-111`) — three side channels, not four.

## Corroboration

Two-reviewer on this slice: fable proposes the deletion; codex's cross-check adopts it after reading `registry.cljc` — "Its removal is justified by the absence of a consumer for that historical side channel" — with one factual correction to carry into the tests: the snapshot is `{head-id → last-model}` and may hold several heads, so it is NOT value-equal to the last `render-head` return; snapshot tests become tests of required rendering behaviour, not a mechanical comparison of differently shaped values. Codex also: "Do not delete unrelated request/error side-channel teardown with the head snapshot."

## Deletion list

- `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/head/registry.cljc`: `head-snapshots` (`:36-41`), `record-head-model!` (`:43-51`), `head-snapshot` (`:53-59`), `on-frame-destroyed!` (`:61-67`), the `record-head-model!` call in `render-head*` (`:172` — return the model directly), docstring lines `:16-19,:30-35,:193-195`.
- `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/head.cljc`: defs `:45-46` and `:47-51` (the `head-snapshots` re-export); hook `:64`; the whole teardown block `:71-89`; ns-docstring mentions.
- `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/request.cljc`: `:12`, `:95-101` (docstring), `:112-124` (head-cleanup call + `:rf.ssr.head/cleanup-failed` emission). Keep `:103-111`.
- `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr.cljc:425-430`: comment → the head hooks that remain (`:ssr/reg-head`, `:ssr/render-head`, `:ssr/active-head`, `:ssr/head-model-html`).
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:862-869` (`head-snapshot` def); `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_ssr.cljc:113-122` (wrapper).
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind/directory.cljc:774-777` (`:ssr/head-snapshot`), `:782-785` (`:ssr/head-on-frame-destroyed`), and the trailing sentence of `:753` ("Also invokes `:ssr/head-on-frame-destroyed` …").
- `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn:1345-1347` (the `["re-frame.core" "head-snapshot"]` row with its `:action`/`:justification`); regenerate `spec/api-manifest.edn` (row `:128` goes).
- Tests: `ssr_head_test.clj:549-604` (four deftests: `head-snapshot-cleared-on-frame-destroy`, `head-snapshot-isolated-across-frames`, `rf-head-snapshot-resolves`, `rf-head-snapshot-returns-per-frame-map`) and `:714-770` (hook-throws test) — delete; `:170-183` — re-express as "the second `render-head` call returns the second head's model" (behavioural, per codex); `ssr_teardown_corner_test.clj:180-221` (`on-frame-destroyed-tolerates-missing-head-hook`) — delete; `:45-91` → "clears all THREE side channels" (drop `:62-77` and `:89-91`); `:97-126`, `:132-174` — drop the snapshot assertions, keep request/response/error-trace ones. Fixtures: `test_fixture.clj:11,35,85`, `test_support.clj:58,80` — drop the `head-snapshots` reset.

## Consumers to migrate

None in app, tool or framework production code. Framework: `request.cljc` (above). Tests/fixtures: above.

## Spec, docs, examples, skills, tests

- `spec/API.md` (HOT ZONE): row `:342` deleted; `:29` namespace-table entry and `:327` list drop `head-snapshot`; `:375` "via `active-head` / `render-head` / `head-snapshot`" → the two; `:26` if it names it. **Fold the head-surface doc drift here, since the same lines are being edited**: `:327` says "the surfaces below live in `re-frame.ssr`" and `:29` lists `render-head`, `active-head`, `head-model->html` under `re-frame.ssr` — they live in `re-frame.ssr.head` (`head.cljc:39-44`; `ssr.cljc` carries no head def) and reach consumers through `re-frame.core`. Say so in both places.
- `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2025` (HOT ZONE): delete the `:rf.ssr.head/cleanup-failed` catalogue row — its only emitter goes with `request.cljc:115`, and the error-catalogue channel conformance test (`implementation/core/test/re_frame/error_catalogue_channel_conformance_test.clj`) would otherwise pin a row with no emitter.
- `spec/011-SSR.md:729` (teardown list "request, response, pending-error, and head-snapshot" → three); `spec/Runtime-Subsystems.md:151` ("chains `:ssr.head/on-frame-destroyed`") and `:325` ("head snapshots").
- Docs: `docs/api/re-frame.core.md:1503-1507` (section), `docs/api/re-frame.ssr.md:16` (list), `:566` (teardown description's head clause), `:691`, `:729`; `skills/re-frame2/references/cross-cutting/api-cheatsheet.md:135` (row).
- **Fold one more skills drift line here (same skills tree; no code bead will touch it)**: `skills/re-frame2/references/cross-cutting/ssr-authoring.md:158` says "Head rides the same `:rf/render-hash` channel as the body … any mismatch (head or body) emits `:rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch`". Per `spec/011-SSR.md:1262-1264,1284-1289` the head rides its OWN `:rf/head-hash` channel (rf2-1oxjxk), the body hash is body-only, and the bundled client never compares the head hash — so a head-only divergence is SILENT unless the host recomputes `active-head` and compares; `:rf.ssr/head-mismatch` stays host-suppliable via `:failing-id`. Rewrite the bullet to that. (rf2-ygimu, PR #9004, fixed four other claims in this file on 2026-09-02 and left this one.)
- Examples/testbeds: none reference it. Migration README: untouched (no v1-era name).
- Conformance corpus / mcp-conformance: unaffected — no fixture names `head-snapshot`; `spec/conformance/fixtures/ssr-head-emits.edn:38` / `ssr-head-hydration.edn:68` use `:ssr/active-head` as an EXPECT channel key, which stays.

## Sequencing and hot-zone

Touches `spec/API.md` and `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` → one-toucher; serialise behind any in-flight API.md / 009 PR, and @ssr.3's implementation beads (also API.md) go after this one. Shares `late_bind/directory.cljc` with @ssr.1 (different rows; merges cleanly, but not the same worktree). `implementation/ssr-ring/test/.../test_support.clj` is in the tree rf2-9guv edits (`node.clj`, `node_crossing_test.clj`) — different files.

## Risks

Low. The one behavioural edge is teardown: after removing the head clause, `re-frame.ssr/on-frame-destroyed!` MUST still clear `pending-error-traces`, `request-slots`, `response-slots` and release the payload claim — `ssr_teardown_corner_test.clj:45-91` pins that (re-titled to three channels). `ring_test.clj` does not `with-redefs` `head-snapshot` (only `rf/active-head` at `:2815,2866`), so ssr-ring tests are unaffected beyond the fixture reset.

ITEM 2 — ssr-authoring.md:158. THE PRIOR NOTE'S READING DOES NOT HOLD. That note offered, explicitly as a claim rather than a ruling, that the line was deliberate v1 documentation of a known limitation and needed no change, and instructed whoever took it to read the passage and record "no change needed, and why" if it was accurate at tip. Read at source. It is NOT accurate, and it is wrong on both of its load-bearing claims. THE BEAD'S OWN DESCRIPTION WAS RIGHT ALL ALONG — the folded drift line, citing spec/011-SSR.md, and the acceptance criterion that flowed from it.

The bullet claimed (i) head rides the body's :rf/render-hash channel, and (ii) that ANY mismatch, head or body, therefore emits :rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch. spec/011-SSR.md §Head/meta contract contradicts both in three separate places: "the head rides its OWN :rf/head-hash channel ... separate from the body's :rf/render-hash"; "The body channel (:rf/render-hash) is body-only"; and "folding head + body into one hash was reverted" — because the documented client boot hashes only the bare body render-tree, so a unified hash could never match the client's.

VERIFIED IN THE SHIPPED CODE, not only the spec, because a spec-only check would not settle it: render-head-hash, the payload's :rf/head-hash and the data-rf-head-hash wire attribute all exist in implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/{lifecycle,payload,pipeline,shell,streaming}.clj.

WHY THIS WAS WORTH FIXING RATHER THAN MINUTIAE — the two false halves fail in OPPOSITE directions, and the second is the dangerous one. The old text told a reader head drift at least SURFACES, misattributed as a body mismatch. In fact the body channel never sees it and the bundled v1 client never reads :rf/head-hash, so head drift is SILENT. A reader budgeting for a noisy-but-visible failure got the opposite of the truth. That is a correctness defect in a teaching surface, not a wording preference.

WHAT MADE THE CONTRARY READING PLAUSIBLE, recorded so it is not re-derived: the line already used :rf/render-hash, the name that SURVIVED #9316, and never mentioned head-snapshot, the thing #9316 deleted — so on the two tokens a #9316-residual check would reach for, it looked clean. Its staleness predates #9316 and belongs to rf2-1oxjxk (the reverted unified hash), which is why the earlier grep on head-snapshot and "head hash" found nothing. The audit's phrase "conflates head and body hashes" was exact.

The rewritten bullet states: the separate :rf/head-hash channel; that it hashes the canonical head MODEL rather than emitted <head> HTML; the silence; the host-side recompute via active-head that supplies :rf.ssr/head-mismatch through the generic :failing-id seam; and the omission of the channel for explicit-:head-string or degraded head resolution. What the old text got RIGHT is kept — :rf.ssr/head-mismatch is host-suppliable today and runtime-emitted only post-v1.

title: test(adapters/reagent): land the linearlite overlapping-writes regression the rf2-9man fence could not
description:
Follow-up to rf2-9man (PR #9197), which fixed examples/capabilities/resources/linearlite so the three writes commit at the granularity they wrote at (`:patches`, not whole-board `:populates`). The FIX is on main; what is missing is the DURABLE witness.

WHY IT IS NOT IN THAT PR. Examples are test-free by ruling (rf2-8cevm), so the witness cannot live under examples/. Its home is the adapter test tree — implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/linearlite_example_cljs_test.cljs, which already drives the example's real registrations behind the deterministic capturing `:rf.http/managed` stub. That tree was outside the rf2-9man worker's fence (concurrent work), so the two tests below were planted there, RUN, and removed. Measured on the pre-fix example both FAIL; on the post-fix example both PASS; the 11 pre-existing tests in that suite are green either way (13 tests / 61 assertions; captured exit 1 before, 0 after).

TASK: paste the two deftests at the end of that suite (they use its existing load-board! / reply-success! / issue-by-id / last-managed-args helpers verbatim, no new fixture), drop the TMP naming, and run `npm run test:cljs`.

TEST SOURCE (verbatim, as run):

;; OVERLAPPING WRITES (rf2-9man) — independent instances must not clobber
;; ============================================================================

(deftest tmp-repro-overlapping-writes-do-not-clobber
  (testing "TMP: two writes under distinct instances, settled in dispatch order"
    (load-board!)
    (rf/dispatch-sync [:linearlite/commit-edit "srv-1" "Alpha!"])
    (let [args-a @last-managed-args]
      (reset! last-managed-args nil)
      (rf/dispatch-sync [:linearlite/change-status "srv-2" :done])
      (let [args-b  @last-managed-args
            reply-a {:issues [{:id "srv-1" :title "Alpha!" :status :backlog}
                              {:id "srv-2" :title "Beta"   :status :in-progress}]}
            reply-b {:issues [{:id "srv-1" :title "Alpha!" :status :backlog}
                              {:id "srv-2" :title "Beta"   :status :done}]}]
        (is (some? args-a) "TMP-0a: A lowered a request")
        (is (some? args-b) "TMP-0b: B lowered a request")
        (reply-success! args-a reply-a)
        (is (= :done (:status (issue-by-id "srv-2")))
            "TMP-1: settling A must not erase B's still-pending optimistic move")
        (reply-success! args-b reply-b)
        (is (= "Alpha!" (:title (issue-by-id "srv-1"))) "TMP-2: A's accepted title survives")
        (is (= :done (:status (issue-by-id "srv-2"))) "TMP-3: B's accepted move survives")))))

(deftest tmp-repro-overlapping-writes-reverse-order
  (testing "TMP: replies arrive in the reverse of the order the server applied them"
    (load-board!)
    (rf/dispatch-sync [:linearlite/commit-edit "srv-1" "Alpha!"])
    (let [args-a @last-managed-args]
      (reset! last-managed-args nil)
      (rf/dispatch-sync [:linearlite/change-status "srv-2" :done])
      (let [args-b  @last-managed-args
            reply-a {:issues [{:id "srv-1" :title "Alpha!" :status :backlog}
                              {:id "srv-2" :title "Beta"   :status :in-progress}]}
            reply-b {:issues [{:id "srv-1" :title "Alpha!" :status :backlog}
                              {:id "srv-2" :title "Beta"   :status :done}]}]
        (reply-success! args-b reply-b)
        (reply-success! args-a reply-a)
        (is (= :done (:status (issue-by-id "srv-2")))
            "TMP-4: A's older snapshot landing last must not revert B's accepted move")
        (is (= "Alpha!" (:title (issue-by-id "srv-1"))) "TMP-5: A's accepted title survives")))))

1. implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/linearlite_example_cljs_test.cljs — `successful-write-commits-the-server-board-via-populates` still PASSES (its hand-built whole-board reply merges correctly through the new create patch) but the name and its testing-string now describe a consequence the example no longer uses. ## Post-merge audit of PR #9234 (2026-09-05)

The two landed tests are deterministic and do prove both the transient and permanent cross-instance clobber for one consequence. However, both use A = commit-edit and B = change-status, and only A's older whole-board reply is applied after B exists. Consequently they go red when edit-title's :patches is changed back to :populates, but remain green if change-status alone is changed back: B's newer whole-board snapshot already contains A. They likewise never overlap create-issue, whose temporary-row reconciliation is a distinct patch implementation.

Minimal repair: add compact data-driven/paired cases in which each of create-issue, edit-title, and change-status is the older stale writer while a different instance's later optimistic/accepted change must survive.
