REPAIR: the row now names the tracked vocabulary suite; the tracked egress-projection suite joins it so both of the tier's live guarantees are pinned; and an fs.existsSync guard inside the loop makes the whole class of fail-open loud (the file's own idiom, ~15 existing uses). The SECURITY_TIER_FILES block immediately below is the same bug found one tier over (rf2-qxg24). ONE-FILE under the one-toucher rule, on MEASURED evidence, not judgement: the classifier's full 29-key output is byte-identical for the phantom path, the tracked vocab path and the tracked egress path (diff exit 0 on both comparisons), so the change alters neither what the classifier outputs nor what the test pins about those outputs -- it corrects the test to match the script's existing unchanged behaviour, the PR #8664 case. report-changed-surfaces.sh deliberately untouched. GATE: mirror suite captured exit 0, 346 tests passed (345 before; the egress row adds one). SABOTAGE: planting the phantom back gives captured exit 1 naming the guard's message -- direct proof the fail-open is closed, since that same row was green before this change. Restore verified by git blob hash.

title: story-mcp specs contradict explain-variant raw-author-data policy
description:
Evidence
- The authoritative Story-MCP privacy table says `explain-variant`'s entire map, including every plan-resolved value slot, is static author data and ships raw (`tools/story-mcp/spec/002-Tool-Registry.md:158-168`, rf2-7k5mce).
- The very next paragraph at lines 169-172 still promises that a declared-sensitive value redacts whether it arrives through a live derived tree “or a plan-resolved arg.” That is no longer true for explain-variant.
- Runtime docs and API are internally consistent with the new policy (`tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/docs.cljc:365-383`, `spec/API.md:324-344`), and focused tests at `tools_test.clj:3514-3616` prove classified `:db-seed`, `:effective-args`, `:network`, sub-overrides, and step payloads ship raw.
- The document claimed as the single-sourced peer, `tools/story/spec/006-MCP-Surface.md:119-198`, still places explain-variant among live/value-bearing tools, says its plan-resolved slots path-project, excludes its resolved step values from static metadata, and implies an include-sensitive escape hatch. That contradicts both implementation and the Story-MCP table.

Impact
This is a safety-contract contradiction, not cosmetic wording: readers can believe classification marks protect authored values exposed through explain-variant when the intentional runtime behavior sends them raw and offers no `:include-sensitive` gate. The same section simultaneously states the opposite, so clients and reviews cannot infer the actual boundary.

Recommendation
Rewrite the stale paragraphs in both normative specs to consistently state the rf2-7k5mce policy: explain-variant is a no-run author-data projection; its whole map ships raw; it is excluded from the live-value scrub set and sensitive-read gate. Cross-check the remaining tool lists and examples against the four actual value-surfacing tools.

Risks / contracts
Do not silently reintroduce scrubbing as a documentation fix: raw author data is deliberate, matches get-variant/variant->edn and the human Explain panel, and is pinned by tests. If that policy itself is reconsidered, treat it as a separate security decision with migration and protocol review.
acceptance_criteria:
- `spec/002-Tool-Registry.md` contains no claim that explain-variant plan-resolved args redact.
- `tools/story/spec/006-MCP-Surface.md` classifies explain-variant consistently as wholly raw author metadata and removes it from live/value-bearing/gated tool sets.
- Both specs clearly warn that classification marks do not scrub authored registration values exposed by explain-variant.
- The four runtime-value tools and their sensitive-read gate remain accurately enumerated.
- Existing explain-variant raw-value tests and Story-MCP test suite pass unchanged in semantics.
close_reason: PR #9089. Contradiction resolved in favour of the SHIPPED CODE: tool-explain-variant wraps story/explain in result/edn-result and reaches no egress projector; spec/API.md and three pinned tests agree; the Story-MCP privacy table already stated the rf2-7k5mce policy. Rewrote the stale prose on both sides. tools/story-mcp/spec/002-Tool-Registry.md no longer claims plan-resolved args redact and now states plainly that classification marks do not reach author metadata (keep secrets out of a variant's registration). tools/story/spec/006-MCP-Surface.md removes explain-variant from the live-state and value-bearing sets, moves its ENTIRE explain map into the author-published static class, and marks the rf2-q8ebq.1 setup-order/script-order carve-out retired. The four runtime-value tools and the --allow-sensitive-reads gate remain accurately enumerated. No scrubbing reintroduced; explain-variant tests unchanged in semantics and green.

title: Stop Story-host DOM tests leaking hashchange listeners across cases
description:
Evidence:
- tools/testbed-support/test/re_frame/testbed/story_host_dom_cljs_test.cljs runs two tests against the real browser window.
- Each mount leaves the installed hashchange function in host/hash-listener* and registered on js/window, as production is designed to do.
- The :after fixture unmounts React roots, then reset-host-handles! resets host/hash-listener* to nil without calling removeEventListener. That discards the only exact function identity able to unregister the listener.
- The next :before repeats the reset, so the second test's mount cannot remove the first test's listener; it registers another. The final fixture similarly leaves listeners on the shared browser page.
- The fake-window Node suite does not expose this because clear-window! discards the entire fake window/Set between tests.

Impact:
The suite named no-listener-or-root-leak itself leaks real hashchange listeners between tests and into later browser namespaces. Later hash changes can invoke stale host code against a removed #app node, creating order-dependent failures; the current assertions inspect only the stored handle, not the real window registry, so they remain green.

Recommendation:
Add teardown that removes the exact recorded host/hash-listener* from js/window before resetting the atom. Add a browser-visible assertion/probe proving one test leaves no registered host listener (or otherwise prove balanced add/remove) so the cleanup cannot regress silently.

Risks/contracts:
Remove only the listener owned by the host using its recorded identity. Do not blanket-replace window handlers or weaken the production defonce/hot-reload behavior. Keep Node fake-window cleanup valid.

Acceptance:
- DOM-test teardown unregisters the recorded hashchange listener before discarding its handle.
- A regression that resets the handle without unregistering makes the browser suite red.
- Both Story-host tests can run repeatedly/in either order without accumulating listeners; browser and focused Node gates pass.
acceptance_criteria: Unregister the exact recorded host hashchange listener before fixture state is reset, add non-vacuous browser coverage for balanced listener ownership, and keep production hot-reload plus Node fake-window contracts passing.
close_reason: PR #9089. Premise held exactly as described: the DOM fixture nilled host/hash-listener* without removeEventListener, so the next mount's remove-then-add became add-only and stacked a second listener on the shared page. Fix: reset-host-handles! now unregisters the EXACT recorded listener from js/window before discarding the handle (stored identity only; no blanket handler replacement; production defonce/hot-reload untouched; Node fake-window cleanup unchanged). Added fixture-teardown-leaves-no-hashchange-listener-on-the-page, which wraps js/window's listener API for one mount+teardown cycle, asserts the census saw exactly one add (non-vacuity) and that the cycle nets to zero - so a reset-without-unregister regression makes the browser suite red. SCOPE NOTE: the file is tools/testbed-support/test/, outside this dispatch's fence; the change is confined to that one test file and is flagged in the PR body. Verified locally with the focused node build (npm run test:testbed-support): 684 files, 0 warnings, 17 tests / 63 assertions, exit 0 - the new test's body gates on (browser?) and no-ops there. The :browser-test gate that runs the real-DOM assertion was NOT run locally (needs a full browser-test compile plus Chromium); CI owns it.

title: ssr-node latency envelope ignores the runtime partition
description:
## Evidence

- The pre-registered condition in implementation/ssr-node/src/envelope.cjs:40 and the ENVELOPE property at :71-72 bound only state EDN text to 64 KiB.
- The measured request in test/envelope.test.cjs:67-79 contains no runtime partition and computes only the byte lengths of two state values. It omits key bytes as well.
- Runtime became a second cloned request partition in crossing commit 9a42302f7a. Current protocol.cjs:329-373 counts every UTF-8 key and value per partition, and :458-468 enforces one combined state.bytes + runtime.bytes ceiling.
- The runtime-partition change did not touch envelope.cjs or envelope.test.cjs; git log --follow shows the registration still comes solely from f39829caa6.
- As written, the claimed condition admits any runtime payload below the separate body/protocol ceiling, while the witness measures none of it. The test therefore does not falsify the published envelope over the request domain the prose now describes.
- No existing bead found by ssr-node, runtime-partition, state-budget, or envelope searches owns this drift; rf2-8arzr.3 added the combined protocol ceiling but explicitly left the latency witness outside its fence.

## Impact

The pre-registered latency promise can be read as covering a runtime-heavy request that its only witness never measures. The test also uses a byte definition different from the validator it is meant to condition, making its green verdict weaker than the stated contract.

## Disposition

Amend or version the registration without refitting the p50/p95/max ceilings: define the 64 KiB condition over state and runtime together, rename stateBudgetBytes accordingly, and have the witness send non-empty data in both partitions. Count UTF-8 key plus value bytes with the same semantics as validatePartition. Record the amendment explicitly so the original pre-measurement provenance remains auditable.

## Risks

Do not silently rewrite history or tune ceilings after measurement. The latency numbers and sample count were pre-registered and must remain unchanged unless a separately preregistered successor envelope is introduced. The reference entry allowlists constrain which runtime key can be used.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The registration and README describe one explicit 64 KiB condition over state plus runtime, while preserving the existing latency ceilings and sample count.
2. The measured request contains non-empty allowlisted state and runtime partitions.
3. The witness byte calculation includes every UTF-8 key and value and matches protocol.cjs semantics.
4. A runtime-heavy controlled request that exceeds the combined condition is rejected by the witness precondition rather than counted as an eligible sample.
5. git history or an explicit amendment note continues to distinguish the original preregistration from this contract repair.
6. The ssr-node suite is green, including the envelope row.
close_reason:
Confirmed and fixed in PR #9078. Every element of the premise held at my tip: src/envelope.cjs bounded only state EDN text to 64 KiB (condition at the header, ENVELOPE.stateBudgetBytes); test/envelope.test.cjs's measured request carried no runtime partition and summed the byte lengths of two state VALUES, omitting every key as the bead says; and src/protocol.cjs's validatePartition counts Buffer.byteLength(key) + Buffer.byteLength(value) per partition and enforces ONE combined state.bytes + runtime.bytes ceiling.

ONE CLARIFICATION ON THE CEILING, since the two numbers differ and the difference is not a disagreement: protocol.cjs's ceiling is maxRequestBytes, default 1 << 20 = 1 MiB, a REFUSAL ceiling; the envelope's 64 KiB is a narrower pre-registered SAMPLING CONDITION under which the latency figures are claimed. Two layers, and both are kept. What they must share is how a byte is counted, and now do.

REPAIR (AC1-AC3): stateBudgetBytes -> requestBudgetBytes, same 64 KiB, restated over state + runtime together; a new exported requestBytes() counts keys and values across PARTITIONS read from protocol.cjs rather than naming the two fields locally, so a third partition cannot be added to the wire and leave the condition measuring two of three — which is exactly how this drift happened; the measured request now carries a non-empty allowlisted runtime partition (:rf.runtime/routing, the only key app/root's runtimeAllowlist permits) and is asserted inside the budget as a PRECONDITION before any sample is taken. README's condition row and a new paragraph say the same thing. Zero residual references to stateBudgetBytes repo-wide.

AC3 is pinned rather than asserted in prose: a new row admits a request at maxRequestBytes exactly N and requires validateRequest to REFUSE it at N-1, which is only true if requestBytes and validatePartition agree key for key.

AC4 PROVEN, and the false-green is MEASURED rather than argued. Permanent control row: a request busting the condition on runtime alone is over budget by requestBytes while validateRequest still accepts it — so the row is about the envelope's condition, not the protocol ceiling. Plant on the measured row (single-line anchor, match count 1 read first): runtime oversized to 70000 bytes gives 'AssertionError: the sample request must sit inside the registered 65536-byte budget; it is 70155 bytes', captured exit 1, 5 pass / 1 fail. On that SAME request the pre-repair formula computes 124 bytes and admits it — 124 vs 70155 is the size of the false green. Restore verified by git blob hash (cdee2d42bd94950c818118c2af886da811c3ddb1), not by reading a diff.

AC5: no ceiling and no sample count moved — p50 5 ms, p95 25 ms, max 250 ms, 200 samples are the values registered in f39829caa6, and an explicit AMENDMENT block in src/envelope.cjs records what was corrected (the condition's DOMAIN) and what was not (every number), keeping git log --follow provenance readable. Measured overhead with the runtime partition added: p50 0.18 ms, p95 0.28 ms, max 1.59 ms — well inside the untouched ceilings.

AC6: 9 suites green, 107 tests, 107 pass, 0 fail, captured exit 0 on the final rebased base; envelope.test.cjs 4 rows -> 6.

title: api-manifest roster gate can be orphaned again because its tests bypass build-manifest
notes:
FOUND BY SLICE F (rf2-8arzr.6), 2026-09-02, at base de3f2a00038. The manifest gate is GREEN and still misses three public namespaces, because the gate only checks what its own hard-coded roster names.

MEASURED: `cd implementation/scripts/api-manifest && clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.gen --check` exits 0, "spec/api-manifest.edn in sync (494 public vars)". Note the manifest lives at spec/api-manifest.edn and spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn -- NOT implementation/api-manifest.edn, which is where rf2-8arzr.6 s own scope text and several briefs point. That path does not exist.

THE THREE NAMESPACES, all with genuinely public vars and ZERO ^:no-doc markers:
- re-frame.ssr.ring.node (implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/node.clj) -- default-endpoint :128, default-timeout-ms :133, default-admission-ms :138, wire-margin-ms :145, validate-opts! :193, http-timeout-ms :230, renderer :360.
- re-frame.ssr.render-state (implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/render_state.cljc) -- validate-policy-opts! :175, project :333, serialize :365, deserialize :383, restore! :400.
- re-frame.hicasso.server (implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/server.cljs) -- payload-script :89, document :106, render :145, render-body :331.
grep for ssr\.ring\.node / render-state / hicasso\.server / render-body across BOTH manifest files returns zero hits each.

ROOT CAUSE: implementation/scripts/api-manifest/src/re_frame/api_manifest/gen.clj:88-119 defines `jvm-namespaces` as a literal list. It names re-frame.ssr (:103) and re-frame.ssr.ring (:104) but not re-frame.ssr.ring.node and not re-frame.ssr.render-state. `all-jvm-vars` (:202-213) iterates that literal list plus `extra-vars` (:121-130, two entries). re-frame.hicasso.server is CLJS-only and would need a :cljs-only sidecar row in spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn (:63); the roster there holds only the 16 day8.re-frame2-xray.* namespaces, re-frame.adapter.reagent, re-frame.adapter.uix, re-frame.core and re-frame.hicasso.

THE BACKSTOP IS DEAD, AND ITS OWN DOCSTRING SAYS WHY THAT MATTERS. gen.clj:141-162 defines `namespaces-under`, documented as "a completeness gate that quietly finds nothing is the defect it exists to prevent". A repo-wide grep for `namespaces-under` across .clj/.cljc/.cljs returns exactly ONE hit: its own definition at gen.clj:141. It is never called. implementation/scripts/api-manifest/test/ is empty. So a new public namespace joins the tree and nothing notices -- which is exactly what happened three times over across slices A, C and E.

WHY SLICE F DID NOT FIX IT: F was fenced to docs and manifests with an explicit "nothing under implementation/*/src/, this is not a code slice" instruction. Fixing this needs (a) a gen.clj roster change, (b) tier/owner/status classification judgement for ~16 vars, (c) a :cljs-only block for re-frame.hicasso.server, and (d) wiring namespaces-under so it cannot regress. That is a code slice with real judgement in it, and it touches a REQUIRED CI check (lint.yml job `api-manifest`, declared :592, aggregated at :786).

ALSO NOTE, for whoever takes this: spec/API.md CANNOT gain var-rows for these symbols until the manifest carries them. api_md_check.clj validates that every var-row in spec/API.md resolves to a manifest entry, so adding a row first would RED the required check. Slice F therefore recorded the three namespaces as PROSE in spec/API.md s SSR namespace note and said they are not yet manifested, citing this bead. When this lands, promote that prose to rows if the tiering warrants it.

TIERING HINT (not a ruling): all nine re-frame.ssr.ring vars are :implementation tier (spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn:1418-1426), and docs/api/ coverage is only gated for :front-porch / :advanced / :adapter / :testing tiers (doc_api_check.clj `check-coverage!`), so classifying these as :implementation would add no docs/api obligation.
RESOLVED BY PR #9040, 2026-09-03. The premise held and the cause was more specific than 'nobody wired it'.

VERIFIED AT SOURCE: git grep -F namespaces-under over .clj/.cljc/.cljs returns exactly ONE hit, its own definition at gen.clj:141. Controlled against all-jvm-vars — a same-shaped hyphenated symbol in the same file — which returns three hits including two call sites, so the instrument works and the one-hit result is real.

ROOT CAUSE, which the bead did not have: the gate is not new. rf2-o8xev (c504e47d11) built exactly this three-way reconciliation over implementation/freehand/src, asserted FIRST in build-manifest, with a 201-line test. The freehand retirement (rf2-0yp7w.6, c951808b47) deleted the tree and — correctly, since the gate refuses to build when a source namespace is named by neither roster — retired the rosters, the assertion AND its call site together; its own commit message says they 'retire together'. What survived was namespaces-under and source-file->ns-sym: two pure helpers with no caller. THE GATE WAS ORPHANED, NOT FORGOTTEN, which is worse, because an orphan reads like a live backstop to anyone grepping for one.

WIRED, data-driven rather than hardcoded to one tree: roster-covered-roots names the trees; a namespace is accounted for by one of THREE rosters (jvm-namespaces, a sidecar :cljs-only row, or internal-namespaces); roster-drift reports :unaccounted/:stale/:contradictory; assert-roster-complete! throws naming the namespace and both remediation paths; build-manifest calls it FIRST. Enrolment intersects jvm-namespaces with what is on disk rather than filtering by prefix — the two SSR trees share the re-frame.ssr prefix across different artefacts, so a prefix filter would mis-assign both.

ENROLLED: re-frame.ssr.render-state (5 public vars) and re-frame.ssr.ring.node (7), exactly the vars and line numbers this bead names, verified at tip. Both :tier :implementation :owner 011 :status v1 — the tiering spec/API.md:328 already states. The tiering hint was VERIFIED rather than trusted: doc_api_check.clj:148 gates docs coverage on #{:front-porch :advanced :adapter :testing}, so :implementation adds no docs/api obligation. Manifest 494 -> 506.

33 SSR namespaces recorded internal; all 37 across the two trees now classified. NO ^:no-doc was added anywhere — those trees contain zero no-doc markers of any kind, before or after.

DELIBERATE RED: before, exit 0 'in sync (494 public vars)'. Planted a new public namespace re-frame.ssr.roster-probe under a covered root: exit 2, failing BY NAME with both remediation paths. Restored, verified by git blob hash 59dd06f93953ed0306ac35bfb75e7b585481a029 equal to the committed object. 14 tests pin all three drift directions, the throw, the failure MESSAGE (it must name both remediation paths, so the reader is not sent to the nearest silencer) and the LIVE trees — the last is what fails if the gate is ever orphaned again. Suite 74 -> 88 tests.

TWO OF THIS BEAD'S OWN PREMISES DID NOT HOLD, corrected here: (1) 'implementation/scripts/api-manifest/test/ is empty' — it is not, six tracked test files including gen_test.clj; the new one is a seventh. (2) The spec/api-manifest.edn path correction the bead makes IS right; implementation/api-manifest.edn indeed does not exist.

NOT DONE, and each has a bead: re-frame.hicasso.server is still unscanned (rf2-3ne8) — implementation/hicasso/** was held by PR #9035 during this work, and it is CLJS-only so it needs a :cljs-only row, not a jvm-namespaces entry; the gate's third arm is already built and tested for it. spec/API.md:328's 'not yet carried by the manifest' clause goes stale on merge (rf2-63fw, post-merge only). And 243 namespaces remain under trees the gate does not cover (rf2-qvhx) — measured 276 unenrolled in total, this PR covering 33.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #9040 (three-lens review).

CORRECTNESS. The landed mechanism is currently wired correctly: build-manifest calls assert-roster-complete! first, both JVM crossing namespaces resolve and contribute the expected 5 + 7 rows, and the two documentation repairs describe the live code. No runtime defect was found in the reconciliation itself.

COMPLETENESS / REGRESSION GAP. The original defect was specifically an implemented namespaces-under helper whose production call had disappeared. The new 14-test roster_completeness_test.clj suite does not call build-manifest at all. Its live-rosters-account-for-the-live-trees test says it covers the assertion build-manifest makes, but invokes roster-drift directly. The only build-manifest calls anywhere under the test tree are pre-existing duplicate-row and implementation-facade tests in gen_test.clj; they exercise later failures and cannot observe removal of the roster assertion. Thus deleting gen.clj's single line 575 call recreates the orphan while the dedicated suite remains green. The author's planted-source demonstration proves the present call works, but it is not a durable regression test.

IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY / MINIMAL FIX. Add one behavioral integration test that redefines covered-source-namespaces to include a synthetic unaccounted namespace, invokes build-manifest with the live sidecar, and requires the named roster exception. With the production call removed, that test must fail because manifest generation succeeds. This is one compact test; no new checker or abstraction is needed.
close_reason:
PR #9045. The audit's finding held at source: build-manifest calls assert-roster-complete! first (gen.clj:575), but all 14 tests drove roster-drift/assert-roster-complete! DIRECTLY — live-rosters-account-for-the-live-trees claims to cover the build-manifest assertion while invoking roster-drift itself. The only build-manifest calls under test/ were gen_test.clj's duplicate-row and implementation-facade rows.

FIX: three tests driving the PRODUCTION entry point — the named refusal, its :unaccounted ex-data, and the ordering against the duplicate-row check (a sidecar broken both ways must surface the ROSTER refusal). Each redefines covered-source-namespaces to report one synthetic unaccounted namespace and requires build-manifest to throw. No new checker, no abstraction, as specified.

TWO-STATE PROOF: suite 88 tests/184 assertions -> 91/189, exit 0. With the line-575 call deleted, exactly the three new tests fail (captured exit 1) and THE PRE-EXISTING 88 STAY GREEN — the audit's claim measured rather than argued. Restored, verified by git blob hash 59dd06f93953ed0306ac35bfb75e7b585481a029 equal to the committed object.

title: method reread: inverse-correction test does not test whether the replacement is established
description: PR #8931 adds one advertised discharging question: would the evidence that falsified the old claim also falsify the new one? Applied to its own frozen-clock example, completion alive falsifies dormant but does not falsify about-to-report, so the written test lets the unsupported inverse pass. The next sentence reaches the right conclusion only by switching to a different discriminator: a stopped worker produces the same frozen reading, so the observation establishes neither state. The rule therefore does not operationalize the failure it was added to catch.
acceptance_criteria: Replace the question with a concise test that distinguishes merely refuting the old claim from positively establishing its replacement, and make both named examples fail that test for the stated reason. Preserve the corrected worker outcomes, ambiguity guidance, and asymmetric-cost wait rule; add no new mechanism.
notes: AUDIT PR #8931: completeness — the new rule does not catch its own two motivating overshoots; correctness — non-falsification of a replacement is not evidence establishing it; implementation quality — the bold test and its immediate explanation use different criteria. Minimal prose repair only.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #8962, verified on main at commit 2a018d54fd. The discharging test in loops.md §6 now asks what you would expect to SEE that is different if the new claim were false, and both named examples fail it explicitly - the frozen clock (identical reading from a stopped run and one about to report) and the containment scan (identical output whether it is right usually or rarely, so 'settles the common case' rests on an unmeasured frequency). Ambiguity guidance and the asymmetric-cost wait rule preserved verbatim; no new mechanism added, per the acceptance criteria.

title: patterns/websocket: clean disconnect strands every in-flight request
description:
## Scope

Fix the canonical runnable WebSocket pattern's clean-disconnect path in examples/patterns/websocket/connection.cljs and cover it in the external behavior wrapper implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/websocket_cljs_test.cljs. Keep the existing machine topology, request/reply API, socket-epoch guard, queue/reconnect behavior, and test-free-example policy.

## Correctness finding

A clean :ws/disconnect destroys the live socket actor but neither clears nor fails requests already stored in :in-flight. Their scheduled timeouts are stamped with the destroyed socket id, so :current-socket? rejects those timeouts after teardown. The slot and its waiting :reply callback can therefore survive forever, including across a later reconnect.

The unexpected-drop path already handles exactly this invariant through :on-socket-lost; clean disconnect bypasses that action.

## Evidence

- examples/patterns/websocket/connection.cljs:174-201 documents and implements the required loss behavior: clear all :in-flight slots and dispatch each waiting reply event with {:ok false :error :ws/connection-lost}. Its own comment explains that the old socket id makes a later timeout fail :current-socket?, otherwise leaking the slot forever.
- connection.cljs:271-293 registers each request in :in-flight and schedules :ws/request-timeout with the current :source-socket-id; lines 404-412 guard that timeout with :current-socket?.
- connection.cljs:356-364 routes unexpected :ws/closed through :on-socket-lost, but routes :ws/disconnect directly to :disconnected with no cleanup action.
- examples/patterns/websocket/messages.cljs:179-191 deliberately emits no :closed event while the actor is being destroyed, and lines 278-290 repeat that teardown must not redispatch into the dying actor. Therefore no later close event accidentally repairs the omission.
- examples/patterns/websocket/views.cljs:102-105 exposes this path as the runnable "Disconnect (clean)" button.
- implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/websocket_cljs_test.cljs:507-522 checks clean disconnect only for state/tags/socket teardown. It creates no request and never inspects :in-flight or a callback.
- The same wrapper's drop-fails-in-flight-request-test at lines 609-646 proves the intended behavior for an unexpected drop using a :silent-no-echo request: the slot clears and the callback receives an explicit failure. timeout-fails-in-flight-request-test separately proves the still-live-socket deadline path.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start the WebSocket example in a fresh frame and connect to the mock transport.
2. Dispatch a :ws/request whose body is {:type :silent-no-echo}, with a unique request id, a reply event, and a finite timeout. Confirm its id is present under [:data :in-flight].
3. Before the timeout, dispatch [:ws/disconnect].
4. Inspect the connection snapshot and reply-event observations. The machine is :disconnected and its actor id is gone, but the request id remains in :in-flight and no failure reaches the reply event.
5. Deliver the already-scheduled :ws/request-timeout carrying the former socket id. The :current-socket? guard rejects it because there is no live socket; the slot and callback remain stranded.
6. As a control, use the existing unexpected-drop path for the same request; it clears the slot and fires the failure callback.

## Expected Behavior

Once a request is accepted into :in-flight, it reaches exactly one explicit terminal outcome: a reply, a live-socket timeout, or a connection-termination failure. Leaving :active through clean disconnect must clear every on-wire request and notify every registered reply event exactly once.

## Actual Behavior

Clean disconnect terminates the only socket capable of replying while retaining all on-wire request records. The epoch guard then suppresses their timeout cleanup, so callers can hang indefinitely and a later reconnect inherits stale bookkeeping.

## Failure scenario / invariant

A user starts an RPC-like request over a real WebSocket and clicks the example's clean Disconnect control, or application code cleanly disconnects during navigation/logout. The transport closes successfully, but UI work awaiting the registered reply receives neither success nor failure. Reconnecting does not resolve it, and the stale :in-flight entry is permanent.

Invariant: destroying/replacing the socket that carried an on-wire request must settle that request exactly once and remove its correlation slot. Epoch rejection may prevent stale events from touching a new socket, but must not suppress the only cleanup path for the old one.

## Recommended minimal fix

Factor the existing "fail and clear every in-flight request" part of :on-socket-lost into one small action/helper. Use it both for guarded unexpected :ws/closed (alongside the retry increment) and for :ws/disconnect while leaving :active. Reuse the established explicit :ws/connection-lost result unless the example deliberately documents a distinct clean-disconnect error. Do not synthesize a socket :closed event during actor teardown.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Extend the external WebSocket wrapper with a deterministic :silent-no-echo request, assert the request is genuinely present in :in-flight, then dispatch clean :ws/disconnect.
2. After disconnect, assert :disconnected, no live socket actor id, an empty :in-flight map, and exactly one reply-event invocation naming the request id with :ok false and the documented connection-termination error.
3. Deliver or advance the old socket-stamped timeout after disconnect and assert the callback count remains exactly one and no request slot/state is resurrected. This is the at-most-once control.
4. A positive control proves the same silent request remains in flight before either disconnect or timeout; removing the clean-disconnect cleanup action makes the new test fail on both the retained id and missing callback, so the witness cannot pass vacuously.
5. Existing unexpected-drop, live-timeout, reconnect/epoch, queue, correlation, subscription, and actor-teardown tests remain green.
6. npm run test:cljs and npm run test:examples-compile pass.

## Non-goals

- A managed WebSocket facility, generalized request-cancellation API, or protocol framework.
- Replaying on-wire requests after reconnect; the current at-most-once fail-not-replay policy remains.
- Changing reconnect backoff, offline queueing, subscriptions, credential handling, inbound schema policy, or the socket actor topology.
- Adding tests inside examples/; behavior remains owned by the external wrapper.
- Broad edits to the WebSocket spec/skill or to the other pattern examples.

## Related / duplicate search

Fresh all-status title, description, and notes searches covered websocket, socket, disconnect, clean disconnect, manual disconnect, ws/disconnect, in-flight, in-flight request, connection-lost, request timeout, callback, strands, and flight. No bead owns this clean-disconnect request leak.

rf2-iyjae is adjacent but distinct: it corrects credential and inbound-frame trust boundaries and explicitly makes connection topology, correlation, timeout, and loss semantics non-goals. The existing source comments reference historical request-drop and timeout fixes (rf2-r1rkvb, rf2-vqg8l6), but those ids are not present in the current tracker and their implemented paths do not cover clean :ws/disconnect.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #8839 (worker/ws-disconnect-b2jpr, d953d7e28e). Clean :ws/disconnect out of :active now settles every in-flight request exactly once: the fail-and-clear half of :on-socket-lost was factored into a fail-in-flight helper in examples/patterns/websocket/connection.cljs, used by both the guarded :ws/closed door (with the retry bump) and the :ws/disconnect door (without it). Topology, request/reply API, epoch guard, queue/reconnect behavior unchanged. Reply-error decision: reuse :ws/connection-lost, NOT a distinct value — the published contract (spec/Pattern-WebSocket.md §5 + pitfalls, example README) documents exactly that value for connection termination, and schema.cljs's LocalRequestFailure is a deliberately closed enum of :ws/connection-lost/:ws/timeout enforced at the release-resident RequestOutcome boundary; a distinct value would widen a closed contract for no caller benefit. Spec needed no edit (its listing omits :ws/disconnect entirely). Coverage: new wrapper deftest websocket-clean-disconnect-fails-in-flight-request (external wrapper per test-free-examples) — silent-no-echo request parked in-flight (positive control), clean disconnect -> slot cleared + exactly ONE reply with the documented body via a counting reply target forwarding through the boundary-validated :ws.app/request-reply, stale destroyed-socket timeout delivered post-disconnect AND post-reconnect resurrects nothing (at-most-once + no-leak-across-reconnect controls). Gates (local, exits captured): npm run test:cljs split compile exit 0 (1862 files, 0 warnings) + run exit 0 (11113 tests / 54529 assertions, 0 failures 0 errors); npm run test:examples-compile exit 0 (:examples/websocket compiled fresh in-run). Control: with the one-line :action :fail-in-flight routing reverted, run exit 1 with 7 failures ALL in the new test, red on both the retained slot and the missing callback; restore verified by git blob hash == HEAD object d35690f1cd, then recompile exit 0 + rerun exit 0. Follow-up filed: rf2-ni0ko (:ws/fatal door, same class, reachable only by consumer code).

title: bug(pair-mcp): CWD port discovery strands the session after an ephemeral-port restart
description:
## Scope

Repair restart recovery for the documented step-5 CWD-relative nREPL port discovery in `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/**`. The coherent surface is the discovery result in `src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/nrepl.cljs`, its consumption by `server.cljs`, focused discovery/port-stability tests, and the transport README/spec wording that currently says this branch cannot retain a stable file identity.

## Correctness finding

The CWD fallback successfully reads one of three concrete port files, but returns only `{:port n}` and deliberately drops the winning filename. `discover-and-cache!` therefore stores `:port-file nil`; `ensure-connection!` only re-reads a cached endpoint when `:port-file` is non-nil. If the fallback's nREPL restarts on a new ephemeral port, every later tool call keeps the old endpoint and can only reconnect to that old port. The MCP session cannot discover the new port until the whole MCP server is restarted or the operator changes launch configuration.

The stated reason for dropping the path is incorrect: a relative candidate read against Node's process CWD has a stable, unambiguous absolute identity via `node:path.resolve` (or by joining it to `process.cwd()`). No project-home inference is needed.

This is P2: it makes a shipped, documented fallback permanently non-self-healing after a routine dynamic-port restart and turns subsequent app-facing tools into repeated transport failures, but it does not corrupt application state.

## Evidence

- `src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/nrepl.cljs:256-260` implements step 5 as `{:port (some read-port-file port-file-candidates)}`. It loses which candidate succeeded and returns no `:port-file`.
- The same file's `read-port-at-base` already returns `{:port ... :port-file ...}` for a winning candidate, and its comments explain why exact candidate identity is required for restart detection.
- `src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/server.cljs:278-297` caches the discovery result. With no project-home and no returned port-file, the CWD branch necessarily caches `:port-file nil`.
- `src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/server.cljs:426-438` re-reads only `(when port-file ...)`; a nil file takes the cached-connection path. The port-change and vanished-file recovery branches at lines 440 onward are consequently unreachable for CWD discovery.
- `test/re_frame2_pair_mcp/nrepl_test.cljs:827-843` positively asserts that the CWD result has a nil `:port-file`, so the current suite freezes the defect instead of exercising restart recovery.
- `spec/002-nREPL-Transport.md:87-104` specifies per-tool-call exact-file re-read but explicitly exempts the CWD fallback because it claims there is no stable path. `README.md:132-144` documents this fallback for environments without the Shadow HTTP path.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Use an MCP client with no usable roots and make the Shadow HTTP probe unavailable; launch the MCP server with the app project as its CWD.
2. Put P1 in one standard relative port file, such as `.nrepl-port`, and make an app-facing tool call. Step 5 attaches successfully to P1.
3. Restart the app nREPL on a different ephemeral port P2 and rewrite the same file; leave P1 closed.
4. Make another app-facing tool call. It retains the connection object bound to P1 rather than reading P2. Repeated calls still target P1; only restarting/reconfiguring the MCP server recovers.

## Failure scenario / invariant

A file-backed endpoint change must be observed before every app-facing call. Every discovery branch that obtains its port by reading a file must retain the exact winning file identity, so a change replaces the old connection and a disappearance triggers rediscovery. The CWD branch violates that invariant solely because it throws away the filename it just read.

## Recommended minimal fix

Make the step-5 scan return both the port and the exact winning candidate resolved against the process CWD. Reuse the existing file-backed result shape and the existing `ensure-connection!` replacement/disappearance branches; do not add a watcher, polling service, extra reconnect state machine, project-root inference, or new public option. Update the test and prose that currently encode the false no-stable-path premise.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A focused `discover-port*` test with roots unsupported and the HTTP probe unavailable proves the CWD fallback returns the successful port and an absolute `:port-file` for the exact candidate that supplied it; an earlier missing candidate must not be reported as the winner.
2. A focused server test seeds a session from that CWD discovery shape, changes the injected file read from P1 to P2, calls `ensure-connection!`, and proves the P1 connection is closed exactly once and the returned authoritative connection targets P2 without rerunning the full discovery cascade.
3. A vanished-file test proves the same CWD-derived cache enters the existing rediscovery path rather than silently reusing P1.
4. Non-vacuity: the new P1-to-P2 witness is demonstrated to fail when the CWD discovery result's `:port-file` is removed (the pre-fix behavior), and pass with the repair. Report that red/green control in the PR.
5. Control: env-var discovery remains a fixed endpoint with no invented file identity, while explicit-file, roots, and HTTP precedence/result behavior remains green. No candidate is re-read twice merely to reconstruct its identity.
6. `cd tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp && npm test` passes, including the focused discovery and port-file-stability namespaces; the relevant transport README/spec statements describe CWD fallback as file-backed and restart-aware.

## Non-goals

- No filesystem watcher, port-range probing, Shadow process monitor, background retry loop, or generic connection-lifecycle rewrite.
- No change to discovery precedence, roots elicitation, HTTP probing, explicit `--port-file`, or `SHADOW_CLJS_NREPL_PORT` semantics.
- No compatibility alias, migration ceremony, new flag, public tool, or additional project-home heuristic.
- No broad cleanup of port parsing or unrelated socket timeout/error handling.

## Related / duplicate search

All-status title and full title/description/notes searches covered `pair-mcp`, `nREPL`, `port`, `port-file`, `cwd`, `cwd-scan`, `cwd-relative`, `ephemeral port`, `stale port`, `restart detection`, and `reconnect`. No open, in-progress, deferred, or closed bead owns CWD fallback file identity or restart recovery. Historical source comments cite the earlier exact-port-file work for explicit/roots/HTTP discovery; this issue is the omitted fifth branch of that invariant, not a duplicate of an active tracker item. `rf2-ahjbc` is an open Pair-MCP stream-surface retirement and does not touch transport discovery.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #8848 (commit abba851486): the step-5 CWD nREPL port fallback now resolves candidates against process.cwd() via read-port-at-base and surfaces the winning candidate as an absolute :port-file, so the server's per-tool-call re-read observes ephemeral-port restarts and vanished files on this branch exactly like steps 1/3/4; :project-home stays nil (no inference). Composed P1->P2 witness + vanished-file test in port_file_stability_test.cljs; discovery winner-identity/read-once/env-no-file tests in nrepl_test.cljs; spec/002 + README now describe the fallback as file-backed and restart-aware. npm test 1108/4011 green; pre-fix revert reds exactly the new witnesses (recorded in PR).

title: bug(mcp-base): dedup aliases legitimate payload values as cache references
description:
## Scope

Fix the shared structural-dedup wire codec in `tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/dedup.cljc` and its JSON-side mirror in `tools/mcp-conformance/lib/dedup-envelope.cjs`. Keep Pair-MCP and Story-MCP tool names, arguments, opt-out behavior, and the `:rf.mcp/dedup-table` outer envelope unchanged. Update the focused specs/tests that define the reference representation.

## Correctness finding

Dedup references are not distinguishable from legitimate payload data. The Clojure/CLJS decoder classifies every symbol whose namespace is `de-dupe.cache` as a cache reference, without requiring the symbol to name a real entry. The JSON mirror is broader: after JSON erases the symbol/string distinction, it treats every string beginning `de-dupe.cache/` as a reference. Therefore `expand` is not the exact inverse promised by the codec for arbitrary persistent data. A payload scalar can become `nil`, another cached subtree, a thrown missing-reference error, or a cycle merely because its value occupies the codec's in-band namespace.

## Evidence

- `dedup.cljc:160-165` defines `cache-element?` as `symbol?` plus namespace equality only; `dedup.cljc:347-360` immediately routes every such value to `expand-entry` and reads `(get cache cache-id)` even when the table has no matching slot.
- `dedup-envelope.cjs:62-64,81-83` uses `startsWith('de-dupe.cache/')`; `dedup-envelope.cjs:137-141` then throws when that ordinary string has no table entry. JSON serialization makes real reference symbols and ordinary payload strings share this same representation.
- Both shipped consumers enable this codec on value-rich, programmer-owned data: Pair-MCP epoch/snapshot/subscribe payloads and Story-MCP run/preview/record payloads. An unrelated repeated subtree is enough to activate the wrapper, so the colliding scalar need not itself repeat.
- The current cross-host dedup suite proves common collection kinds and real references, but has no literal payload value in the reference namespace and no JSON string collision arm.

## Steps to Reproduce

Evaluate the real JVM codec with:

```clojure
(require '[re-frame.mcp-base.dedup :as d]
         '[re-frame.mcp-base.vocab :as v])
(let [shared  {:big [:repeat :me]}
      payload {:literal 'de-dupe.cache/not-a-ref
               :a shared
               :b shared}
      wrapped (d/dedup-value payload true)
      cache   (get wrapped v/dedup-table-key)]
  {:wrapped? (contains? wrapped v/dedup-table-key)
   :expanded (d/expand cache)
   :equal?   (= payload (d/expand cache))})
```

Current result is non-vacuously wrapped, but `:literal` expands to `nil` and `:equal?` is false. In the Node mirror, placing the ordinary JSON string `"de-dupe.cache/not-a-ref"` beside a real cache reference throws `cache reference ... has no matching entry`.

## Failure scenario / invariant

A re-frame app legitimately stores a namespaced symbol in app-db, a story emits one in rendered/diagnostic data, or a structured payload contains a string with the same spelling. The payload also contains ordinary repeated state, which is common in epoch pairs and enables dedup. The server advertises a successful dedup envelope, but the agent reconstructs data different from the server's value (or cannot reconstruct it at all). The required invariant is: for every supported payload value `x`, `expand(de-dupe-eq(x)) = x`, and the JSON projection must preserve the same semantic value; cache references must be unambiguous from user data.

## Recommended minimal fix

Retain the outer envelope and make the existing reference tokens collision-free rather than adding a compatibility layer. During the encoder's existing discovery walk, record literal payload symbols and strings that can collide with `de-dupe.cache/cache-N`, and allocate cache ids that skip those spellings. On decode, classify only an exact cache-id token that is present in the current cache, not every value sharing the namespace/prefix. Apply the same exact-entry rule in the Node mirror. This preserves the compact wire shape while making the encoder's own output unambiguous. If a smaller closed reference representation proves simpler, change it in one pre-alpha cut across the base spec, both decoders, and conformance fixtures; do not support two formats.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Add a cross-host test in `re-frame.mcp-base.dedup-test` whose payload contains (a) an ordinary `de-dupe.cache/not-a-ref` symbol, (b) an ordinary generated-looking `de-dupe.cache/cache-1` symbol, and (c) an unrelated repeated subtree. Assert the result actually contains `:rf.mcp/dedup-table` (non-vacuity/control), `expand` equals the original payload, and both literal symbols remain symbols with their exact values.
2. Add the JSON-mirror counterpart with ordinary strings `de-dupe.cache/not-a-ref` and `de-dupe.cache/cache-1` beside at least one real cache reference. Assert `decodeDedupEnvelope` reconstructs the exact strings and the real reference. As a positive control, a deliberately missing genuine reference must still fail loudly, proving reference resolution was not disabled wholesale.
3. Existing real-reference compression remains active: a repeated subtree produces more than the root cache entry and expands exactly on JVM and CLJS.
4. The reference grammar and collision rule are stated once in `tools/mcp-base/spec/dedup.md` and mirrored by the Node conformance decoder; no prefix-only decoder remains.
5. Focused commands pass non-vacuously: from `tools/mcp-base`, `clojure -M:test -n re-frame.mcp-base.dedup-test` and `npm run test:cljs`; from the repository root, `npm run test:dedup-envelope --prefix tools/mcp-conformance`.

## Non-goals

- Redesigning which tools are dedup-eligible, changing the default-on posture, or removing the `dedup false` escape hatch.
- Adding a general serialization framework, schema registry, compatibility alias, or dual-format decoder.
- Optimizing compression ratios or changing equality-vs-identity pooling.
- Hardening arbitrary attacker-authored cache tables beyond preserving the existing loud failure for malformed genuine references.

## Related / duplicate search

All-status tracker searches were run for `dedup`, `de-dupe`, `de-dupe.cache`, `cache reference`, `cache-ref`, `cache-N`, `cache element`, `namespaced symbol`, `symbol collision`, `payload symbol`, `unknown cache`, `dedup table`, `round-trip`, and `roundtrip`, including description and notes searches where supported. No bead describes this alias/corruption outcome. Closed `rf2-ntbd1` concerns package ownership of the epoch diff codec and explicitly leaves dedup in mcp-base; it is not a duplicate. Open dedup mentions concern recorder/stream/tool-surface design, not cache-reference representation.
acceptance_criteria:
- Cross-host codec test is forced through a real dedup wrapper by an unrelated repeated subtree, then round-trips literal reserved-namespace and generated-looking symbols exactly.
- Node JSON decoder preserves same-spelling ordinary strings while resolving a real cache reference; a missing genuine reference remains a loud-failure positive control.
- Existing repeated-subtree compression remains non-vacuously active and exact on JVM and CLJS.
- Focused mcp-base JVM/CLJS and conformance dedup-envelope commands pass.
notes:
--- 2026-09-01 11:58 AUSEST — implemented, PR #8854 (worker/mcp-dedup-kjv05) ---

PREMISE VERIFIED AT TIP. dedup.cljc's cache-element? was symbol? + namespace
equality only, and dedup-envelope.cjs classified on startsWith('de-dupe.cache/'),
throwing on a missing entry. Both confirmed before any edit; the finding holds.

WIRE DECISION — escaping, NOT the recommended id-skipping. References are now
SPELLED: in value position `de-dupe.cache/cache-<digits>` is a reference,
`de-dupe.cache/!<rest>` is an escaped literal of `de-dupe.cache/<rest>`, and
anything else in the namespace is payload data. The encoder escapes (one leading
`!`) every payload token that would otherwise read as one of the first two forms,
so its own output is unambiguous by construction. Reversible under repetition;
applied to symbols AND same-spelled strings, type-preserving, so the JSON
projection is exact as well as the Clojure round-trip. Escape runs as a pre-pass
BEFORE the counting walk so both passes hash the same subtrees and pooling still
fires on a subtree carrying a colliding literal.

WHY NOT ID-SKIPPING (the description's "recommended minimal fix"): skipping
colliding ids forces the decoder to classify by TABLE PRESENCE, and that silently
drops the loud failure on a genuinely missing reference — which acceptance
criterion 2 requires kept. The two halves of AC2 are not jointly satisfiable under
id-skipping. Escaping satisfies both: `cache-<digits>` is a reference whether or
not the slot exists (missing => loud), while ordinary namespace-occupying values
decode verbatim. Taken as one pre-alpha cut across codec, spec and Node decoder;
no dual-format path.

UNCHANGED: wire namespace, `cache-N` key spelling, `cache-0` root,
`:rf.mcp/dedup-table` envelope, id allocation, tool names/arguments/opt-out. Cache
KEYS never carry an escape. No consumer source needed touching (pair-mcp,
story-mcp, wire-vocab DedupTable schema all untouched) — the round-trip tests are
the evidence. Clojure-side `expand` keeps its existing quiet-nil for a hand-written
dangling reference; hardening that is a stated non-goal.

FILES: tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/dedup.cljc,
tools/mcp-base/test/re_frame/mcp_base/dedup_test.cljc (+6 deftests),
tools/mcp-base/spec/dedup.md (§Reference grammar and the collision rule — the one
normative statement), tools/mcp-conformance/lib/dedup-envelope.cjs,

GATES (final rebased base, origin/main 4e27fbbe49; exits captured on the same
command line as the redirect):
  clojure -M:test -n re-frame.mcp-base.dedup-test  exit 0  20 tests / 69 assertions

     all 11 pre-existing tests still green.
  2. Escape pre-pass removed from de-dupe-eq => exit 1, 5 failures + 1 error, all
     in the new tests, namespace/assertion counts unchanged from the green run.
  3. Broken anchor planted in spec/dedup.md  => exit 1, gate named file+line+anchor.
Every new fixture is forced through a REAL wrap by an unrelated repeated subtree
and asserts :rf.mcp/dedup-table is present, because the collision alone is not a
dedup opportunity and the assertions would otherwise pass vacuously.

ACs: 1 ✓ (payload-symbols-in-the-reference-namespace-round-trip-as-data), 2 ✓
(Node arm + POSITIVE CONTROL that a missing genuine reference still throws), 3 ✓
(colliding-payload-tokens-are-escaped-on-the-wire pins >1 slot and exact expansion
on both hosts; full JVM + CLJS suites green), 4 ✓ (grammar stated once in

(all three focused commands pass non-vacuously).
AUDIT PR #8854 (2026-09-01): REOPENED. The new collision grammar misses namespaced KEYWORDS, although Cheshire erases them to the same JSON string as symbols, strings, and real cache references. Real boundary probe with payload {:literal :de-dupe.cache/cache-1 :a shared :b shared}: dedup/expand is locally exact, but Cheshire emits root.literal as "de-dupe.cache/cache-1" beside real refs of the same spelling, and decodeDedupEnvelope reconstructs literal as the cached subtree {"big":["repeat","me"]} instead of the keyword's JSON projection. Root cause: token-name/retoken escape only symbols and strings. This leaves common re-frame app-db data corrupt across the shipped Clojure-to-JSON-to-Node seam and violates the exact-inverse claim. Minimal repair: include de-dupe.cache keywords in the escape grammar and preserve keyword type on Clojure expand; cover both value and map-key positions through a forced real wrapper plus actual Cheshire/Node projection, while retaining loud missing-ref behavior and the existing wire/API shape.
--- 2026-09-01 14:12 AUSEST — AUDIT REOPEN CLOSED, PR #8879 (worker/mcp-dedup2-kjv05) ---

AUDIT PREMISE VERIFIED AT SOURCE, AND IT UNDERSTATED THE BLAST RADIUS. Reproduced the
audit's probe across the real CLJ -> Cheshire -> Node seam (real dedup-value, real
cheshire.core/generate-string, real decodeDedupEnvelope) BEFORE any edit, comparing the
decoded result against the payload's own JSON projection. 3 of 6 arms failed, exit 1:

  kw-value   {:literal :de-dupe.cache/cache-1 :a shared :b shared}  -- the audit's probe
             verbatim. `literal` decoded as {"big":["repeat","me"]}, the cached subtree.
  kw-key     the same keyword in map-KEY position. The key resolved to the subtree and the
             entry landed under its JSON.stringify -- unreachable by its own name.
             NOT NAMED BY THE AUDIT; found by the reproduction.
  kw-escaped payload :de-dupe.cache/!cache-1. Unescaped, so the decoder stripped a marker
             that was never added and returned .../cache-1. A DIFFERENT corruption from the
             aliasing one -- the escape's own reversibility-under-repetition breaking.
             NOT NAMED BY THE AUDIT.

kw-plain, sym-value and str-value passed, so #8854's symbol/string fix stands and was not
disabled. After the fix: 6 of 6, exit 0, with the Node decoder BYTE-IDENTICAL.

FIX SIDE: ENCODER, continuing #8854's direction rather than adding a reader rule. The
classifier side cannot be made to work at all here -- by the time the Node mirror sees a
token, JSON has erased symbol/keyword/string onto one string, so no reader-side grammar can
separate them. The repair is to CLOSE the set the encoder escapes rather than widen it:
`token-name` now tests `ident?` (was `symbol?`) and `string?`, and `retoken` preserves all
three types. Symbol, keyword and string are exactly the scalars a JSON encoder renders as a
bare namespaced string; no other Clojure scalar can produce a slash-bearing name in this
namespace. The set is now closed, not merely larger.

THE NODE DECODER NEEDED NO LOGIC CHANGE, and that is the result rather than a shortcut: its
grammar is type-blind, so it already decoded the wider output under the same three rules.
Only its contract comment and its fixtures moved. That property is now stated in both files
so the next widening does not go looking for a decoder edit.

WHY THIS SURVIVED A GREEN SUITE, recorded because it is the reusable lesson: `cache-element?`
tests `symbol?`, so an unescaped payload keyword is never aliased on the JVM or in CLJS and
every round-trip assertion passes. The Clojure round-trip CANNOT SEE this bug. The new
host-side tests therefore pin the WIRE SPELLING, not only the round-trip -- confirmed by the
planted-fault run below, where the round-trip test stayed green while the spelling tests went
red. A keyword is the ordinary spelling of both a value and a map key in re-frame app-db data,
so this was the likeliest of the three collisions to be hit in practice.

RESIDUAL AMBIGUITY -- one, inherent to JSON, not to this codec: the Clojure TYPE is not
recovered across the wire. A payload symbol, keyword and string in this namespace all reach a
Node consumer as the same string, as they would anywhere else in the payload; JSON has no
symbol or keyword. The restored guarantee is that the JSON PROJECTION passes through the codec
unchanged (encode-then-decode is the identity on it), alongside the exact Clojure round-trip on
the host. Stated in tools/mcp-base/spec/dedup.md so it is not refiled as a bug.

HOW THE MIRRORED PAIR WAS PROVED TO AGREE: primarily by the boundary probe -- one artefact
crossing the seam, the unmodified decoder fed the new encoder's real Cheshire output, 3/6 ->
6/6. Committed coverage mirrors it: the Clojure side pins the wire spelling, and the Node
fixtures are transcribed from a real Cheshire encode of the matching payloads rather than
hand-built. RECORDED HONESTLY IN THE SPEC: no committed gate runs the whole seam in one
process -- mcp-base's suites have no JSON encoder and no access to the Node decoder, and
mcp-conformance's Node unit cluster deliberately boots no JVM. Mirrored spellings plus an
out-of-band probe are the coverage. Building a committed crossing gate was considered and
rejected as out of scope and cross-artefact-coupling (mcp-base is a published library and must
not reach into mcp-conformance); if wanted it is a separate bead, not a silent addition here.

    its (cache-element? value) arm)   cited 347-360 -> 477 / 484 at base -> 503 / 510 now

  dedup-envelope.cjs missing-entry    cited 137-141 -> 184 at base -> 199 now

title: surface-review(resources): make active-route resource replanning a first-class causal command
description:
## Scope

Add one public event-vector command for rerunning the active route's Resources plan when an app-db-derived identity input (principal, tenant, permission set, locale, impersonation) changes without navigation. Cover the Resources↔Routing late-bound seam, exact route-owner reconciliation, durable plan/blocking/readiness state, conformance tests, Spec 012/016 and API/resource docs, and the RealWorld-on-resources receipt. Keep Resources optional and vector-first.

## Findings

Named `{:from-db ...}` subscriptions deliberately re-key when resolver inputs change, but remain passive. The newly selected scoped key is therefore `:idle` until some causal path ensures it. Navigation normally supplies that cause, but identical navigation is intentionally a no-op and there is no public command that reruns the current route's effective resource plan without changing the URL.

The flagship works around this gap with the 39-line `:auth/ensure-viewer-route` event. That app event reads leaf `rf/handler-meta`, invokes each entry itself, and dispatches independent ensures. It is not the route planner: it omits inherited parent resources, local `:after` ordering, identity collapse, atomic planning, exact plan ownership diff, blocking-slot replacement, and route readiness/error repair; it also calls `:when` with nil instead of the planner's reserved `{}` ctx. A cold restore on a composed route can therefore omit a parent-owned read, and a successful hand-ensure after the initial nil-scope planning failure leaves the durable route plan/readiness facts stale.

The runtime already computes the authoritative answer once: the route planner materializes contributor/local-id, canonical params, resolved scope, scoped key and byte key-id; collapses and orders the effective parent chain; diffs prior identities; and returns the exact identity/blocking maps Routing commits under the active nav-token. The missing piece is a public causal door back through that machinery.

## Recommended Action

Ship one public command, `[:rf.route/replan-resources {:cause <edn>}]`, implemented through the existing late-bound Resources↔Routing integration. It should read the current resolved route and nav-token, rerun the canonical effective parent-to-leaf resource planner against the current app-db, and atomically reconcile the standing plan under the same route activation:

- retain/adopt unchanged usable identities without a forced fetch;
- ensure added or changed identities with the existing route owner and caller cause;
- remove that owner only from identities the replanned route no longer requires;
- replace the durable `:resource-plan` and `:resource-blocking` slots and re-project route transition/error from the new plan;
- preserve route id/params/query/fragment/nav-token and do not run guards, `:on-match`, history or scroll effects.

Use the ordinary fail-closed planner boundary: no partial ensures on a failed plan, and document/test the exact prior-owner cleanup and route-error result. Reuse the existing `:rf.resource/route-plan` evidence with an explicit replan cause rather than inventing a parallel planner or helper-function API.

Replace RealWorld's app-side planner copy with this event. Make its personalized feed admission explicit in route data (for example, only when the following-feed query arm is active) so confirmed-anonymous home does not contradict the existing strict nil-scope planning rule. Teach the account/tenant-switch recipe as: resolve/clear the old scope causally, commit the new identity, then replan the active route.

## Evidence

- `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/subs.cljc:35-50,84-120` — a `{:from-db ...}` sub re-keys reactively and reads the new key as idle until a route/event ensures it; subscriptions never fetch.
- `examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/auth.cljs:189-261` — `:auth/ensure-viewer-route` reconstructs the leaf route's declaration and dispatches per-entry ensures by hand.
- `examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/routing.cljs:54-89` — the public home route mixes viewer/session identities and currently claims a nil session feed is simply omitted, while no `:when` admits that distinction.
- `implementation/resources/test/re_frame/resources_from_db_scope_cljs_test.cljc:198-208` — the shipped contract proves a nil named route scope is a whole-plan `:rf.error/resource-route-plan`, not a silent omission.
- `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/route.cljc:700-867,1023-1260` — the canonical planner already materializes exact identities, composes/collapses the branch, applies plan diff, and returns identity/blocking maps.
- `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/events.cljc:247-306` — Routing commits those maps beside `:current` under the active nav-token; the app workaround never updates them or readiness.
- `implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/realworld_resources_cljs_test.cljs:1026-1139` — restore tests assert newly created entries but do not assert repaired route error/readiness, stored plan membership, or an inherited parent read.
- `spec/012-Routing.md:1386` — the spec explicitly reserves force reload as a separate named contract instead of overloading fragment/identical navigation.
- `implementation/resources/deps.edn` and `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources.cljc:406-545,641-643` — Resources is optional and its event family/route behavior already installs through late binding, so the command belongs on that seam without a static Routing dependency.
- Commit `d8a0f670704abc008eb151067f13a1e7cc976c48` removed named read helpers because vectors are the semantic API identity; this command should likewise remain an event vector. `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn:1237-1271` has no need for a new facade function.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The documented public event replans the active route in the dispatching frame from its current registered effective parent chain and current app-db, while leaving URL, route address, fragment and nav-token byte-for-byte unchanged and firing no guard, `:on-match`, history or scroll work.
- Replan uses the same `:when`/ctx, params and scope resolution, schema/canonical identity, contributor attribution, `:after`, branch ordering, identity collapse, blocking and keep-previous semantics as ordinary route entry; there is one planner, not an app-visible approximation.
- A same-route scope change A→B is covered: unchanged identities are retained without a forced request, B identities are ensured and owned, A-only identities lose the route owner, and the durable plan/blocking maps equal the newly materialized plan.
- An initial unresolved-scope plan error followed by app-db resolution + replan is covered: no navigation occurs, route error/readiness is repaired, exact plan membership is stored, and required loads start. The inverse/failing replan proves no partial ensure and the documented prior-owner cleanup/error result.
- Parent-chain coverage proves a leaf replan restores an inherited parent resource; a regression that reads only leaf `handler-meta` must fail. Coverage also pins a conditional occurrence entering/leaving the plan.
- RealWorld deletes `:auth/ensure-viewer-route`'s planner reconstruction in favor of the public command and tests successful restore, failed restore/confirmed anonymous, and a composed-route deep link including route readiness and plan membership, not only cache-entry existence.
- Spec 012/016, the Resources API/reference/concepts or how-to docs, examples and test prose agree on the command, passive-sub boundary, nil-scope behavior and trace cause. API-manifest drift remains green; no named facade helper is added.
- Proportionate Resources/Routing/RealWorld test gates pass, with a negative control that fails when effective-parent composition or durable readiness/plan replacement is removed.

## Non-goals

- No subscription-driven fetch, committed-read demand, app-db watcher, or automatic replan on every resolver input write.
- No general route reload that reruns guards, `:on-match`, history, scroll, or arbitrary route metadata.
- No named helper-function sugar, compatibility alias/window, second query grammar, or duplicate planner.
- No silent global fallback and no global change making nil route scopes silently optional; conditional resources remain explicitly admitted.
- No refactor of ordinary explicit `:rf.resource/ensure`/`refetch` for non-route owners.

## Related beads

- `rf2-hic-050` — STOP verdict for committed-read resource demand; this proposal preserves that ruling by adding an explicit causal event.
- `rf2-hic-054` — blessed event/sub async-resource recipes; the proposed command removes a route-planner reconstruction those public primitives cannot faithfully express.
- `rf2-hic-044` — current-primitives resource-demand witness; no demand/runtime ownership model is reopened here.

A full title/description/notes scan of all existing beads found no active or closed task for current-route resource replanning, force reload, principal-switch replan, or `:auth/ensure-viewer-route`.

description:
Merged-PR audit #10113 (4e24f5d461c95de7bfefc6b8bd3ed6de3098ead6). The registrar-global correction is right, but its replacement rationale now says Static displays a per-frame current-route slice and therefore four of five Static tabs change with the host-frame picker. Static Routes displays no such slice. Choosing another host frame deliberately leaves its catalogue and hermetic simulations unchanged; the new prose makes that correct behavior look like a missing or broken frame projection.

Decisive source: static/routes/panel.cljs:248-257 reads only static tab-data, expansion/simulation UI state, and registered-routes. Its tab-data at :394-399 depends only on registered-routes, query and sim-url. panels/routing_helpers.cljc:531-560 projects exactly those values and explicitly excludes :current/:from-id/:to-id/:navigated? as Dynamic concerns. panels/routing.cljs:677-691 reads the route catalogue using rf/registrations {:source :store :kind :route}; :804-807 creates current-route-slice, and :811-822 consumes it in the DYNAMIC routing-tab-data, not Static. A source-wide check of static/routes finds no current-route/observed-frame/target-frame read beyond the four Panel reads just traced.

Correct the new 018-Event-Spine.md:127 rationale and the changed static/shell.cljs ribbon explanation/comment to name the three actual per-frame Static surfaces: machine snapshots, flows, and app-db schemas. Static Routes and Interceptors are catalogue surfaces. Also reconcile the directly cited false copies in static/shell.cljs namespace docstring :39-41 and 007-UX-IA.md:2193/:2200, so the correction does not cite the same false claim again. A concise correction or removal of the numerical rationale is sufficient. Preserve the frame picker, selection across mode toggles and the now-correct distinction between process-global registrar catalogues and genuinely per-frame stores. Do not add a current-route display or make Static Routes frame-filtered just to satisfy this prose.

The original rf2-u40qy audit brief itself repeated the inaccurate current-route example from the namespace contract; the new production-path trace corrects that earlier evidence. This is a new separately trackable documentation finding against the closed owner, not a request to reopen or rewrite its historical notes. No exact match among the 22 literally open Beads inspected. This finding is source-path evidence, not a mounted-runtime test. The semantic error is not graded by the successful link/docs CI checks.
acceptance_criteria: New picker rationale and its cited per-tab split describe the three actual per-frame Static projections; Routes is documented as a shared catalogue with hermetic simulations. Verify the Static input graph versus Dynamic current-route-slice, preserve existing picker behavior, and retain global event/sub/route/interceptor/machine-definition catalogue semantics.

title: Trace panel derived SUB and VIEW verbs are specified but not produced: decide whether to build the vocabulary or strike it
description:
The Trace panel's derived SUB and VIEW verbs are specified but not produced. `spec/023` §5 marks itself
**PARTIALLY SHIPPED** and says so in terms: the shipped behaviour is the operation's terminal name segment
with hyphens folded to spaces, plus a fixed set of explicit overrides, and the derived verbs "are NOT
produced" — they fall through to the terminal segment instead.

## Provenance and why it is a separate item

Surfaced 2026-09-18 by the worker on rf2-1if4f (PR #9972) while correcting a stale COMMENT that claimed one
of those verbs was in the override map. **The comment was the defect it was sent for; this is the gap the
comment was wrong about.** It stopped the false claim and deliberately did not close the gap, on the ground
that this is a behaviour change wanting its own item and its own red-then-green evidence. That judgement
was right and this bead is the consequence.

**Nothing owned it**: a search over the non-terminal board found no item covering the derived-verb gap
(three loose matches on unrelated subjects, checked individually).

## What to establish first, before writing any code

**Derive the affected set from §5 itself rather than from this bead.** The section lists the derived SUB
verbs and the derived VIEW verbs separately, each with the terminal-segment string it currently renders as.
Read both halves — the original report named only the SUB half, and a count taken from a summary is exactly
what this project keeps paying for. Report the set you derived and how.

Then answer the question the spec does not: **is the target vocabulary still wanted?** §5 calls itself the
target vocabulary rather than the rendered strings, but it was written before several rounds of Trace panel
work landed. **"The spec is aspirational here and should be struck instead" is a legitimate outcome** and
would be a cheaper, honest one — the stance is explicit that we do not litigate every last fine detail, and
a vocabulary nobody has missed in practice may not be worth building.

If it IS wanted, the repair is in the producer (`trace_helpers`), not in the spec.

## Evidence the change would need

A derived verb is a RENDERING change, so a green suite proves only that it still compiles. **Red then
green, with a control that could have failed**: pin the current terminal-segment rendering for at least one
verb before the change so the test goes red on the old behaviour, and keep a row that must NOT change —
one of the explicit overrides — green throughout, so the change is shown to be scoped.

Say which direction each test pins. A verb map that over-applies is a visible wrong label; one that
under-applies is invisible.

## Fence

    tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/trace_helpers.cljc
    its existing test namespace
    tools/xray/spec/023-Trace-Panel.md   -- §5 only, and only to record what you actually shipped

**Do not restate a count anywhere in the spec edit.** That section already carries one number that has to
stay true; do not add a second.

## Lane and gate notes

This touches code, so the shadow-cljs exclusive applies: the node lane is the machine-wide resource, and
two concurrent runs wedge silently. **Ask for the lane; do not take it.**

clj-kondo will not redden on anything graded below error here — read the findings and the warning count,
not the exit code (CLAUDE.md item (w)). And the JVM runner prints no namespace names on success, so
searching a green log for your namespace proves nothing; site your discrimination at a line unique to your
new tests.

title: Incomplete newer-events contract: filtered-empty view suppresses stale-focus notice
description:
Brief reconciliation: the implementation DOES follow the brief's explicit instruction not to render when the list is empty. That clause conflicts with the same source's accepted amendment that presence is independent of the filtered list. The worker did not simply overlook an instruction. The concrete gap is the distinction between a genuinely empty raw spine and a nonempty spine whose view filters hide every row. Resolve that distinction in the brief/contract and implementation together; the existing fully empty-buffer test should remain valid. This is a bounded consistency correction, not a request to reopen the chosen marker design.

Merged-PR audit #9946 (99a65ae43edbc867c322af0c4214ba882612ce92), source rf2-y8doi.30. The ruled amendment requires marker presence and count to come from the spine, independent of the filtered list. The new count does use raw spine bundles, but marker presence still depends on visible rows.
At tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/shell.cljs:2429, (when (and stale-read? (seq event-bundles)) ...) gates the marker using the locally rebound, filtered/rendered event-bundles. That vector originates in :rf.xray/filtered-event-bundles, with frame-view scope, pills and mutes already applied. The comment at 2426-2427 equates no visible rows with nothing newer, which is false.
Concrete case: raw spine has dispatches 1,2,3 in the pinned frame; focus is RETRO on 1 and :head? false; a filter/mute hides all three visible rows. newer-count is 2, but (seq event-bundles) is nil, so the marker is absent while L4 still reports the older pinned epoch. This is the filtered-vector failure the accepted ruling explicitly sought to avoid.
Required correction: make presence independent of rendered-list emptiness; if guarding the genuinely empty buffer, use the same raw focusable spine domain, not the filtered view. Preserve no marker while following or paused-but-current, and keep the existing click-to-follow behavior. Add the missing raw-nonempty / rendered-empty case to the current marker tests. The existing filtered-vector test retains one visible focused row, and the empty-state test empties BOTH vectors, so neither covers this case. No new visual design, chrome, or public API is needed. Source/control-flow review establishes this; no local CLJS build was run for the audit.
