title: xray(filters): the :http-correlation typed pill matches a flat :correlation-id tag no producer stamps, so the correlation pill's right-click filters the event list to nothing
description:
Filed 2026-09-17 by the delegated decider for rf2-y8doi.18 (Xray review wave C6), from the Codex review's executed probe. The dossier's option B rested on "the exchange is one right-click away (correlation pill → L2 filter)"; that route is broken at the matcher, so it is filed here rather than carried by the C6 worker.

## Project stance (verbatim, from CLAUDE.md; paste it into any dispatch preamble unchanged)

> Posture is that we are pre-alpha and focused on elegance, power and a masterpiece.
> But we are not over-engineering or gold plating. Also, we trust the programmer.
> We're trying to facilitate high productivity for them (and the AI they use) via a
> library with excellent ergonomics and low friction. We don't need to litigate every
> last fine detail and drown in the minutiae.

## The defect (verify every cite and every "nothing does X" below at your trunk, with a control, before editing)

- The managed-fx HTTP record's correlation pill (`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/managed_fx_template.cljs` ~:97-119) says "Right-click to filter the event list to this HTTP exchange" and dispatches `[:rf.xray/filter-by-http-correlation correlation-id]`, where `correlation-id` is the caller's `:request-id` read off `:rf.fx/args` (`managed_fx_helpers.cljc` `args-correlation-id`).
- The event handler (`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/filters.cljs` ~:548-554) appends an IN pill `{:kind :http-correlation :params {:correlation-id <id>}}`.
- The matcher (`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/filters/typed_predicates.cljc` ~:196-208) is true iff some trace event in the event-bundle has `(tag-of ev :correlation-id)` equal to the id — a FLAT `:correlation-id` tag. Its comment claims "HTTP / WebSocket / managed-fx surfaces stamp this tag on the issuing effect + every downstream response/abort event".
- No runtime producer stamps that tag. Measured 2026-09-17 at trunk 7c2099d753: ripgrep `:correlation-id` over `implementation/**/src/**/*.clj*` reads 0 files; control: the same pattern over `tools/xray` reads 30+ hits (all in the panel/filter code and their tests). Codex executed the matcher against both producer-shaped rows (issuance row and completion row) and it returned false; a control with the invented flat tag returned true.
- Result on screen: the programmer right-clicks the pill and the L2 event list filters to NOTHING — an empty list that reads as "this exchange produced no events". Same class as C6's wrong status: a confident false answer in a dev tool.
- The 020 spec documents the flat tag as the contract (`tools/xray/spec/020-Filter-Predicates.md` ~:38, row `:http-correlation`); rf2-y8doi.47 is the 020 truthing bead. Sequence: land this fix first so .47 truths 020 against the fixed matcher, or .47 records the row as designed-not-built if this bead is not taken first. Do not edit 020 from this bead unless the mayor says .47 is not in flight.
- The existing tests pin the invented shape: `tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/filters/typed_predicates_cljs_test.cljc` ~:150-176 (`(tagged {:correlation-id "abc-123"})`), ~:207-209, ~:305-309. They are the C16 class (rf2-y8doi.28): a fixture asserting a shape the runtime never produces.

## What the producers actually carry (the join keys; verify)

- Issuing row: `:rf.fx/handled`, op-type `:rf.fx`, tags `:rf.fx/id :rf.http/managed`, `:rf.fx/args {… :request-id <id> …}`, `:frame`, `:rf.trace/dispatch-id` — in the issuing bundle's `:effects` slot (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/fx.cljc` `emit-handled!`, called ~:1654 after the handler returns).
- Completion row: `:rf.http/replied`, op-type `:info`, tags = the reply's `trace-summary` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/reply.cljc` ~:618-626): `:status`, `:rf.reply/work-id [:rf.work/http logical-id issuance attempt]` (logical-id = the caller's `:request-id`, else the originating event-id — `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/reply.cljc` ~:84-98), `:rf.reply/work-kind`, `:rf.reply/work-status`, `:attempt`, `:rf.frame/id`, `:completed-at`; `:correlation` / `:value` / `:error` / `:meta` elided. Emitted from the transport callback outside any handler scope (`transport.cljc` ~:538-557), so it lands in `[nil :ungrouped]`, which is NOT an event-bundle the L2 list shows as the issuing event's.
- Failure rows: op = `(:kind failure)` (`:rf.http/transport` etc.), op-type `:error`, tags = the redacted failure map (`transport.cljc` ~:919) — carries `:request-id` (verify); ungrouped except the synchronous body-prep failure (~:2072-2086), which lands in the issuing bundle.
- The reply dispatch: a fresh run whose event vector carries the canonical reply map with `:correlation {:request-id <id>}` — check what the `:rf.event/dispatched` trace row's tags carry for it (the event vector under `:rf.event/v`?) before deciding whether the reply-dispatch bundle is matchable.

## The design question this bead owns

title: merge criterion trap (a): the job-key discriminator also matches on:-block trigger keys - all 11 workflow files over-count, and the discharge procedure cannot tell the two apart
description:
FOUND 2026-09-17 by the rf2-4nkf4 worker, as a side observation while enumerating the required-checks
aggregators, and filed SEPARATELY on purpose. The worker recorded it on rf2-4nkf4's notes and
correctly declined to act on it — that bead was fenced to trap (c). But rf2-4nkf4 is about to close,
and a finding living only in the notes of a closing bead is the shape rf2-9h0f9's own filing note
names: **a finding cited as support for another finding never gets its own item.**

## THE OBSERVABLE

CLAUDE.md's merge-criterion trap **(a)** prescribes a job-key discriminator, and is emphatic that it
needs two leading spaces:

    git diff <merge-base> origin/main -- .github/workflows/ | grep -cE '^\+  [a-z][a-z0-9_-]*:[[:space:]]*$'

The two-space requirement is correct and well-evidenced. **What the pattern does not do is check
that the matched key sits under `jobs:`.** A workflow's `on:` block puts `push:`, `pull_request:`
and `workflow_dispatch:` at exactly the same indent, so they match too.

## MEASURED OVER EVERY WORKFLOW FILE — ALL ELEVEN OVER-COUNT

Discriminator count against the real job count parsed with PyYAML:

    lint.yml                        12  vs   8    over by 4
    docs.yml                         9  vs   6    over by 3
    portability.yml                  6  vs   3    over by 3
    expensive-tests.yml              9  vs   7    over by 2
    post-merge-workflow-sanity.yml   3  vs   1    over by 2
    test.yml                        73  vs  71    over by 2
    release.yml                      8  vs   7    over by 1
    release-story.yml                8  vs   7    over by 1
    release-machines-viz.yml         4  vs   3    over by 1
    release-xray.yml                 4  vs   3    over by 1
    template-release.yml             4  vs   3    over by 1

Worked example, `portability.yml`: the discriminator matches at lines 55, 62, 64, 71, 164 and 294;
the first three are `push:`, `pull_request:` and `workflow_dispatch:` under `on:`, and only the last
three are jobs.

## SEVERITY, STATED HONESTLY — THIS IS NOT A FOURTH FAIL-OPEN TRAP

**It can only inflate, never deflate.** So the case trap (a) calls dangerous — *"a zero is the
reassuring answer"* — is UNAFFECTED: an over-counting pattern cannot manufacture a false zero.

**And the discriminator is applied to a DIFF of added lines, not to whole files**, so the figures
above are the upper bound rather than the everyday error. It fires spuriously only when a diff ADDS
`on:`-block keys, which means a NEW workflow file (whole `on:` block added) or a new trigger on an
existing one.

**The realistic cost is a PHANTOM BAND, and it arrives through the discharge procedure.** Trap (a)
already says a non-zero count is a question, and prescribes discharging it by reading the
`+++ b/<path>` lines and then *"the `on:` block of each named file, counting only keys in files
carrying a `pull_request` trigger."* That procedure asks whether the FILE has a pull_request trigger;
it never asks whether the MATCHED LINE was a job key. So a reader who follows it exactly, on a diff
adding a new workflow, reads the phantom keys, confirms the file is pull-request-triggered, and
concludes "real new checks" — inventing a band higher than the tree produces. CLAUDE.md already
prices that outcome in the rename paragraph: *"it invents a band that never existed, after which
every PR reads five checks short of a phantom — indistinguishable from a change genuinely missing
five jobs, and the next move is to hunt for coverage that was never gone."*

So: same cost as the rename case, reached through a different door, and it is why this is worth
recording rather than shrugging at.

## THE LIKELY FIX IS SMALL

One clause in trap (a)'s discharge step: after naming the files, **confirm each matched key sits
under `jobs:` rather than under `on:`** — the mechanical tell being that `push`, `pull_request`,
`workflow_dispatch`, `schedule` and `workflow_call` are trigger names, or more robustly that the
block beneath a job key carries `runs-on:`/`uses:`.

**Do NOT change the two-space pattern itself** — it is right, and its evidence (reads 1 on
`366e4fca79`, 0 on `4cf4d711a2`) stands. **Do NOT add a gate.** **Do NOT restate trap (a)**, whose
mechanism, its qualification and the rename mirror are all correct.

## NOT ESTABLISHED

  * **Whether this has ever fired in practice.** No history was taken. Every band measurement this
    session read 0 workflow diff lines, so the discriminator returned 0 and the defect could not
    express itself.
  * **Whether a real diff adding a workflow file exists in recent history** to demonstrate it end to
    end. The measurement above is over whole files, which is the upper bound, not the operational
    case. **Whoever takes this should construct or find that diff before writing**, because the
    strength of the clause depends on the operational error being real rather than theoretical.
  * Whether the `runs-on:`/`uses:` tell is reliable across this repo's workflows, including
    `workflow_call` jobs. Not checked.

## PROVENANCE

The worker's own words, recorded on rf2-4nkf4: portability has 3 job keys, not the 6 the mayor's
brief stated, *"because portability's `on:` block puts `push:`/`pull_request:`/`workflow_dispatch:`
at the same indent as job keys. Doesn't change the finding. Not acted on — (a) is fenced and already
carries a discharge procedure."* The mayor re-derived it independently before filing: discriminator
6, PyYAML 3, with the line numbers and their parent sections listed above, then swept all eleven
workflow files.

title: core: delete the sub-arg cache-fragmentation guardrail — it warns about a hazard the value-keyed cache cannot have (rf2-pk4i6 item 15)
description:
Shortlist item 15 of the rf2-pk4i6 senior-review wave. Size S. Source: rf2-pk4i6.4#1. **Mike ruled the whole wave as the triage recommended** (*"rule rf2-pk4i6 as your recommendation"*), and the triage's recommendation for this item is: **DELETE THE GUARDRAIL.**

## The finding

The dev warning `:rf.warning/sub-arg-cache-fragmentation` fires exactly when a query-vector arg is `=` to the previous one but NOT `identical?`, and its hint says *"The sub-cache keys by identity, so every render mints a NEW cache entry: the cache grows unbounded."*

**That hazard cannot happen.** The sub-cache is a persistent map keyed by the query vector under `=`, so an `=`-equal fresh map or vector arg is a cache HIT, not a new slot. Spec 006 §Value-keyed cache-key contract says so verbatim: *"Two subscriptions whose query vectors are `rf=` — regardless of allocation identity … resolve to one cache entry."* The args that DO fragment — fresh closures, JS objects, things not `=` to anything — are precisely the ones the heuristic deliberately never flags.

It is also a false positive by construction: two components each holding a hoisted-but-distinct `{:filter :a}` alternating renders will warn, with one slot involved. And it costs a `swap!` plus a full `=` walk of the arg on every dev subscribe, retaining the last arg per sub-id for the process lifetime.

**Under "trust the programmer" this is a nagging diagnostic that is also WRONG** — an AI reading the docs today learns a false model and hoists args for nothing. That is the stance's own reasoning, not a gloss on it.

## What to do

Delete the two fns, the `defonce`, the late-bind enrolment, the call site in `subs.cljc`, and the test file. Replace the "rookie mistake" paragraph in `docs/core/subscriptions.md` with ONE sentence: the cache is value-keyed, so inline `=`-equal args are fine and only non-`=` args (closures) miss.

**The triage's own re-verification note reads: "no — the reviewer quotes 006:874-876 verbatim and the `:sub-cache (atom {})` seat; a wrong nag needs no run to delete."** So the premise was NOT re-verified at tip. Verify it yourself before deleting anything — the measured premise-failure rate on this wave is roughly one in fourteen citations, and a deletion is the least reversible thing on the shortlist.


FOUND BY THE rf2-ifzg4 WORKER (PR #9890, shortlist item 5) and deliberately NOT fixed there, because `tools/` was outside that item's surface. Filed so the finding is not lost.

THE FINDING. `derive-stale?` in `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/resources_helpers.cljc` RE-IMPLEMENTS `state/entry-stale?` from `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/state.cljc`. Spec 016 explicitly claims a SINGLE SHARED DERIVATION for staleness; there are two.

WHY IT MATTERS, AND WHY IT IS P3 RATHER THAN HIGHER. The worker reports the two are SEMANTICALLY IDENTICAL TODAY, so nothing is broken and no user sees a wrong answer. What is broken is the invariant: a claim of single-derivation that the tree does not satisfy. The hazard is drift -- the next change to staleness moves one copy, Xray then disagrees with the framework about whether an entry is stale, and the disagreement surfaces as a TOOL bug rather than as the duplication it is. PR #9890 is exactly such a change to the surrounding semantics (a durable invalidation now survives a failed refetch) and happened not to touch the predicate itself.

WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the duplication is deliberate. Xray is bundle-isolated from production -- nothing in `implementation/` may require from `tools/` -- so a tool that cannot import the framework's predicate may have had no choice, in which case the right repair is a comment naming the constraint and the sibling, not a merge. CHECK THAT FIRST. "It is deliberate and here is why" closes this bead.

SCOPE IF IT IS NOT DELIBERATE: the options are to share the derivation through whatever seam the isolation rule permits, or to keep two copies with a pin that fails when they diverge. Prefer the pin if sharing would weaken the bundle-isolation boundary, which is a stronger invariant than this one.

SURFACE: tools/xray/**, and spec/016-Resources.md only if the single-derivation claim needs qualifying. Do NOT edit implementation/resources to suit the tool.

title: resources: rf2-omahf follow-ups - spec 016 SSR-projection clause still says hydration arms no timers; verify an owned hydrated :poll-interval-ms entry starts polling
description:
FOLLOW-UP from rf2-omahf (PR #9857, merged as 0e8b100eeb). There are two parts, both under Mike's ruling D, and no new decision is needed.

PART 1: STALE SPEC CLAUSE (a definite edit).
- Where: spec/016-Resources.md, the SSR projection rule's paragraph beginning "Shipping such a row emptied of its data" (about :1661; re-derive the line at tip).
- The problem: it still justifies dropping the row with "collectable by nothing either, since inactive GC is driven by a timer armed when an entry is committed and hydration arms no timers". Since #9857, the client arms each hydrated entry's GC timer once after its :rf/hydrate commit, so "hydration arms no timers" is now false.
- The fix: correct that one clause so it no longer contradicts spec 016 :1216/:1226. Keep the paragraph's conclusion, which is to drop the row. Re-read the paragraph in full, because removing its premise must not leave the conclusion unsupported. If the drop-the-row rule no longer follows once the clause is corrected, STOP and report; do not change the rule.

PART 2: A CLAIM, NOT REPRODUCED. Reproduce it first.
- The worry: a hydrated entry whose owner rode the wire, and whose resource declares :poll-interval-ms, may never start polling on the client. The suspected cause is the same fresh-skip gate that kept GC from arming (was-owner-free? / owner-newly-attached? in resources events.cljc). PR #9857 arms GC only, per the ruling.
- How to measure: on the JVM lane with :platform :client frames, run the rf2-omahf regression shape (implementation/resources/test/re_frame/resources_hydrated_gc_arming_cljs_test.cljc) with a :poll-interval-ms resource. Use both instruments: the schedule-timers emissions and the real host timer table.
- If it DOES reproduce: whether a hydrated owned entry should start polling after hydration is a contract question for spec 016 §Poll (the :poll timer is "armed lazily client-side"). Record the evidence, and STOP for Mike if the fix would change what spec 016 says. If spec 016 already requires polling to start, fix it on the #9857 precedent: the same post-commit rearm fx arms the poll timer too. Commit a RED regression first.
- If it does NOT reproduce: record the run that shows a poll timer arming, and close this part.

title: fix(story-ui): sidebar reads "VARIANTS-GRID · 0" for a grid that renders five cells, and the :dev/:docs/:test mode tabs carry no ARIA tab role (getByRole('tab') finds nothing)
description:
From the rf2-rln91 Story-parity research (ai/findings/Story/fable/report.md, R9), exercised on the shell at :8043 with Playwright at trunk 98e8ffe9cb.

TWO SMALL DRIFTS on the first screen a user sees:
1. The sidebar count for the auto-generated variants grid reads "VARIANTS-GRID · 0" while the grid renders five cells. Find the count site in tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/ and count what the grid renders.
2. The mode tabs (007-Mode-Tabs.md; :dev / :docs / :test) are not exposed as ARIA tabs: role selectors fail, text selectors work. Add role="tablist"/"tab" with aria-selected, which also makes them reachable to the a11y panel and to automation.

ACCEPTANCE: "VARIANTS-GRID · 5" for a five-cell grid; `getByRole('tab')` finds the three modes. GATES: UI cljs tests; a Playwright walk recorded in the PR body. Not a hot zone.
notes:
WORKER RESULT (branch worker/storyui-a, PR #9795, commit c0c1298884), 2026-09-14.

(a) HOLDS, and is fixed. The count site was tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/sidebar.cljs workspace-grid-grouping, which counted the workspace body's :variants slot. A :variants-grid enumerates its anchor story's variants from the registry (:for, or the Workspace.<path> id) and carries no :variants slot, so it read 0. It now counts rf.story.ui.workspace/resolve-layout, the same cell vector workspace-view renders. The existing test case that pinned a :variants-grid counting its :variants slot encoded the defect, and was replaced by a registry-enumerated regression covering both anchors.

(b) DOES NOT HOLD; no change made. mode_tabs.cljs has carried role="tablist", role="tab" and aria-selected since its first commit (adea36724d, PR #454), and did at the research trunk 98e8ffe9cb. shell.cljs mounts the strip only while a single variant is selected and no workspace is. Playwright against the login-form Story shell compiled from this branch BEFORE the fix: on the first screen (#/stories, nothing selected) the strip is not mounted, getByRole('tab') finds 0 and text selectors for Canvas/Docs/Tests also find 0; with :story.login-form/idle selected, getByRole('tab') finds 3 (Canvas, Docs, Tests), the "Story mode" tablist holds 3, and aria-selected marks Canvas. The research walk observed the unmounted first screen, not missing roles.

Walk evidence for (a): before the fix the sidebar header read "VARIANTS-GRID· 0" while the grid's own data-test-grid-total read 5; after the fix it reads "VARIANTS-GRID· 5".

Gates (captured exit codes): sidebar-chips namespace alone exit 0, 7 tests / 33 assertions / 0 failures (7 = 6 before plus the 1 new); Story UI CLJS set (sidebar, test-mode-pane, evidence-spine, story-ui, budgets, workspace-substrate-routing) exit 0, 102 tests / 565 assertions / 0 failures; JVM load of the .cljc test namespace exit 0, 1 test / 2 assertions; clj-kondo --fail-level error exit 0 with 0 errors (2 warnings, both identical at the base).

== SCOPE CORRECTION: the ARIA half is WITHDRAWN; the count half stands with its root cause (mayor re-frame2-fe, 2026-09-14 11:20 AUSEST) ==
The ARIA finding in this bead's description is retracted at source: tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/mode_tabs.cljs:174-182 already renders the strip with `:role "tablist"` and `:aria-label "Story mode"` and each button with `:role "tab"` and `:aria-selected`. The COUNT half stands, and the root cause is at tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/sidebar.cljs:621-633 `workspace-grid-grouping`: its docstring says `:count` is "the body's `:variants` count; a `:variants-grid` that enumerates from the registry reports its explicit `:variants` count when present, else 0", and the body does `(count (:variants body))` at :633 — so an auto grid that enumerates by `:for` from the registry reports 0 while rendering N cells. title: Incomplete: quiet replay still adopts a traced grandchild's dispatch identity
description:
Merged-PR audit #9791 (6537d8b4ccaba7f2e72af4a27f49e7986930646e), against closed rf2-c74lr. Removing the first-commit fallback fixes the two reported strangers, but the claim that a replay committing no own epoch now reports nil remains incomplete. A normal two-level queued cascade makes the unchanged first-observed-dispatch acquisition adopt the grandchild and return its epoch under the quiet parent event name.

Locations: implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/state.cljc, arm-commit-observation!, note-observed-dispatch! (around 379-398), note-commit!; implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc, perform-replay!'s arm / dispatch-sync / take window.

Executed reproduction through public rf/replay-epoch!, with actual current source, plain-atom adapter, epoch depth 10, and no observation/trace/dispatch stubs or timing interleaving:
1. Register :audit/parent to increment :runs and, only from its second invocation, return :fx [[:dispatch [:audit/child]]]. Register :audit/child to set :child true and return :fx [[:dispatch [:audit/grandchild]]]. Register :audit/grandchild to set :grandchild true.
2. Make a frame and dispatch [:audit/parent] once. Its source epoch is 1 and it queues nothing yet.
3. Re-register :audit/parent with the SAME handler and {:rf.trace/no-emit? true}, then rf/replay-epoch! that source epoch.
4. Actual database: {:runs 2 :child true :grandchild true}. Retained trigger events: [[:audit/parent] [:audit/child] [:audit/grandchild]]. There is no replay-parent epoch.
5. Actual result: {:ok? true :source-epoch-id 1 :event-id :audit/parent :epoch-id 3}; epoch 3 resolves to [:audit/grandchild]. Required result: :epoch-id nil.

Cause: the quiet parent's own dispatched emit and its child's enqueue emit are suppressed by the parent's no-emit scope. When the traced child queues the grandchild, tracing is active again. This is the first :rf.event/dispatched captured on the arming thread, so note-observed-dispatch! treats its id as the replay's. note-commit! subsequently correlates the grandchild's commit perfectly to that WRONG target. The fallback is not involved. Same thread alone does not identify the armed caller when its own trace was absent.

Controls, executed in fresh frames in the same completed probe:
- Quiet parent -> traced child with no grandchild: result epoch-id nil; history has only source parent and child; both execute.
- Ordinary traced parent -> child -> grandchild: result names the new PARENT epoch (7 in the probe), and history contains source parent, replay parent, child, grandchild. All execute.

Required correction: bind the observation to the replay invocation's own dispatch identity, or bound identity acquisition so a suppressed replay can never acquire a later traced descendant as its target. Do not replace dispatch identity with handler/event-vector equality: the existing same-handler listener-nesting regression must remain correct. A quiet replay with any queued cascade must return nil when it produces no own epoch; ordinary traced replay must still return its own retained epoch and nil when evicted. Preserve thread isolation, nested-listener handling, strict replay inputs and failed-dispatch cleanup. No public policy surface, new diagnostic family or general tracing redesign is requested.

Regression: extend the same-thread quiet queued-child case with a traced child that queues a traced grandchild. On both JVM and CLJS assert all handlers execute, only source parent/child/grandchild records exist, and public replay returns nil. Keep child-only quiet and ordinary traced two-level controls.

Evidence: C:/Users/miket/.codex/tmp/audit-re-frame2-pr9791-grandchild-probe-1.clj, .log and .exit. Probe exit 0 asserts the observed wrong grandchild result and both correct controls; log prints the actual repository state.cljc resource URL. No repository source changes. The entire shipped replay namespace independently runs 21 tests/151 assertions, 0 failures, exit 0 on landed state; historical state plus new tests gives 2 failures, exit 1. Current CI epoch 546/7343 and CLJS 12080/60219 also pass but do not exercise this second queued edge.

Deduplication: inspected all 13 literal-open Beads; none records this wrong grandchild dispatch-identity acquisition and correction. Closed rf2-c74lr remains closed, with its description/criteria/close_reason/closed_at preserved and only an appended forward pointer. No mayor notification or acknowledgment is inferred.
acceptance_criteria: On JVM and CLJS, a recorded parent re-registered :rf.trace/no-emit? that queues a traced child which queues a traced grandchild executes all three handlers but returns :epoch-id nil; history contains no replay-parent epoch. Child-only quiet and ordinary traced two-level controls, thread isolation, same-handler listener nesting, retained/evicted epoch identity and cleanup stay green.
notes:
VERDICT (rf2-1mudg), 2026-09-13 AUSEST: fixed in PR #9793 (worker epochgc-a). The branch is based on a586921b94.

PREMISE VERIFIED AT SOURCE (trunk 26f47c8a51 and a586921b94). `note-observed-dispatch!` in `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/state.cljc` treated the first `:rf.event/dispatched` id seen on the arming thread as the replay's target. Nothing tied that id to the replay's own dispatch. The executed regression reproduced the bead on JVM and CLJS: with the tests added and state unchanged, the replay reported an epoch that resolved to `[:review/grandchild]`.

CORRECTION TAKEN: the observation is now bound to the dispatch's lineage (Spec 009, section Dispatch correlation).
- `arm-commit-observation!` records `(some-> rf.trace/*handler-scope* :dispatch-id)`. That is the dispatch-id of the handler scope the arming caller is in, or nil at top level.
- The armed caller's own dispatch carries exactly that id as its `:rf.trace/parent-dispatch-id`. Everything its cascade enqueues names a run inside the cascade as its parent instead.
- `note-observed-dispatch!` now also receives the parent id, which `capture.cljc` passes through. The first id from the arming thread decides the outcome, once. It is taken when its parent matches the arming scope. Otherwise the slot closes with `:dispatch-id nil`, which no commit can match, so take answers nil.
- Closing the slot is exact: the caller's own emit comes before its drain starts, so once a descendant has reported, the caller's emit never will.
- No event-vector equality is used, so `replay-result-is-not-rescued-by-matching-the-event-id` still pins that rule.
- There is no public API change, no new diagnostic, and no core, spec or router change. `dispatch-sync!` was not touched.
- Thread isolation, listener nesting, strict inputs and the `finally` take are unchanged.

REGRESSIONS in `implementation/epoch/test/re_frame/epoch_replay_cljs_test.cljc`, on JVM and CLJS:
- `quiet-replay-reports-nil-not-its-queued-grandchilds-epoch` is the tooth. All three handlers run, the history is source parent, child and grandchild, and the result is `:epoch-id nil`.
- `traced-replay-over-two-queued-levels-reports-its-own-epoch` is the traced two-level control. It reports the new parent record.
- The child-only quiet case and the older neighbours are kept.

EVIDENCE:
- RED with the tests committed before the fix: the JVM replay namespace exited 1 at 23 tests / 160 assertions with 1 failure. The CLJS replay namespace compiled (exit 0), then exited 1 at 20 tests / 141 assertions with 1 failure. Both failures were the new tooth.
- GREEN with the fix: the JVM replay namespace exited 0 at 23 / 160.
- jvm-epoch (`clojure -M:test`) exited 0 at 548 tests / 7352 assertions. rf2-c74lr landed at 546 / 7343, so the difference is exactly the two new deftests.
- The cljs lane exited 0 at 12084 tests / 60250 assertions, with the run naming this worktree's config.
- clj-kondo reports 0 errors and 0 warnings. Splint exits 0; all 9 of its style warnings predate this change.
- The retired-spellings, composition-vocab, image-keys and require-alias-dialect ratchets all exit 0.

ITEM READ: the history was walked to creation. There are 6 snapshots, all byte-identical on the text fields, with no notes and no children. The brief and the item agreed.
FIXED in PR #9793 (worker epochgc-a), merged by the mayor on the five-clause criterion as trunk `a2e28855fe`. Epoch-only: no core, router, spec or public-API change.

CAUSE, confirmed at source: replay took the FIRST `:rf.event/dispatched` id seen on its own thread as its own dispatch. A quiet parent's own emit and its child's enqueue emit are both suppressed, so the first id to arrive was the traced child's enqueue of the grandchild, and the grandchild's epoch came back as the replay's.

FIX: replay's observation now binds to the replay's OWN dispatch through the parent link Spec 009 already defines on every dispatch (`:rf.trace/parent-dispatch-id`). At arming, `state.cljc` records the dispatch-id of the handler scope replay runs in (nil at top level); the replay's own dispatch carries exactly that as its parent, while anything its cascade queues names a run inside the cascade. In `note-observed-dispatch!` the first id from the arming thread decides once: taken if its parent matches, otherwise the slot closes empty and replay returns `:epoch-id nil`. Closing is safe because the replay's own emit always precedes its drain. `capture.cljc` passes the parent id through. No event-vector matching; thread isolation, listener nesting, strict replay inputs and `finally` cleanup unchanged.

EVIDENCE: two new deftests in `implementation/epoch/test/re_frame/epoch_replay_cljs_test.cljc`, each on JVM and CLJS — the quiet parent -> traced child -> traced grandchild regression (all three run, only source records exist, replay returns nil) and a traced two-level control returning the new parent record; the child-only quiet case kept. Red before the fix (JVM exit 1, 23/160, 1 failure; CLJS exit 1, 20/141, 1 failure — both resolving to the grandchild); green after (JVM replay ns exit 0; `jvm-epoch` 548/7352 exit 0; `cljs` 12084/60250 exit 0).

description:

The repair landed in `make-ratom-adapter` in `implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs` — deliberately there rather than in `make-ratom-spine` — because that is where the injected activation op arrives, so stock Reagent and reagent-slim share one repair with no second subscription algorithm and no edit in either adapter namespace. reagent-slim already injects `:activate-reaction! reagent2.ratom/activate!`, and its lane was green in PR #9768's run.

WHAT IS MISSING IS THE ASSERTION, NOT THE FIX. Nothing in the slim tree pins that behaviour, so a future change to the shared helper could regress reagent-slim silently while the stock-Reagent test stays green.

Keep the same six pins. PR #9768's body and rf2-gwye.47's notes describe the intended test.

THIS IS A TEST-ONLY BEAD. If you find yourself editing `spine.cljs` or either adapter's source, STOP and report — the fix is already in and a second one would be a duplicate subscription path, which is precisely what #9768's placement avoided.

THE CONTROL IS THE DELIVERABLE. Show the new test RED against the pre-fix shared helper (revert `activating-subscribe-container`'s wiring in your worktree, run, restore) and GREEN after. Verify the restore by hashing the bytes against the committed blob, and treat a match by EITHER the default or the --no-filters form as a good restore.

title: story spec 017: name :rf.error/story-check-unknown and state that check atoms run as terminal expectations
description:

Its subsection on :compose resolution names :rf.error/story-compose-unknown for an unresolved :compose id. The section "Checks" (under "Checks and assertions") says only that checks preserve identity, inherit and compose, and that a failed check shows both the check id and the underlying records.

GAP: after PR #9717 the plan compiler does two things no spec sentence states:
- it rejects an unresolved :checks id (own, inherited or composed) with :rf.error/story-check-unknown;
- the runtime dispatches a check's atoms after the script, as terminal expectations beside :assertions, against the final settled state and deduped with them.

SMALLEST CHANGE: add two sentences.
- Under the :compose resolution subsection or under Checks: every :checks id MUST resolve to a registered check, or plan construction fails with :rf.error/story-check-unknown.
- Under Checks: a check's assertion atoms run as terminal expectations, with the terminal :assertions, after the script settles.

GATE: mkdocs build --strict (the spec tree is staged into the docs build by mkdocs_hooks.py) and scripts/check_doc_slugs.py.

title: docs: an under-indented fence ends its list — 12 measured splits where steps restart at 1
description:
A fence indented FEWER THAN FOUR COLUMNS under a list marker at column 0 ends the list.
python-markdown wants the child block at owner_indent + 4; at 1, 2 or 3 columns it is not a child
of the item, so the list CLOSES and the markers after it open a NEW list that restarts at 1.

Both lists render as valid markup, so `mkdocs build --strict` has no warning to promote and both
link gates pass -- the same silent-by-construction shape as the lazy-continuation class rf2-2brt
just cleared, reached through indentation instead of a missing blank line.

THE WORKED CASE, measured end to end. `spec/012-Routing.md`, the "Mechanism" ordered list:

    line 1098   `2. **Capture.**`          marker at indent 0
    line 1100   fence at indent 3          <-- wants 4
    line 1105   closing fence at indent 3
    line 1107   `3. **Threading.**`
    line 1119   `4. **Validation.**`

Rendered through the gate's own mkdocs config loader, the section emits TWO `<ol>` elements:

    ol1 direct items: Allocation, Capture
    ol2 direct items: Threading, Validation, (nested) Match, Mismatch

NEITHER `<ol>` CARRIES A `start` ATTRIBUTE, so a reader sees "1. Allocation, 2. Capture,
1. Threading, 2. Validation". Steps 3 and 4 present themselves as steps 1 and 2 of a second list.
Adding ONE COLUMN to the two fence lines merges it back to a single `<ol>`, and the `<li>` set is
IDENTICAL either way -- six items before, six after -- so the repair rejoins without adding,
dropping or re-nesting anything.

=== THE NUMBERS, AND WHICH OF THEM IS MEASURED ===

CONFIRMED BY RENDER -- 12 REAL SPLITS ACROSS 10 FILES. Method: re-indent every candidate fence in
a file to owner_indent + 4, render both versions through `_load_renderer()` in
`scripts/check_flattened_lists.py` (mkdocs' OWN config loader, eleven extensions -- NOT
`extensions=['extra']`), and count `<ol>` + `<ul>`. A DROP is the defect; no drop means the
candidates in that file split nothing.

    docs/EP/EP-0004-subscription-inputs.md                     lists 18 -> 16   (2)
    docs/core/flows.md                                          lists  9 ->  7   (2)
    spec/005-StateMachines.md                                   lists 155 -> 154 (1)   HOT ZONE
    spec/009-Instrumentation.md                                 lists 74 -> 73   (1)   HOT ZONE
    spec/012-Routing.md                                         lists 63 -> 62   (1)
    spec/Pattern-NineStates.md                                  lists 19 -> 18   (1)
    skills/re-frame-migration/references/guided-handlers-state.md  lists 14 -> 13 (1)
    skills/re-frame2/references/fundamentals/frames.md          lists  7 ->  6   (1)
    skills/reagent-migration/references/catalog-judgment.md     lists  9 ->  8   (1)
    docs/design/freehand/decisions/D004-state-identity-and-addressing.md  12 -> 11 (1)

ONE OF THE TWELVE IS NOT ON THE PUBLISHED SURFACE. `design/freehand/` is in `mkdocs.yml`'s
`exclude_docs` block, so that page never renders on the site and its split is invisible to every
reader -- and the tree is a retired subsystem besides. The published-surface figure is therefore
11 SPLITS ACROSS 9 FILES; decide deliberately whether the tenth is worth touching rather than
sweeping it in.

594 IS THE CANDIDATE COUNT AND IT IS NOT THE DEFECT COUNT. DO NOT REPAIR ON IT. The source-side
screen -- marker at indent I, then a fence at more than I but fewer than I+4 -- reads 594 sites
across 51 files, and the RENDER confirms 12. That is a 2% hit rate, and the concentration is
inverted from where a reader would look: `docs/api/re-frame.core.md` carries 112 candidates and
produces ZERO real splits, `re-frame.ssr.md` 59 and zero, `docs/story/api/runtime.md` 39 and zero.
The reason is structural rather than lucky -- in those pages the under-indented fence is the LAST
block of its item, so there is no following marker for the closed list to strand. A fence only
splits a list when the list CONTINUES past it.

I filed this only after confirming by render, because a bare 594 in a bead is read downstream as
measured fact and would have sent a worker at a 98% phantom.

=== THE WORK ===

For each confirmed file, add the columns that bring every SPLITTING fence to owner_indent + 4 --
opening AND closing fence, both lines, or the block does not close where it opened. Leave the 582
non-splitting candidates alone: they are correct as written, and "fixing" them is churn against
pages that render properly today.

The instrument is not a diff count. VERIFY EACH FILE BY RENDER, both directions: the `<ol>`+`<ul>`
count must DROP by the stated amount, and the `<li>` multiset must be UNCHANGED. An `<li>` count
that moves means the repair re-nested something, which is the failure mode to watch -- over-indent
past owner_indent + 4 and the fence becomes a child of the wrong item, or worse, a code block.

`spec/005-StateMachines.md` and `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` are HOT-ZONE files on CLAUDE.md's
roster, so this is ONE worker for the whole set, sequential, never split across two.

NO AUTOMATED GATE COVERS THIS CLASS. `check_flattened_lists.py` grades consecutive ITEM pairs and
an escape splits the root list rather than failing its pair test, so it reads 0 here before and
after; the two link gates never look at list structure; and `mkdocs build --strict` has no warning
to promote because both renderings are valid markup. Verify by hand, by render, and say so in the
PR body. Whether this class earns a permanent gate is rf2-jzv2's open half and is NOT decided here.

RELATED, NOT DUPLICATE: rf2-2brt (lazy continuation -- a missing BLANK LINE swallows a marker into
the paragraph above; 202 real, now zero) and rf2-jzv2 (the escaped-continuation instrument). This
bead is the INDENTATION sibling of that family. The `spec/012` case was found by listhot-a while
repairing rf2-2brt and deliberately left alone as out of class -- correctly.

title: machines: :id-prefix is accepted, documented and IGNORED on the declarative spawn path (+ spec/005:4558 names the wrong default)
description:
Two findings about `:id-prefix`, both surfaced by the rf2-1sip decision dossier (2026-09-09, worker spawncnt-a) and carved off rather than folded in. They share one surface and should ship together, but they are NOT the same kind of defect: one is code ignoring a documented option, the other is prose describing a default the code does not have.

## Finding 1 — `:id-prefix` IS ACCEPTED AND THEN IGNORED on the declarative `:spawn` path

MEASURED by JVM probe on trunk: a declarative `:spawn {:machine-id :pc/child :id-prefix :pc/mine}` allocates `:pc/child#1` under counter key `:pc/child`. The supplied prefix has no effect whatsoever.

The mechanism, at the line numbers the dossier measured:
  * `validation.cljc:1501` ACCEPTS `:id-prefix`, so nothing complains at registration.
  * `spec/005-StateMachines.md:2798`, `:2972` and `:4558` DOCUMENT it.
  * `allocate-one` (`transition.cljc:2350-2360`) reads `:machine-id`, not `:id-prefix`.
  * `transition.cljc:2402` and `:2471` then overwrite `:id-prefix` with the child's `:machine-id` anyway.

So an author reading the spec, writing the documented option, and getting no error has been silently ignored. That is the worst shape a knob can have: it fails in the reassuring direction at authoring time and is diagnosable only by reading the allocator.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS, and this is the reason it is filed rather than mentioned: `:id-prefix` is the only namespacing escape an author has from the collision rf2-1sip documents — two parents spawning the same child type both get `<child-type>#1` and silently share one actor. rf2-1sip's option (f) plus a working `:id-prefix` is explicitly the smaller, stance-consistent alternative to its recommended option (e). **So whether this is repaired, and how, depends on how rf2-1sip is ruled.** If (e) is taken, `<type>#<n>` becomes frame-unique and `:id-prefix` becomes a convenience rather than a workaround; if (f) is taken alone, `:id-prefix` becomes load-bearing and must work.

## Finding 2 — `spec/005:4558` describes a default the implementation does not have, and the implementation is right

`005:4558` says `:id-prefix` "defaults to the parent's `:machine-id`". The implementation uses the CHILD's `:machine-id`. The implementation's choice is the sane one — a generated address naming the child's type is what every existing `<type>#<n>` literal in the tree assumes, and naming the parent's type would make sibling children of different types collide with each other.

**So this one is a prose correction, not a behaviour change.** Do not "fix" the code to match the sentence.

## Sequencing, and why this bead is not dispatchable today

- **Finding 1 is HELD on Mike's ruling for rf2-1sip.** Do not repair it before that ruling; the repair's shape is decided by it.
- **Finding 2 touches `spec/005-StateMachines.md`, a hot-zone one-toucher.** At filing it was held by `worker/regions-a` on PR #9513. Re-measure ownership at dispatch rather than trusting this line.
- Both citations were measured at trunk `61fcf65238` and `spec/005` line numbers on this file have moved twice in one day (PR #9500 +17, PR #9508 +38 more). **Re-measure every number here before acting on it.**

## Gates

`spec/` is staged into the strict build by `mkdocs_hooks.py`, so `python -m mkdocs build --strict` covers `spec/005` (bare `mkdocs` exits 127 on this box). `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` covers its anchors and repo-relative targets. Note that `scripts/check_retired_spellings.py` does NOT reach `spec/005` — its `.md` reach is `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` only, so its green there is vacuous. Finding 1's repair, if ruled in, is `implementation/machines` `clojure -M:test`.

title: CLAUDE.md: record the two bd show false zeros (word-wrap, backtick stripping) in the instrument catalogue
description:
`bd show` RENDERS a bead's notes; it does not print the field. Two distinct false zeros
follow, and both bite the exact act every ruling and recovery brief prescribes — "verify by
effect: probe `bd show` for known content".

(1) WORD WRAP. A probe string longer than the render width is split across lines, so a
grep for it reads 0 on content that landed correctly. Hit three independent agents in one
session (2026-09-08). Mitigation in use: flatten whitespace before probing, and take a
negative control string you did NOT write.

(2) BACKTICK STRIPPING — new, and not previously recorded. Measured 2026-09-08 while
auditing rf2-ornb's notes for the `--notes` backtick-substitution damage: a backtick probe
read 0 off `bd show`, while the field itself carried 168 literal backticks and was
byte-identical to its source (`cmp` clean). The zero was the renderer, not the note.

Both fail in the REASSURING direction for a verification step whose whole purpose is to
catch silent loss — an agent that has just been warned about a silent note-damage mode
reads a 0 and concludes the damage happened, or (worse, in the other direction) probes for
content it did write, reads 0, and re-appends a duplicate.

THE GUARD: read the FIELD, not the rendering.
    bd show <id> --json | jq -r '.[0].notes'
Probe that. Same rule this repo already states for `.beads/issues.jsonl` (select on the
identity field, never grep the rendered line).

WORK: add this to CLAUDE.md's instrument-misreporting catalogue under Workflow, as a
labelled item alongside the existing (a)-(j). It is the same class and belongs in the same
list. Keep the measured figures and both directions.

title: ssr-node render(): validation/clone TOCTOU reads the caller's object twice, and a throwing postMessage leaves the isolate stuck busy
description:
FOUND 2026-09-05 by the ssrnode-c worker while landing rf2-2hmg (PR #9297). Inside the fence but outside that bead's question, so reported rather than fixed. TWO separate defects in one file, filed together because they share a cause: `render()` does work in an order that assumes `postMessage` cannot throw.

DEFECT 1 — VALIDATION/CLONE TOCTOU. `validatePartition` returns the CALLER'S OWN OBJECT rather than a copy, so the validator and the structured clone read one object TWICE. An accessor can therefore be a well-formed string on read 1 and unclonable on read 2. This is not theoretical: it is the mechanism the worker used to reach `service.cjs:108`, driving a real non-Refusal through the real Service with a caller-authored Symbol, and observing it cross onto a public refusal as `"DataCloneError: Symbol(...) could not be cloned."`.

DEFECT 2 — STUCK ISOLATE. `render()` sets `pendingRender` BEFORE `postMessage`, so a throwing `postMessage` leaves the isolate marked busy until the deadline fires. The window is bounded by the deadline rather than unbounded, which is why this is P3 and not higher.

WHY THEY ARE ONE BEAD: both are `render()`'s ordering, and a repair to either that does not consider the other is likely to move the problem rather than close it. Defect 1's fix (clone or freeze before validating) may make defect 2 unreachable by removing the throw; defect 2's fix (set `pendingRender` after a successful post) closes it regardless. Decide whether one repair subsumes the other, and say so.

BOTH FAIL CLOSED AND SELF-LIMIT — this is P3 deliberately. Defect 1 produces a refusal rather than a wrong render; defect 2 releases at the deadline. Neither corrupts output. Under the stance's "don't litigate the minutiae", a verified "the bounded window is acceptable" for defect 2 IS a legitimate outcome if the repair costs more than the exposure — but say so with the deadline value quoted, rather than leaving it unexamined.

CHECK BEFORE ACTING — these are the worker's claims, not findings of mine. Confirm `validatePartition` really does return the caller's object (not a copy) at tip; confirm `pendingRender` is really set before the `postMessage` call; and re-derive both line numbers, since #9297 rewrote parts of this file.

A TEST-DESIGN NOTE THE WORKER ESTABLISHED AND WORTH REUSING: the witness for defect 1 must assert the partition value is READ TWICE, because only the clone reads it again — a test that merely passes a bad value proves nothing about the TOCTOU. That control is fix-independent, so it stays valid after the repair.

FENCE. IN: `implementation/ssr-node/**`. OUT: `spec/Conventions.md` catalogues the `:rf.ssr-node/*` code MEMBERS and is hot-zone — if a member changes, that is a separate sequenced edit, not part of this. #9297 established the bar: it added and removed no member, so no spec edit was owed.
notes:
2026-09-05 — WORKED, PR #9304 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9304), branch worker/ssrnode-d. NOT CLOSED; awaiting merge.

BOTH PREMISES VERIFIED AT SOURCE at tip 68961fe037, line numbers re-derived after #9297:
- validatePartition really did return the caller's own object — protocol.cjs:490 read `request[partitionField]`, :533 returned it unchanged.
- pendingRender really was set before the post — isolate.cjs:222 assigned it, :230 called postMessage.

BOTH FIXED. NEITHER REPAIR SUBSUMES THE OTHER, and the answer to the bead's question is that fixing one and citing it as cover for the other would have moved the problem. Read-once removes the CALLER's route to the throw, so through service.renderFrames defect 2 became unreachable — but not closed, because Isolate.render() takes an unvalidated request and the reorder closes the stranding whatever throws. Defect 2's fix alone would have left a well-formed request still refused for a value nobody validated.

DEFECT 1 IS WIDER THAN FILED. validateRequest built its returned request from fresh reads for every scalar too. Measured on the unfixed tree, reads per field on one validating request: entry 7, timeoutMs 5, buildId 4, args 3, requestId 3. The repair is the principle rather than the instance — read once, validate what you read, return what you validated — so the partitions come back as fresh objects of the checked values and no second read is left to disagree with the first. No defensive copy, no freeze, no re-check.

DEFECT 2's EXPOSURE IS WORSE THAN "a bounded busy window", which is why it was not accepted as-is under don't-litigate-the-minutiae. Deadline quoted: createService's defaultTimeoutMs = 1000, maxTimeoutMs = 5000 — so at most 5000 ms, 1000 ms by default. But `dead` stayed false, so pool.release() returned the isolate to the idle list STILL MARKED BUSY and the next caller was refused SERVICE_SATURATED by an isolate doing nothing; then the deadline's own callback ran _terminateWorker(), killing a healthy thread, forcing a pool replacement, and burning one further request on ISOLATE_LOST before it healed. Fix cost: three lines of reordering, no new state.

REDS QUOTED BEFORE THE FIX (each witness written first, watched fail, then fixed): "the normalized request must not alias the caller's own partition object"; "the request must carry the EDN text that was validated" with actual Symbol(rf2-ey07-second-read); "these fields were read more than once" listing entry (7) buildId (4) args (3) requestId (3) timeoutMs (5); and "a post that threw must leave nothing in flight", true !== false.

THE READ-COUNT WITNESS #9297 ESTABLISHED IS KEPT and now reads 1 where it read 2, with the render succeeding on the first-read value. egress §7's other three rows went red on the fix because the fix removed their route — that red is the evidence the caller route is closed. The last-resort arm is NOT removed (it is what guarantees renderFrames throws nothing but a Refusal); with no caller able to reach it, it is driven at the seam it guards, a Service over a stand-in pool, and §7's header says plainly that this is the weaker witness rather than dressing it up.

A postMessage that throws still rejects RAW, deliberately: service.cjs's last receiver is the only thing that both writes the operator's stderr copy and publishes the contract's wording, so building a Refusal in the isolate would have left the operator no copy at all. render()'s docstring now names the exception instead of overstating itself.

NO SPEC EDIT OWED: no :rf.ssr-node/* code member added or removed, the same bar #9297 met. Nothing outside implementation/ssr-node/** touched. service.cjs's comment and the README both described the closed route in the present tense and were corrected in the same commit.

title: spec/009 says recover-but-emit is frame-destroyed's ONLY behaviour and there is ONE surface — the SSR require-live-frame! precondition throws it
description:
FOUND 2026-09-05 by the spec006-a worker while landing rf2-pyav (PR #9294), and CONFIRMED AT SOURCE BY THE MAYOR. It is a correction to a premise I put in FOUR briefs across the rf2-6g6e family, so it is filed rather than left in a worker report.

THE PREMISE I PROPAGATED: "there is no live throwing surface for :rf.error/frame-destroyed at all". That is what spec/009-Instrumentation.md's frame-destroyed row says, in two places, as a WHOLE-CATEGORY claim:
  - "The retired re-frame.ui (frame) operation bundle was a SECOND, throwing surface for this category until it went with that artefact on 2026-08-16 (rf2-0yp7w); nothing replaced it, so RECOVER-BUT-EMIT IS NOW THIS CATEGORY'S ONLY BEHAVIOUR."
  - and in the Recovery cell: "ONE surface: the retired ui (frame) bundle threw instead of recovering".

THE CONTRADICTING SITE, verified at tip: implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/render_state.cljc.
  :299  (defn- require-live-frame! [frame-id])
  :302  names :rf.error/frame-destroyed
  :411  documents it plainly — "that is not live THROWS :rf.error/frame-destroyed"
  called at :351, :416 and :422.
Control that the instrument is honest: the same grep finds 13 defn forms in that file.

So a live, non-retired site throws this exact error id today, and 009 says the category has only one behaviour and one surface.

WHAT IS AND IS NOT IN DISPUTE. This is very likely a WORDING defect in 009 rather than a defect in the SSR code: require-live-frame! is an SSR PRECONDITION, not an incarnation fence, and the reasons 009 gives for recover-over-throw (teardown and hot-reload races are indistinguishable from real use-after-destroy bugs; these ops fire from host cleanup where a throw breaks the teardown) do not obviously apply to an SSR render entry point, which is a synchronous call from application code with a caller who can handle it. The rf2-pyav worker took exactly this reading and scoped its own spec/006 sentence to "incarnation fence" so 006 is true without overreaching — which is why #9294 is unaffected either way.

THE RULING NEEDED, and it is a spec-wording call rather than a code change unless the second option is chosen:
  (a) NARROW 009's claim to the OPERATION realms it is actually about (dispatch / dispatch-sync / subscribe against a destroyed frame), and say explicitly that the SSR precondition is a separate, deliberately-throwing surface with its own rationale. Smallest change; keeps both documents true.
  (b) RULE THE SSR SITE WRONG and make it recover-and-emit like the rest. Much larger, changes runtime behaviour on a production path, and needs its own argument about what an SSR render should do when handed a dead frame — returning partial markup may be worse than throwing.
  (c) LEAVE 009 AS IS on the grounds that "this category" means the operation-realm category and a reader should infer that. Not defensible: 009's own Recovery cell says "ONE surface" without qualification, and I read it the strong way four times today.

CHECK BEFORE ACTING: re-read 009's frame-destroyed row at tip (it is very long — the relevant clauses are "recover-but-emit is now this category's only behaviour" and the Recovery cell's "ONE surface"), and confirm require-live-frame! still throws rather than emits. Both were true at 2026-09-05 17:0x AUSEST.

A SECOND, LOOSER SITE reported by the same worker and NOT part of this bead: spec/006:1210 says subscribe "raises" :rf.error/frame-destroyed where :1166 correctly says it does not throw. That is loose wording rather than wrong-by-retirement, in a different passage, and it was deliberately left so the six rf2-kuky children queued behind spec/006 are not blocked. Fold it in only if the ruling touches 006 anyway.

FENCE if dispatched after a ruling: spec/009-Instrumentation.md is HOT-ZONE and single-toucher — seven rf2-kuky children want it. Under option (a) the diff is one row and should stay one row. Under option (b) the code half is implementation/ssr/** and must be sequenced separately from the spec half.

## Problem

`spec/API.md`'s `sensitive?` row and `spec/Privacy.md:81` say `rf/sensitive?` is "the framework-published predicate every forwarder composes against", replacing per-consumer reimplementations. At tip it has 0 direct tool callers; each tool reaches it through its own one-line alias:

- Xray `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/config.cljc:789-797` `sensitive-event?` → `(rf.privacy/sensitive? ev)`; sole caller `suppress-sensitive?` at :810.
- Story `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/config.cljc:666-674` `sensitive-event?` → `(rf.privacy/sensitive? ev)`; sole caller `suppress-sensitive?` at :710.
- pair-MCP `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/sensitive.cljs:21-26` `sensitive-event?` → `(rf.mcp-base.sensitive/sensitive-event? ev)`; callers in the same file at :68 and :95.

The prompt counted four; at tip there are three thin delegations. The fourth candidate, `re-frame.mcp-base.sensitive/sensitive-event?` (`sensitive.cljc:174-187`), is NOT an alias: it is the zero-framework-dependency Node-bundle mirror with fail-closed semantics (truthy non-boolean ⇒ drop + log + `malformed-count`), which the review keeps.

The framework predicate itself (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/privacy.cljc:38-41`) is `(true? (:sensitive? trace-event))` — a malformed truthy stamp (`"true"`, `:yes`) passes as NON-sensitive, the fail-open reading mcp-base's docstring (`sensitive.cljc:144-172`) explicitly refuses.

## Evidence

Predicate census (`^\(defn-? (sensitive\?|sensitive-event\?|sensitive-stamp\?|include-sensitive\?|suppress-sensitive\?)`, non-test src): `privacy.cljc:38`; mcp-base `sensitive.cljc:144, :174`; pair-MCP `sensitive.cljs:21`; story-mcp `args.cljc:65` (`include-sensitive?` — parses the MCP arg, not a stamp predicate, keep); Story `config.cljc:655, :666, :688`; Xray `config.cljc:781, :789, :799`. Direct callers of `rf/sensitive?` / `rf.privacy/sensitive?` in tools: the two aliases only. `skills/re-frame2/references/tooling/story-recorder.md:46` teaches `(rf/sensitive? trace-event)` — the teaching is right, the code goes round it.

## Target API

```clojure
;; privacy.cljc — fail-closed, one predicate
(defn sensitive? [trace-event]
  (and (map? trace-event)
       (let [s (:sensitive? trace-event)]
         (cond (true? s) true (false? s) false (nil? s) false :else true))))
;; Xray / Story: (rf.privacy/sensitive? ev) inline in suppress-sensitive?; the alias defns go.
;; pair-MCP: call rf.mcp-base.sensitive/sensitive-event? directly at :68 and :95; the alias goes.
```

mcp-base keeps `sensitive-stamp?` / `sensitive-event?` (its bundle cannot load `re-frame.privacy`) and its `malformed-count` / `reset-malformed-count!` counters — those are envelope bookkeeping and out of scope (the fable proposed demoting the counters to private/test; leave them, zero cost).

## Corroboration

One-reviewer (fable §The problem para 4, §Simpler elegant target "Predicate" row). Codex did not comment on the predicate. The fail-closed hardening matches a ruling already made for mcp-base (`sensitive.cljc:144-172` docstring) and can only drop MORE, never less.

## Deletion list

`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/config.cljc:789-797`; `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/config.cljc:666-674`; `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/sensitive.cljs:21-26` (+ the "Delegates to …" docstring sentences at :85 and :115 that name the alias).

## Consumers to migrate

Xray `config.cljc:810`; Story `config.cljc:710`; pair-MCP `sensitive.cljs:68, :95`. Tests naming the aliases (re-measure with `git grep -n "sensitive-event?" -- tools/*/test`): expect Xray `trace_collector` tests, Story `config` / `recorder` tests, pair-MCP `sensitive_test.cljs` / `strip_sensitive` tests.

## Spec, docs, examples, skills, tests

- `spec/API.md` `sensitive?` row (:728 region) — "replaces per-consumer reimplementations" becomes true; add "fail-closed: a non-boolean truthy stamp counts as sensitive" (hot-zone, one line); `spec/Privacy.md:81` same sentence; `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` §Privacy (:2809-2846) if it states the `(true? …)` semantics (grep `true?` in that range; hot-zone).
- `docs/api/re-frame.core.md:1155` example — add a malformed-stamp line.
- Skills: `story-recorder.md:46` unchanged.
- Tests to add: `implementation/core/test/re_frame/privacy_test` (or the nearest privacy suite): `(rf/sensitive? {:sensitive? "true"})` ⇒ true, `{:sensitive? :yes}` ⇒ true, `{:sensitive? false}` / `{}` / non-map ⇒ false; Xray and Story `suppress-sensitive?` tests still green.
- `spec/api-manifest.edn`: `re-frame.core/sensitive?` row unchanged; Xray / Story config manifests — if `sensitive-event?` is rowed in a tool manifest (`tools/xray/spec`, `tools/story/spec`), delete the row.
- Migration README: none.

## Sequencing and hot-zone

No hot-zone file beyond one-line touches to `spec/API.md` / `spec/009` — coordinate the line with whichever egress bead holds those files at dispatch time, or land this bead after egress.3. Parallel-safe on the tool sources.

## Risks

Strictly stricter. The only behavioural delta is a malformed stamp now suppressing in Xray / Story panels, matching what the MCP wire already does.

title: Clarify boot pattern callback locals in re-frame2 skill
description:

title: reagent-slim ratom runtime: replace compressed private helper names
description:
## Finding

The private reactive-kernel helpers in `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/ratom.cljs` use compressed names inherited from an early implementation: `arr-len`, `arr-eq`, `in-context`, `add-w`, `remove-w`, and `notify-w`. ## Evidence and ambiguity cost

- Lines 75-85 implement array length plus element-by-element `identical?`; `arr-eq` can be read as Clojure value equality even though it is stricter identity comparison.
- Lines 87-108 use `in-context` only to call the Reaction body under the dynamic context; the preposition does not disclose that this is a callback runner.
- Lines 120-141 define the watch mutation/notification trio. `add-w`/`remove-w` also invalidate `watchesArr`, while `notify-w` materializes that cache and invokes every watcher; none of those effects is visible in the abbreviations.
- Repository-wide exact searches show all six definitions and calls are confined to this namespace. Targeted `git log -S` traces them to the initial Stage 4-A implementation, with no compatibility migration or external-consumer history.

## Recommendation

Rename them to `array-length`, `arrays-identical?`, `call-with-ratom-context`, `add-watch-entry!`, `remove-watch-entry!`, and `notify-watches!`. Expand nearby one-letter helper locals where their roles are otherwise unclear, and update in-slice explanatory/test comments.

## Contracts and risk

All candidates are private Vars. Do not touch `pr-atom`; its unused argument is independently owned by `rf2-6r9j.29`.

## Duplicate search

All-status bead data was searched by exact symbol and by ratom/reactive-helper naming concepts. No existing bead owns these renames; `rf2-6r9j.29` is the separate vestigial `pr-atom` receiver removal.

title: Repair stale implementation security catalogue entries
description:
## Finding

`implementation/SECURITY.md` is an intended catalogue of concrete shipped controls, but its inventory contains a duplicate row and several stale/incorrect control descriptions.

## Evidence

- The `project-egress` control appears twice, at lines 25 and 41, with the same bead and implementation link; both rows entered together in commit `926ac87cb2`.
- Lines 45-46 assign Reagent Slim controls to `day8/re-frame2-reagent`; the published coordinate in `implementation/reagent-slim/deps.edn` is `day8/reagent-slim`.
- Line 46 says `reserved-prop-key?` checks “over set `reserved-prop-keys`”. Since commit `5eb32a331d`, the predicate itself is the roster (three identity comparisons), and its source docstring explicitly records removal of the set.
- The introduction says “Four sections” while listing five. The audit heading says “38-bead audit trail”, but a deterministic first-column count yields 49 table rows and 45 distinct `rf2-*` IDs; the nearby statement of 45 distinct IDs is current.

## Impact

The source controls remain live, but the security catalogue misattributes an artefact, describes an implementation that no longer exists, and gives conflicting provenance totals. That weakens the document as an audit and release-review index.

## Recommendation

Remove the duplicate catalogue row; correct the Reagent Slim coordinate and predicate description; and update the section/count labels from the table's live inventory.

## Risks and contracts

This is catalogue repair, not authorization to remove or weaken source controls. Preserve all distinct security checks and historical bead/provenance links, retain the correct 45-distinct-ID statement, and make no runtime or gate behavior changes.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `project-egress` has one catalogue entry and no distinct control/provenance row is lost.
2. Reagent Slim rows name the published `day8/reagent-slim` coordinate and describe the current predicate implementation without referring to a removed reserved-key set.
3. The introductory section count and audit-trail heading agree with the live document/table inventory, while the correct 45-distinct-ID statement remains accurate.
4. Source controls and gate behavior are unchanged, and relevant Markdown link/table validation passes.
close_reason:
PR #9092 (worker/catvest-a), head 8b3ffa3fe1. All four evidence claims re-derived at source; all four held. Two path details in the bead text were slightly off — noted below.

1. DUPLICATE ROW — CONFIRMED, MERGED rather than deleted. project-egress appeared at SECURITY.md:25 and :41, same fn, same owning namespace (re-frame.projection), both entered by 926ac87cb2. The surviving row sits at the first position (natural order: value primitive, then record primitive) and carries every clause of BOTH — the :rf.egress/* profile + known :frame resolution, frame-owned classification, delegation of every tree-shaped slot to elide-wire-value, "the required step before any off-box sink" (row 41's phrasing), and the "(Spec 015 SS-Direct reads)" fail-closed pointer that only row 41 had. Nothing distinct lost. Acceptance 1 met.

2. REAGENT-SLIM COORDINATE — CONFIRMED, with a path correction. The bead cites implementation/reagent-slim/deps.edn; the real path is implementation/ADAPTERS/reagent-slim/deps.edn (git ls-files finds no implementation/reagent-slim). The claim itself is exactly right: that file's clein block declares lib day8/reagent-slim, while day8/re-frame2-reagent is a DIFFERENT artefact — implementation/adapters/reagent/deps.edn — whose own header calls itself the "stock Reagent adapter" and which the slim deps.edn calls "the bridge that continues to ship in parallel". So the two rows misattributed reagent2.dom.server and reagent2.impl.template to the bridge. Both now name day8/reagent-slim.

3. PREDICATE DESCRIPTION — CONFIRMED. reserved-prop-key? at implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/impl/template.cljs:243 is three identity comparisons, and its docstring header reads "THE ROSTER IS THE FUNCTION BODY (rf2-lhdp0)" with the costing that motivated dropping the PersistentHashSet. No reserved-prop-keys var exists anywhere in the artefact — grep returns only reserved-prop-key? call sites. The row now describes the shipped implementation AND records that the set was removed under rf2-lhdp0, so the history survives. Acceptance 2 met.

4. COUNTS — CONFIRMED by independent count. "Four sections" introduced a five-item list, now "Five sections". The decisions log: 49 data rows (48 with an rf2- first cell plus one "EP-0017 Security Considerations" row), 51 total id occurrences, 45 DISTINCT — exactly the bead's figures. Heading moved 38-bead to 45-bead, the number the document's own next-but-one sentence ("All 45 distinct ids in the Bead column...") already asserted. That sentence is untouched and still accurate. Acceptance 3 met.

ANCHOR PROPAGATION — the part rf2-efioe explicitly deferred as "out of this fence". The heading is an anchor target: spec/Security.md links it at :19 and :302 and states the count in prose at :400; spec/Ownership.md:71 states it too. All four moved in the same commit. Not assumed — reverting just the two anchors made scripts/check_doc_slugs.py exit 1 naming both lines and the target file, so leaving them would have reddened the PR.

GATE — AND rf2-efioe'S CONCLUSION ABOUT THIS FILE IS NOW STALE. That bead's close reason recorded, with two sabotage measurements, that NO gate covered implementation/SECURITY.md. rf2-i4nb2 has since widened check_readme_links.py to git-tracked non-README markdown beside source, and CLAUDE.md now names this very file as an example of that third roster. Re-measured here: a broken target planted in the file makes scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci exit 1, naming file, line and missing path. Both gates green on the final tree; both controls reverted and the restores verified. Acceptance 4 met — the diff is prose only, no runtime or gate behaviour changed.

HAND-CHECKED, because no gate reads them: table column uniformity across all 15 blocks in implementation/SECURITY.md, all 15 in spec/Security.md and the 1 in spec/Ownership.md — 0 mismatches, which also proves no edited cell gained an unescaped pipe.

FLAGGED, NOT TAKEN: spec/Ownership.md:70 carries "the 38-decision bead log" describing spec/Security.md's OWN decisions log — 49 rows there too by the same count method. Different catalogue, different owning document, outside this bead. Worth a follow-up.

title: Remove the security tier's fixed-corpus pseudo-property
description:
## Scope

Remove or genuinely diversify the pseudo-property `every-schema-kind-rejects-every-malformed-schema` and its private `gen-malformed-schema` from `implementation/security/test/re_frame/security/fail_closed_invariant_security_cljs_test.cljc`.

## Evidence

`malformed-schemas` is a closed six-value vector. `boundary-seam-never-passes-a-malformed-schema` already exhaustively invokes `validate-with-registered-fn` for every one of those six values. `meta-bearing-surfaces-never-pass-a-malformed-schema` already exhaustively invokes `validate-event!`, `validate-fx!`, and `validate-sub!` for every one. The later "property" wraps that exact vector in `gen/gen-elem` and randomly re-invokes the same four functions 80 times; it cannot produce a new schema shape and, unlike the earlier `doseq` checks, its sampling does not itself guarantee that every corpus member was selected despite its title. `app-db` has a separate exhaustive test and is not part of the pseudo-property.

The test came in with the exhaustive rows in commit d4a33175d7; no later production contract made its sample distinct. Current JVM and CLJS security lanes are green (94/723 and 95/730 respectively), confirming the suite is live rather than orphaned.

## Impact

The row adds repeated validator work and expected malformed-schema emissions to both runtimes while supplying no additional input or invariant. It also presents random sampling as stronger "every malformed schema" evidence than the exhaustive loops immediately above it.

## Recommendation

Delete the generator binding and redundant test. If a future contributor can define a generator that produces malformed schema structures outside the named corpus, add that as a genuinely generative property instead of sampling the fixed vector.

## Risks / contracts

Retain the exhaustive boundary, event/fx/sub, app-db, and throwing-validator tests. Do not weaken the fail-closed contract or remove named malformed cases.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `gen-malformed-schema` and the fixed-corpus re-sampling test are removed, or the generator is changed to produce demonstrably new malformed structures not already exhaustively enumerated.
2. Every entry in `malformed-schemas` remains exhaustively checked against `validate-with-registered-fn`, `validate-event!`, `validate-fx!`, and `validate-sub!`.
3. The app-db malformed-schema and throwing-validator fail-closed rows remain.
4. Both `clojure -M:test` from `implementation/security` and `npm run test:security` pass.
close_reason: PR #9111. Deleted gen-malformed-schema and every-schema-kind-rejects-every-malformed-schema. Premise confirmed at source: gen/gen-elem over the closed six-value malformed-schemas vector cannot produce a shape outside the corpus, and the two doseq tests immediately above already invoke all four validators (validate-with-registered-fn; validate-event!/-fx!/-sub!) over every member exhaustively, so the property asserted a strict subset. Chose deletion over honest relabelling because the invariant is asserted more strongly four lines above -- an honest label would have named a duplicate. Retained the exhaustive boundary-seam, meta-bearing, app-db and throwing-validator rows and every named malformed case. Also corrected the ns docstring, which claimed generated coverage for EVERY boundary. Security JVM 92/717 and npm run test:security 93/724, both 0 failures 0 errors; the -2 tests / -6 assertions against the bead's recorded 94/723 and 95/730 baselines are exactly this row plus rf2-6r9j.94's. title: Drop unused spec-resource roots from the Hicasso bench classpath

- The sole live spec-resource consumer is re-frame.api-manifest.cljs-publics under implementation/scripts/api-manifest/probe/src. That directory is not on the standalone bench source path, and neither API-probe macro consumer is in the bench tree.
- The only spec/ strings in the bench tree are explanatory comments; no bench code reads spec data.
