title: Resources ledger: remove prune-record superseded by indexed batch pruning
description:
Evidence
- implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/work_ledger.cljc:516-526 defines prune-record, but exact repository search finds no production caller; its only executable consumer is a direct unit test at resources_work_ledger_cljs_test.cljc:843.
- The live operation is prune-terminal-for-key at work_ledger.cljc:548-599. It already holds byte work-id ids and removes all drop-ids in one reduce, then updates the inverse-index bucket in bulk; it cannot use prune-record, which accepts a structured work-id and recomputes its byte identity.
- Comments at work_ledger.cljc:416 and :562 nevertheless claim the live index is maintained through put-record/prune-record.
- Commit 0813d08aa1 introduced prune-record. Commit b0edd0265c added the inverse index and the batch prune implementation, leaving the now-superseded helper, its direct test, and stale comments.

Impact
A superseded single-row deletion API and its direct-only test imply that production pruning exercises code it bypasses. The stale comments obscure the actual atomic/batched inverse-index maintenance path and can misdirect future fixes.

Proposed disposition
Remove prune-record and replace/delete its direct-only test in favor of assertions through prune-terminal-for-key. Correct comments to name put-record plus the batch prune as the live incremental maintainers. Preserve bounded tail retention, non-terminal rows, byte-key isolation, index self-heal, and empty-bucket cleanup.

Risks
Do not regress the O(rows-for-key) index path into a whole-ledger scan or repeated structured-id conversion. Internal namespace consumers outside the repository are not a documented API but should be considered under normal release policy.
acceptance_criteria:
- prune-record is absent and comments describe the actual batch prune path.
- Tests through prune-terminal-for-key prove old terminal rows and their inverse-index members are removed, the retained tail/non-terminal rows survive, empty buckets disappear, and an absent installed index self-heals.
- Vector/list identity collision coverage and resource work-ledger JVM/CLJS suites pass.
close_reason: Removed work-ledger/prune-record (implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/work_ledger.cljc) and corrected the two comments (at the inverse-index preamble and inside prune-terminal-for-key) that named it as a live incremental index maintainer. Premise verified at tip by two instruments: fixed-string census over 4818 tracked files (line-oriented AND whitespace-flattened) and clj-kondo var-usage analysis. Both agree: ZERO production callers; the only executable consumer was the resources work-ledger test. Control put-record fired in both, across 6 namespaces incl. production events and mutation-events. CASCADE NOT NAMED IN THE BEAD: prune-record was the sole caller of the private index-remove, so that helper is removed with it (leaving it would have added an Unused-private-var warning - the after-lint confirms none appeared). The live path is unchanged: prune-terminal-for-key still holds byte work-id ids, removes all drop-ids in one reduce and updates the inverse-index bucket in bulk, with no regression to a whole-ledger scan or repeated structured-id conversion. WHAT THE DELETED TEST WAS GUARANTEEING, and whether the live path still does: prune-record's only executable consumer was NOT a dedicated unit test of it but one of three operations interleaved in a randomised 500-op property test asserting the incrementally-maintained inverse index equals a full rebuild after EVERY op, with no empty buckets. That property is retained over the two remaining operations, and the criteria this bead sets are already met by dedicated tests that were not touched: prune-terminal-for-key-matches-full-scan-reference (old terminal rows and their index members removed, retained tail and non-terminal rows survive), prune-self-heals-on-wholesale-installed-ledger (absent installed index self-heals), the randomised test's own no-empty-buckets assertion, and the event-level succeeded-completes-and-prunes-record / succeeded-prunes-old-terminal-rows-beyond-tail. No guarantee was dropped. Landed in PR #9079.

title: Retire the unconsumed routing plan-projection helper
description:
## Problem

`implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/resolve.cljc` carries an R0 `plan-projection` helper plus `r0-projection-keys`, but no runtime, Xray, trace tool, example, skill, or conformance consumer calls it. Its only caller is the dedicated unit test. Executed navigation exposes plan evidence through the separate live `plan-trace-tags` mapping, so the on-demand projection described as a tooling feature has no remaining/realized consumer.

## Evidence

- Repo-wide symbol search finds `plan-projection` only in `resolve.cljc`, the facade's internal-seam comment, and `routing_plan_seam_test.clj`; no `tools/`, `examples/`, `skills/`, or other implementation namespace calls it.
- `r0-projection-keys` occurs only in its definition, `plan-projection`, and that same unit test.
- Whole-routing `clj-kondo` analysis reports zero production-source usages of `plan-projection` and one test usage.
- `resolve.cljc:365+` implements `plan-trace-tags`, and `navigate.cljc` plus `url_change.cljc` call that mapping on real commit branches. It does not delegate to `plan-projection` because the trace projection intentionally summarizes/redacts carrier values.
- `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` names `:rf.route/planned`/`plan-trace-tags` as the observable projection. No API or tooling page promises the internal function.
- The API-manifest generator classifies `re-frame.routing.resolve` as internal, and the facade explicitly declines to re-export a RoutePlan constructor/projection (`routing.cljc:89-96`).
- Both helper and key list arrived in `da9c355466`; subsequent work made the trace mapping reachable but introduced no on-demand tool consumer.

## Impact

This is a test-maintained parallel feature with no consumer. It duplicates the notion of a plan projection while differing intentionally from the actual observable trace mapping, which makes future plan-field changes pay for and reason about a second projection that no product path reads. Its docstring currently overstates that Xray/trace tooling reads it.

## Proposed disposition

Remove `plan-projection`, `r0-projection-keys`, and the test whose only purpose is pinning them; update source comments that claim a tool reads the helper. Preserve the live route-plan construction and `plan-trace-tags` behavior. If an actual tool consumer is intentionally pending, require that concrete consumer and a supported access boundary to land before retaining this helper rather than keeping an internal speculative API indefinitely.

## Risks

Do not collapse `plan-trace-tags` into a raw `select-keys`: its bounded/redacted trace shape deliberately differs from the internal carrier-bearing plan. Preserve the `:rf.route/planned` contract and all real navigation-door coverage. Recheck out-of-repo/public-release commitments before deleting even though current API/manifests classify the namespace internal.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Either a concrete in-repo tooling consumer uses one supported on-demand plan-projection boundary, or the unused `plan-projection`/`r0-projection-keys` pair and its isolated test are removed; no source comment claims a nonexistent Xray/trace consumer.
2. `:rf.route/planned` remains emitted through the live `plan-trace-tags` path from every navigation commit door with its current bounded/redacted shape.
3. Routing plan-seam, navigation, URL-change, and instrumentation tests pass, including non-vacuity for the real emitted projection.
4. Repo-wide symbol and API-manifest checks show no orphaned reference or accidental public contract after the disposition.
close_reason: Removed in PR #9148 (worker/routevest-a). Premise re-verified at branch tip: plan-projection appeared only in resolve.cljc (its def plus two docstring mentions), the facade's internal-seam comment at routing.cljc:93, and routing_plan_seam_test.clj; r0-projection-keys only in its own def, plan-projection, and that same test. No tools/, examples/, skills/ or other implementation namespace called either. Deleted both plus the single deftest (plan-projection-exposes-only-the-r0-keys) that was their only consumer, and updated the test ns docstring's constructor list. Live behaviour preserved: plan-trace-tags is untouched and remains the ONE mapping both door commit branches emit :rf.route/planned through, per Spec 009; it was NOT collapsed into a raw select-keys, so its bounded/redacted shape is intact. Source comments no longer claim an Xray/trace consumer reads an on-demand helper — the facade seam comment now points at the trace, and a tombstone in resolve.cljc records that a future on-demand view must land with a concrete consumer rather than as a speculative internal helper. Gate: implementation/routing clojure -M:test exit 0, 553 tests / 3451 assertions / 0 failures. That gate was proven to read this branch by a planted fault in routing_plan_seam_test.clj, which turned it red at exactly the planted assertion with test/assertion counts unchanged; the file was restored and verified byte-identical by git blob hash.

title: core/derivation/graph.cljc:819-836 repeats rf2-yk2d's dead do-not-rename sentinel and its two false claims
description:
Found while fixing rf2-yk2d in PR #9070. implementation/core/src/re_frame/derivation/graph.cljc:819-836 carries the IDENTICAL defect that rf2-yk2d recorded for its egress sibling, and it was left standing because #9070's file fence did not include graph.cljc.

The site: `defonce ^:private bundle-isolation-sentinel "rf.derivation.graph/sentinel:rf2-6xm07h-2026-06-12:do-not-rename"` at :835-836, under a comment at :819-833 asserting the same two things rf2-yk2d measured false for egress:

  (1) "implementation/scripts/check-bundle-isolation.cjs greps the counter bundle for this exact string" - it does not. The roster entry for `derivation-graph` in check-bundle-isolation.cjs uses the sentinel `rf/family` ("re-frame.derivation.graph family marker"), not this literal.

  (2) "The string survives :advanced because string literals are not renamed" - the var is `^:private` and nothing consumes its value, so Closure DCEs it exactly as it does the egress one.

SAME HISTORY, and the tree already records it: commit 4e43784ec7 (2026-07-15, "test: require emitted bundle isolation controls") moved BOTH entries - egress and its derivation-graph sibling, the latter onto `rf/family` - off the planted strings when these controls became emitted-module greps. check-bundle-isolation.cjs's roster comment says so in as many words. Both vars were simply left behind; #9070 removed one.

MEASURE BEFORE ACTING, do not take this bead's word for it. The check that settles it is a fixed-string grep of the EMITTED module, never the .cljc:
  grep -cF "rf.derivation.graph/sentinel:rf2-6xm07h-2026-06-12:do-not-rename" implementation/out/bundle-isolation-positive-control/derivation-graph.js
Expect 0. Run a control in the same file with the same instrument - `grep -cF "rf/family"` on the same artefact - so a zero is a measurement rather than a broken needle. Build the artefact with `npm run test:bundle-isolation` (or just the `shadow-cljs release ... bundle-isolation-positive-control` half of it) first.

SUGGESTED FIX, matching what #9070 did for egress so the two siblings stay symmetrical: remove the var, and replace the comment with one that says the sentinel for this namespace is not in this file, names `rf/family` as the literal the gate actually greps, and records that the defonce was removed. Weigh removal against keeping-and-correcting on its own merits - #9070's reasoning for removing was that a corrected comment still leaves the false `do-not-rename` instruction inside the string literal itself, and that the roster already teaches a removed literal perfectly well (its first named trap, `re-frame.derivation.egress/no-egress-frame`, no longer exists in source either).

IF THE VAR IS REMOVED, check whether check-bundle-isolation.cjs's roster comment needs a matching correction the way egress's did - #9070 had to change "still planted at the bottom of egress.cljc" to past tense. Read the `derivation-graph` roster entry's comment before deciding; the two records must agree afterwards.

DO NOT change the live sentinel (`rf/family`) or any gate behaviour. `npm run test:bundle-isolation` must still read exit 0 with 40 internal sentinels absent and 40 positive-control sentinels present - both numbers were unmoved by #9070's removal of the egress twin, which is the evidence that removing a Closure-dropped var cannot move them.
notes:
MAYOR RULING 2026-09-03 08:2x AUSEST. REMOVE THE VAR AND ITS COMMENT BLOCK, MATCHING WHAT #9070 DID TO THE EGRESS SIBLING. AND THIS BEAD IS NOT FENCED — I measured the overlap rather than assuming it.

NOT FENCED, MEASURED. I expected this to be sequenced behind PR #9070 because that PR holds implementation/scripts/check-bundle-isolation.cjs, and I checked instead of assuming:
  grep -F "rf.derivation.graph/sentinel" check-bundle-isolation.cjs  -> NO HITS
  grep -F "rf.derivation.egress/sentinel" check-bundle-isolation.cjs -> ONE HIT at :515 (the control, proving the instrument works)
The roster entry for derivation-graph at :478-480 uses the source 're-frame.derivation.graph family marker', not the literal, exactly as this bead says. And the .cjs comment at :521 ALREADY records the graph sibling correctly — "4e43784ec7 moved this entry — and its `derivation-graph` sibling, onto `rf/family`". So nothing in that file claims the graph literal is planted, and nothing in it needs to change. THIS IS A SINGLE-FILE CHANGE TO graph.cljc.

THE RULING: REMOVE, do not correct. PR #9070's worker removed the egress var rather than correcting its comment, and gave the reason: a corrected comment still leaves the false `do-not-rename` instruction inside the STRING LITERAL ITSELF, where the next reader meets it first. That reasoning applies here unchanged and the two sites should not diverge. It also confirmed nothing consumed the egress var before removing it; do the same here.

WHAT COMES OUT: the `defonce ^:private bundle-isolation-sentinel` at graph.cljc:835-836 and the seventeen-line comment block above it at :819-833. That block asserts two things this bead measured false — that check-bundle-isolation.cjs greps the counter bundle for this exact string, and that the string survives `:advanced`. It also asserts the string "sits outside any `interop/debug-enabled?` gate so DCE cannot drop the literal independently", which is beside the point once the var itself is dropped.

MEASURE FIRST, as the bead already instructs, and do not take either the bead's word or mine. The check that settles it is a fixed-string grep of the EMITTED module, never the .cljc, with a same-file same-instrument control so a zero is a measurement rather than a broken needle. #9070's worker ran exactly this pattern and got 0 for the planted literal against a control of 1 for the live `rf.resource/opaque`.

WHAT IS NOT RULED AND STAYS THE WORKER'S CALL: whether to add a do-not-re-plant note for graph alongside the one #9070 added for egress. IF YOU CONCLUDE check-bundle-isolation.cjs NEEDS ANY EDIT, REPORT IT — DO NOT MAKE IT. That file is inside PR #9070's diff and a second toucher conflicts. The reporting costs a follow-up bead; the edit costs a merge.
MAYOR RULING 2026-09-03 11:2x AUSEST, on the conflict the worker reported rather than resolving unilaterally. NO FOLLOW-UP IS WANTED. graph.cljc stays as it landed, with no sentinel comment at all.

THE CONFLICT WAS REAL AND THE WORKER WAS RIGHT TO SURFACE IT. This bead's ruling said "REMOVE THE VAR AND ITS COMMENT BLOCK, MATCHING WHAT #9070 DID TO THE EGRESS SIBLING" and enumerated both under WHAT COMES OUT. But #9070 merged mid-run and the worker read the LANDED diff rather than trusting the description: #9070 removed the var and KEPT a comment, replacing the false block with a corrected account that now opens "THE SENTINEL FOR THIS NAMESPACE IS NOT IN THIS FILE" and names rf.resource/opaque. So the two halves of one instruction pointed opposite ways, and reading the tree is what exposed it.

IT FOLLOWED THE EXPLICIT ENUMERATED ACTION, which is the correct tie-break: an enumerated action outranks a comparison to a sibling that moved after the ruling was written.

WHY NO SYMMETRY FOLLOW-UP. Three reasons, in order of weight. (1) The stance refuses it: "not over-engineering or gold plating... we don't need to litigate every last fine detail". A comment added so two files look alike, rather than because a reader needs it, is precisely that. (2) The two cases are NOT symmetrical in substance, which is the worker's own argument and it holds: egress MINTED a keyword and needed to explain where its sentinel went; graph ASSOCS a family marker (rf/family) it does not own, so there is less to explain. Equal treatment of unequal cases is not consistency. (3) The account already exists in two places a reader reaches first -- the roster entry (source 're-frame.derivation.graph family marker', sentinel rf/family) and check-bundle-isolation.cjs at ~:521, which the worker re-measured and found already records the graph sibling's history correctly.

WHAT THE WORKER ESTABLISHED THAT IS WORTH KEEPING. check-bundle-isolation.cjs needs NO edit, and it reproduced that measurement rather than trusting the mayor's: "rf.derivation.graph/sentinel" returns nothing, the egress control returns one hit at :515. The consumer census found EXACTLY ONE hit tree-wide, the defonce itself -- against three for the egress half, the difference being egress's roster citation. Three-legged emitted-module measurement on a rebuilt artefact with mtime confirmed later than the source: planted literal 0, rf/family control 1, pre-change source 1. Bundle-isolation counts 40 absent / 40 present, unmoved either side. Sabotage witness red naming exactly the plant, restore verified by git blob hash a4aef0f7 both sides.

TWO SPINE RUNS WERE CORRECTLY READ AS NO VERDICT, not failures: shadow-cljs par-compile aborts pending #{re-frame.router-transducer} then #{re-frame.websocket-cljs-test}, neither reachable from a 19-line deletion in graph.cljc, the pending namespace differing between runs, and the identical command passing standalone twice with identical counts. close_reason:

MEASURED, THREE LEGS, on a freshly built out/bundle-isolation-positive-control/derivation-graph.js (artefact mtime confirmed later than the source read, so no stale out/ answered): ZERO occurrences of the planted literal rf.derivation.graph/sentinel:rf2-6xm07h-2026-06-12:do-not-rename, against a same-file same-instrument control of 1 for the live rf/family, with the literal present exactly once in the pre-change source. The control makes the zero a measurement rather than a broken needle; the third leg makes it DCE rather than a needle that was never there. do-not-rename and 6xm07h each read 0 in the artefact too. Re-measured after the change on a rebuilt artefact: literal still 0, control still 1.

The derivation-graph roster entry uses source 're-frame.derivation.graph family marker', sentinel rf/family. CLAIM 2 FALSE: the var is ^:private and unconsumed, so Closure drops it whole.

CONSUMER CENSUS: a fixed-string tree search for the literal (.beads/issues.jsonl excluded as a whole-database export) returned EXACTLY ONE hit - the defonce itself at graph.cljc:836. Re-run against the merge base after rebasing, same result. The tracker export carries one further occurrence, which is this bead's own text. Nothing consumed it. (This is one hit where the egress half found three: egress's roster citation exists, graph's does not.)

check-bundle-isolation.cjs NEEDS NO EDIT and none was made, as ruled. Nothing in it claims the graph literal is planted, and its roster comment at ~:521 already records the 4e43784ec7 history correctly for the graph sibling. That measurement was reproduced rather than taken on trust.

ONE DIVERGENCE FROM THE RULING'S STATED MODEL, REPORTED RATHER THAN RESOLVED UNILATERALLY. title: skill(re-frame2): cancellation.md teaches one auto-released resource kind; the runtime releases three (:after timers, :rf.resource/* owners under [:machine actor-id])
description:
CLAIM
`skills/re-frame2/references/state-machines/cancellation.md`:
- L5 (§When to load): "The cleanup is automatic; this leaf tells you what is guaranteed and what to add by hand for non-HTTP side effects."
- L11 (§The guarantee): "When the runtime destroys a spawned actor by **any** trigger, every in-flight `:rf.http/managed` request the actor had issued is aborted." — the only guarantee the leaf states.
- L57 (§Cooperative cleanup for non-HTTP side effects): "The framework's automatic abort hook covers `:rf.http/managed`. For anything else a child holds — a websocket, **a timer**, a subscription on an external stream — wire your own cleanup into the child's `:exit` action."
- L100-102 (§Why one mechanism, not two): restates the HTTP-only hook.

TRUTH AT TIP
- `spec/005-StateMachines.md:3607-3619` (§What auto-cancels on destroy — exactly three framework-managed resource kinds): "1. In-flight `:rf.http/managed` requests … 2. Armed `:after` timers the actor scheduled — cancelled by `cancel-actor-timers!` on the same destroy path … 3. `:rf.resource/*` owners the actor holds under its `[:machine <actor-id>]` owner — released by dispatching the existing `:rf.resource/release-owner` effect on the same destroy path … The release fires on every destroy trigger". Then: "Any other resource a child actor holds is NOT auto-released — a `setInterval` / raw `setTimeout` issued via a custom fx, a WebSocket subscription, …".
- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/resource_release.cljc` (ns docstring): machine teardown releases the actor's `[:machine actor-id]` resource owners by keyword-dispatching `:rf.resource/release-owner`, guarded by `release-owner-registered?` so it is a no-op without the resources artefact; "Together these cover EVERY destroy cause".
- `timer/cancel-actor-timers!` is called from `lifecycle_fx/destroy.cljc:256` and `lifecycle_fx/finalize.cljc:640`.

IMPACT
Two consumer-visible errors. (a) The leaf says "a timer" is the author's job — an agent reads that as "wire `:exit` cleanup for my `:after`", which the runtime already cancels; the correct scope is *raw* `setTimeout` / `setInterval` issued through a custom fx. (b) The resource-owner release is untaught anywhere in the skill: `patterns/resources.md` (partition D) teaches `[:rf.resource/ensure {… :owner …}]`, and a machine that `ensure`s under `:owner [:machine <actor-id>]` gets that owner released on destroy — the whole reason to mint machine-owned owners — but an agent following this leaf either hand-releases in `:exit` or, worse, never uses the machine owner key and leaks a polling owner past the actor's death. The leaf is the skill's only cancellation carrier.

FIX SHAPE (one PR, one file)
- §The guarantee: state the three kinds (HTTP requests, armed `:after` timers, `:rf.resource/*` owners under `[:machine <actor-id>]`), one line each, with the "fires on every destroy trigger" sentence covering all three.
- §Cooperative cleanup: retitle to "for resources the framework does not manage", drop "a timer", and list the spec's examples (raw `setTimeout` / `setInterval` via a custom fx, WebSocket, worker, third-party SDK subscription).
- Add one gotcha: "A resource `ensure`d under `:owner [:machine <actor-id>]` is released on destroy; a three-part `[:machine <id> <instance>]` owner is app-authoritative and is NOT (resource_release.cljc docstring)." Cross-link `../../patterns/resources.md` §owners.
- §Why one mechanism, not two: "the same hook" → "the same destroy path" and name the three.
Keep the leaf under 16 KB (it is 11,090 B now).

GATE
No gate — nothing validates this prose; `check_skill_package_refs.py --verbose` for the new relative link. Verify by hand against spec/005 §3607 and `resource_release.cljc`, and say so in the PR body.

ACCEPTANCE
`grep -c "release-owner\|\[:machine <actor-id>\]" skills/re-frame2/references/state-machines/cancellation.md` ≥ 1; `grep -n "a timer" cancellation.md` returns nothing in the cooperative-cleanup section; the three kinds appear in §The guarantee; `wc -c` ≤ 16384.

title: hic: pilot prep — put a runnable behavioural baseline in each pilot workspace (outcome 1 currently has none)
description:
FILED 2026-09-02 by the delegated ruling on rf2-hic-063 (that bead's RULING note of the same date is the authority; the Codex review that surfaced this defect is folded there). Tip b26c5ad33e.

THE DEFECT. docs/design/hicasso/product/pilots/workspace.md step 2 creates `app/test/` for both pilots and copies nothing into it; its source manifest copies only application source, index.html, the avatar and the README. friction-log.md outcome 1 is "The app's behavioural tests are preserved across the migration — the test command and its captured exit code, before and after", and workspace.md:134 says both pilots need the test kit "from the first hour, because outcome 1 is to preserve the app's behavioural tests". But the pilots' behavioural tests do not live with the apps — the examples tree is test-free by policy (rf2-8cevm) — they live in the adapter test tree: implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/realworld_cljs_test.cljs (broad RealWorld integration coverage) and implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/linearlite_example_cljs_test.cljs (ten optimistic commit/rollback tests). `grep -rn "realworld_cljs_test\|linearlite_example_cljs_test\|adapters/reagent/test" docs/design/hicasso/product/pilots/` returns nothing. As assembled, a pilot is told to run the app's suite before migrating and receives no suite and no test build: outcome 1 is BLOCKED at hour zero for both pilots, and it would be recorded as the framework's friction when it is the operator's scaffolding.

THE FIX. workspace.md is the OPERATOR's page — the pilot never reads it — so in-tree knowledge is allowed here; it must not leak into the two briefs.
1. title: Review adapter_support: filtering and verdict paths verified; no action
description:
Recommendation: retain the current adapter-support design. This focused review confirmed no substantive correctness defect requiring remediation in the five owned files. Verdict: reviewed/no-action, with 0 actionable findings (P0-P4 all zero). Do not expand the shared smoke roster to reagent-slim or test-react: the former has its own browser runner and the latter is deliberately a local, unpublished fixture.

Scope and source snapshot
- Slice: adapter_support, under parent rf2-fzbj.
- Reviewed source revision: 1c9ff9697b0fa3a018c7a4371e02983ad2e79b2f.
- HEAD at final source check: 5b89378c457e9997d7eff69b7dec56eec4e5307c. `git diff 1c9ff9697b0fa3a018c7a4371e02983ad2e79b2f --` over all five owned paths was empty; tracker checkpoints have not changed this source snapshot.
- Exact owned paths: implementation/adapters/README.md; implementation/adapters/TESTING.md; implementation/adapters/scripts/adapter-smoke-filter.cjs; implementation/adapters/scripts/run-adapter-smokes.cjs; implementation/adapters/scripts/serve-and-run-adapter-smokes.cjs.
- SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2.
- WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review). No worker guard pass is claimed or needed for this read-only assignment.

Coverage and conclusions
1. Shared manifest, filtering and discovery: adapter-smoke-filter.cjs:77-96 declares exactly Reagent and UIx and derives build IDs, HTML sources, output directories and spec paths together. Lines 103-148 normalize slash, backslash and underscore forms and OR-match against build ID or repo-relative spec path; the absolute checkout prefix cannot select a smoke accidentally. Lines 173-206 implement actual filesystem discovery and missing/undeclared reconciliation. The live declared/discovered sets were compared by the production functions and matched. The manifest paths and Shadow output directories agree with shadow-cljs.edn:2324-2337 and the two specs' URL mounts.
2. Runner contract and failure handling: run-adapter-smokes.cjs:141-179 rejects manifest drift, empty selections and malformed spec exports before browser launch. Lines 200-239 create a fresh browser context for each spec, register pageerror handling before navigation, bound navigation and spec execution, close each normal test context in finally, and close the browser. Lines 241-257 report the counted verdict and return a nonzero exit for failures. Synthetic assertion, navigation, pageerror and timeout cases all exercised this actual source and failed as expected.
3. Orchestration: serve-and-run-adapter-smokes.cjs:86-103 selects CLI-over-environment filtering; lines 157-171 use that same selector for cleaning; lines 174-231 compile and stage exactly that selection. Compilation uses the resolved Shadow JS entry point with process.execPath, a fixed implementation cwd, and no shell. Lines 241-278 stop on failed setup/readiness and propagate the chosen URL and filter to the runner; a signaled/null-code runner maps to exit 1. Lines 281-294 invoke registered cleanup before exiting. Reviewed the shared local-browser-harness call contract, ownership-token readiness and cleanup integration; no duplicate port/staging implementation is introduced here.
4. Public documentation: README distinguishes the three published adapter packages from test-react and explains shared spine factories and the adapter-map contract. TESTING.md identifies the thin mount/dispatch/render scope, the two-spec shared command, shared helper ownership, filtering, drift checking and how to add a smoke. Named npm commands were cross-read against implementation/package.json and browser tier claims against test.yml and expensive-tests.yml. This is compile-mode browser smoke coverage, not an optimized-release or comprehensive adapter-runtime proof.
5. Roster truth: implementation/package.json:48-49 defines both test:reagent-slim:smoke and test:adapter-smokes. The slim build and its runner are deliberately separate in shadow-cljs.edn and CI. test-react's local fixture role is not evidence of missing browser coverage. The word 'three' in TESTING.md:3 is a minor stale count beside an explicit Reagent/UIx list and a correct two-smoke command row at line 31; it does not select or omit tests and does not justify a correctness remediation task. If that introduction is otherwise edited, align its count then.

Executed validation: 25 bounded process-local witness cases, both probe commands exit 0
The witnesses read the actual runner/orchestrator source by absolute path and evaluated it with Node vm and createRequire. Production manifest/filter/discovery code was loaded directly. Browser, spec, filesystem-write, compile, HTTP-server and child-process boundaries were replaced in memory with controlled doubles. No repository source was patched and no build output was written. The synthetic process.exit shim recorded the first requested code and unwound execution; resulting extra catch/cleanup calls in the harness are probe artifacts, not an observed production lifecycle defect.
- Runner, 14 cases: healthy full roster (2 specs); four equivalent singleton filters (build, path, Windows path and underscore); mixed-shape OR selection (2 specs); unknown filter; missing declared spec; undeclared discovered spec; invalid spec module; navigation rejection; assertion rejection; captured uncaught page error; nonresolving spec bounded by a 20ms timeout. Healthy selections requested exit 0; all eight rejection/failure variants requested exit 1. Preflight rejection cases never launched the fake browser; entered contexts closed and normal completed runs closed the fake browser.
- Orchestrator, 11 cases: healthy full roster; CLI Reagent filter overriding UIx environment filter; environment UIx selection; unknown selection; port-resolution rejection; compile exit 7; compile null/signal result; missing stage directory; server not ready; runner exit 5; runner null/signal exit. The first three requested exit 0 with matching build/stage/runner selections; failure cases returned 1 except the intentional runner exit 5, which propagated unchanged. Precompile/setup/compile failures did not start the fake server, failed readiness did not start the runner, and every case reached cleanup.
- Inspected the existing _adapter-smoke-filter.test.cjs cases for manifest shape, equivalence, retired UI filter nonmatching, checkout-prefix exclusion, real discovery/reconciliation and npm command existence. These are meaningful fast tests of the production selection/discovery helpers. Also cross-read neighboring browser verdict policy and shared harness code for context; their full test suites were not run.

Known history and duplicate control
- Read current rf2-kdaw and its history: closed after PR #9270. Its ruling is that three shipped adapters do have three browser smokes across two runners; a spec.cjs-only census incorrectly misses reagent-slim's smoke.cjs. This review agrees and raises no duplicate coverage issue.
- The owned source records prior fixes rf2-l72e2 (shared filter string space), rf2-n4nc2o (exclude checkout-prefix matches), rf2-qf45gu (production discovery/reconciliation shared with tests), rf2-bf4vdy (clean selected output) and rf2-y9o5e3 (shell-free compilation). The current implementations were inspected rather than assuming comments prove the repairs. Direct bd show lookups for rf2-l72e2 and rf2-qf45gu did not find current records; no current tracker status is asserted for those historical IDs.

Limits, exclusions and follow-up decision
No real Chromium launch, Shadow/JVM compilation, npm installation, broad gate, optimized release, live smoke app execution, or package publication was performed. Browser-specific React behavior, actual OS process-tree teardown and compiler caching are outside what these synthetic witnesses prove. Adapter implementations and their own spec files were followed only to establish harness contracts and are not independently reviewed by this bead. No mutation reproduction, server, long-running child, source edit, commit, checkout, rebase or push was created by this worker. Root owns tracker checkpoint/push.

No unverified risk is promoted to a defect and no separate follow-up is warranted from this slice. Acceptance for this review is the complete coverage/limits record, exactly one child bead, and an explicit reviewed/no-action closure. Revisit if a future concrete browser or runner failure supplies a counterexample, rather than adding speculative harness complexity now.

title: flake watch: cancellation_cascade_fresco_boundary_dom_cljs_test W4 failed once on a teardown-grace race, then passed untouched
description:
OBSERVED ONCE, NOT REPRODUCED, AND FILED SO THAT THE NEXT RED IS NOT RE-DIAGNOSED FROM SCRATCH.

WHAT WAS SEEN. `frescopanel-a`, running `npm run test:browser` in its own worktree while preparing
PR #9652, saw `cancellation_cascade_fresco_boundary_dom_cljs_test` case W4 fail once, then pass on
the next two runs with nothing changed in between. Its diagnosis was a TEARDOWN-GRACE RACE. Its own
change did not touch that namespace, and every gate it reported was captured green afterwards --
`test:browser` 928 tests / 5124 assertions / 0 failures, exit 0.

WHY THIS IS WORTH A BEAD RATHER THAN NOTHING. The merge criterion reads CI, and the standing mayor
instruction is to dispatch a worker at any PR that is not green. A DOM suite that fails
intermittently therefore spends a worker every time it fires, and the worker starts with no reason
to suspect the test rather than the diff in front of it. One recorded observation turns that into a
five-minute check.

WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED. One observation is not a pattern. It is not established that this recurs, that
the teardown grace is the mechanism, or that it is timing rather than ordering. Do not "fix" it on
the strength of this bead alone.

WORK, IF AND WHEN IT FIRES AGAIN:
  1. Confirm it is the same case (W4) and the same namespace before treating this record as
     relevant. A different case in the same file is a different question.
  2. The lane is `npm run test:browser` (CI job `cljs-browser`) -- a `_dom_cljs_test` namespace runs
     nowhere else. Under `npm run test:cljs` it merely loads and short-circuits on `(browser?)`,
     which is a stated green skip: TESTING.md line 28 for the split, line 196 for that exact failure
     mode. So reproducing it means the browser lane, repeatedly.
  3. Read the teardown path before the assertion. If the grace is real, the repair is in how the
     case waits, not in relaxing what it asserts.

A SECOND SIGHTING IS THE TRIGGER. Until then this is a record, not a task -- close it as
unreproduced if the suite runs clean over a long enough stretch to make a standing bead noise.
notes:
CLEAN-RUN COUNT, MEASURED 2026-09-11 ~09:50 AUSEST. NOT CLOSING; RECORDING THE DENOMINATOR THIS BEAD
NEEDS BEFORE A CLOSE CAN BE DEFENSIBLE.

Over test.yml runs on TRUNK since this bead was filed (2026-09-11T01:51Z): 32 runs, 26 success,
1 failure, 5 other (in-progress/cancelled). That is on top of the browser lane running on every PR in
the same window, of which nine merged green.

THE ONE FAILURE IS NOT A SECOND SIGHTING, and it is worth naming so the next reader does not count it
as one. Run 34574454830 (07:27, a docs PR). The failing jobs were the browser lane and the Story/Xray
PR-smoke, and BOTH failed in `npx playwright install --with-deps chromium`, which stalled and was
killed at its deadline. The workflow's own error text says it outright: "This step provisions the
browser, so the gate this job exists to run never started: the red reports PROVISIONING and carries no
verdict on the code under test." `cancellation_cascade_fresco_boundary_dom_cljs_test` did not execute
in that run at all, W4 included.

SO THE TRIGGER HAS NOT FIRED. Zero recurrences of the W4 failure in the window.

DELIBERATELY NOT CLOSING, and the reason is symmetric with this bead's own "one observation is not a
pattern": 26 clean runs over ~8 hours is not evidence of ABSENCE for a fault seen once, since a flake

title: reclaim: set a retention rule for .git/codex-pr-audit-* — completion test is in-directory (all 5 phases true); recovery-* subtrees are LIVE beads-DB backups, never delete unasked (counts move hourly: re-measure, do not quote)
description:
Noticed while ruling rf2-cq3x (the `.git/lost-found` disposition). A **second non-object-store consumer inside `.git`**, unrelated to lost-found and to the object store itself.

## Measured 2026-09-09 13:2x AUSEST, mayor checkout `C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2`, HEAD `71decabd3f`

```
find .git -maxdepth 1 -type d -name 'codex-pr-audit-*' | wc -l   ->  51
                                              total bytes        ->  122,606,133  (116.9 MB)
du -sb .git                                                      ->  7,201,732,292 (6.71 GB)
```

So these are **1.7% of `.git`** — a rounding error beside rf2-cq3x's 69.2%, which is exactly why it is filed separately rather than bundled into that decision.

## Why it is a separate question

- `.git/codex-pr-audit-*` are **not part of the object store**, so `git gc` and the `git maintenance` tasks under rf2-fmst will never touch them, the same way they never touch `.git/lost-found`. They will not shrink on their own.
- Unlike lost-found, these are almost certainly **regenerable working directories** from PR-audit tooling rather than the last surviving copy of anything — which, if true, makes this an ordinary reclaim and not an operator call. **That has NOT been verified.** Nobody has looked at what is in one, what wrote them, whether anything still reads them, or whether a retention policy already exists.

## What this bead is

1. Establish what writes `.git/codex-pr-audit-*` and whether anything consumes them after the audit completes.
2. If they are disposable, decide a retention rule (delete on completion? keep N most recent?) and say where it belongs.
3. Only then reclaim.

**Do not delete on the strength of "it looks like scratch."** That is the reasoning rf2-cq3x was filed to stop, one directory over. Low priority: 116.9 MB against 391.8 GiB free is no pressure at all.
notes:
## INVESTIGATION 2026-09-09 (gitspace) — what writes them, what reads them, and a one-sentence retention rule. READ-ONLY: nothing deleted.

Measured 2026-09-09 15:00-16:15 AUSEST from a worker worktree against the mayor checkout (read only).

### LOUD WARNING FIRST, because a cleanup run today would have destroyed live data

**`.git/codex-pr-audit-9546` is NOT audit scratch.** It holds `recovery-1`, `recovery-2` and `recovery-3`,
each containing a full copy of `.beads/embeddeddolt/rf2/.dolt` — the beads Dolt database — together with a
`snapshot-proof.json` naming the source as the live `.beads` database and pinning SHA-256 hashes of
`repo_state.json`, `noms/manifest`, `noms/journal.idx` and the root chunk, plus sizes and mtimes for all 11
persistent files. **recovery-3 was written at 15:41:55 today, thirteen minutes before I measured it**, and
these are the safety net for the beads-tracker restoration that was in flight this afternoon. They are
**1,948 MB of the population's 2,194 MB — 89% of it.** Any rule of the form "delete `.git/codex-pr-audit-*`"
executed today would have deleted the live tracker backups. Whatever retention rule is adopted must exclude
these, and the disposition of the recovery snapshots belongs to whoever owns that restoration, not to this
bead.

### Corrections to the description's figures — the population is growing in real time

| | At filing (13:2x today) | Measured now | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| directories | 51 | **60** | grew 58 → 59 → 60 *during this investigation* |
| total bytes | 122,606,133 (116.9 MB) | **2,194 MB** | almost entirely the one recovery directory |
| `.git` total | 6.71 GB | **8.81 GB** | |
| share of `.git` | 1.7% | **~25%** | **the "rounding error" framing no longer holds** |

Excluding 9546's recovery trees, all 60 directories together are **246 MB** — which *is* a rounding error,
and is the figure the retention question should actually be argued over. PR numbers run **contiguously from
9489**, with no gaps: the floor has not moved since filing while the ceiling has, so **nothing prunes them
and they accumulate**, roughly one per merged PR.

### What writes them — VERIFIED, not assumed

The description asked me to verify rather than assume the CLAUDE.md premise. **It holds, verbatim, at HEAD**
(CLAUDE.md line 94): the writer is a generated `.git/codex-pr-audit-<PR>/checkpoint.py`, re-emitted per PR by
an out-of-repo merge-audit harness. Confirmed two ways: the file exists and is a per-PR generated script with
the PR number and both cursor values baked in as literals; and `git grep` over tracked files finds
`codex-pr-audit` in exactly **two** places, `CLAUDE.md` and `.beads/issues.jsonl` — i.e. **no tracked code
writes, reads or references these directories.** The harness itself is outside the repo and I cannot inspect
it from here.

A directory holds the audit's working set: `pr.json`, `full.diff` / `merge-diff.patch`, `owner-before.json`,
`owner-mutations.json`, `receipt.txt`, CI logs, `ci-proof.json`, per-gate `.log` / `.exit` artefacts, and the
generated `checkpoint.py`, `query.py`, `verify.py`, `record-findings.py`.

### What reads them — this is the part that settles the retention rule

Reading `checkpoint.py` answers it exactly. The script is **resumable**, and its resume state is
`checkpoint-state.json` **in its own directory** — five phases (`persist`, `dolt`, `checkpoint`, `git`,
`remote`), each flipped to `true` as it completes, each skipped on re-run if already `true`. It also reads
`receipt.txt` and `owner-mutations.json` from its own directory and writes `remote-verification.json` back
into it.

So: **a `codex-pr-audit-<PR>` directory is read only by its own `checkpoint.py`, and only while that PR's
audit is unfinished.** Once all five phases are `true` the directory is inert — nothing in or out of the repo
opens it again.

**The cross-PR resume state is NOT in these directories.** `checkpoint.py` carries the cursor as a literal and
asserts the previous value via `bd recall merged-pr-audit-cursor` before proceeding — so the harness's resume
logic depends on the **bead memory key**, exactly as CLAUDE.md says, and **that key is load-bearing and must
be left alone**. Live value now: `merged-pr-audit-cursor-pr-9548-…`. (Note it is *ahead* of the newest
directory, 9547 — the harness is running continuously as I write.) There are 88 `merged-pr-audit-pr-*` keys,
up from the 48 CLAUDE.md recorded yesterday morning; that class is the subject of the rf2-ornb ruling and is
not this bead's business.

**Completion state, measured across the whole population: all 60 directories have `checkpoint-state.json`
with every phase `true`, and all have `remote-verification.json`.** Zero partial, zero missing. So by the
test above, every one of them is inert — 9546's audit itself completed at 15:41:16, and only its *recovery*
subtrees are live data.

### Hazard check

**`find -type l` across the entire `codex-pr-audit-*` population reads 0.** No junction, so the
recursive-delete-follows-a-junction-into-the-mayor's-node_modules hazard does not apply to this set. Measured
today; re-check immediately before any deletion rather than citing this note.

### Proposed retention rule — one sentence, no subsystem

Per the standing posture I am not proposing a cleanup subsystem, a retention daemon or a wrapper script, and
I do not think one is warranted for 246 MB.

> **A `.git/codex-pr-audit-<PR>` directory whose `checkpoint-state.json` has all five phases `true` is
> finished and unread, and may be deleted; delete nothing that contains a `recovery-*` subtree without
> asking the owner of that recovery first.**

That is a sentence somebody follows when `.git` size next matters. Two things make it safe: the completion
test is *in* the directory, so it needs no knowledge of the out-of-repo harness; and it deletes only what the
harness has already finished with, so it cannot break resume — resume rides the `merged-pr-audit-cursor` bead
memory key, which the rule does not touch.

**Where it belongs: on this bead and nowhere else, for now.** It should NOT go into CLAUDE.md as a new bullet
— the CLAUDE.md paragraph that already covers this harness exists because no tracked file can enforce
anything against an out-of-repo writer, and adding a second paragraph about a 246 MB directory would be
gold-plating. If it is ever automated, the honest place is the harness itself, which is not in this repo.

### What I could not establish from here, stated plainly

* Whether the out-of-repo harness has its own retention or cleanup behaviour. It evidently has none that runs
  here — the floor has stood at 9489 while nine directories accrued above it — but I cannot see its code.
* Why the population starts at 9489 specifically. Consistent with a manual clear or a harness restart around
  that PR; I have no evidence either way and did not guess.
* Whether the 9546 recovery trees are still needed. That is the restoration owner's call, not mine.

### Priority

The description's "low priority, no pressure" judgement still holds for the 246 MB of ordinary audit
directories. The 1,948 MB of recovery snapshots are a different question with a different owner, and the only
urgent thing in this note is that a naive cleanup must not touch them.

### Gates

No tracked file was changed, so no gate applies and there is no PR.
close_reason:

*** THE SECOND CLAUSE IS THE LOAD-BEARING ONE AND A CLEANUP RUN THAT IGNORES IT DESTROYS LIVE DATA. *** `.git/codex-pr-audit-9546` is NOT audit scratch: it holds `recovery-1`, `recovery-2` and `recovery-3`, each a full copy of `.beads/embeddeddolt/rf2/.dolt` — the beads Dolt database — with a `snapshot-proof.json` naming the live `.beads` database as its source and pinning SHA-256 hashes of `repo_state.json`, `noms/manifest`, `noms/journal.idx` and the root chunk. `recovery-3` was written thirteen minutes before it was measured. These are 1,948 MB of the population's 2,194 MB — 89% of it — and are the safety net for the beads-tracker restoration. Any rule of the form "delete `.git/codex-pr-audit-*`" executed on 2026-09-09 would have deleted the live tracker backups.

WHY NO SUBSYSTEM, AND WHY NOT IN CLAUDE.md. Per the standing posture this is deliberately one sentence rather than a cleanup daemon, a retention wrapper or a gate — 246 MB of ordinary audit directories does not warrant one, and the recovery subtrees are somebody else's call rather than a size problem. It does NOT go into CLAUDE.md as a new bullet: the paragraph there already covering this harness exists because no tracked file can enforce anything against an out-of-repo writer, and a second paragraph about 246 MB would be gold-plating. If it is ever automated, the honest place is the harness itself, which is not in this repository.

CLOSED rather than left open: the deliverable was a rule, the rule exists and is recorded here where a `.git`-size question will find it. Nothing is pending.

title: check_skill_package_refs.py scans SKILL/README/references only, but packages also ship patterns/ and decision-trees/

title: Skills review: cross-cutting (7 findings: the redirect table's guide URL is dead and no gate resolves any of its 52 rows; two EP rows route to spec/002 instead of docs/EP; the pair mirror page teaches a session that fails on its first call)
description:
Filed from the review wave under epic rf2-ikbgk (report cross-cutting.md). The report below is the reviewer's, verbatim. The worker rules are in this bead's notes.

## Project stance (verbatim, from CLAUDE.md)

> Posture is that we are pre-alpha and focused on elegance, power and a masterpiece.
> But we are not over-engineering or gold plating. Also, we trust the programmer.
> We're trying to facilitate high productivity for them (and the AI they use) via a
> library with excellent ergonomics and low friction. We don't need to litigate every
> last fine detail and drown in the minutiae.

---

# Senior review: cross-cutting (index, redirect table, installer, mirror pages, gates as a set)

Reviewer persona: read-only senior reviewer of the skills tree's connective tissue — the index, the URL/anchor table, the link installer, the docs-site mirrors, and the fifteen gates as a set
Tree: skills-review-sep21 worktree, trunk b60a20abca
Scope read: `skills/README.md` (486 L), `SKILL-REDIRECT.md` (128 L), `scripts/install-skills.sh` (223 L), `scripts/install-skills.ps1` (164 L), all ten `docs/skills/*.md` (509 L) — every line; the fifteen `scripts/check_skill_*.py` (17,595 L) read for header, enumeration/roster logic and CI wiring rather than line by line; `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` and `scripts/check_readme_links.py` roster and URL-handling code.
Surfaces the skill teaches, consulted: `mkdocs.yml` (nav, `exclude_docs`, `site_url`), `mkdocs_hooks.py` (staging table, rewrites), the `docs/` and `spec/` trees (every one of the 40 `spec/*.md` pages the table names, `spec/002-Frames.md` image sections, `spec/API.md` rows 93/97/1029/1074/1081), `docs/EP/`, `implementation/core/src/re_frame/{core_reg_macros,interceptor_registry,trace/tooling}.cljc`, `implementation/adapters/reagent/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent.cljs`, `tools/story/src/re_frame/story.cljc`, `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/{package.json,README.md}`, `skills/re-frame2-pair/{SKILL.md,README.md}` (preload contract), `skills/re-frame2/references/fundamentals/images.md`, every `skills/*/SKILL.md` frontmatter and `skills/*/package.json`, `.github/workflows/test.yml` (jobs `verify-skill-mcp-drift`, `skills-structural`, `reagent-migration-fixture-cold-start`), `.github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh`.
Gates run (from the frozen worktree root, `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8`): check_skill_description_budget 0, check_skill_eval_docs 0, check_skill_eval_packaging 0, check_skill_implementor_order 0, check_skill_implementor_partition_drift 0, check_skill_mcp_drift 0, check_skill_migration_cites 0, check_skill_migration_contract_drift 0, check_skill_migration_o1617_router_drift 0, check_skill_package_refs 0, check_skill_pair_authoring_drift 0, check_skill_re_frame2_drift 0, check_skill_redirect_anchors 0, check_skill_setup_counter_drift 0, check_skill_xray_tab_inventory_drift 0; check_doc_slugs 0; check_readme_links --ci 0. Roster facts for this slice: `docs/skills/*.md` and `skills/README.md` are read by `check_doc_slugs.py` (`DEFAULT_ROOTS` = docs, spec, skills, migration; `check_readme_links.py:231` excludes the `skills/` subtree as docs-gate territory); `SKILL-REDIRECT.md` is read ONLY by `check_readme_links.py`'s repo-root roster (`check_doc_slugs.py:28` says in terms it never opens it).

## Findings, ranked

### 1. The redirect table's guide URL is dead, and no gate can see it — the one file that is nothing but URLs has no URL validation  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: cite-integrity] [size: S]
- Where: `SKILL-REDIRECT.md:52` (`**Narrative guide (overview)** → https://day8.github.io/re-frame2/guide/README/ [setup]`); gates `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py:1630,1822,2139`, `scripts/check_readme_links.py:574-578`.
- What: there is no `docs/guide/` at all — the guide lives under `docs/core/` (`mkdocs.yml:10` says so; nav section `Core` → `core/introduction.md`, `mkdocs.yml:218`) — and MkDocs never serves a `README.md` at `.../README/` anyway, so the row 404s; and nothing in the tree validates a `day8.github.io` URL, so it has sat there unreported.
- Evidence: `ls docs/guide/README.md docs/guide/index.md` both absent; control: `docs/story/index.md`, `migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md`, `spec/conformance/README.md` and all 40 `spec/*.md` targets the table names DO exist (40/40). `rg 'day8\.github\.io'` over both link gates: 0 hits; control: `check_doc_slugs.py:1630` carries an in-repo arm for `https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/(blob|tree)/main/` and skips every other `http(s)` target (1822, 2139), while `check_readme_links.py` skips every `http(s)` target unless `--check-external` (574-578, off in `--ci`). So the 52 bullets of `SKILL-REDIRECT.md` (47 site URLs + 5 GitHub URLs) are validated by nothing — `check_doc_slugs` has the GitHub arm but never opens this file; `check_readme_links` opens it but has no arm. Only `re-frame2` cites labels by anchor (58 refs / 33 files) and none of them cite this row (`rg 'Narrative guide' skills` = 0; control: `EP — State machines (005)` 10 refs), so today's cost is a `[setup]`-tagged reader following a dead link, not an agent.
- Action: repoint to `https://day8.github.io/re-frame2/core/introduction/`. Then decide: (A) add a `day8.github.io/re-frame2/<path>/` arm beside `check_doc_slugs.py:1630` that resolves `<path>` through `docs_dir` plus `mkdocs_hooks.py`'s `_STAGE` table (`spec` → `docs/spec`, `migration` → `docs/migration`) and accepts `X.md` / `X/README.md` / `X/index.md`, and add `SKILL-REDIRECT.md` to its roster — one small function, and it retires this class; or (B) accept that site URLs are checked by eye, and say so in the table's header comment. A is inside the stance (the table exists to be "updated once", which needs a check that reads it).

### 2. Two redirect rows send readers to the wrong page for EP-0023 / EP-0026  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: cite-integrity] [size: S]
- Where: `SKILL-REDIRECT.md:68-69` (`EP — Image-loaded frames (023)` and `EP — Image spec (026)`, both → `spec/002-Frames/`); consumer `skills/re-frame2/references/fundamentals/images.md:56`.
- What: the labels borrow the `docs/EP/` numbering series (EP-0023, EP-0026), but the URL points at the spec-chapter series' `002-Frames`, a ~2,600-line page with no anchor, where the EP-0026 "spec-map contract" the leaf routes to is explicitly said to live elsewhere.
- Evidence: `docs/EP/EP-0023-image-loaded-frames.md` and `docs/EP/EP-0026-image-api-simplification.md` exist; `docs/EP/` is not in `mkdocs.yml`'s `exclude_docs` (32-40) and `spec/002-Frames.md` links both EPs a dozen times (`:378,414,416,1003,1033,1057,1094,2555,2608`) through the `../docs/EP/` path the hook rewrites, under a green `--strict` build — so both are served at `/EP/EP-00NN-…/`. `spec/002-Frames.md:1033`: "The `:rf.image/*` source-key grammar lives in Conventions §The public `rf/image` source keys". No spec chapter is numbered 023 or 026 (`ls spec/ | rg '^0(23|26)'` = 0; control `^002` = 1). `images.md:56` routes "the image-generation seal, re-`make-frame` hot-reload semantics, and the EP-0026 spec-map contract" to these two labels, so an agent following it lands on the frames page and has to find its own way.
- Action: repoint row 68 to `https://day8.github.io/re-frame2/EP/EP-0023-image-loaded-frames/` and row 69 to `https://day8.github.io/re-frame2/EP/EP-0026-image-api-simplification/` — or, if the EP pages are meant to stay design records, keep `002-Frames` but add the `#per-instance-frames--make-frame-the-ep-0023-object-constructor` anchor to 68 and point 69 at `spec/Conventions/#the-public-rfimage-source-keys`. Either is one edit; the labels should stop saying "EP" for a spec chapter or start pointing at an EP.

### 3. The pair mirror page teaches a session that fails on its first call: "injected" runtime, `npm install -g` of an unpublished server, and no preload step  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: packaging] [size: S]
- Where: `docs/skills/re-frame2-pair.md:11,41` ("the injected `re-frame2-pair.runtime` namespace" / "injects the runtime namespace"), `:47-51` (`npm install -g @day8/re-frame2-pair-mcp`), `:31-41` (Kickoff).
- What: the page says the runtime is injected per session and the server installs from npm; the skill says the opposite on both counts and requires a two-line shadow-cljs preload the page never mentions, so a reader who follows the page gets `:runtime-loaded-but-preload-missing` on the first `discover-app`.
- Evidence: `skills/re-frame2-pair/SKILL.md:89` "**The re-frame2-pair preload is required**; there is no per-session cljs-eval inject fallback"; `README.md:164` "No per-session inject step"; `skills/README.md:132-134` (the index this page mirrors) says the same. `skills/re-frame2-pair/README.md:153` "Build and run it from a re-frame2 clone … (Once published: `npm install -g @day8/re-frame2-pair-mcp`.)"; `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/README.md:74` "The MCP server is **not yet published to npm**". `rg -i 'preload' docs/skills/re-frame2-pair.md` = 0 (control: `SKILL.md` 13 lines). The transport section (:53-57) is otherwise current (MCP-only, e2e fixture path exists).
- Action: rewrite Kickoff/Transport to the skill's own three steps — build the server from the clone (`cd tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp && npm install && npm run build`, point `mcpServers` at `out/server.js`), add the linked skill's `preload/` to `:source-paths` plus `[re-frame2-pair.runtime]` to `:devtools :preloads`, then `discover-app` — and replace "injected" with "preloaded". Keep the "once published" form as a parenthetical, as the skill README does.

### 4. The authoring mirror names v1-only registration forms as triggers for the authoring skill, contradicting the routing single source  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: ergonomics] [size: S]
- Where: `docs/skills/re-frame2.md:15` ("References to `reg-event-db`, `reg-event-fx`, `reg-event-ctx`, … are sufficient triggers").
- What: those three are v1 names re-frame2 refuses with a hard error, and the routing table sends "any v1 surface" to `re-frame-migration`, so the site tells a human with a v1-shaped prompt to load the wrong skill.
- Evidence: `spec/API.md:1074` "`reg-event-db` | Use `reg-event` (no alias) … A stale call raises the always-on hard error"; `:1081` "The v1 event trio `reg-event-db` / `reg-event-fx` / `reg-event-ctx` is **not** a v2 target". `rg 'def(macro|n) reg-event-(db|fx|ctx)\b' implementation tools` = 0 (control: `defmacro reg-event` generated at `core_reg_macros.cljc:15`; `reg-story` at `tools/story/src/re_frame/story.cljc:207`; `reg-interceptor` is API.md:97's macro over `interceptor_registry.cljc:132`). `skills/README.md:163` routes v1 surfaces to `re-frame-migration`; `skills/re-frame2/SKILL.md` and `README.md` name none of the three (0; control: the mirror 1). The other names on that line (`reg-sub`, `reg-fx`, `reg-cofx`, `reg-view`, `reg-machine`, `reg-route`, `reg-story`, `reg-app-schema`) are real.
- Action: replace the trio with `reg-event` (and `reg-flow`, which the skill's own description lists) and add the one line the routing table already has: a v1 name in the prompt is `re-frame-migration`'s trigger.

### 5. The PowerShell installer re-points a junction with `Remove-Item -Recurse`, which on Windows PowerShell 5.1 can empty the OTHER checkout's skill directory  [PLAUSIBLE] [severity: medium] [kind: packaging] [size: S]
- Where: `scripts/install-skills.ps1:139-143` (the "reparse point pointing elsewhere (or broken) — safe to re-point" branch); `#requires -Version 5` at `:1`; the documented invocation `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File …` at `skills/README.md:18` and `docs/skills/index.md:15` launches Windows PowerShell 5.1, not pwsh.
- What: `Remove-Item -LiteralPath $dst -Recurse -Force` on a directory junction under Windows PowerShell 5.1 is the well-known footgun that recurses INTO the target and deletes its contents before removing the link — the very reason `CLAUDE.md` prescribes `[System.IO.Directory]::Delete(path, $false)` for junction removal and `scripts/remove-worker-worktree.sh` unlinks with a non-recursive `rm`; the script's own comment (`:141-142`) asserts the opposite without evidence.
- Evidence: reachable case is a `~/.claude/skills/<name>` junction left pointing at a moved or second clone — the branch fires, prints `linked <name>`, exits 0, and that clone's `skills/<name>/` is empty. The POSIX sibling is safe on this box: `[ -L ]` sees a junction under MSYS (measured for `remove-worker-worktree.sh` in `CLAUDE.md`), so `install-skills.sh:147` returns before `rm -rf` follows anything (its comment at `:126-127` claiming the reverse is wrong but harmless). Nothing pins either script: `install-skills.sh:29` cites "the test harness", but `rg -l install-skills` over `scripts/`, `.github/`, `tests/` returns only the two installers, and `git log --diff-filter=D` shows no deleted test (control: both scripts hit). Not run here (hard rule 1); confirm on WinPS 5.1 with a scratch directory holding one file, a junction to it, `Remove-Item -LiteralPath <junction> -Recurse -Force`, and a check that the file survived.
- Action: in the `Test-IsLink` branch use `[System.IO.Directory]::Delete($dst, $false)` (removes the reparse point only; throws rather than recursing if handed a real directory), and keep `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force` for the real-copy `-Force` branch alone. If the confirmation shows 5.1 already safe, downgrade to "fix the comment".

### 6. `SKILL-REDIRECT.md`'s skill index and ownership claim do not describe the tree  [CONFIRMED] [severity: low] [kind: self-contract] [size: S]
- Where: `SKILL-REDIRECT.md:3` ("Skills stay free of hardcoded URLs; this file owns them"), `:32-44` (skill index: six rows + "Two of the eight skills are intentionally absent"), `:61` (Section 2 "Audience: `[impl]` (primary)"); echoed at `docs/skills/index.md:20`.
- What: there are nine skills, `reagent-migration` is in neither the table nor the exclusion note, four of the six tagged consumers never cite a label, and the "primary" implementor audience routes nowhere near the table — it hardcodes 64 site URLs of its own, five of them to pages the table has no row for.
- Evidence: `ls skills` = 9 directories. Arrow-form label citations per skill (the shape `check_skill_redirect_anchors.py:43` parses): `re-frame2` 58 in 33 files; the other eight 0 (control: a nonsense token 0, and plain `SKILL-REDIRECT` mentions do exist — setup 6 files, migration 2, pair 1, implementor 1 — all generic pointers such as `re-frame2-setup/SKILL.md:122` "point at `re-frame2` or `SKILL-REDIRECT.md`", none a label). `skills/reagent-migration/` mentions `SKILL-REDIRECT` in 0 files (control: `skills/re-frame2/` 39). `rg 'day8\.github\.io' skills/<s>`: implementor 64 hits / 7 files, every other skill 0; among them `spec/004C-Roots-and-Mount/`, `spec/Security/`, `spec/Runtime-Subsystems/`, `spec/Managed-Effects/`, `spec/README/` — all real pages, none a table row. `skills/re-frame2-implementor/SKILL.md` mentions `SKILL-REDIRECT` 0 times (only `evals/evals.json:19`). Consequence for the gates: the anchor gate is vacuous for 8 of 9 skills, and a URL rename now means a seven-file sweep in the implementor that no gate reads (finding 1).
- Action: correct eight → nine and add a `reagent-migration` line to the exclusion note (or a row); then decide: (A) the implementor routes through the table — add the five missing rows and convert its 64 URLs to label cites, which also puts it under the anchor gate; or (B) amend `:3` and `:61` to say the implementor pins the spec by checkout and cites pages directly, and drop `[impl]` as "primary". B is the smaller change and matches what the implementor actually does.

### 7. Every mirror page describes an older skill, and the concrete casualty is the leaf rosters and phase counts they carry  [CONFIRMED] [severity: low] [kind: packaging] [size: S]
- Where: `docs/skills/{re-frame-migration,re-frame2,re-frame2-xray,reagent-migration,re-frame2-pair}.md` "Where the skill lives" bullets; `docs/skills/re-frame-migration.md:7,30` ("six-phase"); `:45` ("Guide chapter 18").
- What: the class the sibling reviewers already report, noted once here; what ELSE it breaks is the per-page leaf inventory and the phase description, which no gate reads because each mirror links the `references/` DIRECTORY rather than the files.
- Evidence: commits to `skills/<name>` since its mirror was last touched — re-frame2 115, pair 36, migration 29, improver 22, pair-retro 17, implementor 12, xray 7, reagent-migration 5, setup 3. Leaf rosters vs `ls skills/<name>/references`: migration lists 8 of 23 (missing `inventory-and-plan.md`, `guided-views-m11.md`, `floor-gate.md`, `runtime-smoke-test.md`, `issue-filing.md` and ten more — two of which `skills/README.md:303,311` singles out); xray 8 of 11 (`launch-lifecycle.md`, `launch-programmatic.md`, `shared-components.md` absent); reagent-migration 3 of 8 (`procedure.md`, `mental-model.md`, `gotchas.md`, `end-state.md`, `ssr-hydrate.md` absent); re-frame2 roughly 16 of 31 (no `flows.md`, `images.md`, `views.md`, `history.md`, `machine-schemas.md`, `xray.md`, `ssr-authoring.md`, …); pair 7 of 8 (`screen-reads.md`, which `SKILL.md:188` routes to). `re-frame-migration/SKILL.md:75-77` has Phase 0a and 0b before Phase 1 (the index says "2-pre-flight-plus-6-phase", `skills/README.md:74`); the mirror's kickoff excerpt runs 1-6. `docs/core/25-from-re-frame-v1.md` is un-numbered in nav (`mkdocs.yml:308`) and its H1 is "From re-frame v1"; "chapter 18" names nothing. `rg 'docs/skills' scripts/*.py` = 0 (control: `skills/README` in two gates), so only link validity is gated. Setup and implementor rosters match (4/4 each); pair-retro matches (1/1).
- Action: decide: (A) hold each mirror to what `docs/skills/index.md:66` promises — pitch, triggers, kickoff, link to `SKILL.md` — and delete the leaf rosters and phase walk-throughs, which is a deletion and stops the class; or (B) keep them and have the worker regenerating each page copy the roster from `package.json` `files[]` / `ls references`. A fits the stance; B re-drifts.

## Drift census
- Index vs tree: MATCHES. `skills/README.md` claims checked against disk/CI: nine skills; installer commands and flags; five `tests/` dirs (5/5 on disk) and all three bb suites plus the reagent-migration fixture wired in `test.yml` (`skills-structural` :6173, `reagent-migration-fixture-cold-start` :6463 — the setup drift test is no longer local-only, the comment at :6255 records the wiring); `LICENSE`, `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `package.json private:true` and the baseline `files[]` on 9/9; 14 pattern leaves (14/14); nREPL-localhost reminder in setup (3 lines); Xray 10/5 tabs (`panels.md:20,66`); every `reg-*` in the trigger row real; `re-frame.adapter.reagent` real. One omission: `:230-233` names `re-frame2` and `re-frame2-pair` as the only skills shipping beyond the baseline, but `re-frame2-pair-retro` ships `agents/` too (`files[]` and disk).
- Redirect table vs targets: DRIFTS. 52 bullets; 49 resolve to a real source page (40 `spec/*.md`, migration README, story index, conformance README, VERSION, CHANGELOG, releases, examples, source); 1 dead (`guide/README/`, finding 1); 2 wrong page (023/026, finding 2). Skill index: eight → nine, `reagent-migration` unaccounted, `[setup]`/`[mig]`/`[pair]`/`[impl]` tag consumers cite zero labels (finding 6). Anchors: the gate parsed every leaf reference green (exit 0); all 58 live citations use the em-dash the labels carry.
- Installer vs README: MATCHES on documented behaviour, read on both platforms — link never copy, every `skills/*/` dir, idempotent, refuse copy without `--force`/`-Force`, `--check`/`-Check`, `--target`/`-Target`; exit 1 when a copy was skipped. One PLAUSIBLE hazard in the `.ps1` re-point branch (finding 5); the `.sh` junction comment is wrong but inert; the "test harness" `.sh:29` cites does not exist.
- Gates vs the drift classes the nine sibling reports will care about: DRIFTS (gaps). title: Authoring CSRF drift gate mistakes sensitive paths for schema entries
description: Confirmed while reviewing skills/re-frame2 in rf2-iuak6. scripts/check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py csrf_fence_problems rule 7b applies CSRF_SCHEMA_ENTRY_RE to every bracketed :csrf-token occurrence, without establishing that it is a Malli :map entry. Adding the supported registration metadata :sensitive [[:csrf-token]] to the FormAction reg-event yields CSRF-TOKEN-REQUIRED-IN-SCHEMA even when its actual event schema explicitly marks the token optional. Expected: ordinary classification paths should pass; a required token entry in a real schema should still fail. The current review keeps the classification advice inline to respect shared-script ownership. Extend the bounded parser/negative controls, then put the classification metadata directly in the canonical recipe.

Correctness: Inspected dispatched server-frame setup, both debug postures, wire decoding, strict-vs-structural schema controls, JVM view evaluation and real registration redaction with a schema-only counterexample. title: core-instrumentation: always-on error record :event skips the event registration's :sensitive marks (dev trace and sink route redact, corpus record ships raw)
description:
## Defect

The always-on error record built by `error-emit/dispatch-on-error!` puts the dispatched event under `:event` after only two scrubs: the router's path-overlap / `redact-interceptor` pass (`redacted-event-from-ctx`) and an app-db-rooted `elide-wire-value` walk. It never applies the event REGISTRATION's own `:sensitive` / `:large` marks — the EP-0015 owner of event args. The other two channels for the same failure both apply them: the dev trace (`project-trace-event` → `project-event-tags`) and the frame sink route (`project-error-record` → `project-event-slot`). So `reg-event :login {:sensitive [[:password]]}` throwing delivers `[:login {:password "hunter2"}]` raw to every `register-error-listener!` consumer.

Two of those consumers matter:
- The SSR error-projection listener lifts `:event` onto `:tags` for projectors. On the always-on path, custom SSR error projectors therefore see the raw arg — in production, the only path that runs.
- The dev browser console fallback prints the record.

The namespace docstring still presents this record as the feed "For off-box observability shippers (Sentry, Honeybadger, Rollbar)" with `:event` "(elided)".

## Where

- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/error_emit.cljc:607-613` — `elided-event` is `elide-wire-value event {:frame frame-id}` only. `:633-641` builds the record, and `:645` fans it out.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:1085` — `emit-event (rf.privacy/redacted-event-from-ctx ctx)`, which carries the overlap / `redact-interceptor` paths but not registration marks. Passed to `emit-error-both!` at `:1125`.
- The registration pass exists and is always-on: `implementation/core/src/re_frame/classification.cljc:424-458` (`redact-event-by-registration`), published as `:classification/redact-event-by-registration` at `:1251`. `projection.cljc:274-316` already uses it for the sink route.
- Consumers: `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/error_listener.cljc:408-467` (generic lift of `:event` onto `:tags`); the dev console fallback at `error_emit.cljc:232-271`; the namespace docstring at `error_emit.cljc:16-36`.

## Failure scenario

`(rf/reg-event :login {:sensitive [[:password]]} (fn [_ _] (throw (ex-info "login failed" {}))))`, then `(rf/dispatch-sync [:login {:user "bob" :password "hunter2-PASSWORD"}])` on a frame with an `:observability :errors` sink.
- Dev trace `:event` → `[:login {:user "bob", :password :rf/redacted}]`.
- Sink record `:event` → `[:login {:user "bob", :password :rf/redacted}]`.
- Corpus record `:event` → `[:login {:user "bob", :password "hunter2-PASSWORD"}]`.

## Evidence

EXECUTED — a bounded JVM probe from the reviewer scratch dir against the frozen tree at `034d0c8fc8` (nothing written to the tree), producing exactly the three results in the scenario. The dev-trace and sink results are the controls; the probe finds the password in the corpus record.

Bounding (inspected): since rf2-kuky.69 the registry is IMPLEMENTATION-tier (`error_emit.cljc:124-133`, Spec 009 §Observability channels), so the framework's own capture sites are its main readers. That is why this is filed at P3 rather than as an off-box P1. Query-vector records (the `:rf.error/sub-*` / subscribe realm) are raw by ruling (#6441 / rf2-zwgqe) and are not affected. The 2026-09-16 review of this slice (rf2-pk4i6.11) did not raise this. A tracker full-text search finds no bead on registration redaction of the corpus record.

## Smallest fix

In `dispatch-on-error!`, when the event is not a raw-identity query vector, pass it through the `:classification/redact-event-by-registration` hook (under the record owner's resolution scope, as `projection/redact-event-by-registration` does) before the existing `elide-wire-value` walk. Also correct the namespace docstring so it no longer directs off-box shippers here. Fence: `implementation/core/src/re_frame/error_emit.cljc`, plus a test beside the error-emit record-shape tests. No hot-zone file.

## Gates

JVM core artefact: `clojure -M:test` from `implementation/core`. `dispatch-on-error!` is plain cljc. `npm run test:cljs` covers the CLJS lane. `implementation/ssr` `clojure -M:test` is a consumer check.

## Decision needed

No.
notes:
## Worker verdict (2026-09-23): FIXED as prescribed, in PR #10281 (commit d1ea3bc301)

Reproduced at trunk 4b627ee9e2, exactly as described:
- dev trace `:event` → `[:login {:user "bob", :password :rf/redacted}]`;
- sink record → the same;
- corpus record → `[:login {:user "bob", :password "hunter2-PASSWORD"}]`.
After the fix, all three are redacted.

Fix: `re-frame.error-emit/dispatch-on-error!` now runs a private `redact-event-by-registration` before the existing `elide-wire-value` walk. It calls the always-on `:classification/redact-event-by-registration` hook inside the record owner's resolution scope (`:live-frame/call-with-frame-resolution`, as `projection/redact-event-by-registration` does). It's skipped for raw-identity query vectors and nil events, as before. Both hooks are late-bound; an unbound hook is inert. The ns docstring now says the registry is implementation-tier (rf2-kuky.69) and points off-box shippers at the frame's `:observability :errors` sink.

Regression: `re-frame.error-record-event-registration-redaction-cljs-test` (new, dual-runtime, always-on, on the prod-gate roster and green there). A real throwing handler under a real sink route, with the sink record as the in-test control.
