title: CLJS schema :decode may skip json-transformer coercion: nothing requires malli.transform
description:
UNVERIFIED — found by source reading only, by the http-decode worker (rf2-v1cxy, PR #10485); not yet run.

Claim: on CLJS, schema-driven :decode coerces nothing. spec/014 §Schema-driven step 3 says a schema :decode "coerces with json-transformer". On CLJS, malli.transform/json-transformer only resolves if something in the build requires malli.transform. Nothing in the framework does: re-frame.schemas.malli requires only malli.core and malli.error.

Consequence (by reading): decode runs Malli with a nil transformer, which Malli treats as a no-op (malli 0.20.1 core.cljc:604-609), then validates the UNCOERCED JSON. No warning fires. So a :keyword, :uuid or enum-of-keywords schema could reject a well-formed reply on CLJS that the JVM accepts, because on the JVM requiring-resolve loads the namespace.

MAYOR RULING (2026-09-26): the spec states the behaviour, so this is a code-side defect if it reproduces, not a design choice. Required:
1. REPRODUCE on CLJS first, as a node-lane test: a schema with a :keyword field decoding a JSON string. Use the JVM as the positive control, where it coerces.
2. If it reproduces, make json-transformer available on CLJS whenever schema decode runs. Use the smallest fix at the owner, e.g. re-frame.schemas.malli requiring malli.transform, or the decode path requiring it. Add a CLJS regression, shown red with the fix removed.
3. If it does not reproduce, "the premise does not hold", with the probe, closes it.
Keep bundle isolation in mind: an app that does not use schemas must not pay for malli.transform. Check the bundle-isolation / perf-bundle gates.
notes:
== DOCS FOLLOW-ON (mayor, 2026-09-26)
docs/async/tutorial.md Step 3 currently says JSON coercion needs malli.transform, which a ClojureScript build must require (the JVM loads it). docs/async/http.md:230 links there. Both were written by rf2-s0i3z step 2 (session re-frame2-f8). If the fix makes the framework load malli.transform, both sites need rewording once the PR merges: route that to f8, which has agreed to do it together with the rf2-n1w8n line.

== WORKER VERDICT (httpfix-k3v1o, PR #10522, 2026-09-26): REPRODUCED and FIXED
Probe: new node-lane test re-frame.http-schema-decode-cljs-test. It requires re-frame.schemas and deliberately NOT malli.transform, then decodes {"id":7,"status":"active"} against [:map [:id :int] [:status :keyword]]. With the fix absent, its malli.core precondition passed and decode threw :rf.error/http-schema-validation-failed ("active" not coerced). JVM control: decode-response-body-schema-success-parses-then-coerces coerces the same shape. No cljs/cljc namespace in the tree required malli.transform, and within malli 0.20.1 only malli/transform.cljc itself names it, so the node-test build carried none.
Fix: re-frame.schemas.malli :requires #?(:cljs [malli.transform]) and calls nothing from it. The node-test compile went 2094 -> 2099 files, and the probe goes green.
Bundle isolation: an app without schemas never loads it (only the schemas adapter requires it). Measured with npm run test:schemas-bundle (core + schemas, no http): margin 40.2 KB before, 40.4 KB after (+0.2 KB, the recorded cost of a namespace nothing reaches; rooting costs ~5.5 KB), PASS within 20-44 KB. An app with schemas AND http now pays for json-transformer, which is what spec/014 step 3 specifies. bundle-isolation, perf-bundle and the playground job are left to CI; the playground SCI bundle carries re-frame.schemas but not re-frame.http, so nothing there reaches malli.transform.
FOLLOW-ONS: docs/async/tutorial.md:136 (Step 3) says a ClojureScript build must require malli.transform for coercion, and docs/async/http.md:457 links there; after PR #10522 requiring re-frame.schemas is enough. spec/010-Schemas.md:769 (restrict list) says malli.transform is only required directly by an app reaching managed-HTTP decode. That may want rewording now that the adapter requires it, though it is retained only where the HTTP decoder reaches it. Spec is held and was not edited.
close_reason:
The premise holds; fixed by PR #10522, merged 2026-09-26T07:51:19Z at trunk c6154b8b6d.
- Reproduced on the node lane: with re-frame.schemas required, malli.core was in the build but malli.transform was not, so "active" failed validation against a :keyword field where the JVM coerces it.
- Fix: #?(:cljs [malli.transform]) in re-frame.schemas.malli. The CLJS test re-frame.http-schema-decode-cljs-test went red with the fix removed.
- Bundle: the schemas-bundle gate (core plus schemas, no http) margin moved 40.2 KB -> 40.4 KB under a 44 KB ceiling (+0.2 KB for an uncalled namespace). An app without schemas never loads malli.transform. An app with schemas and HTTP pays for json-transformer, which is what spec/014 step 3 specifies. bundle-isolation and perf-bundle passed in CI.
- Follow-ons routed: docs/async/tutorial.md:136 (Step 3) and docs/async/http.md:457 go to the docs/async review (session re-frame2-f8). spec/010-Schemas.md:769's restrict-list line, which says an app requires malli.transform directly, goes to the spec-reconcile worker (worker/specrec-kusgs).

title: JVM :rf.http/header-invalid trace leaks the rejected header value via :cause (spec 014:165 says omitted)
description:
On the JVM transport, the :rf.http/header-invalid trace leaks the rejected header VALUE through :cause. spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:165 (and docs/async/http.md:98-100, which follows the spec) says the value is omitted.

Measured by the docs/async correctness review (rf2-s0i3z step 2) at trunk f89e28ec64: a header value "tok\nSECRETVALUE" produced a trace whose :cause is the JDK exception message, invalid header value: "tok\nSECRETVALUE". Code: implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/transport_jvm.cljc:193-201.

Headers are exactly where tokens live (Authorization), so this is a secret-in-trace leak on the JVM/SSR path. Fix direction: scrub the value from the JDK message, or replace :cause with a fixed description naming only the header NAME.
notes:
== MAYOR RULING (2026-09-26)
Code-side. The spec (014:165) says the value is omitted, and a header is where tokens live. Replace :cause with a fixed description that names only the header NAME, and carry no part of the JDK message that echoes the value. Add a JVM regression with a sentinel value such as "tok\nSECRETVALUE": the sentinel must be absent from the whole stringified trace, not merely from :cause. Show it red with the fix removed. No spec or docs change. Dispatched in the http cluster with rf2-n1w8n and rf2-ntuvc.

== WORKER VERDICT (httpfix-k3v1o, PR #10522, 2026-09-26): FIXED, both hosts
Reproduced at trunk c7d1190398: a JVM header value "tok\nSECRETVALUE" produced :cause = invalid header value: "tok\nSECRETVALUE". (The trace id is :rf.warning/http-header-invalid; the title's :rf.http/header-invalid is shorthand for it.)
Fix per ruling: :cause is a fixed sentence from re-frame.http.encoding/header-invalid-cause naming only the header NAME. Applied on the CLJS host too, beyond the bead's JVM scope: Fetch Headers.append leaks identically (Node 24 message: Headers.append: "tok\nSECRETVALUE" is an invalid header value.), and spec/014:165 covers both hosts.
Regressions: JVM invalid-header-warning-carries-no-part-of-the-rejected-value (http_transport_security_test.clj) and CLJS cljs-fetch-invalid-header-warning-carries-no-part-of-the-rejected-value (http_cljs_test.cljs). Each asserts the sentinel is absent from the pr-str of every captured trace event. Red at trunk and red with each host's fix planted out (JVM: 1 failing assertion; CLJS: 1 failure); restores verified by committed blob hash. Green after: http JVM 533 tests / 4173 assertions, exit 0; full node lane 12918 / 66961, exit 0. No spec change.
close_reason:
Fixed by PR #10522, merged 2026-09-26T07:51:19Z at trunk c6154b8b6d.

- Fix: :cause is now a fixed sentence naming only the header NAME, from a new re-frame.http.encoding/header-invalid-cause. The CLJS side got the same fix, because Node's Headers.append error echoes the value the same way, and spec/014:165 covers both hosts.

title: test(pair-mcp): the nREPL-not-found checks match a substring, so the wrong error id passes
description:
ROUTING (mayor, 2026-09-26): dispatchable. No live worker holds tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp. The test runs on the shadow-cljs lane (:server-test), which is machine-wide exclusive, so the dispatch needs an explicit lane grant: queue it behind the current holder. The issue's instructions are the spec. Its step 3 plant (the server emits the bare fallback -> red) is the required control. Also re-verify the issue's claim that the docs/skills pages were corrected: if docs/skills/re-frame2-pair.md or skills/re-frame2-pair/references/{errors,mcp-transport}.md still name the bare :nrepl-port-not-found at tip, fix them in the same PR.

From GitHub issue #10517 (closed into this bead). Original text:

**Type:** bug (test strength) · **Priority:** P3 · **Size:** small, one test file

## Gap

When no nREPL port resolves, `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/server.cljs` (~lines 330-337) throws `ex-info` with the message `":rf.error/pair-mcp-nrepl-port-not-found"` and data `{:rf.error/id :rf.error/pair-mcp-nrepl-port-not-found …}`. It uses that id as the reason in the degraded envelope (~line 616), and falls back to the bare `:nrepl-port-not-found` only when the error carries no id.

`tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/test/stdio-roundtrip.js` checks this in three places (lines ~222, ~235, ~247), all with:

```js
text.includes('nrepl-port-not-found')
```

That substring is inside both the namespaced id and the bare fallback. So the test passes whichever one the server emits, and would still pass if the namespaced id were lost. The header comment (line ~15) and line ~120 also name the bare `:nrepl-port-not-found` as the expected envelope.

That is how the docs came to name the wrong id. `docs/skills/re-frame2-pair.md`, `skills/re-frame2-pair/references/errors.md` and `references/mcp-transport.md` all said `:nrepl-port-not-found`, and nothing checked them against the server. They were corrected in the `docs/skills` review PR.

## What to do

1. Tighten the three assertions to match the full id, `:rf.error/pair-mcp-nrepl-port-not-found`. Or parse the envelope and compare its reason field, if the envelope is structured.
2. Update the comments at ~15 and ~120 to name the id the server emits.
3. Prove the tightened test bites. Temporarily make the server emit the bare fallback (drop the `:rf.error/id`), confirm the test goes red, then revert.
4. Leave the `:unknown-tool` check at ~256-266 alone. Its substring use is a negative assertion, so it is correct as written.

## Acceptance

- The three checks fail if the server emits anything other than `:rf.error/pair-mcp-nrepl-port-not-found`, shown by the step 3 plant.
- The node lane that runs this test is green.
- The test takes the shadow-cljs build lane (`:server-test`), so follow the machine-wide shadow-cljs exclusive in CLAUDE.md.
notes:
== LANE QUEUE (mayor, 2026-09-26 17:21 AUSEST)
The shadow-cljs lane was released by worker/httpfix-k3v1o at 17:21, and nobody holds it now. This bead is FIRST in the lane queue. Grant the lane explicitly in its dispatch brief when a worker slot frees, after checking that no one has taken it since.

== NOTE (mayor, 2026-09-26)
PR #10518 (docs/skills pass, open) edits skills/re-frame2-pair/references/errors.md and mcp-transport.md, and its correctness commit is titled 'real nREPL-not-found reason'. It is probably the 'docs/skills review PR' this issue refers to. The eval-cljs, snapshot and get-path checks in tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/test/stdio-roundtrip.js now compare the envelope's structuredContent.reason for equality with "rf.error/pair-mcp-nrepl-port-not-found" (one shared predicate, isNreplPortNotFound); the header and roots/list comments name the emitted id; the :unknown-tool negative check is untouched.

And NO CI job runs pair-mcp's stdio-roundtrip.js: test.yml's pair-mcp job runs npm test, check:descriptors, build and test:stdin-eof-shutdown, and the node test/stdio-roundtrip.js step in test.yml is story-mcp's copy; implementation/scripts/test-mcp-conformance.cjs likewise runs only story-mcp's. title: spec/012-Routing: not-found placeholder view does not exist; bare :keyword slot rule contradicts itself
description:
MAYOR RULING (2026-09-26): the code is the reference here. There is no built-in placeholder view. Correct spec/012 lines ~116/~1069 to say that the not-found slice is committed and :rf.warning/no-not-found-route is emitted. Make ~1414 agree with ~1347 and the registry: a bare :keyword slot is refused at reg-route with :rf.error/route-keyword-unbounded-unsupported. Do not implement a placeholder. From GitHub issue #10488 (closed into this bead). Original text: **Type:** bug (spec) · **Priority:** P2 · **Found by:** the docs/routing review (#10481, superseded by #10483) ## Summary `spec/012-Routing.md` disagrees with the implementation in two places, and in one of them it also contradicts itself. The routing guide (#10483) now follows the code, so the spec is the outlier. ## Evidence (measured at trunk `origin/main`, 2026-09-26) **1. The not-found placeholder view does not exist.** - `spec/012-Routing.md:116` and `:1069` say that when no `:rf.route/not-found` route is registered, the runtime "falls back to a built-in placeholder view (a minimal `

Not Found

` page)". - No such view is implemented. Searching `implementation/` for `placeholder` and `Not Found` finds nothing outside tests. - What the code actually does: the not-found slice is still committed and `:rf.warning/no-not-found-route` is emitted (`implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/plan.cljc:202,234`, `url_change.cljc:391`). **2. The bare `:keyword` slot rule contradicts itself.** - `spec/012-Routing.md:1347` says a bare (unbounded) `:keyword` route key "is rejected fail-loud at `reg-route`" with `:rf.error/route-keyword-unbounded-unsupported`. - `spec/012-Routing.md:1414` (keyword-interning defence #2) says a bare `:keyword` query slot "is treated as an unbounded intern site … and the value is preserved as a string". - The code matches line 1347: `reg-route` throws `:rf.error/route-keyword-unbounded-unsupported` (`implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/registry.cljc:366-394`). ## Acceptance - Lines 116 and 1069 describe the real behaviour: no built-in view, the slice is committed, and the warning is emitted. Alternatively, if a placeholder is wanted, it is implemented instead. Pick one; the spec and the code must agree. - Line 1414's defence #2 is rewritten to agree with line 1347 and the code: bare `:keyword` is rejected at registration, and only `[:enum …]` choices intern. - `mkdocs build --strict` stays green (the build stages `spec/`).
notes:

title: re-frame-migration: run the codemod as a git dependency, like reagent-migration, instead of from a pinned checkout
description:

title: skill(resources): shared HTTP decoration recipe registers without a frame
description:
The request-decoration recipe promoted by PR #10534 is not runnable at ordinary namespace load. skills/re-frame2/patterns/resources.md:158-163 registers :auth with only :before: no :frame override, no with-frame wrapper, and no instruction to run it in a frame-scoped boot event. Both SKILL.md and patterns/managed-http.md now route general authentication/base-URL tasks to this recipe. The runtime requires an explicit frame or a carried frame scope, so copying it alongside the resource registrations raises :rf.error/no-frame-context and installs no auth interceptor.

This omission predates #10534; the PR reviewed and promoted the recipe without correcting it. It remains at origin/main 384335618a8bfd6fe85528b639bbf2380b9ec78e. middleware.cljc:174-185 resolves the frame with require-current-frame! when :frame is absent. Its implementation and the core facade match the isolated current-source export used for the probe.

Bounded JVM reproduction ran the recipe interceptor map through the implementation registration function outside any carried frame: TOP_LEVEL_ERROR :rf.error/no-frame-context. The same map with :frame :rf/default succeeds against a live fixture frame. Exit 0; evidence ai/probe-10534-audit-sep23-monitor-3.log and .exit in audit-sep23-monitor. The fixture normally supplies an ambient frame; this probe explicitly binds it nil so it reproduces namespace-load behavior rather than hiding the defect. No HTTP request is issued.

Show the intended existing frame boundary in the recipe (explicit :frame or a frame-scoped boot/with-frame example), and say when that frame is available. Keep the shared decoration pattern; no new API or fallback default is needed. Related earlier closed authoring review: rf2-iuak6.
acceptance_criteria: The documented recipe registers successfully in its stated boot context and targets the intended frame. A no-scope check still raises no-frame-context; no implicit default frame is added.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #10610 (commit c7163a3474, "skill(resources): the request-decoration recipe names its frame").

Defect confirmed at trunk 98facb7f83. skills/re-frame2/patterns/resources.md §Request decoration registered :auth with only :before. re-frame.http.middleware/reg-http-interceptor calls require-current-frame! when :frame is absent, and nothing on the page supplied one.

Fix: the recipe now carries `:frame :app`. A new paragraph says an HTTP interceptor chain belongs to one frame, names `(rf/with-frame :app …)` as the block form, and says a frameless registration at namespace load raises :rf.error/no-frame-context with no :rf/default fallback. It also says the frame need not exist yet: the chain is keyed by frame id and read each time a request is issued, so the recipe can register at load or boot, before frame-root or make-frame creates the frame. No new API and no default were added. SKILL.md:97 and patterns/managed-http.md:34 only route to the recipe and carry no frameless code, so they are unchanged.

Decisive measurement. A scratch deps project on this branch's implementation/{core,http,resources,schemas} extracted the fenced block from the page and load-string'd it in a fresh namespace with re-frame.frame/*current-frame* bound to nil. It then ran make-frame {:id :app}, seeded {:auth {:token "abc123" :user {:id "u-1"}}}, and dispatch-synced [:rf.resource/ensure {:resource :current-user …}] into :app through a :rf.http/managed stub that runs the real request chain (rf.http.test-support/run-request-chain), with no network.
- OLD block (page at 98facb7f83): exit 3. It raised ex-info {:rf.error/id :rf.error/no-frame-context, :operation :reg-http-interceptor, :event-id :auth}, and the :app chain was nil.
- NEW block, verbatim from the edited page: exit 0. The chain registered on (:app), and the captured request was {:method :get, :url "/api/user", :headers {"Authorization" "Token abc123"}}.
- Planted wrong value, `{:frame  :app ` changed to `{:frame  :other ` (match count 1): exit 1. The chain registered on (:other), and the :app request carried no Authorization header.
- OLD block wrapped in (rf/with-frame :app …) before the frame existed: exit 0, same header. This confirms the with-frame alternative the page names.
This meets the acceptance criteria. The documented recipe registers with no scope in play and targets the named frame, and the no-scope form still raises no-frame-context.

title: Route navigation event vectors still carry declared-sensitive params raw on traces: [:rf.route/navigate ...] and [:rf.route/url-requested ...]
description:
Found by rf2-2p7fo's worker (PR #10611, merged at trunk 940f8334f1), outside its fence. Each point below is a CLAIM; reproduce it first.

PR #10611 made navigation URL strings redact what their route declares sensitive:
- `re-frame.routing.resolve/redact-declared-url` replaces declared path segments, query values and fragment with the redaction sentinel, and leaves undeclared parts verbatim;
- it is applied in `plan-trace-tags`;
- core's event redaction reaches it for `[:rf.route/handle-url-change url]` through the late-bind hook `:routing/project-url-change-event-args`.

The worker reports three siblings that still egress raw:
1. `[:rf.route/navigate <route-id> <params>]` and `[:rf.route/url-requested <url>]` carry a declared secret raw in the event vector: the `:rf.event/*` trace rows, and anywhere else event args are projected.
2. `:rf.nav/push-url` fx args carry the declared secret raw. The worker says `nav_fx.cljc` keeps them raw on purpose. If a stated reason exists (the host must receive the real URL), the fx EXECUTES with raw args, and only its trace projection is in question. Verify which of the two applies. If the raw trace is deliberate and documented, record that and drop this point.
3. `implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs/memo.cljc`: the `validate-and-trace` docstring still names only the machine and route subs as projected. PR #10611 added resource and mutation read subs. Correct the docstring to the code.

RULING (mayor, 2026-09-29), from rf2-2p7fo's ruling: a declared-sensitive route param is redacted wherever it egresses, and undeclared parts stay verbatim. So point 1 extends the existing hook or projector, preferring REUSE of `:routing/project-url-change-event-args` and `redact-declared-url` over a new hook. In-process values stay raw.

A resource sub's query vector carrying its declared params is NOT in scope: Spec 015 documents it as a known fail-open.

Evidence: a JVM regression per fixed point, showing:
- the declared param redacted on the trace;
- an undeclared param verbatim;
- red with the fix removed.
close_reason:
FIXED (points 1 and 3) in PR #10618 (branch worker/routeegress-li9em, commit "fix(routing): a navigation request redacts what its route declares sensitive on traces"). Point 2 was dropped as deliberate and documented.

## Point 1: decisive measurement, inline

The real shapes are single request maps, [:rf.route/navigate {:to ... :params ... :query ...}] / {:url ...} and [:rf.route/url-requested {:url ...}], rather than the positional [:rf.route/navigate <route-id> <params>] the bead described.

New JVM regressions sit in routing_url_trace_classification_cljs_test.cljc (dual-target, so the CLJS node lane grades them too). They use a route declaring [[:params :secret] [:query :token]] next to undeclared :other and :page.
- At base: 3 new tests failed, every :rf.event/v copy of the navigate {:to}, navigate {:url} and url-requested request carrying both secrets raw. The undeclared-route control was green.
- With the fix: 8 tests / 31 assertions / 0 failures. A {:to} request reads {:params {:secret :rf/redacted :other "visible"} :query {:token :rf/redacted :page "2"}}. A :url reads "/acct/rf%2Fredacted/visible?token=rf/redacted&page=2". The undeclared-route request is identical? to the dispatched map, and the slice stays raw.
- Sabotage (navigate and url-requested removed from core's chokepoint case): 3 failures, control green. The restore was verified by blob hash.

The fix reuses the hook and projector, as the ruling prefers:
- core redact-event-by-registration sends the first argument of handle-url-change, navigate and url-requested through :routing/project-url-change-event-args;
- routing publishes resolve/project-nav-event-arg behind it. A string, or a request's :url, goes through redact-declared-url. A :to request has the declared :params / :query values and a declared :fragment replaced by :rf/redacted, read off the same url-declarations.
- No new hook was added. The existing directory row is re-described for the widened argument.

## Point 2: deliberate and documented, dropped

:rf.nav/push-url's raw fx args are a trace decision, not only an execution one:
- push-url-meta's docstring declines :sensitive because the pushed URL is the navigation's behavioural identity, which the :effects-routed conformance contract and the epoch :effects projection read off :rf.fx/handled's :rf.fx/args;
- routing_egress_test/push-url-not-marked-routes-real-url pins it;
- Spec 012 §Route data classification lists it as ambient by design.

Residue for the mayor: on the client the declared segment still reaches the trace through push-url's :rf.fx/handled args, one row after the now-redacted navigate event.

## Point 3

The validate-and-trace docstring (memo.cljc) now:
- names the resource and mutation read subs;
- says where each family's classification is read (registry versus owner spec);
- extends the prev-inputs paragraph to the route leaves.

## Further sibling, not fixed

An in-place request ([:rf.route/navigate {:query-merge ...}] or {:query ...} with no :to or :url) names no route, and the event chokepoint has no frame to find the current one. Its declared values still ride raw, and Spec 012 now says so.

title: Use the specified UTF-8 ordering for CEDN-1 map and set tokens
description: EP-0012 Canonical Byte Encoding and spec/Conventions.md:989 require lexicographic UTF-8 byte ordering of map keys and set tokens. implementation/core/src/re_frame/identity.cljc:288-315 instead uses host string sort-by/sort (UTF-16 order). For tokens s: followed by a quoted U+E000 versus U+10000, host order selects U+10000 first, while UTF-8 order selects U+E000 first. A read-only Node token probe confirmed the inversion, and the encode-map/encode-set source matches that host-order mechanism. Existing hosts can agree with each other yet differ from a conforming independent port. Correct sorting or obtain a recorded contract ruling; add meaningful cross-host fixtures for astral/BMP ordering without broad redesign. This follow-up is outside the EP-only PR.
acceptance_criteria: Map and set canonical token ordering matches the normative CEDN-1 byte law on JVM and CLJS, including the U+E000/U+10000 counterexample; portable identity tests pass.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #10746 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/10746). re-frame.identity now sorts CEDN-1 map keys and set elements with compare-canonical-bytes. It ranks the first differing UTF-16 code unit by code point, so the order is UTF-8 byte order with no per-comparison encoding: surrogates rank above U+E000-U+FFFF and nothing else moves.
Measured on both hosts. The new dual-host tests in identity-cedn1-cljs-test (a U+E000/U+10000 mixed map and set, keyword and composite tokens, and a UTF-8 byte-oracle check over a boundary pool) plus two new :canonical-bytes calls in spec/conformance/fixtures/cedn1-path-algebra-golden.edn are RED with the encoder at the merge base: JVM scoped run exit 1, CLJS npm run test:cljs exit 1, each with 7 failures (6 identity assertions + the conformance corpus). With the fix, JVM core full exit 0 (2081 tests / 12004 assertions) and CLJS exit 0 (11743 / 63776). The control deftest ordinary-ordering-is-unchanged is green both before and after.
No committed golden or digest changed: every pinned CEDN-1 fixture was ASCII, where UTF-16 and UTF-8 order coincide. No existing test asserted the UTF-16 order.
Out of scope, left for the mayor to file: routing registry.cljc sorts query keys by canonical-bytes with the host comparator although its docstring claims the CEDN-1 map order; schemas digest.cljc could reuse the comparator.

title: Use the CEDN-1 UTF-8 comparator for routing query-key order (and reuse it in schemas digest)
description:

Its test defects went to rf2-ar8by (closed): read its outcome before acting on a first-pass weakness note.

It enters shadow-cljs through the mayor's lane grant. The rf2-zbnoc.3-.10 workers used one scoped compile holding renamed base copies of only the changed files, plus one plant compile, in a single short window. That is the model.

KEEP BY RULE: tests pinning spec wording or spec/conformance fixtures; gate and ratchet self-tests; tests of documented error ids (rf2-98kzs.3 ruling: an error-id duplicate may go only while a kept test asserts the same id on the identical input); tests cited by name outside their file (scripts/test-core-prod-gate.sh's header comment names suites by family, so check it before folding a whole file away); regression tests for real past bugs, unless a retained test demonstrably catches the same failure.

title: Live machine examples that use HTTP or Fresco in docs/machines/
description:
## This section

`docs/machines/` already has a live cell (`concepts.md`), because machines were in the engine before. What is new is that machines can now be combined with **HTTP** and **Fresco**:
- a machine that spawns `:rf.http/managed`, against a stub;
- machine state rendered by a Fresco view (`(h/sub [:rf/machine id])`).

Pages that reference these today:
- `actors.md`, `fan-out-and-join.md`, `tutorial.md`: machines that spawn requests. A stubbed request makes the actor and the join visible, including a failure path.
- `inspecting-machines.md`: anything inspectable in a cell.
- `concepts.md`: optionally a Fresco version of the turnstile, if the page benefits.

Only add cells for behaviour that needed HTTP or Fresco. Plain machine examples were always possible, so they are not this bead's job.

## Start after

PR #10791 (Playground: Fresco and every optional artefact in cljs-rf2 cells) must be merged first. Check with `gh pr view 10791 --json state`. Until it merges, the engine on `main` cannot run the cells this bead asks for.

## The new capability

The docs' live ` ```cljs-rf2 ` cells run on `docs/cljs/playground-rf2.js`, built from `docs/tools/playground/sci`. That engine now bundles:

- re-frame2 core and reagent2 (reagent-slim), as before;
- **Fresco**: `re-frame.fresco` and its `forms`, `overlay` and `motion` modules;
- **every optional artefact**:
  - machines, flows and schemas (as before);
  - **HTTP**: `re-frame.http.managed`, plus `re-frame.http.test-support` for stubs;
  - **resources**, **routing**, **epoch** and **SSR**.

Before PR #10791, a cell could use only core, reagent2, machines, flows and schemas. So pages teaching Fresco, HTTP, resources, routing, epoch history or SSR could only show static code. Now a reader can run those examples, edit them, and see the result.

## How to write a live cell

The fence is ` ```cljs-rf2 `; there is no separate Fresco fence. A cell runs when the page loads, and again on Mod-Enter after an edit. Its last form is rendered.

- **Which renderer.** The last form renders through **Fresco** when it contains:
  - a Fresco view (`h/defview`), or `h/frame-root` / `h/frame-provider`; or
  - a handler written as data, such as `:on-click [:inc]`.

  Otherwise it renders through **reagent2**. Plain hiccup looks the same either way. One page can mix reagent2 and Fresco cells, but one tree cannot. A plain fn or `reg-view` head inside a Fresco tree raises `:rf.error/fresco-bad-head`.
- **What a cell can require.**
  - `re-frame.core`, which includes `reg-view`, `reg-machine`, `reg-flow`, `reg-app-schema`, `reg-resource`, `reg-route`, `epoch-history` and `restore-epoch!`
  - `re-frame.fresco`, `.forms`, `.overlay` and `.motion`
  - `reagent2.*`
  - `re-frame.schemas`
  - `re-frame.http.managed` and `re-frame.http.test-support`
  - `re-frame.resources`, `re-frame.routing`, `re-frame.epoch` and `re-frame.ssr`
- **Not available:**
  - `h/defhost`, since a cell has no foreign React component to wrap
  - `re-frame.fresco.native`, `re-frame.fresco.server` and the Fresco test kit
  - Story, Xray, and the Ring/Node SSR hosts
- **Frames.** A cell that creates no frame uses `:rf/default`. A cell that wraps its tree in `frame-root` uses that frame, as a real app does.
- **Shared page state.** All cells on a page share the registrar and the frames, so a later cell can render a view an earlier cell registered. Leaving the page unmounts everything, destroys frames and removes the page's registrations.
- **HTTP without a network.** Stub `:rf.http/managed` and route the frame to the stub:

  ```clojure
  (require '[re-frame.core :as rf]
           '[re-frame.http.managed]
           '[re-frame.http.test-support :as http-test-support])

  (http-test-support/install-managed-request-stubs!
    {[:get "https://api.example.com/articles/intro"] {:reply {:ok {:title "Welcome"}}}})

  ;; ... events, subs and a view ...

  [rf/frame-root {:id :demo :fx-overrides {:rf.http/managed :rf.http/managed-test-stub}}
   [article-view]]
  ```

  - Key each stub on the exact `[method url]` the request sends. A miss reaches `:on-failure` with `no stub matched`.
  - Use `{:reply {:failure {...}}}` to demo errors.
  - Install stubs and never uninstall them: the stub stack is global.
  - Real requests also work, but only to `https` endpoints that allow CORS, and they depend on the network. Prefer stubs.
- **Never create a `:url-bound? true` frame.** It would take over the docs site's address bar. Routing works on in-memory frames.
- **Working examples to copy:**
  - The cells in `docs/tools/playground/test/smoke.test.mjs` cover a Fresco view, a data-handler cell, a stubbed HTTP request, a `reg-resource` load, `reg-route` and `render-to-string`; all of them pass in CI.
  - `docs/tools/playground/README.md` has the full rules and a troubleshooting table.

## What to do

1. Read `docs/AUTHORING.md` and follow it. Examples must be real, use the actual API, and be self-contained; keep the page's continuing example domain.
2. Go through each page in this section and find the examples where **running** the code would teach something reading it cannot. Good candidates are behaviour that changes on a click, a request moving through loading, success and failure, data flowing into a view, and a rendered result. Introduce running examples there: convert a static block to ` ```cljs-rf2 `, or add a cell next to it.
3. Do not convert every block. Keep code static when it is:
   - a fragment, an `ns` form or configuration;
   - server-side, or needs the unavailable pieces listed above;
   - or the live version would need setup that buries the point.

   A page with one well-chosen live example beats a page where every block runs. If a page gains nothing, leave it.
4. Within one page, give each cell's registrations distinct ids unless a later cell is meant to reuse an earlier one's. Cells share the registrar.
5. Fix stale prose you touch, but keep the diff to this section.

## How to verify

Nothing in CI runs the docs' cells, so clicking them yourself is the only check. Say what you clicked in the PR body.

- Build the engine: `cd docs/tools/playground && npm install && npm run build`. `npm run build:rf2` enters shadow-cljs, so it uses the machine-wide build lane; ask the coordinator for it first (`AGENTS.md`).
- Run `mkdocs serve` from the repo root. Open every page you changed and use every cell: it renders, its buttons and inputs work, and no cell shows `ERROR`. Then navigate to another page and back.
- Run `mkdocs build --strict` and `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py`.

It runs the complete login table and a cut-down Step 5 view in two frames, one where the server accepts (route stub returning a token) and one where it rejects (:rf.http/managed-canned-failure). Shows :authed with the token in app-db, the guard refusing an empty submit, and lockout on the third failure.

In the second it never answers: the requests go to a no-op reg-fx, so a live :auth/request#N stays in :running. Cancel destroys it, a fresh sign-in spawns a new id, and the 8 s :timeout fires :on-timeout.
- fan-out-and-join.md: runs the session-startup :spawn-all join in two frames. With both endpoints stubbed it reaches :ready with both fold results. With every request failing it goes to :failed through :on-any-failed, and Retry fails again.

title: Test-suite pruning, third pass: implementation/fresco
description:

A later RULING note on the epic wins where the two differ.

In short: assume this suite has more tests than it needs, and prune it to the smallest suite that still catches every bug it catches today. Do not change the code under test. title: O-17 managed-HTTP guide: audit metadata-bearing :on-success/:on-failure/:reply-to prefixes; the reply append drops vector metadata (GH #10939)
description:
GitHub #10939. The O-17 companion migration/from-re-frame-v1/http-fx-to-managed-http.md (callback-mapping rows, :on-success at about L47, reached from skills/re-frame-migration/references/http-fx-to-managed-http.md) calls the split :on-success/:on-failure form the like-for-like rewrite, with the envelope appended in the v1 dispatch shape. Mayor verified at trunk cdc2307dc1: neither file mentions metadata (0 hits for metadata/with-meta), and implementation/core/src/re_frame/reply.cljc `complete` (L271) appends via `(conj (vec event) reply)` at L290. ClojureScript's vec drops vector metadata, whereas http-fx 0.2.4 dispatches `(conj on-success response)`, which keeps it. Equal event-vector values, different behaviour for any handler or interceptor that reads prefix metadata (context, telemetry flags).

Ask (docs): beside the callback mapping, add a generic detection/review rule for metadata-bearing :on-success, :on-failure and unified :reply-to prefixes. Explain how required context and telemetry are preserved or deliberately rehomed through supported, recordable routes (event payload or context/correlation, registration-owned classification). Never silently drop them, never assume metadata-free inputs, and never recommend re-frame.reply or any internal namespace to migrating apps. Acceptance: the metadata distinction sits beside the mapping, with metadata-free and metadata-bearing success/failure controls, and the approved route is verified to keep the required context without confusing equal vector values with equivalent behaviour. Examples stay consumer-independent. Docs only; implementation/core is not in scope unless Mike rules otherwise (the mayor surfaced the substrate alternative, keeping prefix metadata in complete, to him in chat).

Mayor triage 2026-10-05 at trunk cdc2307dc1: valid, filed by Mike; actioned. Read the issue in full (`gh issue view 10939 --json body,comments`). The PR carries 'Fixes #10939' on its own line; the mayor closes this bead at merge and verifies the issue reads CLOSED.
notes:
== MIKE RULING 2026-10-05 22:5x AUSEST: DOCS ONLY ==
Asked in chat whether the fix should also keep prefix metadata in the substrate, by changing reply.cljc complete (L290, `(conj (vec event) reply)`) so it appends to an existing vector without dropping its metadata. Mike chose "Docs only": add the detection and review rule beside the O-17 callback mapping, with controls, exactly as the issue asks. implementation/core and spec/014 stay unchanged.
== WORKER RESULT (o17meta) 2026-10-05: PREMISE DOES NOT HOLD FOR :rf.http/managed. NO EDIT, NO PR ==
I checked at tip c9e120b2e7 and at the issue's cited revisions c6728dd1de and 7eb1642dc2. :rf.http/managed does NOT deliver its reply through re-frame.reply/complete. Its delivery path is http/encoding.cljc build-reply-event, which at L366 at all three revisions appends with (conj value reply-payload). value is the :reply-to / :on-success / :on-failure vector exactly as supplied, so this is the same conj http-fx 0.2.4 uses, and it keeps the prefix's metadata. The (conj (vec event) reply) at core reply.cljc L290 is real and does drop metadata. Its only src callers are resources (events.cljc L270, L555), mutations (mutation_events.cljc L1266) and routing (routing/reply.cljc L183). HTTP is not among them. The machine-shape wrapper refuses user reply addressing outright (:reason :machine-owns-reply), so it offers no user prefix path.

Decisive measurement: a JVM witness (scratch ns, not committed) drove the REAL path. It ran the live HttpClient transport against a local HttpServer, the :fx-overrides :rf.http/managed-canned-success path, and with-request-stubs. A reg-event handler and a registered interceptor recorded (meta event) on every delivery. Exit 0. Results as shipped:
 - metadata-free :on-success [:example/result]: value = the v1 shape, meta nil. Old and new agree.
 - ^{:example/context {:attempt 2}} on :on-success (200), on :on-failure (500), on unified :reply-to, on the canned fx, on with-request-stubs, and on :on-success with a reg-http-interceptor :before registered: value = (conj target reply). Handler AND interceptor both see {:example/context {:attempt 2}}.
 - control 0, a direct rf/dispatch-sync of a meta-bearing vector: the handler and interceptor see the meta, so the router keeps it.
Red control: with-redefs re-spelled build-reply-event as the issue's (conj (vec target) reply). No file was edited. Under that redef every meta-bearing case read meta nil while the values stayed = to the v1 shape. After the redef was released, the meta-bearing case read the meta again. The instrument therefore sees metadata loss when it happens, and as shipped none happens. The source blob hashes of encoding.cljc (8e8c1bf50d) and reply.cljc (6ea23116e4) were identical to HEAD before and after the run. Calling the internal re-frame.reply/complete directly does give (= v1 v2) true with (meta v2) nil, as the issue says, but that is not the HTTP path. CLJS was not executed (no shadow-cljs allowed). By source reading, the path is the same cljc conj, and the CLJS PersistentVector -conj keeps meta.

Why no docs edit: the caveat as briefed ("the managed reply delivers equal values but no prefix metadata") would be FALSE for O-17's subject. A "metadata is kept" caveat would instead pin an unspecified behaviour. Spec 014 and Managed-Effects are silent on prefix metadata, spec/002 L1122 says event-vector metadata is not an opt-channel in v2, and the shared substrate's complete drops it. Census: the unqualified like-for-like reply claim appears only in the O-17 companion (L47, L311). No other skills/re-frame-migration reference repeats it. The skill router's L13 "like-for-like" names a section, and README L125 is about clear-sub-cache!.

For Mike or the mayor: (a) close as not reproducible for :rf.http/managed; or (b) rescope. The real divergence is that HTTP keeps prefix metadata while the shared complete (resources and mutations :reply-to, routing) drops it, and no spec says which is the contract. That is a spec/substrate question, outside the docs-only ruling. The migration worker's failed positive control did not come from the :rf.http/managed reply append. Its source is unidentified.
close_reason:
Closed without a change; the premise does not hold for :rf.http/managed. GitHub #10939 is closed as not planned, with the evidence posted on the issue. Mike ruled "Close + make consistent" in chat (2026-10-05 23:2x AUSEST), which replaces the earlier "docs only" ruling: that ruling rested on the mayor's mistaken framing that HTTP replies go through re-frame.reply/complete.
Evidence: managed HTTP's reply is built by implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/encoding.cljc build-reply-event, which appends to the app's own target with (conj value reply-payload) (about L366). That is the same append as http-fx 0.2.4, so prefix metadata survives. The worker's bounded JVM run (scratch namespace outside the tree, exit 0) covered :on-success 200, :on-failure 500, :reply-to, both test-stub routes, and an HTTP :before interceptor; in every case the vector equalled the v1 shape and carried its metadata to both the handler and the interceptor. A with-redefs red control that stripped metadata made every case read nil, so the probe can see the loss. Blob hashes of encoding.cljc and reply.cljc matched HEAD before and after. The O-17 guide's like-for-like claim (L47, L311) is therefore correct, and no doc changed.
The real inconsistency, the shared core reply.cljc complete (L290, (conj (vec event) reply)) dropping metadata for resources, mutations :reply-to and routing, moves to rf2-vo1dx.

title: Shared reply append keeps prefix-vector metadata, as managed HTTP and v1 already do (resources, mutations, routing)
description:
Follows from GH #10939 (closed; its O-17 premise did not hold for managed HTTP). Mike ruled 2026-10-05 23:2x AUSEST in chat: "Close + make consistent".

Inconsistency, verified at trunk 279fd6d193:
- Managed HTTP's reply append (implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/encoding.cljc build-reply-event, about L366) is `(conj value reply-payload)` and keeps the app's prefix-vector metadata, as v1's http-fx did.
- The shared core append, implementation/core/src/re_frame/reply.cljc `complete` (about L271-290), is `:append (conj (vec event) reply)`. ClojureScript's and Clojure's vec drops vector metadata, so resources (events.cljc about L270 and L555), mutations :reply-to (mutation_events.cljc about L1266) and routing (routing/reply.cljc about L183) deliver equal vectors with nil meta.
No spec states either behaviour. spec/002-Frames.md (about L1122) says event-vector metadata is not a v2 OPTIONS channel, which is a different question from whether an append preserves it.

Ask: make the shared append keep an existing vector's metadata, for example `(conj (if (vector? event) event (vec event)) reply)` after checking what `normalize-target` hands it. Leave non-vector targets unchanged. Add one sentence in the owning spec (find where re-frame.reply's append contract lives, likely spec/Managed-Effects.md or the reply-addressing text; a hot-zone file needs the mayor first). Tests: in core's reply tests, a metadata-bearing target keeps its meta through `complete`, red at base; a metadata-free target is unchanged; and one family-level check (a resource or mutation :reply-to) sees the meta at its handler. Gates: core's JVM lane, and CI for the CLJS lanes; the shadow-cljs lane is likely unavailable. Mayor-filed.
notes:
== RESULT (worker, PR #10949, 2026-10-06 AUSEST)
Change: implementation/core/src/re_frame/reply.cljc complete, `:append (conj (vec event) reply)` -> `:append (conj event reply)`. This matches managed HTTP's build-reply-event `(conj value reply-payload)` (encoding.cljc L366, untouched).
Premise correction: the suggested `(if (vector? event) event (vec event))` has a dead else branch. normalize-target's event-vector? check guarantees :event is a non-empty keyword-headed vector, and every non-vector target (seq, keyword, number, string, eventless descriptor) throws :rf.reply/invalid-target before the append. There was no non-vector coercion to keep.
Callers verified at tip: resources events.cljc L270/L555 (durable-target keeps :event's identity), mutations mutation_events.cljc L1266, routing reply.cljc L183. All reach :append with the app's own target.
Spec sentence: spec/Managed-Effects.md §The reply target, L92 (not a hot-zone file): "The append is to the app's target vector as written, so any metadata on that vector travels with the delivered event in every family, managed HTTP included; the runtime carries that metadata and reads none of it, because event-vector metadata is not an options channel (002 §Routing: the dispatch envelope)." This is consistent with 002-Frames L1122.
Regression control (tests committed before the fix):
- re-frame.reply-cljs-test/completion-keeps-target-vector-metadata: at base, exit 1 with 3 failures, exactly the three meta assertions (short, descriptor and durable forms); with the fix, the ns runs 19 tests / 149 assertions at exit 0.

Lanes: core JVM went from 1704/10101 to 1705/10108 (predicted +1/+7); resources JVM from 750/7639 to 751/7642 (predicted +1/+3). Both exited 0.
Other gates: prod-gate exit 0 (1473 tests, floor 1437); clj-kondo 2026.04.15 0 errors, with 1 warning present at base too; check_doc_slugs exit 0, and a planted bad anchor went red; mkdocs --strict exit 0; all check_* ratchets exit 0. title: reagent-fresco-migration: teach the mixed-renderer tree once in mental-model.md and route the scattered renderer qualifiers and bridge-door copies through it
description:
## Problem

The skill's procedure is incremental: leaf-first, with bridges and holds. So a **mixed tree is the normal state of a migration in progress**: Fresco views over retained Reagent components, Reagent islands kept inside Fresco views, third-party Reagent libraries (re-com, grids, charts). Yet the skill's mental model only teaches convert-versus-hold. Every runtime rule was written as if the tree were all-Fresco, and field reports keep forcing a renderer qualifier onto one rule at a time.

## Evidence (2026-10-02..09)

- **Six field issues in two days came from exactly this gap:** #10926, #10934, #10942, #10965, #10977, #10978. Their fixes, plus resync d2f9b09edd, added about 250 skill lines:
  - a600e43b7e: census rows for re-com heads read as "no crossings".
  - 7cb6777a41: the provisional paragraph named one bridge door, contradicting Step 1 and MIG-22.
  - 82ce948db5: closure and `^{:key}` greps flagged a kept island's code.
  - 195167d4aa: every `r/as-element` was labelled runtime-blocker, which invited replacing a kept island.
  - 6b0a73168d: "hoist the read" froze a retained Reagent chart.
  - aa2b947bc9: "`r/flush` → `hm/settle!`" left a retained grid unrendered, because Reagent's own animation-frame queue was never drained.
- **10 of the 15 change units this week qualified an unconditional rule**, and 6 of those along the renderer axis. Examples: "keeps its view code", "add nothing else", "no surviving `#(dispatch`", "bridged with `h/as-component`", "hoist", "`r/flush` becomes `settle!`".
- **Verified at trunk 9e84689562:**
  - `references/mental-model.md` has **0** mentions of retained, mixed or two renderers.
  - A "kept `r/as-element` island" is assumed as an established shape at `references/procedure.md:202`, `:370` and `references/gotchas.md:128`, but no rule defines it.
  - "Island" means two different things: a React/UIx island with hooks (`procedure.md:89`) and a kept Reagent island (`procedure.md:202`).
  - The census route table at `procedure.md:82` sends `:as-element` to MIG-09/10, whose only advice is to replace it with `h/as-element`, which is exactly what #10965 warned against for a kept island.
  - `references/catalog-reject.md:128` still says "`h/as-component` bridges outward to a React/UIx/Reagent parent", naming only one of the two outward doors that 7cb6777a41 and d2f9b09edd established elsewhere.
- **The same facts are copied into summaries.** The bridge doors are restated about 8 times across 7 files: README L26, `spec/design.md` ~L142, `docs/skills/reagent-fresco-migration.md` ~L69, `SKILL.md` ~L152, `catalog-judgment.md` ~L333-341, `catalog-reject.md` ~L123-128, and `procedure.md` ~L125-149 and ~L464-486. b0ea1f75f3 corrected one premise in 5 files.

## Why it is structural

- The procedure makes mixed trees the default, but the model is binary.
- Each fix re-derives the same three questions at one site:
  - **Who lowers this hiccup?** Fresco or Reagent.
  - **Where does the frame come from?** React context, written by `h/frame-root` / `h/frame-provider` and read by both `h/sub` and `rf/reg-view`.
  - **Whose queue holds the pending work?** React's commit, or Reagent's rAF render queue.
- Without one place that answers them, the next mixed-tree site produces the next qualifier.

## Direction (minimal)

1. **Add one short section, "Two renderers in one tree", to `references/mental-model.md`.** It should cover:
   - Who lowers a hiccup vector: the nearest `h/defview` means Fresco; `r/as-element` or a Reagent component means Reagent.
   - Where the frame comes from.
   - Whose queue holds pending work, and what drains it: `hm/settle!` for an all-Fresco tree; `r/flush` inside `react-dom/flushSync` for a retained Reagent renderer.
   - The bridge directions, with the **kept Reagent island as a named, legal shape**.
   - For retained Reagent views, a link to re-frame-migration's M-11 (`guided-views-m11.md`), which owns frame-correctness there.
2. **Rename one of the two "island" meanings**, e.g. "React island" vs "kept Reagent island".
3. **Replace the renderer qualifiers with one-line pointers to the new section** at: Step 1, Step 3, Step 5 (including the mixed-renderer settle subsection), the provisional-file paragraph, MIG-22, MIG-26, MIG-35, gotchas, and `catalog-reject.md:128`.
4. **Keep exactly one copy of the bridge-door conditions and the value-transport list.** README, `spec/design.md`, the `docs/skills` mirror and the `SKILL.md` summary name the rule and link it, and copy no conditions.
5. **Make the census route for `:as-element`** (`procedure.md:82`) name both cases: replace via MIG-09/10, or keep as a Reagent island.

## Acceptance

- The section exists in `mental-model.md`, and each site listed in Direction 3 refers to it in no more than two sentences.
- The bridge-door conditions appear in exactly one file. The PR records a token search, across `skills/reagent-fresco-migration/`, `docs/skills/reagent-fresco-migration.md` and `docs/core/fresco/20-migration-from-reagent.md`, for distinctive phrases of the two door conditions.
- `catalog-reject.md:128` is fixed or has become a pointer.
- The `:as-element` route names both cases.
- `SKILL.md` + `references/` total no more than the current 2,340 lines (measured at 9e84689562), i.e. the change is net-neutral or smaller.
- `check_doc_slugs.py` and `mkdocs build --strict` exit 0, and the skill's packaging/structural checks pass.

## Notes

No hot-zone files. The sibling census bead touches the `procedure.md:74-91` census table. Coordinate on that block, or land this one first.

Teaching copies of the door conditions / shallow decode / value list across skills/reagent-fresco-migration/ + docs/skills mirror: BEFORE 8 passages in 7 files (procedure.md x2, catalog-judgment.md, catalog-reject.md single-door, SKILL.md, spec/design.md, docs/skills mirror, plus authoring-prompt.md single-door); AFTER 1 passage in 1 file (procedure.md Step 1). README L26 names the doors in its tool list with no conditions and is unchanged. "bridges outward to a" single-door copy: 1 -> 0. Not counted as teaching copies: evals.json (2 expectations) and the mig23 fixture comment, which assert the fact; census.clj's `:as-element` recovery note, which is program output pinned by census_test.

Deviation from Acceptance, needs a ruling: the Acceptance's search also spans docs/core/fresco/20-migration-from-reagent.md, and that human guide carries its own bridge walkthrough (sections "The half-migrated tree" and "Views shared across the boundary", with its own value list). It is the published human-audience page, the bead's own 8-copy count excludes it, and making the guide link into a skill reference (or the skill depend on the guide, which its spec/inputs.md treats as a "read for why" input) is a boundary decision, not a copy cut. So "exactly one file" holds across the skill and its mirror, and the guide is a second, separately owned copy. The two agree but differ in detail: the guide lists nil and functions as crossing [:>] unchanged; the skill lists plain functions and JavaScript objects, and notes r/partial arrives as a fresh wrapper.

title: A reg-* moved to another namespace silently freezes live frames: the old handler runs and later registrations are ignored
description:
## Bug

A live frame can hit a `reg-*` for an id that a different namespace already registered. When it does, the frame's refresh fails and the frame silently keeps its old sealed generation for every id. The old handler keeps running, new and re-edited handlers never take effect, and the two registry queries disagree. The only signal is a dev-only trace warning, and production gets nothing at all.

The ordinary trigger is the routine "move this handler to another namespace" refactor under hot reload. Re-evaluating the old namespace without the form does not remove its slot. After that, hot reload silently stops working for the frame until a full reload. In production the same thing happens when a late-loaded module duplicates an id.

## Evidence

**Where (trunk 475bdcaacf):**
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/live_frame.cljc:982-986`: `make-frame` seals a generation even when `:images` is absent (the default image).
- `live_frame.cljc:369-388` (`call-with-frame-resolution`): before binding the frame's generation, every dispatch and subscribe flushes a pending reprojection through `flush-projection-if-dirty!` (`:1620-1644`), which runs the resilient sweep.
- `live_frame.cljc:1462-1488` (`reproject-live-frames-resiliently!`): a per-frame assembly failure is caught and reported only as `:rf.warning/reprojection-failed` via `rf.trace/emit-error!`. The frame keeps its prior generation, "same as a frame whose composition re-resolved unchanged" (docstring).
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/trace.cljc:895-912`: `emit-error!` is gated on `debug-enabled?` and delivers only to the trace ring and trace listeners. Nothing prints, and production elides the call.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/registrar.cljc:1001-1008`: `handler-meta {:source :store …}` reads the last-writer-wins registrar atom. `{:frame f}` reads the frozen generation.

**Repro (*probed*):** JVM, `clojure -M` from `implementation/core`, plain-atom adapter, no listeners. Run at HEAD 9b20bf0093, whose `implementation/core` and `spec/` are byte-identical to 475bdcaacf.

```clojure
(ns probe.c) (rf/reg-event :probe/count (fn [{:keys [db]} _] {:db (assoc db :count-version 1)}))
(ns probe.a) (rf/reg-event :probe/ev {:doc "a"} (fn [{:keys [db]} _] {:db (assoc db :who :a)}))
(rf/make-frame {:id :probe/frame})                       ; default image
(rf/dispatch-sync [:probe/ev] {:frame :probe/frame})     ;=> {:who :a}

;; the refactor: probe.b now registers :probe/ev and adds a new handler
(ns probe.b)
(rf/reg-event :probe/ev {:doc "b"} (fn [{:keys [db]} _] {:db (assoc db :who :b)}))
(rf/reg-event :probe/other (fn [{:keys [db]} _] {:db (assoc db :other true)}))

(rf/dispatch-sync [:probe/ev]    {:frame :probe/frame})  ; app-db still {:who :a}
(rf/dispatch-sync [:probe/other] {:frame :probe/frame})  ; no effect: unknown to the frozen frame
(:doc (rf/handler-meta {:source :store :kind :event :id :probe/ev}))    ;=> "b"
(:doc (rf/handler-meta {:frame :probe/frame :kind :event :id :probe/ev})) ;=> "a"
(rf/make-frame {:id :probe/frame2})                      ; throws :rf.error/image-duplicate-id
```

Unrelated edits also stop landing (*probed*, separate run). Before the move, re-registering `probe.c`'s `:probe/count` with version 2 takes effect: `{:count-version 2}`. After the move, re-registering it with version 3 leaves app-db at `{:count-version 2}`.

Nothing is printed at any step.

**Contract:**
- `spec/001-Registration.md:323` (rule 2): a cross-namespace duplicate does not clobber, and "two features accidentally sharing an id … fail loudly rather than being masked".
- `spec/002-Frames.md:1079`: the default projection "fails loud on a cross-namespace same-`[kind id]` collision".
- The `:rf.warning/reprojection-failed` row at `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2122` makes the diagnostic dev-only by design. That contradicts both rules above.

## Expected

A cross-namespace duplicate that reaches a live frame fails loudly in every build. The failure names the frame, the id and both namespaces, and the frame never presents a stale program as current without saying so.

## Fix direction

- When a live frame's reprojection fails, report it on the always-on error axis: an `:rf.error/*` record through error-emit, so listeners, frame sinks and the dev console fallback all see it.
  - The record names the frame, the `[kind id]` and both provenance namespaces.
  - It also names the recovery: `(rf/clear kind id)`, then re-evaluate the namespace that should own the id. Re-evaluating the old namespace does not remove its slot.
- Keep the sweep's per-frame isolation. Distinguish "refresh failed" from "unchanged" in its return value.
- The flush runs only after a registration has marked the projection dirty, so one report per failed refresh is enough. Plain dispatches do not repeat it.
- Change the `:rf.warning/reprojection-failed` catalogue row to match.
- This makes the freeze loud, but it does not remove it: the frame stays on its old generation until the duplicate is cleared. Removing the freeze would mean resolving the default path live and failing only the ambiguous id at use (Opus A1, Sol 02's architectural experiment). That is an architecture decision and Mike's call, and it is outside this bead.

## Acceptance

- New JVM test using the repro above. After the move, one always-on error record names `:probe/frame`, `[:event :probe/ev]`, `"probe.a"` and `"probe.b"`. The test fails at trunk, where no record is produced.
- Later dispatches to the frozen frame do not repeat the record. A refresh that changes nothing emits nothing.
- The record is still produced under the core production gate (`-Dre-frame.debug=false`).
- The existing resilient-sweep tests stay green: one failing frame does not stop sibling frames refreshing.

## Notes

- Origin: Opus review (core-frames-registration Insight 1, probed). Sol 02 §1 supports the same failure path from source.
- Related: rf2-mn2ht.17 (error coordinates point at the new file while the old handler runs, after the same move). rf2-gzepz (closed) is a different duplicate-id defect, in HTTP carriers. The `{:source :store}` versus frame query disagreement is Opus A2, an architecture proposal, and is not fixed here.
- Hot zones: `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` (catalogue row). `live_frame.cljc` is not a hot-zone file.

title: Resources: the invalid-params projection may read walker marks with no completeness check (same class as rf2-mn2ht.48; unprobed)
description:
Flagged in rf2-mn2ht.48's own description as UNPROBED, and left out of that fix (PR #11056, merged at d5e10f5d4b) because it is outside its fence. A CLAIM to probe at tip before acting.

SUSPECTED DEFECT: resources' invalid-params projection (implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/classification.cljc, around lines 594-649 at trunk 475bdcaacf) reads the schemas extract hooks the way HTTP did before .48: exact path match, with no completeness check. A params schema with an opaque child ([:ref ...], a local :registry, a compiled child) would then project its marked slots unredacted.

DIRECTION: if the probe reproduces, consult the schema-has-opaque-child? hook that .48 published (the same late-bind hook, already in core's directory) and fail closed, as HTTP now does. If it does not reproduce, close with the probe as the reason.

ACCEPTANCE: a probe with an opaque-child params schema and a :sensitive? mark; if it leaks, a test red at base, green with the fix, red again with the fix reverted.
notes:
== PROBED, REPRODUCED AND FIXED ON BRANCH worker/resources-review, PR #11064 (worker, 2026-10-10 AUSEST) ==
Fix commit 276fea7b3b. Base 72c951f102.

PROBE at base, JVM, schemas artefact loaded, calling registry/validate+canonicalize-params and mutation-registry/validate+canonicalize-params directly. Params {:creds {:token "SECRET-TOKEN-42"} :age "not-an-int"}; the failure is on :age:
- control, inline [:map [:creds [:map [:token {:sensitive? true} :string]]] [:age :int]]: schema-has-opaque-child? false, walker marks ([:creds :token]), thrown :params {:creds {:token :rf/redacted} ...}, no secret.
- local :registry ([:schema {:registry {:app/creds ...}} [:map [:creds :app/creds] ...]]): opaque-child? true, walker marks NONE, thrown :params carried "SECRET-TOKEN-42" raw, for both the resource and the mutation arm.
- [:ref :app/creds] inside a local registry: the same leak.
- embedded compiled child (m/schema ...): the same leak.
The explainer :error slot was already safe: schemas' redact-validation-tags scrubs it whole when the schema has an opaque child. Only :params leaked.
COORDINATES, the second half of the same class: the projection called redact-with-paths in exact mode, so [:items [:vector [:map [:token {:sensitive? true} ...]]]] left every element's :token raw in :params.

FIX, resources/classification.cljc redact-invalid-params-error:
- walker-sees-every-mark? consults the published :schemas/schema-has-opaque-child? hook, exactly as http privacy_body does. When the schema has an opaque descendant, or the hook is unbound, the whole :params slot becomes :rf/redacted. That is the fail-closed answer Spec 010 already gives validation failures for opaque schemas, and the one the shared seam gives :error.
- Per-slot redaction passes {:index-free? true}, so a marked slot redacts in every collection element.
No spec edit was needed: Spec 010's "Compiled / opaque schemas fail closed" paragraph already governs this payload, because Spec 015 names the thrown invalid-params payload as the validator's own failure product.

Tests, in resources_invalid_params_redaction_cljs_test.cljc: invalid-params-behind-an-opaque-child-fail-closed covers the local-registry and [:ref] shapes, each through the resource and the mutation arm. invalid-params-redact-a-marked-slot-in-every-element covers the vector of maps.
Red/green/red-again, clojure -M:test -n re-frame.resources-invalid-params-redaction-cljs-test:
- red at base: exit 1, 6 tests / 9 assertions, 5 failures.
- green: exit 0, 6 / 9.
- red again with classification.cljc reverted to base: exit 1, 5 failures. Restore verified by blob hash.
Full resources JVM lane: exit 0, 624 tests / 1674 assertions. Predicted +2 tests / +5 assertions over 622 / 1669, and that is what moved.

For the mayor (not in this worker's fence): core late_bind/directory.cljc's row for :schemas/schema-has-opaque-child? describes it as consumed by re-frame.http.privacy-body only, and resources now consumes it too. Spec 009's error-table rows for :rf.error/resource-invalid-params and :rf.error/mutation-invalid-params describe only per-slot redaction; they do not mention the opaque fail-closed case or the every-element match.
close_reason: Merged as PR #11064 at 56835a6f99 (commit a7b0574e68). The probe reproduced: with a local :registry, a [:ref ...] or an embedded compiled child in the params schema, the thrown invalid-params :params carried the secret raw for both resources and mutations (the :error slot was already safe), and an exact path match leaked a marked slot inside a vector of maps in every element. The projection now consults the schema-has-opaque-child? hook as HTTP does: when the walker cannot see every mark the whole :params slot is redacted, otherwise marked slots redact in every element. No spec edit (Spec 010 already requires opaque schemas to fail closed). Red at base exit 1 (5 failures), green exit 0, red again exit 1. Resources lane 622/1669 -> 624/1674.

title: Remove :rf.machine/update-snapshot (ruled): delete the fx, its validator, :phase :update-snapshot and spec/doc rows; rewrite core test callers
description:
## Bug

`[:rf.machine/update-snapshot {:rf/machine-id id :rf/patch {:state :idle}}]` rewrites a machine's `:state` with a plain merge. No `:exit` or `:entry` runs, the old state's spawned child stays alive and mirrored, the old state's tags stay on the snapshot, and its `:after` epoch is not advanced. The result is a snapshot no transition could produce: `:idle` carrying `:loading`'s tags and child. Views that read `[:rf.machine/has-tag? id :p/busy]` keep showing the old state.

## Evidence

- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/update_snapshot.cljc:40` (trunk 475bdcaacf): `permitted-patch-keys #{:state :meta :data}`; `:42-69` `apply-patch` is `(merge snapshot clean-patch)` plus a `:data` merge; `:159-202` write it straight into runtime-db. `:tags` is not a permitted key, so it can never be corrected by the patch, and nothing recomputes it.
- Repro, *probed* (JVM, `clojure -M` from `implementation/machines`): two identical machines, one left by an ordinary transition, one by the patch.
  ```clojure
  (defn spec [child-type]
    {:initial :idle
     :states  {:idle    {:tags #{:p/idle} :on {:fetch :loading}}
               :loading {:tags  #{:p/busy}
                         :spawn {:machine-id child-type}
                         :after {60000 :timed-out}
                         :exit  (fn [{data :data}] {:data (assoc data :exited? true)})
                         :on    {:done :idle}}
               :timed-out {}}})
  ;; both dispatched [id [:fetch]], then:
  (rf/dispatch-sync [:p/via-transition [:done]])
  (rf/dispatch-sync [:p/patch :p/via-patch {:state :idle}])   ; plain reg-event emitting the fx
  ```
  Observed:
  ```
  :p/via-transition {:state :idle, :tags #{:p/idle}, :exit-ran? true,  :spawned-mirror nil,
                     :after-epoch {[:loading] 2}, :child-alive? false}
  :p/via-patch      {:state :idle, :tags #{:p/busy}, :exit-ran? false, :spawned-mirror {[:loading] :p/child-p#1},
                     :after-epoch {[:loading] 1}, :child-alive? true}
  ```
  The `:loading` host timer is also left scheduled (its epoch still matches); delivered while the snapshot reads `:idle` it is ignored, so that part is inert unless the snapshot later returns to `:loading`.
- Contract: `spec/005-StateMachines.md:863` — "only the transition's `:target` decides the next state. Actions cannot bypass the FSM." `:890` then documents this fx as an escape hatch that may touch `:state`, without saying that it skips lifecycle, children, timers and tags.
- Zero callers outside the machines artefact's own tests (`examples/`, `testbeds/`, `tools/`).

## Expected

Entering a state through any sanctioned door runs that state's lifecycle and leaves tags, children and timers consistent with the new state; or the door cannot set `:state` at all.

## Fix direction

Mike's call between two designs, both small:

- **Narrow** (Sol's review): drop `:state` from `permitted-patch-keys`, refuse a `:state` key with a clear error, and keep the fx for `:data`/`:meta`. Spec 005:890 loses the `:state` wording.
- **Remove** (Opus's review): delete `:rf.machine/update-snapshot` entirely. A targetless transition already writes `:data`, no documented use case writes `:meta`, and nothing outside the artefact uses it.

Do not add occupancy validation or a re-entry emulation to the patch; that keeps the trap.

## Acceptance

- Narrow: a test that patches `{:state :idle}` onto a machine in `:loading` gets the refusal and the snapshot is unchanged (fails today: state becomes `:idle` with tags `#{:p/busy}`); the existing `:data`-merge tests (`update_snapshot_data_merge_cljs_test.cljc`) still pass.
- Remove: no `:rf.machine/update-snapshot` registration, spec row or test remains; the spec examples at 005:2975-2981 and :3152 that suggest it for recording a spawned id point at a targetless transition instead.

## Notes

- Origin: Opus review (machines #3) and Sol review (machines §6), independently; probed during bead drafting.
- Prior judgement: the correctness review rf2-3x7nj.9 (closed 2026-09-23, item 8) recorded "an update-snapshot `:state` patch bypasses timers, spawns and finality" as the documented escape-hatch trade-off. This bead asks Mike to revisit that with the tag evidence above and the zero-caller census.
- Related: rf2-0hi3x (closed; made the `:data` leg merge).
- Hot zones: `spec/005-StateMachines.md` either way. Removal also touches `spec/009-Instrumentation.md`, `spec/Spec-Schemas.md` and `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn` + the generated `spec/api-manifest.edn` (the `validate-update-snapshot-data!` row), plus non-hot `spec/010-Schemas.md`, `spec/013-Flows.md`, core's late-bind directory entry `:machines/update-snapshot-fx` and a comment in `core/src/re_frame/fx.cljc:796-807`.
- Supporting detail: `ai/findings/advisarial-review/opus/machines.md` §3, Action 2, Conflict 1; `ai/findings/advisarial-review/sol/11-machines.md` §6.
notes:
== RULING (delegated by Mike; decided 2026-10-10 23:50:45 AUSEST at HEAD 200a67df2d) ==

DECISION: Option B, REMOVE `:rf.machine/update-snapshot` entirely. Delete the reserved fx, its handler namespace, its published validator `re-frame.machines/validate-update-snapshot-data!`, the `:phase :update-snapshot` value of the `:where :machine-data` vocabulary, its late-bind directory entry, and every spec, doc, skill and test row that names it. After this, a machine snapshot changes only through a transition (the macrostep), spawn, destroy, or frame-state installation. This is an explicit pre-alpha RETIREMENT of an existing surface, made by Mike's delegate. It is not a reading of the demand bar (see WHERE THE REVIEWS DISAGREED). The `:meta`-leg defect (a `:meta` patch drops the reserved `:rf/snapshot-version` and the machine resets to `:initial`) is discharged INSIDE this bead's scope by the deletion. No separate bead is needed.

WHY (under the stance):
- Elegance, and a minimal API. Spec 005:863 says "only the transition's `:target` decides the next state. Actions cannot bypass the FSM." 005:885 says callbacks "cannot nudge the machine into a state the spec didn't declare." The fx is the one door that contradicts both. Deleting it makes the invariant true with no footnote.
- Every need the hatch claims is already met better:
  - "State plus data in one atomic write" is a transition with a `:target` and an `:action`: one macrostep, one commit, lifecycle intact.
  - "Data plus something else atomically" is an action returning `{:data … :fx …}` (005:885).
  - "Write a machine's `:data` from outside it" is a dispatch to a named targetless transition. Its state is preserved (`transition.cljc:3716-3729`, `internal?` keeps `(:state snapshot)`) and it spawns nothing (`run-spawn-phase`, `:3740-3742`).
  - Restore uses frame-state installation.
- What the hatch adds beyond those is exactly what is broken. A `:state` patch produces snapshots no transition can produce: the old state's tags, a live child that is orphaned one re-entry later, no `:exit` or `:entry`. A `:meta` patch silently resets the machine. Its `:data` leg needed rf2-0hi3x to stop it wiping reserved slots, and it needed the flows-settle fix (rf2-3x7nj.9.7).
- The fx has no consumer. There are zero callers in `examples/`, `testbeds/`, `tools/`, SSR hydration or pair tooling. The machines guide rejected it (rf2-yeg4c: "Rejected: :rf.machine/update-snapshot in the guide"). Its only callers are tests.
- "Trust the programmer" means not nagging them. It does not mean keeping a sanctioned door that silently produces states the programmer cannot see are wrong (`:tags` is filtered out of the patch, so even an informed caller cannot correct it). Deletion adds no diagnostic.
- An extra point (mine, read at HEAD): the fx takes any `:rf/machine-id`. So a callback in machine A can patch machine B's snapshot directly, which is the "quiet reach into someone else's data" that 005:859 forbids ("every cross-encapsulation write [must] be a *named, traced, reusable event*").

REJECTED:
- A, Narrow to `:data` only. Correct but needless. It keeps a reserved fx, a published validator, a `:phase` value and incarnation-fence machinery for a capability with no consumer, which a targetless event already provides. It is the right shape if the surface is ever un-parked (see PRESERVED ANALYSIS). The bead's own draft of A (keep `:data` and `:meta`) is rejected outright: the `:meta` leg resets the machine (Probe 2).
- C, Make a `:state` patch run a real transition. It builds a hidden "go to any state" door that the transition table, Xray and diagrams cannot see, and it reproduces what a declared root `:on {:reset :idle}` already gives (Probe 1's `:p/via-root-on` row). It also opens fresh design questions: `:data` merge order against exit and entry, the callbacks' `:event`, parallel `:state` maps, history. The bead itself says "Do not add occupancy validation or a re-entry emulation to the patch; that keeps the trap."
- D, Keep it and document it. The trap stays with a label on it. It still contradicts 005:863, and the `:meta` reset still needs a fix.

WHERE THE REVIEWS AGREED / DISAGREED:
- The dossier author recommended B, with A (`:data` only) as the fallback. Codex recommended B, keeping `:data`-only only "if Mike can name a present consumer that needs a direct write during the current effect walk". Both reject C and D, and both reject the bead's draft of A that keeps `:meta`. Neither reviewer's facts conflict with the other's. Each independently probed the lifecycle bypass (wrong tags, no exit, an orphaned child) and the `:meta` version reset, and each got the same results.
- The earlier "deliberate" judgements were REVIEWER OPINIONS, not Mike rulings:
  - rf2-pk4i6.3, "Considered, left alone", outside its five numbered findings: "An escape-hatch `:state` patch bypasses exit/entry, timer cancel/arm and history: that is what an escape hatch is — trust the programmer."
  - rf2-3x7nj.9, item 8: "An `:rf.machine/update-snapshot` `:state` patch bypasses timers, spawns and finality. This is the documented escape-hatch trade-off."
  - Neither reviewer saw the stale-tag evidence, the orphaned child, the `:meta` reset or the zero-consumer census. This ruling supersedes both opinions; it does not overrule a Mike ruling.
- Disagreement 1, what licenses deletion. The dossier cited the demand bar (Principles:128, "a public surface ships only for a *named consumer*"). Codex objected that Principles:132 limits the demand bar to NEW surfaces ("Where fixed-and-additive governs how an *existing* surface evolves, the demand bar governs *whether a new surface may exist at all*"), so preservation is the default for an existing one. SETTLED FOR CODEX on the reading of the text. The deletion therefore rests on this explicit pre-alpha retirement: a concrete contract inconsistency, an adequate existing mechanism, and no observed consumer. The precedent is rf2-kuky.15, a delegated ruling (2026-09-06) that deleted the machine `:system-id` and `:on-spawn` families: "RULED: A - delete the :system-id family, the :on-spawn family and the phantom :child-machine". The demand bar does govern any later RE-introduction, which is why un-park triggers are recorded below.
- Disagreement 2, whether a dispatch replaces the patch. The dossier says a dispatched targetless event "lands in the same drain, before any paint" (002:1880). Codex says that is not an exact ordering substitute: the event runs after the current fx walk, so effects later in the SAME walk see the pre-write snapshot, and the event takes part in the normal macrostep and `:always` processing (docs/api/re-frame.machines.md: `[:dispatch [machine-id event]]` "handles the event later, as a separate event, after this one's snapshot has committed"). SETTLED: both statements are true. The ordering difference is the real cost of removal. It is accepted because no caller exists that depends on it, and it is the named un-park trigger.

EVIDENCE (HEAD 200a67df2d; every source file below is unchanged since the dossier's 2fdf565945 except spec/005 (the rf2-mn2ht.26 Level-2 edit, unrelated) and spec/009 (unrelated rows); line numbers re-read at HEAD):
- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/update_snapshot.cljc`:
  - `:40` `(def ^:private permitted-patch-keys #{:state :meta :data})`.

  - Control: a root-level targetless `:remember` transition updated `:data` while keeping the state and the same live child.
- Census at HEAD (Grep `update-snapshot` over the repo, excluding `.beads/`): 107 occurrences across 28 files.
  - No hits in `examples/`, `testbeds/`, `tools/` code (only `tools/story/spec/findings/**` prose), `spec/conformance/`, `spec/Conventions.md` or `spec/API.md`. It is not in the reserved fx-ids table.
