   relies on.
4. Decide each test: keep, simplify, merge or delete.
5. Run the suite again and prove the pruned suite still guards every promise.

Work in small batches by contract group, and commit as you go. Before each batch,
predict the change in test and assertion counts; after it, confirm the counts moved by
exactly that much. If helper agents are available, use read-only ones for the mapping
step. If docs/design/fresco/product/pilots/baseline plainly will not finish in about four hours, stop at a group boundary,
ship what is done, and list the files you did not reach.

Decide each test with two questions:
- If this test were deleted, what bug could ship that no remaining test would catch?
  If you cannot name one, delete it.
- If you can name one: is that bug plausible in this code, would a caller notice it,
  and would nothing else surface it at once (a compile or load error, a boot-time
  validation, most of the suite going red)? If the bug is implausible, harmless, or
  loud anyway, delete the test.

Delete:
- A test another test implies. If A cannot pass while B fails, drop B.
- Extra examples of one behaviour that take the same path through the code.
- Existence and smoke checks: a function exists, a var resolves, something "is
  registered", a result is non-nil, a call "does not throw", when another test
  exercises the same call with a real assertion.
- Change detectors: a test that copies a constant, a data table, a default config, a
  roster or a string out of the source and asserts equality. It fails on every intended
  change and catches no bug. The exception is a value callers depend on exactly, such as
  a public id or a documented default, that nothing else pins: keep one test for it.
- Absence checks for things nothing produces, and negative-input tests for inputs no
  caller passes and the contract does not mention.
- Exhaustive enumeration: one row per enum member, keyword or field when they all take
  one path. Keep one representative plus the members that take a different path.
- Tests of the language, a library or the framework: a constructor sets a field, a
  getter returns it, a map holds the key just put in it.
- Tests that pin how the code works instead of what it does: private helpers already
  exercised through the public path, call order, internal data shapes, greps of the
  implementation's own source, and log, trace or error wording that is not part of the
  contract.
- Tests whose expected value is computed by the same logic as the code under test.
- Assertions that a mock returned what it was told to return, and tests whose mock setup
  is most of the test while the assertion checks the mock.
- Separate per-platform test files asserting the same thing about platform-neutral code.
  A single shared test that runs on both platforms is one test, not two: keep it.
- Tests of test helpers and fixtures.
- Tests of code that has no logic in it, and tests whose only subject is production code
  that no production caller uses.

Simplify every test you keep:
- Assert the whole result with one equality instead of one assertion per field. Drop an
  assertion that a later one in the same test implies.
- Cut setup, fixtures and data to what the assertion needs. Remove unused bindings,
  requires, helpers and fixtures.
- Tests that vary one input become one table-driven test. Keep the boundary rows and
  drop the mid-range ones.
- Tests that repeat the same setup for one assertion each become one test.
- Delete comments and docstrings that restate the code or narrate history. Keep a
  one-line why where a test's purpose is not obvious from its name and body.
- Rename a test only when its name no longer says what it asserts, and first check that
  nothing matches on the name, such as a CI filter, a skip list or a doc that cites it.

Keep, however small:
- The only test of a promise a caller relies on: a normal result, a boundary that takes
  a different path (empty, one, many; zero; the limit and one past it), a promised
  failure.
- A regression test for a bug that actually happened, unless a stronger test now covers
  it.
- The last guard of a security, privacy or redaction promise.
- The last test that keeps a gate able to fail, and the last test holding a published
  doc or spec claim to the code.
When a weak test and a strong test overlap, keep the strong one: the one that would fail
on more bugs.

Do not:
- Weaken an assertion, or swap an exact check for a looser one, to make a merge or a
  simplification easier.
- Delete a test because it fails, is slow or is flaky. Report it.
- Leave unused helpers, fixtures or requires behind.
- Add new tests. If you find a promise with no test, report it.
- Change production code. Dead code and stale docs or spec text go in your report as a
  list, not into your change.
If anything pins test counts or names, such as a count floor or a roster, update it in
the same change. Commit one file or module at a time.

Prove it:
- The suite passes before and after. Report both sets of counts.
- For each group of deletions that rests on a surviving cover, break the code in a place
  the deleted tests guarded and confirm a surviving test fails. Then restore the code and
  confirm it matches the committed file. One plant per group sharing a cover is enough.
  If nothing fails, you removed real coverage: put the tests back.
- A cover must actually run. A skipped test, a fixture the runner never loads, or a test
  on a lane nothing executes covers nothing. Confirm the runner executes a cover before
  resting a deletion on it.
- Run each test file you touched on its own at least once. Deleting a file can break a
  sibling that relied on it loading something first; give such a file its own require.
- A deletion made under the second question needs no plant. Give its one-line reason in
  the report instead.
- A simplification must not change what a test can catch. Where you removed an
  assertion, name the assertion that implies it.

Report:
- Before and after: tests, assertions, lines.
- Deleted tests, grouped by reason. For each, the surviving cover, or the one-line
  reason it was not worth keeping.
- Merges and simplifications: what went into what, and the lines each file lost.
- Notable keeps: tests you considered deleting but kept, and why.
- Plants, and which test caught each.
- Tests outside docs/design/fresco/product/pilots/baseline that your deletions rely on.
- Dead code, stale docs or spec text, and gaps (promises with no test). One line each.

If you are unsure whether a promise a caller relies on is still covered, keep the test
and say so. Losing the only guard of a real promise is still the one mistake that matters
more than leaving an extra test in. But being unsure whether a test is worth keeping is
not a reason to keep it. If you cannot say in one line what plausible regression it
catches that a caller would notice, delete it.

title: Publish the closed conformance fixture grammar as spec/conformance/fixture-file.edn and validate every fixture against it on the JVM
description:
## Ruling

The conformance corpus gets ONE closed fixture grammar, written as plain EDN data in `spec/` (a new `spec/conformance/fixture-file.edn`), and the reference validates EVERY fixture against it on the JVM at every commit, independent of capability filtering. It replaces the "open by convention" posture and the stale, contradicted `Spec-Schemas.md` entries. This is Option C of four (A leave as is, B grade-once with no schema, C = B plus the grammar as data, D = C plus full harness consolidation and port-facing work). Goal 2 ("AI-implementable from the spec alone") is ruled LIVE BUT MEASURED: a port may not consult `implementation/`, and the claim is measured by an occasional bounded probe rather than asserted. This bead is the grammar itself; the roster deletion and prose shrink, and the probe, are the two follow-on beads that depend on it.

Decided 2026-10-16: Mike directed that every dossier recommendation an independent Codex review agreed with be actioned:

> review all decisions. They now have a "Codex Recomendation" section.  Where the original
> recomendation matches the Code Recomendation, create a bead to action the decision.  And then
> remove the file.  Leave behind cases where the two differ materially.

Decisive facts, at trunk 89517e8f54:

1. **The published schema contradicts the corpus, and SA-3 makes it a MUST.** `spec/SPEC-AUTHORING.md:27` (SA-3) requires a schema for the "fixture file". Yet `spec/Spec-Schemas.md:2432` admits only the vector-of-pairs `[:fx [[fx-id args] ...]]` and `:2438` only a message-less `[:throw]`, while the interpreter supports single-effect `[:fx id args]` and `[:throw "msg"]` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/conformance.cljc:359-372`), and an approximate check counts 31 and 10 fixtures using those forms. `spec/Spec-Schemas.md:4630` says "The six operators cover..." against the 29 `:call` ops the corpus uses (and cites a `run-call` that has moved). Each document claims to be canonical for the other's material (`spec/conformance/README.md:369` "The complete DSL operator set"; `spec/Spec-Schemas.md:2467` "this entry is canonical").
2. **The real grammar lives in three hand-kept rosters in test code.** `implementation/core/test/re_frame/conformance_runner.cljc:226-239` (`corpus-checked-expect-keys`, 11 keys), `:241-267` (`sibling-owned-expect-keys`, 15 keys) and `:279-292` (`implemented-fixture-keys`). The spec documents 7 of the 26 `:fixture/expect` keys and 6 of the 29 call ops; the prose calls the format "open by convention" (`spec/Spec-Schemas.md:4713`, `spec/conformance/README.md:67`) and "the corpus is the authority" (`spec/Spec-Schemas.md:4715`). The roster has been hand-repaired three times in six weeks (rf2-9vbg3, rf2-7yth0, rf2-mn2ht.61), each time at the top level only.
3. **Delegation by key name has let expectations go ungraded.** `conformance_runner.cljc:241-250` marks keys "delegated, NOT ignored" to sibling runners that select fixtures by FILENAME (`implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr_conformance_test.clj:242-252` loads only `ssr-*.edn`), and to "frame-lifecycle / destroy runners" (`:247`) that do not exist. Nothing checks below the first level of a fixture or of `:fixture/expect`.

Rejected options:
- **A, leave it:** the SA-3 schema stays wrong, the rosters keep drifting, and a port can learn key meanings only by reading the CLJS runner.
- **B, grade once with no schema:** fixes the reference but leaves the meaning in code, and a hand-corrected Spec-Schemas entry drifts again as it has every previous time.
- **D, C plus consolidation:** a test-only `implementation/conformance/` artefact, merged tiers, a shrunk capability vocabulary, Security.md hostile cases and the HTTP transport seam (rf2-mn2ht.71). Large, across five or more hot zones, and worth it only for a real port. DEFERRED behind named triggers: the artefact when the next duplicated-harness bug appears or a fourth family runner is proposed; the capability vocabulary and security lifts once the probe passes stage 1 and Mike wants a real port; rf2-mn2ht.71 under its own trigger.

Supersedes: the "open by convention" / "the corpus is the authority" posture (`spec/conformance/README.md:64-67`, `spec/Spec-Schemas.md:4713-4715`), the implementor skill's "Derive, never transcribe" (`skills/re-frame2-implementor/references/conformance.md:12`, changed in the follow-on bead), and the hand-kept roster mechanism rf2-mn2ht.61 installed (closed; its fail-loud intent is kept and now enforced by the grammar). No EP is superseded.

NOT decided here, and left exactly as it is: whether `:fixture/spec-version` is deleted from all 241 fixtures and its five runner copies. The two reviews differ on it and Mike has not ruled. The grammar declares it as an optional key; do not delete it from fixtures, runners or README §Versioning.

## Work

**Spec: add `spec/conformance/fixture-file.edn`** — a Malli registry written as plain EDN, readable with `clojure.edn/read` and by any port's EDN reader. It declares:
- the top-level envelope as a closed map: the 18 top-level keys the corpus uses (`:fixture/spec-version` among them, optional);
- `:fixture/expect` as a closed map of the 26 expectation keys;
- `:fixture/calls` as a `:multi` on `:call`, one closed record per op (29 arms), INCLUDING each record's nested expectation keys (`:expect-next-snapshot`, `:expect-effects`, `:expect-error`, `:expect-graph`, ...);
- the handler-body DSL: the 16 step ops (with `:set-runtime`, `:hiccup`, `:merge-into-db`, `:return-head`, `:reduce-input`, `:dispatch-sync`, `:make-frame-capture`, and the single-effect `:fx`, `[:throw msg]` and partial-application `[:fn :k arg ...]` forms the corpus really uses) and the value forms `:cofx-key`, `:db-get`, `:cofx-without`;
- the dispatch-entry shapes: event vectors plus the five map shapes (today's schema refuses every map shape);
- the capability vocabulary as an enum;
- the comparison laws, each defined once.

Counts are at trunk 89517e8f54; the grammar declares whatever the corpus uses when it lands, after the five-channel bug (see Sequencing) has graded or deleted its keys.

**Three design rules for the grammar:**
1. **Close what the fixture format owns; keep embedded runtime INPUTS raw.** The envelope, the expectation key sets, the call records and the DSL instructions are closed. Embedded runtime inputs such as frame configs, registry metadata and event payloads are NOT validated against the runtime's valid-value schemas, because negative fixtures feed invalid data on purpose: `spec/conformance/fixtures/construction-shape-validation.edn:48` (`:initial-events [42]`) and `:55` (`[[]]`) exist to assert runtime rejection.
2. **Keep partial expected runtime values open.** An expected app-db, response or snapshot is a partial value compared by law, not a closed map.
3. **Each expectation key states what it OBSERVES and the LAW it is compared by** (for example `{:observe "the frame's app-db after the drain" :law :submap}`). The laws are the ones the graders really use, not a fixed three. They include `:submap`, which carries the existing nil-or-absent rule: an expected `nil` matches nil OR absent, relied on by 37 fixtures and pinned by `implementation/core/test/re_frame/conformance_submap_test.clj:34`. They also include ordered-subset, equality, absent-path (`conformance_runner.cljc:1747`) and substring containment (`ssr_conformance_test.clj:885`). The annotations are DOCUMENTATION for ports. The reference keeps explicit per-key matchers, and nobody builds a generic law evaluator.

**Code: one JVM deftest** in core's test tree validates every `spec/conformance/fixtures/*.edn` against the grammar, claimed or not, so the capability gate cannot hide a fixture. It reports the offending key's PATH (for example `[:fixture/calls 0 :expect-trace]`). Malli 0.20.1 is already on core's JVM test classpath through the schemas test dep (`implementation/core/deps.edn:102`; the comment at `:73-76` explains it), so no deps change is needed. The precedent for tests reading schemas from `spec/` is `implementation/machines/test/re_frame/spawn_all_schema_extract.clj`. The CLJS lane needs no Malli. Other hosts may implement an equivalent check without Malli.

Where validation finds drift (a key no fixture should carry), either declare it with an observation and a law and grade it, or delete it from the fixture. Do not widen the grammar to admit a vacuous claim.

**Spec prose:**
- Reduce `spec/Spec-Schemas.md` §`:rf/handler-body-dsl` (`:2408`) and §`:rf/fixture-file` (`:4509`, through the "open by convention" and "snapshot" paragraphs at `:4713-4715`) to short pointers at the grammar file. Keep the section headings and anchors so inbound links resolve.
- Give SA-3 (`spec/SPEC-AUTHORING.md:27`) the clause "or in a schema file this catalogue names".
- In `spec/conformance/README.md`, "open by convention" (`:67`, and the "This table is the roster..." paragraph at `:64`) becomes "a new key lands in the grammar first".

**What deliberately stays:** the three runner rosters (the follow-on bead deletes them); the Python well-formedness scanner `scripts/check_conformance_fixture_edn.py` (a no-JVM check, orthogonal to the grammar); `:fixture/spec-version` everywhere; SSR's production-posture evidence; capability tag names; all harness file locations.

## Sequencing

- **Hot zones:** `spec/Spec-Schemas.md` (shrinks once). No `spec/API.md` or manifest change, and no change to `implementation/deps.edn`, `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn` or `.github/workflows/*`. `spec/conformance/README.md` and `spec/SPEC-AUTHORING.md` are not hot zones.
- **Depends on:** the coordinator's separately filed bug for the five expectation channels no runner grades (`frame-lifecycle.edn` `:on-destroy-*`, `sub-chain.edn` `:sub-graph-topology`, `spawn-all-under-ssr-ring.edn` `:trace-not-emitted`, the 19 `:expect-trace` and 4 `:expect-microsteps` call records, and `ssr-redirect.edn`'s fabricated `:html`/`:payload`). Land it first, or carry its per-channel decisions here, so the grammar never declares an ungraded key. The coordinator wires that link.
- **Blocks:** this dossier's follow-on beads (the roster deletion and prose shrink; then the spec-only probe).
- **Cross-dossier:**
  - Precede any un-deferral of rf2-mn2ht.71 (`:fixture/transport`, from `http-one-request-record.md`'s deferred transport seam); its new key then lands in the grammar file rather than in Spec-Schemas.
  - `flows-static-or-retire.md`: if its bead changes `flow-*.edn` fixtures or flow expectation keys, the later of the two updates the grammar.
  - `ssr-server-init-reserved-name.md` renames an event id in ten fixtures; that is not a grammar change, but do not run fixture edits from both beads in parallel.
- `spec/011-SSR.md` is not touched; if it ever is, it is the one i/crlf file.

## Evidence

- **Read in source at 89517e8f54:** every `path:line` above (the working tree differed from 89517e8f54 only in `.beads/issues.jsonl` when this was filed). The 18 / 26 / 29 / 16 counts, and the 19 `:expect-trace` and 4 `:expect-microsteps` records come from two independent read-only EDN parses of all 241 fixtures, which agree with an earlier babashka census.
- **Still needs a run:** the claim that the published schema rejects 112 of 241 fixtures, and its 31 / 10 breakdown for the `:fx` and `:throw` forms, is a Python approximation; a Malli run settles it, and this bead's deftest will. Also unrun: whether every currently graded expectation still holds once its law is written down (budget for a few fixtures turning red), and the size estimates (about 400 lines of grammar EDN, about 240 lines out of Spec-Schemas).
- **Gates:** `mkdocs build --strict` plus `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` for the spec prose; core's JVM tests (`scripts/test-jvm-implementation.sh`) for the deftest. Prove the deftest can fail: plant an unknown key at the top level, in `:fixture/expect` and inside a call record, and watch each go red with its path.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `spec/conformance/fixture-file.edn` exists and reads with `clojure.edn/read`. It declares, as closed shapes, every top-level fixture key, every `:fixture/expect` key, one `:call` record per Mode-B op (each with its nested expectation keys), every handler-body DSL step op and value form, and every dispatch-entry shape the corpus uses when it lands. It also declares the capability vocabulary as an enum and defines each comparison law once.
2. Every expectation key, top-level and call-record, carries an observation statement and a named law. The nil-or-absent rule is stated in the `:submap` law's definition.
3. Embedded runtime inputs are not validated against the runtime's valid-value schemas: `construction-shape-validation.edn` (`:initial-events [42]` and `[[]]`) validates clean against the grammar.

7. `:fixture/spec-version` is still declared (optional) in the grammar and still present on every fixture; README §Versioning is unchanged.

title: Delete the db-focus redaction heuristic; path-scoped handlers declare payload :sensitive explicitly
description:
Delete the router's db-focus redaction heuristic (Spec 009 §Schema-installed redaction). A handler whose payload carries a secret declares it with registration-owned `:sensitive` on `reg-event`, which is what every example already does.

## Ruling

**Decision.** The db-focus heuristic goes. Today, when a handler's chain carries `[:rf.interceptor/path P]` and `P` is a prefix of a classified sensitive app-db path `S`, the router guesses that the event payload is shaped like the app-db slice at `P`. It then redacts the payload at `S` minus `P` in every trace and error emit, and stamps every trace in the handler's scope `:sensitive? true`. That guess is removed. Payload privacy comes only from explicit declarations: registration-owned `:sensitive` paths on `reg-event` (Spec 015 §Registration-owned transient classification), plus the emit-site projectors. This is the first of four beads from one ruling. It is independent of the other three and can go first.

Decided 2026-10-16: Mike directed that every dossier recommendation an independent Codex review agreed with be actioned. Mike's instruction, verbatim:

> review all decisions. They now have a "Codex Recomendation" section.  Where the original
> recomendation matches the Code Recomendation, create a bead to action the decision.  And then
> remove the file.  Leave behind cases where the two differ materially.

Both recommendations reject the heuristic. They reached that view independently.

**Decisive facts (read in source at trunk 89517e8f54):**

1. **The heuristic is the router guessing at payload shape.**
   - `implementation/core/src/re_frame/privacy.cljc:66-206` computes the overlap between the path focus and the classified paths, and builds the `:rf/schema-redaction` interceptor.
   - The router installs it and builds an `:emit-event` from it at `implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:2461-2475` and `:2517-2529`.
   - At `router.cljc:3005-3011` it sets `:rf/sensitive?` on the scope meta. That is the ONLY producer of the `HandlerScope` `:sensitive?` slot: `implementation/core/src/re_frame/trace.cljc:60`, `:243-258`, and its read at `:556-565`.
2. **It misfires three ways.**
   - **Silent miss.** A payload `{:user "ada" :pw "shh"}`, or a positional `[:auth/login "ada" "shh"]`, ships raw. So does the event that first classifies the path, because the overlap is computed before the handler runs.
   - **False flag.** `[:auth/set-remember-me {:remember? true}]` under an `[:auth]` focus redacts nothing, yet every trace in its scope is stamped, so the pair MCP currently drops the whole epoch.
   - **Refactor drift.** Rewrite the handler as `(assoc-in db [:auth :last-login] payload)` without the path interceptor, and the redaction vanishes silently.
3. **Nothing in `examples/` depends on it.** `git grep -c "rf.interceptor/path" -- examples/` finds 0 hits, while the same probe against `implementation/core/test` finds hits in several files (17 in one alone). The examples declare registration-owned `:sensitive` instead.
   - The one deliberate production dependency is the always-on error record's `:event` slot. It is pinned by `implementation/core/test/re_frame/privacy_production_egress_test.clj:69-95`.
   - The registration-owned projection already reaches that record: `implementation/core/src/re_frame/classification.cljc:491-511`.

**Rejected options:**
- **Keep the heuristic.** Inference from interceptor focus misses real secrets, over-stamps harmless runs, and changes privacy behaviour on refactor. An explicit `:sensitive` declaration states the payload shape that the heuristic can only guess.
- **Defer deletion until the pair-MCP drop is ruled.** The deletion does not depend on that call. On the pair's epoch path, `project-egress` already redacts every trigger-event argument, so the heuristic adds nothing there.

**Supersedes:** no ruling bead or EP; no EP prescribes the heuristic. It removes the contract at `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2761-2795` (§Schema-installed redaction).

title: Correct Spec Privacy's claim that projection waits for the handler to return
description: The rule-summary paragraph edited by PR #11384 in spec/Privacy.md:301 still says projection happens at the observation/egress boundary 'after the handler returns, never before'. That timing clause was retained while removing the deleted :rf/redacted-event mechanism, but it contradicts the actual observation contract. At merged 004fabe1b2edb2b21c2428ea21d5b2817538f8be, router.cljc:3001 emits :rf.event/run-start before validate-event! and run-chain at 3043-3052; trace.cljc:877-885 applies maybe-project-marks synchronously before deliver!. Thus even a pre-handler record is already projected, while the handler still receives its original event coeffect. A reader implementing the documented pipeline must not postpone projection until the handler returns. Small prose correction: keep the unmodified-handler-values statement, remove the after-return/never-before clause, and say each observation is projected at its own emit/egress boundary before delivery, whether raised before, during or after handler execution. No runtime change, new gate or policy is needed.

description:

title: Spec 009's :rf.error/ssr-hydration-payload-invalid row still justifies fail-closed by the retired render-tree hash
description:
Found by the worker on #11484 (rf2-6lvfi, merged), outside its fence.

Spec 011 no longer has a render-tree hash channel. Its Hydration-mismatch detection contract (~672) says every React-family root reports recoveries through React adoption alone, nothing else compares output, and the payload carries state rather than a page fingerprint.

spec/009-Instrumentation.md (~2318), the :rf.error/ssr-hydration-payload-invalid row, still justifies failing closed in every build with the retired channel:

"The read-back succeeds silently (9007199254740993 arrives as 9007199254740992, 1/3 as a double), and the render-tree hash agrees whenever the view prints the value identically, so the check fails closed and RUNS IN EVERY BUILD"

Restate that clause for the system as it is. The reason still holds without the hash: nothing on the client compares the payload value with the server's, and React adoption sees nothing when the view prints the value identically. Change only that clause. A repo-wide census outside docs/design/** and findings/ directories found no other normative render-tree hash mention.

title: Schemas: make the Malli bundle the default validator, cache compiled validators weakly, delete the adapter-absent machinery
description:
## Current

The facade always loads the Malli adapter (`implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas.cljc` ~21). Yet the default validator still carries machinery for the adapter being absent:

- the soft-pass arm (`validator.cljc` ~52-63);
- `using-default-validator?` (`validator.cljc` ~350);
- `:rf.warning/schema-validator-unavailable`, its one-shot flag and the clear fn (`storage.cljc` ~352-486, re-exported at `schemas.cljc` ~54-55).

The adapter publishes raw `malli.core/validate` as `:schemas/malli-validate` (`malli.cljc` ~75), which builds a fresh validator on every call. A JVM probe (Malli 0.20.1) measured per check:

| Path | Cost |
|---|---|
| uncached | 5.33 µs |
| weak cache | 0.10 µs |
| precompiled | 0.06 µs |

1,000 fresh closure-bearing schemas filled the cache to 1,000 entries, which fell to 0 after GC. A malformed schema surfaces only at validate time.

## Change

- `default-schema-fns` becomes the Malli bundle itself: `{:validate <cached validator> :explain … :humanize <dev only>}`. The three Malli hooks (`:schemas/malli-validate`, `:schemas/malli-explain`, `:schemas/humanize-explain!`) fold into that value.
- **The cache.**
  - Key it weakly on the schema value: a `WeakMap` on CLJS, a weak map on the JVM.
  - The bundle owns it, so swapping the port drops it, and an entry lives only while a registration holds its schema.
  - It needs no process-wide schema history, cache configuration or user cleanup duty.
- **An optional `:compile` port key.**
  - Dev registration calls it, so a malformed schema such as `[:vector]` throws at the line that wrote it.
  - Registration-time checks go through the port, never by inspecting opaque tokens as Malli.
  - The per-entry runtime catch stays as the backstop for substitute validators.
- Delete the soft-pass machinery and the warning, with its Spec 009 row.

## Acceptance

- After N register/replace/destroy cycles with fresh closure-bearing schemas, no cache entry for a dead schema is reachable.
- Digest and redaction outputs are byte-identical before and after.
- A JVM check costs within 2× of a precompiled validator.

Spec: 010 §Schema implies validation and §Humanize hook. Hot zone: `spec/009-Instrumentation.md`. Touches `schemas.cljc`; sequence it with the schemas facade-trim bead.

Checked at trunk f4e5adad0a.

title: Reagent views resolve their frame from the component tree: plain fns under a frame-provider just work, one rule with hooks
description:
## Problem

Measured at trunk 3959d2a5bf.

- `current-frame` in `implementation/core/src/re_frame/views/provider.cljs` reads `re-frame.frame/*current-frame*` first and the rendering component's `.-context` second. `.-context` exists only on components that carry the `:contextType` `reg-view` attaches. So a plain Reagent function under a `frame-provider` that calls `subscribe` or `dispatch` without an explicit frame raises `:rf.error/no-frame-context`, even in a single-frame app. Migration rule M-11 (`migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md` § M-11, and the plain-fn boundary paragraph under M-41) makes every v1 app review its plain fns for exactly this.
- React hooks read context only (`React/useContext` in `implementation/core/src/re_frame/adapter/use_frame.cljs`), and Spec 006 § One frame-resolution rule for React hooks calls the split deliberate. So a synchronous flush inside `(with-frame :a …)` renders a Reagent view under provider `:b` as `:a`, while a hook in the same tree reads `:b`. This is read from source, not yet probed; acceptance case 5 probes it.
- The reader the plain-fn case needs already ships: `function-component-current-frame` in `implementation/core/src/re_frame/adapter/context.cljs` reads React's context slot for function components.

## Change

While a component render is in flight, the provider found in the tree wins. Resolve in this order:

1. the component's context: `.-context` under `:contextType`, else the React context-slot read that `function-component-current-frame` already performs, whatever the component's form;
2. `*current-frame*`, which still governs when no provider is present or no component is rendering (imperative, headless and server use);
3. nil.

Captured Form-2/Form-3 ops stay fixed for their mount (`reg-view`'s capture in `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_reg_view_macro.cljc`; the keyed Form-3 retarget fixture `implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/form_3_lifecycle_dom_cljs_test.cljs` pins it). The context-slot read is private renderer state; keep it in the one function that already does it rather than adding a second reader.

**Why.** One rule for the whole tree: a human or an AI pair can tell a view's frame by looking at the tree, plain Reagent functions under a provider just work, and the reason 006 gives for the hook rule (one tree resolves one frame under either scheduling mode) applies to ratom renders too.

## Spec and docs that move with it

- `spec/002-Frames.md` § Reading the frame from React context. **Hot zone.**
- `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md` § Frame-provider via React context and § One frame-resolution rule for React hooks become one rule for both tiers. **Hot zone.**
- `migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md`: M-11 narrows to deferred callbacks (which still need captured ops), and the M-41 plain-fn boundary paragraph changes. **Hot zone.**
- Docs that teach `reg-view` as the only way a view acquires its frame, or that plain fns cannot read a provider: census `no-frame-context` and "plain fn" under `docs/` and `skills/`.

## Acceptance

1. A plain Reagent fn resolves the provider's frame under nested namespaced providers.
2. The same on an independent ratom-triggered re-render.
3. The same under StrictMode.
4. The same in a server render.
5. Under provider `:b`, a synchronous flush inside `with-frame :a` resolves `:b` for a Reagent view and for a hook alike.
6. Controls: with no provider, a plain fn falls to an enclosing `with-frame` or raises `:rf.error/no-frame-context`; a deferred callback (a `setTimeout` body) still needs captured ops.
7. `npm run test:cljs`, `npm run test:adapter-smokes` and the Reagent adapter suite green.

## Sequencing

Hot zones: `spec/002-Frames.md`, `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md`, `migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md`. Shares Spec 006 with the core test-flush bead (linked as related); sequence the two.

Breaking: an error becomes a success, and the flush-inside-`with-frame` case changes target. Effort S in code, M in docs. Risk medium, because the context slot is private renderer state.

title: Docs playground: emulate h/render-fn so Fresco render-carrier recipes can run live
description:
## Problem

Found by the rf2-more0 worker (PR #11537). Fresco's callbacks are now two explicit carriers: `h/event` dispatches what it returns, and `h/render-fn` returns markup and carries the supplying frame. The docs SCI playground (`docs/tools/playground/sci`) emulates only `h/event`, so no live docs cell can show `h/render-fn`, and the recipes that need it (a virtual list's `itemContent`, an `on*`-named render prop) cannot run in the browser.

## Change

Add `h/render-fn` to the playground's Fresco emulation, matching the reference: a marked fn whose return passes through `as-element` and carries the supplying frame. Then, where a docs recipe would benefit, give it a live cell. Re-derive at tip after #11537 merges.

## Acceptance

- A playground cell using `h/render-fn` evaluates.
- The playground's own tests are green.
- `mkdocs build --strict` is green.

Effort S. Fence: `docs/tools/playground/**`, which is excluded from the strict docs build (read `mkdocs.yml` `exclude_docs`).

title: Read callback self-id in the machine-owned Resource recipe
description:
Merged PR #11538 moves spawned identity out of :data into :rf/runtime and exposes :self-id on callback context, but the current Spec 016 Machine-owned resource example still reads the removed key. At f3565f964881f2b8b706c27bb97aafa8af0c3970, spec/016-Resources.md:1929-1939 destructures only data, then evaluates (:rf/self-id data :checkout/flow) for its :owner [:machine actor-id]. For every spawned instance carrying ordinary {:cart-id ...} data this selects :checkout/flow, rather than that instance's actual runtime address. Different instances share the fallback owner, and actor teardown releases [:machine <actual-actor-id>], leaving the recipe's owner active. title: [MIKE DECISION] .beads/issues.jsonl passed GitHub's 50 MB warning; at ~6 MB/week it hits the 100 MB push limit in about 8 weeks
description:
## Decision needed

`.beads/issues.jsonl` crossed GitHub's 50 MB warning on the checkpoint push of 2026-10-16 (commit c91503d728): "File .beads/issues.jsonl is 50.13 MB; this is larger than GitHub's recommended maximum file size of 50.00 MB". GitHub REJECTS a push carrying a file over 100 MB, and the checkpoint sequence in CLAUDE.md § Beads durability pushes this file on every checkpoint, so at that point every tracker checkpoint (and every mayor push carrying one) fails.

## Measured (git cat-file -s <rev>:.beads/issues.jsonl)

| committed (UTC) | rev | bytes |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-09-16 07:48 | c20bf545dc | 25,474,602 |
| 2026-10-02 07:55 | 73af948741 | 43,931,245 |
| 2026-10-09 06:55 | c405baa390 | 46,611,690 |
| 2026-10-16 07:03 | c91503d728 | 52,561,042 |

Last week's growth was ~6.0 MB; at that rate the 100 MB limit (104,857,600 bytes) is about 8 weeks away. The fortnight before grew faster.

Composition at c91503d728 (5078 rows): issue rows 50.0 MB, memory rows 2.5 MB. By field: notes 23.7 MB, description 14.6 MB, close_reason 7.9 MB, memory value 2.4 MB, everything else under 0.7 MB each. The 20 rows over 100 KB hold 2.7 MB together (largest rf2-k97c.3 at 326 KB, closed; rf2-uelji at 234 KB, open).

## Options

- **A. Keep the single tracked export and revisit near the limit.** No change now. Cost: the decision comes back under time pressure.
- **B. Shard the export.** Closed beads move into frozen per-month archive files (for example `.beads/archive/2026-09.jsonl`), and the live `issues.jsonl` carries open beads and recent closes. Every record stays in git history, so CLAUDE.md's recovery routes (close reasons and notes from `git show <rev>:...`) keep working with a path change, and git still stores each file as deltas. Cost: `scripts/beads-checkpoint.sh` (both siblings), the pre-commit floor (rf2-or8te), the beads PR-boundary check and the out-of-repo merge-audit harness all learn the layout.
- **C. Stop committing the full export; Dolt remote (`bd dolt push`) is the durable copy.** Commit a slim projection (ids, status, titles, close reasons) or nothing. Cost: notes recovery from git history goes away; CLAUDE.md's recovery routes for `--notes` overwrites and reopen-erased close reasons must be rewritten around `bd history`.
- **D. Git LFS.** Poor fit: LFS stores every version whole rather than as a delta, so ~50 MB per checkpoint, several checkpoints a day, exhausts GitHub's LFS storage quota quickly; `git show <rev>:...` also returns a pointer, breaking the recovery routes.

Not on the table: decaying closed beads (`bd gc` decay is banned here; close reasons are normative records).

## Recommendation

B, scheduled within the next few weeks, not urgent today. It keeps every guarantee CLAUDE.md relies on and bounds the live file. A is the fallback if the sharding change is not wanted now.
close_reason:
RULING (Mike, 2026-10-20 13:41 AUSEST): closed as minutiae; not actioned now.
Measured at close: the tracked .beads/issues.jsonl export is 51.96 MB (GitHub's push warning on cc9ee42946). Pushes still succeed with the GH001 large-file warning, and GitHub's hard limit is 100 MB per file.
No change to the export, Git LFS or the checkpoint flow follows.
The bead had no dependents.

title: Framework integration tests move out of the Reagent adapter tree and run against the Fresco adapter
description:
## Ruling

Mike approved on 2026-10-21 that the framework's example and feature integration tests move out of `implementation/adapters/reagent/test/` into a framework-level test tree, and run against Fresco, the taught default. First convert one and show it runs fixture-switched; then move the rest.

## Problem

Measured at trunk c383c6a92e.

`implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/` holds 81 `.cljs` files (14,904 lines). **19 of them (5,345 lines) are example or feature tests.** Their only Reagent coupling is the fixture's `:adapter rf.adapter.reagent/adapter` key (e.g. `todomvc_example_cljs_test.cljs:13-16`). None requires `reagent.*` or mounts a React root:

- the `realworld_*` tests, all six: `realworld` (1171), `realworld_resources` (890), `realworld_resources_observability` (79), and `realworld_markdown`, `realworld_shared_backend` and `realworld_shared_contract` (154, 230, 155). The last three install no adapter at all.
- `todomvc_example` (32), `linearlite_example` (368), `login` (144), `websocket` (556), `routing` (118) and `http_managed` (183);
- `flows_example` (103), `infinite_feed_example` (301), `resources_example` (155), `nine_states` (156), `long_running_work` (87) and `boot` (250);
- `standard_epochs_views_subs_lifecycle` (213). Its last deftest (`:179`) renders through `rf/reg-view` and `rf/view`.

**Five integration-shaped tests use Reagent itself, so they stay adapter tests:**
- `standard_epochs_diamond_recompute`, whose driver is `reagent.ratom/run!` (`:25`, `:78-99`);
- `core_examples_review`, which renders through `reagent.dom.server` (`:54`);
- `schema_reject_notification` (`r/track!`);
- `cross_spec_dom` (`reagent.dom.client`);
- `runtime` (`r/flush`).

**The examples stay Reagent apps** (e.g. `examples/core/todomvc/core.cljs:16`). The tests drive their events and subscriptions, not their views. A Fresco app installs `re-frame.fresco.substrate/adapter` (`implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco/substrate.cljs:139`). `substrate_react_shared_cljs_test.cljs:58` already uses it as a fixture adapter.

**Wiring.** Tests are selected by namespace suffix: `:node-test` runs every `cljs-test$` namespace on its classpath (`implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:705`). None of the 19 is a `-dom-cljs-test`. The tree is reached through:
- `shadow-cljs.edn:49`;
- `implementation/deps.edn:62` (comment at `:87-96`);
- the classifier `.github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh`, which routes `implementation/adapters/*` (`:601`, `:862`) and cites the tree at `:2011-2013`.

The precedent for a framework-level tree is the test-only tiers: `event-conformance/` and its siblings (`shadow-cljs.edn:228-290`, classifier `:1360`).

## Change

1. **Convert one test first.**
   - Create `implementation/integration/test/re_frame/`, with one helper namespace that names the suite's adapter, `re-frame.fresco.substrate/adapter`.
   - Move `routing_cljs_test.cljs` there, with its fixture reading that var.
   - Run it against Fresco, then flip the var to Reagent and run it again. Record both runs on the bead.
2. **Move the other 18.**
   - Namespaces keep their names.
   - Re-word the docstrings that name Reagent as their subject (`routing_cljs_test.cljs:3`, `:6`, `:51`, `:76`; `http_managed_cljs_test.cljs:2`, `:18`).
   - If `standard_epochs_views_subs_lifecycle`'s last deftest is red under Fresco, that one deftest stays behind.
3. **Wire the tree.**
   - Add it to `shadow-cljs.edn` `:source-paths` beside the conformance tiers.
   - Add it to `deps.edn` `:test :extra-paths`.
   - Give the classifier an arm firing `cljs_node_test`.
   - The tree is CLJS-only, so it needs no `deps.edn` of its own.

**What stays:** 62 files, the five tests above plus the 57 adapter tests (`adapter_*`, `form_*`, `reg_view_*`, `ssr_*` and the rest).

## Spec and docs that move with it

- `spec/Conventions.md:1869-1871`, §Adapter test matrix policy: "the full re-frame2 test suite … executes against the Reagent adapter". Restate it: the integration suite runs on Fresco, and adapter tests stay per adapter. **Hot zone.**
- `implementation/README.md:272-276` says the same.
- Path pointers:
  - `docs/routing/testing.md:228`;
  - `spec/013-Flows.md:337`;
  - `spec/Pattern-WebSocket.md:664`;
  - `examples/patterns/long_running_work/core.cljs:49`;
  - `examples/patterns/nine_states/core.cljs:71`;
  - `skills/re-frame2/patterns/long-running-work.md:158` and `nine-states.md:114`;
  - `implementation/core/test/re_frame/todomvc_cljs_test.cljs:5-6`.
- `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn` and `implementation/deps.edn`. **Hot zone.**
- The classifier and its mirror `implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs`, in one commit. **Hot zone** (CLAUDE.md).

title: ssr-node's render-error stderr lines carry requestId; :rf.error/ssr-ring-import-fn-unresolved is deleted
description:
## Ruling

Mike approved on 2026-10-21 two small sidecar cleanups:

- ssr-node's render-exception stderr line (`reportRenderException`) and its replacement-fault line (`reportReplacementFault`) carry the request's `requestId`, so a JVM 5xx can be matched to its Node stack.
- `:rf.error/ssr-ring-import-fn-unresolved` is deleted, with its Spec 009 row.

`implementation/ssr-node/test/absence.test.cjs` stays. Application exception text stays out of HTTP JSON.

## Problem

Measured at trunk c383c6a92e.

**The JVM sends a correlation id, and the operator's lines drop it.**
- `re-frame.ssr.ring.node` sends the request frame's id as `requestId` on every render (`implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/node.clj:292`). The JVM's error records carry the same frame as `:frame` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/error_emit.cljc:951`).
- The sidecar validates `requestId` as an optional string (`implementation/ssr-node/src/protocol.cjs:509`, `:527-529`). It echoes it on the `complete` frame and the refusal frame, and over HTTP as `x-rf-ssr-request`.
- `reportRenderException(entry, err)` (`implementation/ssr-node/src/worker.cjs:101-104`) writes `[rf.ssr-node] render threw in entry <entry>: <stack>`. It names the entry only, though both call sites (`:248`, `:279`) hold the request.
- `reportReplacementFault(modulePath, err)` (`implementation/ssr-node/src/pool.cjs:60-67`) runs from `Pool.release` (`:224-275`, the call at `:268`). `release(isolate)` is called once, from `service.cjs:130`, where `validatedRequest.requestId` is in scope but not passed.
- So today the only way to match a JVM 5xx to the Node stack behind it is the clock.

**A catalogued error for a maintainer-only mistake.**
- `import-fn` (`implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring.clj:26-53`) is a private macro with two call sites (`:55-56`), both with fixed symbols.
- On an unresolvable symbol it throws `:rf.error/ssr-ring-import-fn-unresolved` at macro expansion (`:37-46`). That is the file's only live use of `re-frame.error` (required at `:12`).
- The id appears in exactly two places: `ring.clj:40` and its row at `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2318`. The control search for `:rf.error/ssr-node-refused` finds it in `node.clj` and Spec 009.

## Change

**requestId on the two stderr lines.**
- `reportRenderException` takes the request's `requestId` and appends it when present, e.g. `render threw in entry app/root (request <id>): <stack>`. Pass `request.requestId` at `:248` and `message.request?.requestId` at `:279`.
- `Pool.release(isolate, requestId)` hands the id on to `reportReplacementFault`. That id names the render whose isolate died and set off the replacement. `service.cjs:130` passes `validatedRequest.requestId`.
- With no `requestId`, each line reads as it does today.
- The id goes to stderr only. No refusal, `detail`, header or HTTP JSON field changes, and no application-authored text moves.
- The other stderr reporters (`reportIsolateFault` in `isolate.cjs:60`, `reportBootException`, `reportUncontractedFault`) are outside this ruling and stay as they are.

**Delete the error id.**
- Remove the `when-not (resolve …)` guard from `import-fn`. An unresolvable symbol then fails at load with Clojure's own compile error from the expansion's `(def … ~src-sym)`. That is the same point of failure, at the same moment, for the only people who can hit it.
- Drop the `re-frame.error` require (`:12`), whose only live use this is.
- Delete the Spec 009 row.

**Stays:** `absence.test.cjs`, and every refusal's fixed wording.

## Spec and docs that move with it

- `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2318`: delete the `:rf.error/ssr-ring-import-fn-unresolved` row. **Hot zone.**
- `implementation/ssr-node/README.md:85` ("The full exception, with its stack, goes to the sidecar's stderr"): add that the line names the caller's `requestId` when the request carried one.
- `docs/ssr/concepts.md:939` ("Everything diagnostic goes to stderr"): one clause saying a render failure's stderr line carries the request frame's id, so it can be matched to the JVM's error record.

## Acceptance

- New `egress.test.cjs` row: a throwing render sent with `requestId: 'corr-throw'` leaves a captured stderr line containing both `render threw in entry` and `corr-throw`. The existing refusal asserts still hold: the same `RENDER_THREW_REFUSAL`, `detail` of `{ entry }` only, and no sentinel in the JSON body.
- `replacementBootFailure` (`egress.test.cjs:337-368`) sends its hung render with a `requestId`. The test at `:370` asserts that the pool line also contains that id.
- A render without `requestId` still writes today's line, with no `(request …)` suffix.
- `git grep ssr-ring-import-fn-unresolved` reads 0, with a control search that still finds `:rf.error/ssr-node-refused`.
- `scripts/check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py` and `error_catalogue_channel_conformance_test` green.
- The ssr-node suite (`npm test` in `implementation/ssr-node`, i.e. `node test/run.cjs`), the JVM ssr-ring suite, `mkdocs build --strict` and `check_readme_links.py --ci` green.

title: O-16 companion: §:halt? puts the halt dispatch in the :final? state's :entry, but v1 fires every rule one event makes ready, in rule order, as one :dispatch-n before halting; a machine takes one transition and runs :entry fx after the :action's
description:
Filed from a downstream v1 -> re-frame2 migration's skills retrospective (suggestion, not a work order). Verified at origin/main 0783705626. Priority 2: following the recipe as written silently reorders or drops a boot dispatch whenever one event makes several rules ready at once.

## Skill file and section

migration/from-re-frame-v1/async-flow-fx-to-reg-machine.md (the O-16 companion):

- §Mapping notes, `:rules` with multi-event `:when` predicates (lines 227-230);
- §`:halt?` (line 237).

## What it says

- :227: "The translation is one rule at a time."
- :230: "Place the transition on that state's `:on` map."
- :237: "If the halt rule dispatched an event (e.g. `:dispatch [:app/ready]`), put the dispatch in the `:final?` state's `:entry` action — the action runs once, on entry."

## What happened (generic)

v1 evaluates every rule on each forwarded event. It collects all the not-yet-fired rules whose `:when` now holds, in declaration order. It emits their dispatches together as one `:dispatch-n` in that order, and only then tears the flow down if any of them has `:halt?`. So when one event completes two rules' `:events` sets, both rules fire, in rule order, before the halt.

That case is common in boot flows. A non-halting rule and the halting "all done" rule often wait on overlapping `:seen-all-of?` sets, so the event that arrives last completes both. On a ~170-file app the boot flow has six rules, three of them halting, and two non-halting rules wait on events that are also in the success-halt rule's set.

The companion's recipe has no place for this:

- **A machine takes one transition per event.** A state's `:on` map has one entry per event, a guarded candidate vector runs only its first passing candidate, and rules placed on different states are handled only by the active one. Translated one rule at a time, a co-ready rule's dispatch is lost.
- **Merged into one transition, the order changes.** If the halt rule's dispatch goes in the `:final?` state's `:entry` as :237 says, it runs after the transition `:action`'s effects. So the halt dispatch always comes last. v1 ran it in rule order, so a halt rule declared before a co-ready rule dispatched first.

Dispatch order is observable: the queue is FIFO, so a "ready" event that v1 ran after a setup dispatch can now run before it, or the other way round.

## Evidence

v1 day8.re-frame/async-flow-fx 0.4.0, day8/re_frame/async_flow_fx.cljs:

- :48-55 `startable-rules`: `(->> rules (remove (comp rules-fired :id)) (filterv (fn [task] ((:when task) (:events task) now-seen-events))))`. This returns every ready rule, in declaration order. `massage-rules` (:76-80) gives each rule `(or id index)`.
- :173-177: `ready-rules`, then `halt? (some :halt? ready-rules)`, then `new-dispatches (rules->dispatches ready-rules forwarded-event)`. `rules->dispatches` (:96) is a `mapcat` over the ready rules in order.
- :187 `{:dispatch-n new-dispatches}`, then :188-200 the halt teardown in the same effect map.

re-frame2:

- spec/005-StateMachines.md:347: "the first candidate whose guard passes wins".
- :679: the cascade runs "exit deepest-first → transition `:action` at the LCA → entry shallowest-first".
- :801: "`:fx` vectors concatenate left-to-right".

## Suggested change

1. In §`:rules`, add a detection step: for each event, list the rules whose `:events` contain it. Any event in two or more rules' sets can make them ready together.
2. For such an event, emit all the co-ready rules' dispatches from the one transition's `:action`, in v1 rule order. Reach the `:final?` state from that transition, or through an `:always` step when the next state depends on which rules fired.
3. In §`:halt?`, keep "put the dispatch in the `:final?` state's `:entry`" only for a halt rule that no other rule can become ready alongside. State v1's rule: every ready rule fires, in declaration order, as one `:dispatch-n`, before the halt.

title: skill(re-frame2-pair): setup.md and README tell consumers to put an absolute preload path on the classpath; committed config needs a relative path (the migration skill's clean-checkout gate fails an absolute one)
description:
Filed from a downstream v1 -> re-frame2 migration's skills retrospective (suggestion, not a work order). Verified at origin/main 2a6fd908a6.

## Skill file and section

skills/re-frame2-pair/references/setup.md, the classpath snippets (lines 31 and 38), and skills/re-frame2-pair/README.md step "2. Preload" (line 156). Conflicting with skills/re-frame-migration/references/xray-replaces-10x.md §2 "Add Xray" (lines 53-55 and 58) and setup.md "The consumability done-gate" (line 121).

## What it says

re-frame2-pair setup.md:31: `{:dev {:extra-paths ["<abs>/skills/re-frame2-pair/preload"]}}}  ;; add this`, and :38: `"<abs>/skills/re-frame2-pair/preload"]  ;; add this (the linked skill's preload/)`.

re-frame2-pair README.md:156: "From a linked clone, put the absolute path to `skills/re-frame2-pair/preload/` on your app's build classpath (no package install)".

re-frame-migration xray-replaces-10x.md:53-55: "<path-to-re-frame2> is the local pinned re-frame2 checkout ... as a path relative to THIS project's deps.edn (an absolute path fails the clean-checkout gate in setup.md)". re-frame-migration setup.md:121: "... each fail the gate. So does an absolute path, or a relative one the runner does not provision".

## What happened (generic)

The Pair docs give only an absolute path, and do not say whether the edit is meant to be committed. A migration (or any team) that keeps the Pair preload wired for everyone commits that `deps.edn` / `shadow-cljs.edn` edit. An absolute path then names one machine's disk: it fails on CI and on every other checkout. The migration skill already rules this out for the sibling Xray `:local/root`, but a worker following the Pair setup has no such guidance. Hit while preparing Phase-4 readiness on a ~170-file app, where the Pair preload would land in committed config.

## Evidence

The quotes above, from `git show origin/main:<file>`. tools.deps accepts a relative `:extra-paths` / `:local/root` entry resolved from the project directory; re-frame-migration setup.md:113 quotes this ("either absolute or relative to the location of the project directory"). shadow-cljs `:source-paths` are relative to the project root too.

## Suggested change

In re-frame2-pair setup.md (both snippets) and README.md:156, replace `<abs>` with `<path-to-re-frame2>`, and add one line: "For config you commit, write this as a path relative to the file that holds it (deps.edn / project.clj / shadow-cljs.edn), over a sibling checkout every runner provides. Use an absolute path only for a local, uncommitted setup." Cross-link re-frame-migration setup.md §The consumability done-gate for a migration.

title: Security tier: one declared token is witnessed redacted across HTTP traces and the SSR hydration payload
description:
## Ruling

Mike approved on 2026-10-21 one security-tier case under `implementation/security/test/re_frame/security/`. A declared token inside a vector of maps is carried both in an HTTP response body and in a spawned machine's `:data`. The test scans the whole HTTP trace body and the whole serialised SSR hydration payload for it. A detector control proves the scan can see the planted value, copying the `embeds?` scan and opt-in control pattern in `implementation/reply-conformance/test/re_frame/reply_egress_projection_conformance_cljs_test.cljc`.

It is blocked by rf2-o5rtr's vertical slice.

## Problem

Measured at trunk c383c6a92e.

**The security tier checks one boundary per suite.** It holds ten files (`implementation/security/test/re_frame/security/`). None issues an `:rf.http/managed` request, spawns a machine, or builds a hydration payload: `git grep` for `rf.http`, `stub-transport`, `reg-machine` and `hydration-payload` there finds only a `:kind :rf.http/server-error` literal (`reply_envelope_egress_security_cljs_test.cljc:68`) and a hydration-install test (`fail_closed_invariant_security_cljs_test.cljc:60`).

**The seams are covered one side at a time:**
- A vector-of-maps body: `vector-of-maps-decoder-redacts-every-element` (`implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_privacy_integration_test.clj:149`). JVM only, against a real server.
- Machine `:data` in hydration: `a-root-keyed-data-declaration-redacts-in-hydration-as-the-trace-does` (`implementation/machines/test/re_frame/machine_ssr_keyed_data_projection_test.clj:18`). It reads `project-ssr-runtime-db`, not the serialised payload.
- Nothing follows one value from an HTTP reply into a machine and out through the page.

**The pieces a case needs exist:**
- `re-frame.http.stub-transport/with-transport` (`implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/stub_transport.cljc:139-149`) replaces only the host send and runs the real pipeline, privacy scrub included, on both hosts.
- `re-frame.ssr/hydration-payload` (`implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr.cljc:182-221`) builds the map a host `pr-str`s into `__rf_payload`, with machine snapshots under `:rf/runtime-db`.
- The pattern to copy: `embeds?` (`reply_egress_projection_conformance_cljs_test.cljc:52-54`) walks `tree-seq` for any string that contains the raw value, map keys and wrapped strings included. Its opt-in control (`:97-98`) shows that the raw value does come back when sensitive egress is asked for.

## Change

Add one dual-runtime file, for example `one_secret_every_egress_security_cljs_test.cljc`, with one case:

1. **Plant.** A unique long literal token, for example `"S3CR3T-one-secret-every-egress"`.
2. **HTTP.** A stub transport answers `{:items [{:id 1 :token <token>} {:id 2 :token <token>}]}`. The request's `:decode` is `[:map [:items [:vector [:map [:id :int] [:token {:sensitive? true} :string]]]]]`.
3. **Machine.** The reply event stores the reply in app-db and spawns a registered machine whose `:data` is the decoded `:items`. The machine declares the token path, e.g. `:sensitive [[:data :items :token]]`.
4. **Scan.** No string in either of these contains the token:
   - every `:rf.http/*` trace event the request emitted, all tags, both as delivered to listeners and after `rf/project-egress` under `:rf.egress/off-box-tool`;
   - `(pr-str (re-frame.ssr/hydration-payload frame {:payload []}))`, which carries the machine's snapshot.
5. **Detector control.** The same scan must find the token in the delivered reply in app-db, which stays raw by design, and in the live machine snapshot's `:data`. So a clean scan means the projection redacted the value, not that the scanner was blind.

Declare the token in whatever form trunk then uses. If rf2-o5rtr's slice moves these owners to static declarations, use that form. The case pins the outcome, not the declaration spelling.

Add `day8/re-frame2-http {:local/root "../http"}` to `implementation/security/deps.edn` so the JVM lane can load it. The CLJS node-test classpath already spans every artefact.

## Spec and docs that move with it

None. If the scan fails, it is a bug against Spec 014 §Response-body classification, Spec 015 or Spec 011 §Payload scope. Fix it in this bead, or file it blocking this bead.

## Acceptance

- The new case passes on both runtimes: `clojure -M:test` from `implementation/security` and `npm run test:security`.
- Delete the machine's `:sensitive` declaration and the case goes red on the hydration scan. Delete the `:decode` mark and it goes red on the trace scan. Revert both before merging, and say in the PR body that both went red.
- The detector-control assertions are in the committed test.
- `npm run test:cljs` green.

## Sequencing

Blocked by rf2-o5rtr. Its vertical slice proves first egress, SSR permit and hydration for one login path, and may change how this token is declared. Write the case once that slice has merged.

title: Static classification stage 1: subsystem declarations apply at egress through one hook per runtime-db root, and per-instance lowering is deleted (EP-0039)
description:
Stage 1 of EP-0039 (static data classification, accepted): subsystem declarations apply at egress through one late-bound hook per runtime-db root, and the per-instance lowering into the elision registry is deleted.

## Ruling

EP-0039 is accepted (operator ruling 2026-10-16, option B with the independent Codex review): durable state is classified by static, authored declarations, and a retained value keeps the redactions it was recorded under. The ruling's sequence is an EP, ONE vertical slice, then the remaining owners. The slice is rf2-o5rtr, and its measurement confirmed the simplification (numbers below). Stage 1 is EP-0039 §Backwards Compatibility step 2: "option D as a stage", not an end state.

## What the slice already built (read it before starting)

`reg-classification` (registrar kind `:classification`), the per-frame classification POLICY in `re-frame.elision` (`frame-policy`, cached per frame against its resolution view, reached through the late-bound `:live-frame/call-with-frame-resolution` seam, never an ambient lookup), `with-policy` (the read-time union with the registry), and the epoch capture (`record-policy` / `recorded-policy`: the policy rides an epoch record's METADATA and `re-frame.epoch.tool-pair/recorded-registry` unions it in). The policy today carries `:app-db` only. Spec 015 §Static app-db classification and §Retained values keep their recorded classification describe it.

## Work

1. Publish the four hooks of EP-0039 §4, each with a 0-arity collect (called while the policy is built, inside the resolution seam) and a pure 2-arity apply `(root-value decls) -> {:sensitive [abs-path …] :large [abs-path …]}`:
   - `:machines/runtime-classification` (re-frame.machines.classification), instances named by `:rf/machine-type` or a singleton's own id;
   - `:resources/runtime-classification` and `:resources/mutation-runtime-classification` (re-frame.resources.classification), named by `:resource/key` / `:mutation/id`;
   - `:routing/runtime-classification` (re-frame.routing.classification), the current slice named by `:route-id` (see rf2-p0767).
   The apply arities are the existing pure re-rooting minus the registry write: `absolute-snapshot-path` + `machine-declarations`, `instance-declaration-paths` / `mutation-instance-declaration-paths`, and the route re-rooting inside `apply-route-classification`.
2. Extend the policy with `:roots` (collect), and have core apply each root's hook to the value being projected (live partition for a direct read, the recorded one for an epoch). A root whose hook is unbound has no classification.
3. Every consumer goes through the hooks: the trace chokepoint, the framework read subs (`[:rf/machine …]`, the route subs, the resource subs) re-seeded at their storage position, the SSR runtime-db projection, the epoch and direct-read projections.
4. Sub memo capture (EP-0039 §5, second bullet): the sub memo captures the policy with each computed value, so `:rf.sub/prev-value` projects under the policy its value was computed with. This replaces the route slice's declaration metadata and the machine sub's read of the registry out of its prior inputs. title: ci: the detect and PR-guard jobs in docs.yml, lint.yml and test.yml still pay a full-history clone (minutes) on every PR; a blobless clone with full history likely keeps their answers
description:
Four PR-path jobs still check out with `fetch-depth: 0` and no filter, so every PR pays a full-history clone in each of them before its required checks can settle: docs.yml `detect` (Detect docs surface; the `build` and `provenance-pins` jobs both `needs:` it), lint.yml `detect` (Detect lint surface), test.yml `detect_changed_surfaces` (Detect changed test surfaces) and test.yml `beads-pr-boundary` (PR guards). On PR #11720 all four were still in their checkout step more than five minutes after starting, while `docs.yml`'s comment calls `detect` a "~5-second job".

Measured on this repository (2026-10-29): old blobs are about 1.92 GiB of a 1.97 GiB object store, against about 57 MiB of commits and trees. A `--filter=blob:none` clone with full history took 25 s locally (95 MiB) against 102 s (470 MiB) for a plain full clone. On CI, the Provenance pins jobs went from an 8m42s checkout (docs.yml, PR #11719 re-run; the first attempt was cancelled at its 10-minute cap) and 5m52s to 11m18s (lint.yml corpus job, three main pushes) to 24 s with `filter: blob:none` under rf2-fuq7l (PR #11720).

What each job reads from history decides the fix. The three detect jobs diff names against a merge base (commits and trees). beads-pr-boundary reads PR commit metadata and changed paths (check-beads-pr-boundary.sh, check-commit-attribution.sh). Neither should need old blob contents, so `filter: blob:none` beside `fetch-depth: 0` is the likely shape. Check each script's git calls first. Unlike the provenance-pins checker, these jobs need no GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH, because a lazily fetched blob for rename detection is harmless here. But confirm that nothing classifies on whether an object exists. portability.yml's ai-tracking-ratchet job is a worked precedent for avoiding the full clone by another route.

Acceptance: each job's checkout and total duration before and after, from the PR's own CI logs; each job's output unchanged on the same PR. Hot zone (.github/workflows/*): one toucher, and sequence after rf2-fuq7l's PR merges.

title: senior review: core: subscriptions, derivation, views and substrate
description:
SENIOR-DEVELOPER REVIEW of one slice of the tree. Part of the review sweep rf2-r5cc2, which partitions implementation/, tools/, examples/ and skills/ into slices; this bead owns exactly the slice below, and its siblings own the rest.

SLICE:
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/ — substrate/, subs (and subs/), views (and views/), derivation/, adapter/, interop, source_coords (and source_coords/), source_store, emit_substrate, core_reg_view_macro
- their tests under implementation/core/test/

FOCUS: The reactive substrate, subscription caching and disposal, derivation, view registration and source-coord annotation (Spec 004, 006).

PERSONA. A senior Clojure/ClojureScript developer who did not write this code, reading it as its next maintainer and as a programmer who has to use it. Judge it against the project stance (CLAUDE.md), quoted verbatim:

> Posture is that we are pre-alpha and focused on elegance, power and a masterpiece.
> But we are not over-engineering or gold plating. Also, we trust the programmer.
> We're trying to facilitate high productivity for them (and the AI they use) via a
> library with excellent ergonomics and low friction. We don't need to litigate every
> last fine detail and drown in the minutiae.

So record material, actionable insights only: a defect, a simplification that removes real weight, an ergonomic sharp edge a programmer (or the AI they use) will hit, a test that cannot go red, a doc or docstring that misleads. Not style preferences, not nagging diagnostics, not defensive belt-and-braces, not renames for taste.

LENSES, in priority order:
1. Correctness — error paths, concurrency, cleanup, and fail-closed behaviour on any security or privacy boundary.
2. Simplicity and clarity — dead code, duplication (within the slice or with another slice), accidental complexity, an abstraction that earns nothing.
3. Ergonomics — the API or tool as a programmer, or the AI they use, actually meets it.
4. Performance — hot spots on real paths, never at the expense of clarity.
5. Test rigour — a test that cannot fail, a gap on a branch that matters.
6. Comments and docstrings — per CLAUDE.md § Conventions & Patterns: present tense, the reason plus a spec pointer, no provenance, no restated spec.

METHOD. Read the slice's source first, then its tests, against the owning spec sections (spec/Ownership.md maps each surface to its spec). A finding is a CLAIM until checked: confirm each one at source, and confirm a behaviour claim with a quick REPL or test run where that is cheap. This is a read-only review: edit no file, and run only read-only commands and the slice's existing test lanes.

OUTPUT, recorded on THIS bead and never in a separate file: write the section to a file and append it with `bd update <this bead> --append-notes "$(cat <file>)"` (never `--notes`, which replaces). Head it `== SENIOR REVIEW FINDINGS (<datetime with zone>, trunk <short sha>)` and include:
- 0 to 15 numbered findings, most important first. Each gives: `path:line` (plus a short quote so it can be re-found by text), what is wrong, why it matters (the concrete failure or cost), the fix (a sketch is fine), size (S/M/L), confidence (verified / probable), and its lens.
- A short "looked at and sound" list, so the review's coverage is visible.
- Cross-slice findings, whose defect lives in another slice's files, in a separate list naming the owning slice. Do not act on them.

Then add the label `findings-recorded` and leave the bead OPEN: its findings become this slice's fix work, which the coordinator dispatches in clusters. If the slice needs nothing, record zero findings with the coverage list and close the bead with that as the reason.
notes:
== SENIOR REVIEW FINDINGS (2026-10-29 10:31:28 AUSEST, trunk 89f5bbc4de)

Slice: implementation/core/src/re_frame/ substrate/, subs (+ subs/), views (+ views/), derivation/, adapter/, interop, source_coords (+ source_coords/), source_store, emit_substrate, core_reg_view_macro, and their tests. Read against spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md, spec/002-Frames.md, spec/001-Registration.md, spec/Derivations.md, spec/Security.md and implementation/SECURITY.md. Paths below are repo-relative under implementation/core/src/re_frame/ unless they say otherwise. Items already ruled were not re-proposed: :subscribe-container stays; no core-graph spike; acquire-cache-reaction!, *acquire-recovery* and *disposal-cause* stay at zero callers; synchronous last-owner release and scoped invalidation stay.

FINDINGS (most important first)

1. The editor-URI scheme denylist is bypassed by a tab, a newline or a C0 control character.
   - Where: source_coords/editor_uri.cljc:142, `(let [trimmed (str/triml uri)`, and :144, `(some #(str/starts-with? lower %) forbidden-uri-schemes)`.
   - Defect: the check left-trims whitespace and then prefix-matches. Browsers parse URLs more loosely (WHATWG URL): they delete every tab, CR and LF anywhere in the URL, and strip leading C0 controls and spaces. So `"java\tscript:alert(1)"` and `"\u0001javascript:..."` pass the check, and the browser then runs them as `javascript:`.
   - Cost: this predicate is the only gate on the `:custom` template, and on the pre-resolved `{:uri ...}` handoff that Xray's and Story's `open!` seams re-check. It fails open on the security boundary that Security.md §Editor URI scheme allowlist names.
   - Fix: normalise as the browser does before matching. Remove `[\t\n\r]` everywhere, left-strip `[\x00-\x20]`, then lower-case. Add these three forms to source_coords_editor_uri_test.clj.
   - Size S. Lens 1. Confidence: verified by JVM probe. The control `"javascript:alert(1)"` returns true; the tab, LF and \u0001 forms return false; `(editor-uri {:custom "java\tscript:alert(1)//{path}"} {:file "x.cljs"})` returns the script URI.

2. Under UIx (the React-hook spine), the dev-only unmount sentinel is appended as an extra CHILD of a non-void view root, which changes or breaks legal views.
   - Where: substrate/spine.cljs:2316, the `:else` branch of `append-unmount-sentinel` (`;; Non-void root — append the sentinel as a CHILD (no Fragment wrap,`). The children are rebuilt at :2321-2329.
   - Defect: the user's children list is rewritten to `[...existing sentinel]`, which has three consequences.
     - (a) A root carrying `:dangerouslySetInnerHTML` now also has `children`, and React throws "Can only set one of `children` or `props.dangerouslySetInnerHTML`".
     - (b) A component root that owns its children (a render-prop / function-as-child, or `React.Children.only`) receives `[child, sentinel]` and throws or misbehaves.
     - (c) The sentinel is unkeyed and sits at index = child count. It moves whenever that count or shape changes: 0↔1 child (`(when loading? ($ spinner))` flips props.children between null and one element), or a root over a `for` list whose length changes (that array is flattened in). Each move makes React unmount and remount the sentinel, which emits a false `:rf.view/unmounted` and a fresh render key for a view that never unmounted. Xray and the Pair MCP consume that event.
   - Cost: dev-only (production returns the bare user fn), so a legal view crashes or mis-traces in dev only. The void-root branch already uses the safe shape.
   - Fix: always use the Fragment-sibling shape the void branch uses, `(React/createElement Fragment nil annotated sentinel-el)`, and update the tests that inspect the non-void output shape. The docstring's layout argument (`:nth-child`, flex/grid) does not hold: a Fragment sibling that renders no DOM changes no layout either.
   - Size S. Lens 1. Confidence: verified by reading against React's reconciliation and `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` rules. A UIx DOM test with a toggling single child, and one with a `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` root, would settle it at runtime. Existing coverage is void roots only.

3. A `reg-view` that renders itself recursively renders the raw, unregistered fn for every nested node.
   - Where: core_reg_view_macro.cljc:165, `` fn-body  `(fn ~sym ~args ``.
   - Defect: the render fn is named with the view's own symbol. Inside the body, that symbol binds the local raw fn, not the Var holding the registered head.
   - Cost: tree views (`[tree-node child]`) are a common shape. Every nested node mounts as a plain fn component: no `data-rf-view` or `data-rf2-source-coord`, no render, unmount or perf traces, and no displayName. Xray and the Pair reverse lookup see only the outermost node.
   - Fix: emit an anonymous `(fn ~args ...)` or a non-shadowing name such as `<sym>-render`. The existing expansion test still holds.
   - Size S. Lens 1/3. Confidence: verified by JVM probe. The inner head is neither the Var value nor `(rf/view ::tree-node)`, and it renders `[:li "leaf"]` without the attrs that the registered render adds.

4. Per-consumer on-dispose callbacks accumulate without bound on shared, long-lived cached reactions.
   - Where:
     - substrate/spine.cljs:3380, `(rf.interop/add-on-dispose! reaction`, in `use-sub`'s `wire!`. Cleanup is at :3437-3472.
     - subs.cljc:2548, `(rf.interop/add-on-dispose! reaction on-dispose)`, in `acquire-watched-reaction!`, which Fresco's collector uses.
   - Defect: every consumer arms its own closure, and nothing removes it. `re-frame.disposable/IDisposable` (disposable.cljs:44) has no remove method, and neither does Reagent's. Releasing the share drops the watch and the ref count, but the closure stays.
   - Cost: a reaction that one long-lived reader keeps cached (a header's `[:selected-id]`, or a layer-2 parent's input) collects one closure per mount/unmount of every other consumer. Each closure retains React's on-change (the fiber), the committed-ref and the query-v. Virtualised rows, route churn and StrictMode double-subscribe all grow it until the reaction finally disposes, and then every stale closure runs.
   - Fix: register ONE on-dispose per reaction that dispatches to a removable per-reaction holder set (a `js/WeakMap` reaction → `js/Set`, or the same "holding dies with either end" pattern `record-holder!` / `rfSubHolders` already use for render owners). The release deletes its own entry.
   - Size M. Lens 1. Confidence: verified. A plain-atom REPL ran 1000 acquire/release cycles over a held slot: ref-count stayed 1 and 1000 callbacks fired at the final eviction. The use-sub site is verified by reading (registration is unconditional; no removal path exists).

5. Under UIx, view render traces carry no frame, stop entirely after 100 renders, and report every re-render as a mount.
   - Where: views.cljs:588, `(let [frame-id (when rf.interop/debug-enabled? (rf.views.provider/current-frame))]`, and views.cljs:575-576, `[id (rf.views.provider/reagent-component-token)]`.

     - `frame-id` is nil, so `:view/render` and `:rf.view/rendered` carry `:frame nil`. `stamp-frame` does not fill a key that is present-but-nil. Epoch capture skips frameless events, so there are no `:triggered-by` / cause links. `claim-render!` counts into a nil bucket nothing resets, so after 100 UIx renders process-wide `:rf.view/rendered` is never emitted again.
     - The token is minted fresh on every render, so `:rf.view/mount?` is always true. The render key never matches the stable key on `:rf.view/unmounted`, and `seen-render-keys` gains one entry per render for the life of the process.

     - Give the hook spine a stable per-instance token: the head holds one in a `useRef`, as the sentinel already does, and the views side reads it.
     - Remove keys from `seen-render-keys` on unmount. That also bounds the set on Reagent.
   - Size S-M. Lens 1. Confidence: verified by reading the path end to end. There is no UIx test of `:rf.view/rendered` today. A UIx DOM test under `frame-provider {:frame :f}` asserting `:frame :f`, a stable render key, and emission past 100 renders would settle it.
