The uncached reaction then NPEs on deref. A single-source kind has the same exposure via `(container-fn frame-id)` returning nil.
   - Cost: Spec 006 §Lifetime contract — frame disposal promises that a subscribe against a destroyed frame does not throw. This is reachable when a JVM `destroy-frame!` runs on another thread mid-subscribe.
   - Test gap: sub_cache_test.clj:205, `layer-2-input-refs-released-when-frame-destroyed-mid-build`, checks ref counts but never derefs the returned reaction.
   - Fix: after the step, if any resolved input or container is nil, release the acquired non-nil inputs and return the constant-nil recovery the `input-error?` branch already builds. Add a deref to that test.
   - Size S. Lens 1/5. Confidence: verified by JVM REPL. A `with-redefs` on `rf.frame/frame` (the in-tree test's technique) fires after `[:a]` is cached and before `[:b]`; the deref threw NullPointerException.

7. JVM memo cells can tear under a concurrent deref and serve a result computed for a different db.
   - Where: subs/memo.cljc:668-669, `(vreset! last-db db)` / `(vreset! last-result computed)`. The same two-write pattern is at :741-743 and :797-799.
   - Defect: input and result live in two volatiles. A reader between the two writes sees the new input beside the old result and takes a memo HIT on it. Two interleaved recomputes can leave a persistent mismatched pair, which keeps serving the wrong value until the input next changes.
   - Cost: the cache's install-race code (subs.cljc:1369-1378) explicitly supports two threads on one frame and query, and the plain-atom reaction runs the memo on every deref.
   - Fix: hold `[input result policy]` in ONE volatile, written once per recompute and read once per call. That is one small allocation per recompute only; reader-conditional it if the CLJS byte budget matters. `locking` on the JVM is the alternative.
   - Size S-M. Lens 1. Confidence: the transient tear is verified by JVM REPL (the worker paused after its first vreset!; a concurrent deref returned 1 while app-db `:n` was 2). The persistent pair is probable, by interleaving argument. No test derefs one reaction from two threads.

8. On the JVM, any process that has dispatched never exits on its own.
   - Where: interop.clj:15, `(defonce ^:private executor (Executors/newSingleThreadExecutor))`, and :165-166, the scheduled executor.
   - Defect: both use the default thread factory, which makes non-daemon threads.
   - Cost: every async `dispatch` goes through `next-tick`, and `:dispatch-later` and machine `:after` use the scheduled executor. So a JVM script, a codegen `-main` or a static-export job hangs after finishing. The repo's own runners hide it by calling `System/exit`.
   - Fix: pass a ThreadFactory that makes named daemon threads for both executors. State the trade-off in the docstring: work still queued when main returns is dropped, so scripts use `dispatch-sync`.
   - Size S. Lens 3. Confidence: verified by probe. `next-tick` followed by return from main hung until a 90 s timeout killed it; the control without `next-tick` exited in about 2 s.

    - Defect: opts are compared with `=`, and CLJS fns compare by identity. Inline `:fx-overrides {:http (fn ...)}`, or interceptors built during render, differ on every render although nothing changed. The error then prints two maps that look identical.
    - Cost: a legal, idiomatic React shape fails loud at the first re-render.
    - Fix: compare with fn-insensitive equality (treat fn leaves as equal, or compare fns only by presence). At minimum, when the two maps print the same, say "opts differ only by function identity — hoist the fns out of render".

The subscriber's own write succeeded but it catches a foreign error, the outer drain's real failure is lost, and a throw from the nested body itself is dropped because `:escaped` is occupied.

Its ex-data column adds :received for the policy-shape arm, and :received plus :bad-key (key or key path, e.g. [:backoff :base-ms]) for the numbers arm, matching Spec 014 §Retry and backoff. The PR's CI is green.

title: senior review: xray: panels
description:
SENIOR-DEVELOPER REVIEW of one slice of the tree. Part of the review sweep rf2-r5cc2, which partitions implementation/, tools/, examples/ and skills/ into slices; this bead owns exactly the slice below, and its siblings own the rest.

SLICE:
- tools/xray/src/**/panels/**
- tools/xray/test/**/panels/**, tools/xray/test/**/panels_e2e/**

FOCUS: Xray's inspection panels (App-DB diff, epoch, machine inspector, event spine, routing, resources, local render) against tools/xray/spec.

PERSONA. A senior Clojure/ClojureScript developer who did not write this code, reading it as its next maintainer and as a programmer who has to use it. Judge it against the project stance (CLAUDE.md), quoted verbatim:

> Posture is that we are pre-alpha and focused on elegance, power and a masterpiece.
> But we are not over-engineering or gold plating. Also, we trust the programmer.
> We're trying to facilitate high productivity for them (and the AI they use) via a
> library with excellent ergonomics and low friction. We don't need to litigate every
> last fine detail and drown in the minutiae.

So record material, actionable insights only: a defect, a simplification that removes real weight, an ergonomic sharp edge a programmer (or the AI they use) will hit, a test that cannot go red, a doc or docstring that misleads. Not style preferences, not nagging diagnostics, not defensive belt-and-braces, not renames for taste.

LENSES, in priority order:
1. Correctness — error paths, concurrency, cleanup, and fail-closed behaviour on any security or privacy boundary.
2. Simplicity and clarity — dead code, duplication (within the slice or with another slice), accidental complexity, an abstraction that earns nothing.
3. Ergonomics — the API or tool as a programmer, or the AI they use, actually meets it.
4. Performance — hot spots on real paths, never at the expense of clarity.
5. Test rigour — a test that cannot fail, a gap on a branch that matters.
6. Comments and docstrings — per CLAUDE.md § Conventions & Patterns: present tense, the reason plus a spec pointer, no provenance, no restated spec.

METHOD. Read the slice's source first, then its tests, against the owning spec sections (spec/Ownership.md maps each surface to its spec). A finding is a CLAIM until checked: confirm each one at source, and confirm a behaviour claim with a quick REPL or test run where that is cheap. This is a read-only review: edit no file, and run only read-only commands and the slice's existing test lanes.

OUTPUT, recorded on THIS bead and never in a separate file: write the section to a file and append it with `bd update <this bead> --append-notes "$(cat <file>)"` (never `--notes`, which replaces). Head it `== SENIOR REVIEW FINDINGS (<datetime with zone>, trunk <short sha>)` and include:
- 0 to 15 numbered findings, most important first. Each gives: `path:line` (plus a short quote so it can be re-found by text), what is wrong, why it matters (the concrete failure or cost), the fix (a sketch is fine), size (S/M/L), confidence (verified / probable), and its lens.
- A short "looked at and sound" list, so the review's coverage is visible.
- Cross-slice findings, whose defect lives in another slice's files, in a separate list naming the owning slice. Do not act on them.

Then add the label `findings-recorded` and leave the bead OPEN: its findings become this slice's fix work, which the coordinator dispatches in clusters. If the slice needs nothing, record zero findings with the coverage list and close the bead with that as the reason.
notes:
== SENIOR REVIEW FINDINGS (2026-10-29 17:26:53 AUSEST, trunk daa0e2d311)

Slice: tools/xray/src/**/panels/** (58 files, 42,231 lines) and tools/xray/test/**/panels/**, panels_e2e/** (115 files, 33,883 lines), read against tools/xray/spec 003, 004, 013, 016, 018, 021, 023-028 and spec/015. Nothing in the slice changed between trunk 8c71b53d13 (where the review started) and daa0e2d311. Paths: P/ = tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/, T/ = tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/. "verified" means checked at the cited line and, where it says "probe", confirmed by a JVM run against the real substrate whose decisive output is quoted inline. The findings are grouped by surface so each one is a single fix cluster.

1. Cancellation-cascade row jump does nothing, and its test cannot fail. P/cancellation_cascade_events.cljs:72,85,90 `(conj [:dispatch [[:rf.xray/select-dispatch-id`.
   - Wrong: all three child fx are `[:dispatch [[event] {:frame here}]]`. The reserved `:dispatch` fx takes the event vector itself (fx.cljc `reserved-fx-handlers` hands `args` straight to `child-dispatch!`), so each is refused with `:rf.error/invalid-event`. Clicking a decision, teardown or abort row moves no focus, switches no tab and leaves the popover open. The rows also carry no `:frame` (P/cancellation_cascade.cljs:285,318,361), so `select-dispatch-id` gets nil frame on a multi-frame host.
   - Test: T/panels/cancellation_cascade_cljs_test.cljs:116 asserts `:selected-tab` is `:epoch`, which is already the sub's default (registry.cljs `(get db :selected-tab :epoch)`), so it passes with nothing dispatched.
   - Fix: `[:dispatch [:rf.xray/select-dispatch-id dispatch-id frame]]` (children inherit the parent's `:frame` through `child-dispatch-opts`, so drop the opts), carry `:frame (get-in ev [:tags :frame])` on the three row builders, and make the test start from a non-`:epoch` tab and assert focus moved and the popover closed.
   - Size S. Lens correctness + test rigour. Verified, probe: `[:dispatch [[:probe/b] {:frame :probe/g}]]` logged `:rf.error/invalid-event ... got {:type :vector, :count 2}. Nothing was dispatched.` while the control `[:dispatch [:probe/b]]` in the same run set `:b true`.

2. Past epochs are redacted under TODAY's classification, so a departed secret shows in clear. P/app_db_diff_subs.cljs:304 `redact (fn [v] (local-render/local-render-value v observed-frame))`; same per-slot approach in P/epoch_panel.cljs `redact-record-db`.
   - Wrong: both walk each record slot (`:db-before`, `:db-after`, runtime-db partitions) as a bare value. That walk reads route and machine classification from the frame's LIVE runtime-db, whereas Spec 015 §Retained values keeps the recorded classification. After navigating away from a route declaring `:sensitive [[:query :token]]`, the head epoch's pre-image shows the raw token in the `:rf/route` section's "was" annotation; a destroyed machine's `:data` ghost should leak the same way (not probed).
   - Related: `:rf.xray/selected-epoch-record` (P/app_db_diff_subs.cljs:112-116) is a RAW record sub with zero src consumers; its docs (app_db_diff_subs.cljs:13-15,26-27, app_db_diff.cljs:51-53) say the Epoch `:db` diff reads it and "runs its own `db-diff-paths`" (no such fn exists; the Epoch panel deliberately refuses this sub). A panel author following the docs reaches the one record sub that skips the egress seam.
   - Fix: project the focused record once with `rf/project-egress` (`:kind :rf/epoch-record`, `:rf.egress/profile :rf.egress/local-redacted`, `:rf.egress/include-large? true`, `:rf.egress/include-runtime-db? true`, `:frame observed`) in both panels and read slots from the projected record; keep `local-render-value` for the cold-boot live value only. Delete `:rf.xray/selected-epoch-record` and repoint its two test readers at `:rf.xray/app-db-current+diff`.
   - Size M. Lens correctness (privacy). Verified, probe: route `:sensitive [[:query :token]]`, navigate away; the panel's path gives `"SECRET123"`, the record-level door gives `:rf/redacted` and keeps the sibling `"posts"`. Dead-sub claim verified by repo-wide grep with the definition as control.

3. Resources §2 Live instances shows a `:sensitive? true` resource's scope, params, error body and cursors raw, while §3/§5/§6/§6d/§8 redact them. P/resources.cljs:1524-1526 `(h/project-instances entries now-ms (on-box-resource-egress-fn observed-frame))`; P/resources_helpers.cljc:837-843 `:cursor (summarize (eg next-param :params))`.
   - Wrong: the coarse `:sensitive?` claim classifies only `:data` in runtime-db, so the §2 on-box egress matches nothing for scope/params/`:error`/`:refresh-error`/`:page-error`/`:cursor`/`:page-params`. An HTTP 4xx body echoing submitted fields renders in the `error` preview. §6c's gate (resources_helpers.cljc:1580-1586) looks only at exempt keys, so it prints a descriptor scope §6 redacts for the same invalidation. Spec 024's own rule ("redacting some and printing the rest is the same leak in a different shape") condemns it.
   - Fix: thread `sensitive-rids` into the §2 egress so a sensitive resource's non-`:data` slots collapse to `:rf/redacted`; add the settlement row's `:affected-keys` to the §6c gate. (Root alternative is cross-slice, see below.) Spec 024 L150-154 vs L188-195 must agree on whether scope/params are on-box identity.
   - Size S-M. Lens correctness (privacy). Verified, probe: §2 previews `{:id "SECRET-abc123"}`, `{:kind :rf.http/http-4xx, :body {:echo "SECRET-abc123"}}`, `{:after "SECRET-abc123"}` while `work-row` for the same resource gives `[redacted]`; §6c scope `"[:rf.scope/session {:user 42}]"` vs §6 `"[redacted]"`.

4. The Derivation Graph tab shows sensitive values raw on-box, and its off-box redaction test cannot catch the route case. P/derivation_graph.cljs:534 `(let [summarized (h/summarize-graph graph)]`; P/derivation_graph_helpers.cljc:429 `summarize-node`.
   - Wrong: Xray's on-box default is `:rf.egress/local-redacted` (P/local_render.cljc ns doc: "ONE projection seam every Xray panel routes a FRAME-SOURCED value through"), and Routing/App-DB/Resources/Epoch honour it. The Graph tab previews `:value`/`:params`/`:query`/`:state` straight from the raw graph, so a route token hidden on the Routing tab appears on the Graph tab (the screen-share leak the profile exists to stop). Spec 025 §"On-box rendering is RAW" sanctions this; it predates and contradicts the tool-wide default, so the spec changes with the fix.
   - Test gap: T/panels/derivation_graph_redaction_cljs_test.cljc:127 builds a route `:params {:current {:params {:token ...` shape `route-slice-algebra-view` never produces and classifies the matching app-db path, so it stays green while real route-declared params pass the off-box walk raw (latent: the off-box path has no production caller). T/panels/derivation_graph_view_cljs_test.cljs:55 `(defn- tab-data` is a hand copy of derivation_graph.cljs:536-542 although its ns doc says drift "surfaces here".
   - Fix: in live mode project value fields before summarising (`local-render-route-slice` for the route node, `local-render-value` with `(:frame graph)` elsewhere); lift the tab-data composite into a pure `h/tab-data` called by both the sub and the test; rewrite the redaction fixture to `reg-route` with a `:sensitive` param and a real navigation. Amend Spec 025 §Privacy.
   - Size M. Lens correctness (privacy) + test rigour. Verified, probe: route `{:sensitive [[:params :token]]}` navigated for real; Graph preview `"{:token \"secret-abc123\", :tab \"posts\"}"`, Routing seam `{:token :rf/redacted, :tab "posts"}`, `redact-graph-for-egress` `{:token "secret-abc123", ...}`.

5. Trace panel target column reads tag names no producer emits. P/trace_helpers.cljc:488-489 `(get tags :rf.sub/old tags-absent)`, :500 `(:rf.view/cause-sub tags)`, :457-459 `(:rf.db/path tags)`.
   - Wrong: subs emit `:rf.sub/prev-value`/`:rf.sub/value`, views `:rf.view/triggered-by`/`:rf.view/cause-subs`, and `:rf.event/db-changed` carries no path. SUB rows never show `old -> new` and VIEW rows never show `<- cause`, though Spec 023 §3/§5 and the ns doc promise both. Same mistake the file already fixed for `:rf.fx/args` (comment at :467). Dead fallbacks `:rf.fx/effect-id`, `:rf.flow/id`, `:rf.flow/path` likewise match nothing. T/panels/trace_helpers_cljs_test.cljc:153-155 fabricates `:rf.db/path :rf.db/old :rf.db/new`; sub and view causes are untested.
   - Fix: read `:rf.sub/prev-value`/`:rf.sub/value` by key presence and `:rf.view/triggered-by`; drop the never-emitted reads; rebuild the fixtures on the real trace builders. Spec 023 line ~385 (db-changed target "path old -> new") should say the per-path list carries it.
   - Size S. Lens correctness. Verified: `git grep -F` over implementation/*/src/* finds `:rf.sub/old` in 0 files and the control `:rf.sub/prev-value` in 7; `:rf.view/cause-sub` occurs only as the prefix of `:rf.view/cause-subs`.

6. App-DB `display-value` realises lazy seqs, so an endless seq in app-db hangs the host page. P/app_db_diff_format.cljs:40-41 `(or (vector? v) (set? v) (sequential? v)) (some needs-elision? v)` and :92-93 `(doall (map rewrite v))`.
   - Wrong: runs on every section value and before-image (P/app_db_diff_state.cljs:390,398) before the inspector, which itself bounds non-`counted?` seqs at 1001 for exactly this case; the core walker deliberately never forces a seq. A `(range)`/`(cycle ...)` in app-db freezes the tab; a finite lazy seq runs app code from inside the devtool. The "O(1)" claim at :46-52 is also false (full-tree scan per call).
   - Fix: treat non-`counted?` sequentials as leaves in `needs-elision?` and `rewrite`; better, run `display-value` once in the sub, not per render.
   - Size S. Lens correctness. Verified (JVM analogue of the private CLJS expression): local-render realised 0 of 5000 elements and kept the seq identical; the same `some` pre-scan realised 5000 of 5000.

7. Epoch projection misreads nested work inside one epoch. P/epoch/projection.cljc.
   - (a) :612 `(some #(= :rf.machine/action-ran (op %)) events) :reg-machine`: a plain `reg-event` whose `:fx` destroys a machine runs the `:exit` cascade synchronously, so flavour flips to `:reg-machine` and the view hides the handler's source block and `:db` diff.
   - (b) :640, :703 `(when-let [do-fx (find-op events :rf.fx/do-fx)]`: nested walks (exit-action fx, resource release) emit a bare `do-fx` before the router's terminal one that carries `:rf.event/fx`, so `:fx-vec` is nil and the HANDLER `:fx` section vanishes.
   - (c) :1656 `handler-wrote-db?` and :1974 `db-commit?` count any `:rf.event/db-changed`; a post-walk flow settle's commit becomes a phantom handler `:db` row (`{:fx-id :db :status :ok}`) and the HANDLER `:db` shows the flow's write.
   - (d) :2149 `(or (= "rf.fx" (op-ns ev))` with :2156 `(get fx-outcome-op->status o :ok)`: `:rf.fx/push-url-failed`/`replace-url-failed` become extra check-mark rows, so a failed navigation renders two oks and epoch outcome `:ok`.
   - (e) :1891 `(if (and fx-id (not (contains? a fx-id)))`: machine fx attribution is first-wins per fx-id, so two actions emitting `:dispatch` both attribute to the first.
   - Fix: (a) derive `:reg-machine` from a machine trace whose actor is the event id (or drop :612) and attach the cascade whenever rows exist; (b) select the `do-fx` that carries `:rf.event/fx`; (c) count db ops only before the first fx-walk op, the window `candidate-rejected-at?` already uses; (d) filter on `(contains? fx-outcome-op->status o)`, no `:ok` default; (e) a FIFO per fx-id.
   - Size S each. Lens correctness. Verified, probes on the real substrate: (a)/(b) flavour `:reg-machine`, fx-vec nil, two `:rf.fx/do-fx` in the ops; (c) `:E-db-effect-row {:fx-id :db, :status :ok}`, `handler-wrote-db? true`; (d) rows `[[:rf.nav/push-url :ok] [:rf.nav/push-url :ok]]` (synthetic trace shaped on the nav_fx emit); (e) `[[[:a/left] :notify-exit] [[:a/entered] :notify-exit]]`.

8. Epoch HANDLER `:db` diff compares two different privacy policies, and the redaction seam behind it is untested. P/epoch_panel.cljs `redact-record-db` (before side, via `local-render-value`, which sets `:rf.egress/include-large? true`, P/local_render.cljc:161-163) against the t1 trace snapshot (projection.cljc ~1568-1576), which classification.cljc `project-db-tags` already passed through `elide-wire-value` at emit.
   - Cost: on a frame with a `:large` classification every handler returning `:db` diffs a raw large "before" against a `:rf.size/large-elided` "after", so the panel's main what-changed signal shows false changes. No test references `redact-record-db` or asserts a redacted slot through `:rf.xray/epoch-pipeline`, so dropping the seam stays green.
   - Fix: take both sides under one policy (folds into finding 2's record-level projection); add a sub-level test declaring one sensitive and one large path with a raw sibling as control.
   - Size S. Lens correctness + test rigour. Both option sets verified at source; the rendered mismatch is probable. Note implementation/core epoch/tool_pair.cljc says "the t1/t2 stamps are stored raw", contradicting the emit-time projection; one comment is stale (cross-slice).

9. Epoch view and panel: four small defects. P/epoch/view.cljs, P/epoch_panel.cljs.
   - (a) :2348 `(case source :after-timer ...` and :2429: no `:machine-action` arm, though fx.cljc stamps it for every machine-emitted `:dispatch`/`:dispatch-later` and the projection builds its parent-epoch enrichment (projection.cljc ~171,191). A machine's child dispatch gets no parent-epoch link or delay chip; `:after-timer`/`:machine-spawn` without enrichment also lose the "from " prefix. Fix: a `:machine-action` arm; have `dispatch-source-enriched-label` return the full verb and delete the second `case`. No test mentions `:machine-action`.
   - (b) :5022 `(keyword (str "sub-row-" (some-> row :sub-id name)))` plus projection.cljc ~2851 `attach-to-sub-row` matching on sub-id alone: `[:item 1]`/`[:item 2]` (or `:a/total`/`:b/total`) share violation testids, `:site-id` and inspector `:mount-id`, and one failing instance shows its violation under every instance. Fix: key by row index; attach by query vector.
   - (c) :5364 `:row-key (fn [_ i] (str "view-" i))` with :5372-5373 mouse enter/leave: React fires no mouseleave on unmount and index-keyed rows clear the NEW view's id, so the host-app highlight stays on when the epoch moves under the pointer. P/reactive_panel_view.cljs:241-262 carries a copy with the same bug. Fix: one shared helper that clears by class and runs from the container's detaching ref.
   - (d) P/epoch_panel.cljs:121 `resolve-event-recordables` returns nil for a REGISTERED event that declares no requirements, which the projection reads as "no resolver, show all" (projection.cljc ~322), so exactly those events present every undeclared token leaf as a recordable input. Fix: return `#{}` for a registered event.
   - Size S. Lens correctness. Verified by reading at each line.

10. Machine panels: a fail-open redaction, a retro mode that cannot be entered, and a process-global tick loop.
   - (a) P/machine_inspector.cljs:210-212 `(catch :default _ ev))]` then `(or (get-in out [:tags :snapshot]) snapshot)`: if `project-trace-event` throws, the raw snapshot is returned, so Static Machines (which reads `:rf.xray/machine-snapshots`) shows sensitive `:data` in clear; the trace path has no such catch. Fix: on catch return `(assoc snapshot :data :rf/redacted)`. Verified by reading.
   - (b) P/machine_after_rings.cljs:388,666 `[:rf.xray/machine-scrubber-position]`: only tests dispatch `:rf.xray/set-scrubber-position`, so the gate is always `:present`; on spine Prev the rings keep sweeping current timers over a past epoch's chart, contradicting Spec 003 §M.2. `resolve-now-ms`, `focused-cascade-time-ms`, the `:focused-detail` read (a re-render per bundle change for an unused anchor), the scrubber sub and event are dead as a result. Fix: hide rings when focus `:mode` is `:retro` and delete that machinery (S), or build real retro (M). Verified by repo-wide grep (writers: tests and specs only).
   - (c) machine_after_rings.cljs:318-333,444,460 `(swap! tick-state assoc :frame frame :mounted? true)`: one `:frame` and one boolean `:mounted?` per process, so unmounting one of two overlays freezes the survivor and two frames fight over `:frame`; `kick-tick!` also arms with empty specs, when no ref exists to clear it. Fix: state keyed by frame with a mount count, armed from the ref. Mechanism verified by reading; visible effect probable (a two-overlay DOM test settles it).
   - (d) P/machine_canvas.cljs:320 `(chart-tree props identity [after-rings/AfterRingsOverlay-bridge])`: both production callers of the Reagent `Chart` head (static/machines/topology.cljs:123, sim.cljs:881) pass `:show-after-rings? false`, so the bridge, `AfterRingsOverlay-component` and the prop never run, yet they are the only path the canvas and boundary DOM tests cover; the live `Chart-view` path's `:mounted?` gate has no DOM test. Fix: delete the bridge path and point those tests at `Chart-view`. Verified by grep of the call sites.
   - Size S-M. Lens correctness + simplicity + test rigour.

(continued in part 2 of 2)
== SENIOR REVIEW FINDINGS (continued, part 2 of 2)

11. App-DB and Views panels render a state they are not in for evicted, no-epoch or withheld focus.
   - P/app_db_diff_subs.cljs:186,207 `:value (if record (:db-after record) db)`: a pinned-but-evicted epoch or a no-epoch bundle silently shows the LIVE db with no diff; Spec 021 §10.7/§11.3 require a placeholder per panel. T/panels_e2e/evicted_epoch_all_panels_cljs_test.cljs:166,177 asserts against `:rf.xray/selected-epoch-record`, a sub the panel never reads, so it cannot go red.
   - P/app_db_diff_helpers.cljc:525-527 `demap`: a nil/destroyed observed frame redacts the whole value to `:rf/redacted`, which `demap` turns into `{:top {} :areas []}` and the panel says "app-db has no user-domain keys yet", hiding the redaction; T/panels/app_db_diff_helpers_cljs_test.cljc:70-78 pins that reading.
   - P/reactive_panel_view.cljs:726-729 says "Focused event-bundle has no reactive activity captured yet." exactly when no record was found (evicted pin, no epoch); T/panels/reactive_panel_view_cljs_test.cljs:74 locks it in. Trace and Epoch already map `focus/resolve-focus-status` to the shared messages (trace.cljs:1269).
   - Fix: resolve through `focus-resolver`'s 3-arity, carry a `:status` on `:rf.xray/app-db-current+diff` as the Epoch pipeline does, give each panel evicted/no-epoch/withheld bodies, and repoint the e2e test. The App-DB copy for an unselected or withheld frame is a Spec 004 gap (Spec 008 promises it).
   - Size M. Lens correctness + test rigour. Verified by reading and probe (whole-redacted value -> `{:top {}, :areas []}`).

12. Managed-fx and Resources: the failing fx has no record, §2 costs grow with cache size, and three reads come from the wrong source.
   - (a) P/managed_fx_helpers.cljc:1184-1193 walks only the bundle's `:effects`; `:rf.error/fx-handler-exception`, `:rf.error/no-such-fx` (op-type `:error`) and `:rf.fx/skipped-on-platform` (`:warning`) land in `:other`, so the panel shows 0 records exactly for the failing case, and four `fx-event->status` arms (383-394) plus the `:aborted` arm of `surface-events->phase` (476-479) are unreachable. Fix: also take `:other` rows carrying `:rf.fx/id` and `:rf.fx/args` (M), or delete the dead arms (S). description:
SENIOR-DEVELOPER REVIEW of one slice of the tree. Part of the review sweep rf2-r5cc2, which partitions implementation/, tools/, examples/ and skills/ into slices; this bead owns exactly the slice below, and its siblings own the rest.

SLICE:
- skills/re-frame2-setup/**
- skills/re-frame2-xray/**

FOCUS: Setting up a re-frame2 project and Xray: does following the skill produce a working project on a clean machine?

PERSONA. A senior Clojure/ClojureScript developer who did not write this code, reading it as its next maintainer and as a programmer who has to use it. Judge it against the project stance (CLAUDE.md), quoted verbatim:

> Posture is that we are pre-alpha and focused on elegance, power and a masterpiece.
> But we are not over-engineering or gold plating. Also, we trust the programmer.
> We're trying to facilitate high productivity for them (and the AI they use) via a
> library with excellent ergonomics and low friction. We don't need to litigate every
> last fine detail and drown in the minutiae.

So record material, actionable insights only: a defect, a simplification that removes real weight, an ergonomic sharp edge a programmer (or the AI they use) will hit, a test that cannot go red, a doc or docstring that misleads. Not style preferences, not nagging diagnostics, not defensive belt-and-braces, not renames for taste.

LENSES, in priority order:
1. Correctness — error paths, concurrency, cleanup, and fail-closed behaviour on any security or privacy boundary.
2. Simplicity and clarity — dead code, duplication (within the slice or with another slice), accidental complexity, an abstraction that earns nothing.
3. Ergonomics — the API or tool as a programmer, or the AI they use, actually meets it.
4. Performance — hot spots on real paths, never at the expense of clarity.
5. Test rigour — a test that cannot fail, a gap on a branch that matters.
6. Comments and docstrings — per CLAUDE.md § Conventions & Patterns: present tense, the reason plus a spec pointer, no provenance, no restated spec.

METHOD. Read the slice's source first, then its tests, against the owning spec sections (spec/Ownership.md maps each surface to its spec). A finding is a CLAIM until checked: confirm each one at source, and confirm a behaviour claim with a quick REPL or test run where that is cheap. This is a read-only review: edit no file, and run only read-only commands and the slice's existing test lanes.

OUTPUT, recorded on THIS bead and never in a separate file: write the section to a file and append it with `bd update <this bead> --append-notes "$(cat <file>)"` (never `--notes`, which replaces). Head it `== SENIOR REVIEW FINDINGS (<datetime with zone>, trunk <short sha>)` and include:
- 0 to 15 numbered findings, most important first. Each gives: `path:line` (plus a short quote so it can be re-found by text), what is wrong, why it matters (the concrete failure or cost), the fix (a sketch is fine), size (S/M/L), confidence (verified / probable), and its lens.
- A short "looked at and sound" list, so the review's coverage is visible.
- Cross-slice findings, whose defect lives in another slice's files, in a separate list naming the owning slice. Do not act on them.

Then add the label `findings-recorded` and leave the bead OPEN: its findings become this slice's fix work, which the coordinator dispatches in clusters. If the slice needs nothing, record zero findings with the coverage list and close the bead with that as the reason.

title: Migration classpath checker must skip empty or comment-only source files
description:
Audit of merged PR #11685 (e482c15effb10fa97f8cdc2c81b9598db7e0adad), correctness lens. The fenced checker remains byte-identical at current HEAD.

description:

## Ruling

EP-0039 is accepted (operator ruling 2026-10-16, option B with the independent Codex review). This is EP-0039 §Backwards Compatibility step 3. The vertical slice rf2-o5rtr built `reg-classification`, the per-frame policy and its epoch capture, and moved the login draft password onto it; its measurement confirmed the simplification. Stage 1 (subsystems at egress) lands first.

## Work

Move every in-tree app-db classification effect to a `reg-classification` beside its feature, because the effects are deleted below and the tree must stay green: the realworld ceremony sites `:auth/classify-token` (examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/core.cljs) and `:settings/load` (realworld_resources/settings.cljs), every other `:sensitive` / `:large` / `:clear-*` effect a handler returns (census by the effect keys in returned maps, not by prose), the tests that install classification through effects, and the conformance fixtures with `:source :effect`.

3. Close the effect map to `:db`, `:rf.db/runtime` and `:fx`: a handler returning one of the four is refused by `:rf.error/effect-map-shape`, whose message names `reg-classification`; `:rf.error/classification-effect-shape` goes.
4. Delete, counted at trunk f776a3a322 (562 lines of whole forms and named ranges):
   - re-frame.elision (352 in forms): `write-elision-slot` 27, `effect-owner` 7, `add-claims` 14, `remove-claims` 22, `remove-owner` 19, `replace-owner-claims` 10, `reconcile-runtime-db-effect` 42, `apply-elision-transform` 10, `swap-elision-slot!` 29, `classification-effect-keys` 7, `classification-effect-axis` 10, `classification-effect?` 6, `classification-effects` 5, `classification-effect-defect` 47, `apply-classification-effects` 56, `elide-candidate-value` 21, `elide-pending-db` 20; plus 59 comment lines (the multi-owner registry section 162-188, the no-rollback note 286-289, the commit-plane effects section 375-402);

5. Decide, and record on this bead, whether the epoch record's policy reference stays in record metadata (the slice's choice, which needed no Spec-Schemas edit and never egresses) or becomes a stripped `:rf/epoch-record` slot.
6. Spec graduation per EP-0039 §Spec sections the implementation changes: Spec 015 (§Durable app-db — the four commit-plane effects goes, §SSR loses the registry omission, §Failure posture, §What is removed, the §Tests fixture rows), Spec 002 §Commit-plane data-classification effects, Conventions (the reservations and the two `:rf.runtime/elision` runtime-db rows), Spec-Schemas `:rf/effect-map` and `:rf/runtime-db`, the Spec 009 classification error rows, spec/API.md with both manifest sidecars.

After stage 1 merges. HOT ZONES: spec/002-Frames.md, spec/Conventions.md, spec/Spec-Schemas.md, spec/009-Instrumentation.md, spec/API.md with its two manifest sidecars — queue behind any bead holding them. Propagation follows this.

Stage 1 is PR #11694 (closes rf2-4q7tv). What stage 2 inherits:

- Subsystem claims are never in the registry now. `re-frame.elision/registry-of` builds the live classification as: raw `[:rf.runtime/elision]` registry, then `with-policy` (the `:app-db` declarations), then `with-runtime-classification` (each root hook applied to the live runtime-db under `:roots`). `elide-candidate-value` does the same over the candidate runtime-db, and `re-frame.epoch.tool-pair/recorded-registry` does it over the recorded runtime-db under [recorded-policy current-policy]. == WORK 5 DECISION (epoch record policy reference) — 2026-10-29

Decision: the epoch record's policy reference STAYS IN RECORD METADATA (the stage-1 slice's choice). No stripped `:rf/epoch-record` slot.

Why:
- It is the smaller change: `re-frame.epoch.assembly` already attaches the policy the record was captured under as metadata (`re-frame.elision/record-policy`), and `re-frame.epoch.tool-pair`'s recorded registry reads it back (`re-frame.elision/recorded-policy`). A slot would add a Spec-Schemas `:rf/epoch-record` key, a strip at every egress and a test for the strip, to carry the same value.
- Metadata never egresses, so the reference cannot leak a declaration list onto the wire, and the record's public shape is unchanged.
- The one thing a slot would buy is surviving serialisation or a metadata-dropping transform. A record leaves the box only projected, so the raw record a later re-projection reads is always the in-memory one that still carries its metadata. No in-tree consumer serialises a raw record and re-projects it.
- Measured: `a-cleared-flows-output-keeps-its-recorded-classification` stays green through the recorded policy at the PR head.
